findings.title: 'tablets'/'tablet' maps to electronics, so every GCC pharmacy pair is compared as an electronics product and a correct Supplements chip is silently overridden
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: On the explicit_pair/vision branch the deterministic token map must not outrank an unambiguous domain signal. Minimum fix: drop 'tablet'/'tablets' from _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS (the electronics tablet sense is already covered by 'ipad'-class model names reaching A2b, and 'tablets' as a dosage form is far more frequent in GCC queries than the device sense); better fix: gate the electronics reading on a co-occurring device signal the way is_supplement_query already gates its AMBIGUOUS tokens (price_service.py:1294-1305) — i.e. move tablet/tablets into an AMBIGUOUS set needing a device corroborator (inch/GB/wifi/cellular/brand), else fall through. Ship behind ENABLE_AMBIGUOUS_CATEGORY_TOKENS so flag-off is byte-identical.
findings.test_first: tests/test_category_classifier_ambiguous_tokens.py::test_pharmacy_tablets_are_not_electronics — assert classify_category_from_text('Panadol Extra 24 tablets vs Adol 500 tablets') != 'electronics', and assert await _resolve_pair_category(explicit_pair_products, 'supplements', parser_path=False)[0] == 'supplements'. Companion: assert classify_category_from_text('Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 tablet 256GB') == 'electronics' so the device sense survives.
findings.impact: The mobile app's ONLY compare path is explicit_pair (HomeScreen streamComparison({product_a,product_b}) at both 97b5f15 — the bundle on phones — and 76ace90), so name detection DRIVES and the LLM never gets a vote. Any OTC/pharmacy pair phrased with the single most common GCC pharmacy word gets: the electronics spec schema (display/processor/ram/storage/battery/rear_camera/os/connectivity requested from GPT for a paracetamol box = ~11 wasted schema slots per product), electronics hero dimensions (Performance / Build quality / Ecosystem / Future-proofing on a painkiller), electronics CATEGORY_FAIRNESS (unit='GB', _extract_storage) so like-for-like reconciliation is dead, and electronics priority adjustments. Measured 1/40 in my supplements corpus but that corpus favours dose-suffixed names; every 'X tablets vs Y tablets' phrasing hits it. Pharmacy is a stated GCC launch category.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced through the real runtime functions at 76ace90. `"tablet": "electronics", "tablets": "electronics"` are at exactly 1096-1097; classify_category_from_text (1156) sweeps _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS after the is_supplement_query short-circuit, so all four pharmacy pairs return electronics. Reachable with no flag: HomeScreen sends {product_a,product_b} -> explicit_pair -> _parser_path=False -> det=name_cat wins and flips a real chip (switched=True). Electronics unit="GB" confirmed. Caveat: the finder's own companion test ('Galaxy Tab S10 tablet 256GB' == electronics) would FAIL under their own minimum fix (dropping the tokens) — only the corroborator variant satisfies both. Not in M13/M18/mobile docs; new. P1 stands.

findings.title: _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS contains zero Arabic tokens: 0 of 58 Arabic/mixed-script queries classify, so every Arabic compare without a chip pays the A2b GPT call or lands in 'other'
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add an Arabic synonym block to _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS keyed on the same 9 canonical values — at minimum عطر/عطور/بخور/دهن عود -> fragrances, جوال/هاتف/موبايل/لابتوب/تلفزيون/شاشة/مكيف/غسالة/ثلاجة -> electronics, حليب/أرز/زيت/شاي/قهوة -> grocery, فيتامين/فيتامينات/مكمل/بروتين -> supplements, شامبو/بلسم/صبغة/زيت شعر -> haircare, كريم/سيروم/غسول/واقي شمس -> skincare, مكياج/أحمر شفاه/مسكارا/فاونديشن/بودرة -> makeup, عباية/حجاب/ثوب/شماغ/بشت/قفطان/حذاء/ساعة/نظارة -> fashion. classify_category_from_text uses `\b{token}\b` which works for Arabic under re.UNICODE, but multi-word Arabic tokens need the same whitespace normalisation canonicalize_category already does. Ship behind ENABLE_ARABIC_CATEGORY_TOKENS; flag-off is byte-identical because the map is only consulted on a hit.
findings.test_first: tests/test_category_classifier_arabic.py::test_arabic_queries_classify_deterministically — parametrise 9 canonical Arabic queries (one per category) and assert classify_category_from_text returns the right canonical key for each; assert the A2b escalation is NOT reached by patching classify_category_llm to raise and asserting _resolve_pair_category still returns the right category with selected_category=None, parser_path=False.
findings.impact: On the explicit_pair path (the shipped app) an Arabic-typing user who does not tap a chip always reaches the blind branch at SCS@76ace90:379 -> classify_category_llm, i.e. an extra gpt-4o-mini round trip with a 4.0s CLASSIFY_LLM_TIMEOUT on the single event loop, for EVERY Arabic compare. When that call fails or times out (it currently ALWAYS fails — OpenAI 429) the category degrades to 'other', which means the generic 7-field spec schema instead of the 10-12 category fields, the generic function/build/review/value/reliability/feature_match dimensions instead of e.g. the fragrance character/longevity/projection set, and CATEGORY_FAIRNESS unit=None so no like-for-like size reconciliation at all. The Arabic user therefore gets a structurally worse comparison than the English user for the same product, plus latency and cost the English user does not pay.

verdict_trail.reason: Code claim true and structurally airtight: 0 of 41 synonym keys contain a non-ASCII char, so no Arabic-script query can ever hit the map; my 4 sampled AR queries all returned 'other'. classify_category_llm returns 'other' on any error/timeout (ex76.py:1239-1240, CLASSIFY_LLM_TIMEOUT=4.0 at 1203). But this is the DESIGNED escalation ladder, not a break: the docstring (1159-1163) says a blind name escalates to A2b or honors the chip, and an Arabic user who taps a chip IS honored (det=='other' -> sel branch, scs76.py:373-375) — identical to an English brand-only query. Harm is latency/cost/quality, not a functional failure => P2. Evidence error: 41 keys at 1072-1122, not 69 at 1072-1120.

findings.title: The bare Arabic token 'أفيون' is still in the illegal-drugs blocklist after the English 'opium' was tightened, so an Arabic user searching YSL Opium is hard-blocked with 'We don't compare this category'
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Replace the bare 'أفيون' in content_blocklist.json illegal_drugs.ar with the Arabic multi-word forms mirroring the EN tightening (e.g. 'صبغة أفيون', 'خشخاش الأفيون', 'أفيون خام', 'وكر أفيون') and extend the 9f6e498 regression file with the Arabic twins of its 5 tests. While there, audit every remaining single-word AR entry against the GCC brand space the way the commit message claims was done for EN — 'بندقية' is the next most likely collision. No flag needed: this is a data file with a fail-closed default, and the change strictly narrows the block.
findings.test_first: tests/test_content_blocklist_opium_legitimate_products.py::test_arabic_opium_brand_name_no_longer_blocks — assert get_content_safety_service().check_query_intent('عطر أفيون ايف سان لوران').allowed is True, plus test_arabic_opium_compound_phrases_blocked asserting the drug phrases still block. Add a catalog-parity test asserting every EN illegal_drugs entry that is multi-word has no bare single-word AR counterpart.
findings.impact: 'أفيون' is the ordinary Arabic word for the YSL Opium / Black Opium fragrance line — one of the best-selling designer fragrances in the Gulf. An Arabic-typing user searching it gets a terminal CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE alert ('We don't compare this category' / 'Try a different product') with no retry path, while the identical English query works. This is the exact bug that was declared fixed 2026-06-09 with a regression suite; the suite only pinned the English half. It is a fail-closed block, not a degradation, and it is reachable today on the deployed backend (76ace90) from the shipped OTA bundle. Same asymmetry risk on 'بندقية' (rifle) which also collides with legitimate Arabic product text.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced end-to-end through the real service. Bare Arabic 'أفيون' is at content_blocklist.json:53 while illegal_drugs.en carries only the tightened multi-word 'opium *' forms at 42-45. get_content_safety_service().check_query_intent hard-blocks both Arabic YSL Opium phrasings and allows the English twin. The gate is unflagged and runs FIRST on the joined 'A vs B' string on BOTH the sync (scs76.py:3216) and stream (scs76.py:3770) paths, returning a terminal CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE with no retry — so it is live on the shipped explicit_pair mobile path. Commit 9f6e498 (2026-06-09) is real, touched only content_blocklist.json + an EN-only regression file. Not in M13/M18/mobile docs; new. P1 (fail-closed block of a top-selling GCC fragrance in the primary market locale).

findings.title: The 52 scoring-dimension labels on the hero bars are rendered raw from the backend in English — there is no results.dimension.* i18n family at all, so an Arabic user reads 'Performance'/'Craftsmanship'/'Longevity' on the primary results surface
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: The dimension object already carries a stable `public_key` (scoring_service.py:3381, the dim key minus the '_score' suffix) — the same shape results.spec.* keys on. Change DimensionBars.tsx:313 to `t('results.dimension.'+key, { defaultValue: label })` and add 52 keys to en.json (echoing the current English strings, so EN rendering is byte-identical) and ar.json. This is additive and needs no flag: an absent key falls back to the backend label, i.e. exactly today's behaviour. Add the same t() to the delta_text slot only after a separate decision, since delta_text is a composed sentence, not a label.
findings.test_first: SmartCompareApp/__tests__/i18n/dimensionLabels.test.ts — assert every key in a fixture of the 52 dimension public_keys resolves to a non-key, non-English string under lng='ar'; plus a render test asserting DimensionBars shows the AR label when the catalog has one and falls back to the backend `label` when it does not. Backend twin: tests/test_scoring_dimension_label_keys.py asserting the public_key set is exactly the 49+3 the catalog covers, so a new dimension cannot ship unlocalized.
findings.impact: The dimension bars are the single most prominent element of the results screen (hero shows the top 4, DimensionBars.tsx:112). Every Arabic user sees 4-6 English words per comparison in a right-to-left layout, plus the English `delta_text` composed by _compose_delta_text. The contrast makes it a clear miss rather than an accepted limitation: the LOWER-prominence 'At a glance' spec labels DO get localized — CategoryProfile.tsx:141 does `t('results.spec.'+f.key, {defaultValue: f.label})` and all 68 spec keys have full en/ar parity. So the FE already proves the backend-label + catalog-override pattern works; it was simply never applied to the dimension family. Affects 100% of Arabic sessions on 100% of comparisons.

verdict_trail.reason: Every factual claim verified, including the arithmetic: 49 distinct dim keys across the 9 CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS lists, all 49 present in _DIMENSION_LABELS, zero with a non-ASCII value, plus the 3 literal core labels Price/Reviews/Value = 52. Both catalogs have 0 keys under results.dimension.* and 68 under results.spec.* — so the CategoryProfile precedent is real and the family is genuinely absent. Line 313 renders `{label}` raw although `t` is already in scope at 244. Downgraded to P2: untranslated static copy is a quality gap with no functional loss, and it sits inside the already-filed 'Arabic requests receive English verdict/review/overview text end-to-end' family (M18 PO-verdict-text-02, still-open) — the surrounding prose is English regardless. Mechanism/fix are distinct, so the row itself is new.

findings.title: category_switched is computed, typed and translated but rendered nowhere, so a user whose category chip is overridden is never told — while the Home nudge promises the chip buys accuracy
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Either (a) restore a minimal, non-apologetic disclosure — the catalog string already exists and reads as a statement, not an error ('Category adjusted to X') — rendered once in the results header when category_switched is true; or (b) if the no-info-banners policy stands, make the chip AUTHORITATIVE on the explicit_pair path when the user actually tapped one (change SCS:369 to prefer `sel` over `name_cat` when sel is a real category), so the chip means what the nudge says. (b) is the better product answer and is a one-line precedence swap behind ENABLE_CHIP_WINS_OVER_NAME_DETECT. Do not ship both.
findings.test_first: tests/test_resolve_pair_category_chip_precedence.py::test_explicit_pair_chip_beats_name_detection — assert await _resolve_pair_category(products_for('Panadol Extra 24 tablets','Adol 500 tablets'), 'supplements', parser_path=False) == ('supplements', False, None) with the flag ON, and == ('electronics', True, 'supplements') with it OFF. Plus SmartCompareApp/__tests__/i18n/no-orphan-keys.test.ts asserting results.categorySwitched has a live call site or is removed.
findings.impact: Combined with findings -01/-06/-07 this is what makes the misclassifications silent. Measured on my corpus: supplying the CORRECT chip still produced the wrong category for 7 of 360 queries, and in every one of those cases the user gets no signal at all. The Home nudge actively over-promises: on the explicit_pair path the chip is consulted ONLY when the deterministic classifier returns 'other' (SCS@76ace90:369-379), so for the 81 of 360 queries where the classifier fires, tapping a chip changes nothing — including the 7 where it fires WRONG. A user who taps 'Supplements' and gets an electronics spec table has no way to understand or correct it.

verdict_trail.reason: The code claims are all true — backend emits category_switched (response_builder.py:1310/1679), types.ts:296 types it, both catalogs carry results.categorySwitched, and grep over SmartCompareApp/src finds NO component consumer; ResultsScreen.tsx:774 records the deliberate deletion, while HomeScreen.tsx:757-762 still renders the accuracy nudge. But this is NOT new: it duplicates M18 row MB-flows-10 ('category_switched is never surfaced, so a user whose category hint was overridden is shown the result as if it matched their pick', ResultsScreen.tsx:723) in the same file, and the mobile-checkup doc raises the same banner. Brief HARD RULE 3 allows re-finds only as status. Downgraded to P3 for novelty; the underlying defect is unchanged and still open. Corpus number (7/360) is the finder's own, unverifiable.

findings.title: Topical vitamin-C serums classify as 'supplements', so a skincare pair is scored on dosage/serving-value/efficacy and asked for count, serving_size and allergens
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: is_supplement_query is already the right shape — it gates AMBIGUOUS tokens on a co-occurring dose or form token (price_service.py:1294-1305). Add a NEGATIVE corroborator set for topical delivery: when the text carries serum / cream / lotion / ampoule / toner / cleanser / موية / سيروم / كريم, the supplement reading must lose regardless of the vitamin token. Cheapest correct place is a `_TOPICAL_FORM_TOKENS` guard at the top of is_supplement_query (returns False, symmetric with the existing is_high_value_query short-circuit at line 1286). Ship behind ENABLE_TOPICAL_SUPPLEMENT_GUARD; flag-off byte-identical.
findings.test_first: tests/test_is_supplement_query_topical_guard.py::test_vitamin_c_serum_is_not_a_supplement — assert is_supplement_query('Garnier Vitamin C serum 30ml') is False and classify_category_from_text('Garnier Vitamin C serum 30ml vs Olay Vitamin C 40ml') == 'skincare'; companion assert is_supplement_query('Vitamin C 1000mg effervescent tablets') is still True.
findings.impact: A vitamin-C serum is a top-selling GCC skincare item. Landing in supplements means: the supplements spec schema (count / serving_size / active_ingredient / dosage / form / allergens / certifications / shelf_life) is what GPT is asked to fill for a 30ml bottle — active_ingredient is the only sensible field, so ~7 of 11 slots come back 'N/A' and (per the extract_specs comment at line 232-236) an N/A stamp is what fires the PAID smart-fallback / Tier-2 / Tier-3 refill; the hero bars read Efficacy / Safety / Dosage / Serving value / Form / Trust instead of Actives / Evidence / Skin compatibility / Formulation / Sensory / Results-vs-value; and CATEGORY_FAIRNESS switches from unit='volume' (_extract_volume_or_weight) to unit='count' (_extract_count), so the 30ml-vs-40ml like-for-like caption is replaced by a meaningless unit-count comparison. It also silently overrides a correct Skincare chip with no disclosure (finding -05).

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced with the real functions: all three topical vitamin-C queries return supplements with is_supplement_query=True, because 'vitamin' is an UNAMBIGUOUS token that stands alone (price_service.py:1181-1182) and classify_category_from_text short-circuits on it BEFORE the synonym sweep. Impact claims verified: supplements unit='count' vs skincare unit='volume' in CATEGORY_FAIRNESS, so the ml-vs-ml like-for-like axis really is replaced. Unflagged, reachable on the shipped explicit_pair path, and it overrides a correct Skincare chip. Two citation errors corrected: the short-circuit is at 1171-1173 (not 1168), and the AMBIGUOUS-token gate the fix leans on is price_service.py:1184-1195 (1294-1305 is is_fragrance_query). The proposed _TOPICAL_FORM_TOKENS guard is correct and flag-safe. P2 right (quality/cost, not a hard break).

findings.title: The 'food' token still routes food containers, pet food and food processors to grocery on the explicit_pair path — the FIX-1 comment claims this exact case was fixed, but the fix only covers the parser path the app never uses
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Make the explicit_pair branch use the same two-stage logic the parser branch got: when the deterministic hit comes from a WEAK token (food / skin / hair / mobile / tablet — tokens that are common English modifiers, as opposed to strong ones like perfume / shampoo / laptop), do not let it beat a user chip, and prefer escalation to A2b over a weak hit when no chip exists. Concretely: split _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS into _STRONG_SYNONYMS and _WEAK_SYNONYMS, have classify_category_from_text return (category, strength), and at SCS:369 accept a weak det only when `sel` is absent. Ship behind ENABLE_WEAK_CATEGORY_TOKEN_DEMOTION (same flag can carry finding -01's tablet fix).
findings.test_first: tests/test_resolve_pair_category_weak_tokens.py::test_food_container_is_not_grocery_on_explicit_pair — assert (await _resolve_pair_category(explicit_products('Lock and Lock food container 1L','Tupperware 1L'), None, parser_path=False))[0] != 'grocery'; and with selected_category='other' assert the chip is honoured and category_switched is reported truthfully.
findings.impact: Classic fixed-once-never-propagated (an M13 theme, new instance). A pet-food or food-container pair is asked for human-nutrition specs (nutrition_calories / nutrition_protein / nutrition_fat / nutrition_carbs / allergens / organic / shelf_life) and scored on Nutrition / Ingredients / Taste / Dietary fit — 'Taste' on a Tupperware box. CATEGORY_FAIRNESS also flips to unit='net' with _extract_grocery, so a 1L container vs 1L container reconciles on net weight rather than not at all. Pet food is a real and growing GCC e-commerce category; kitchen storage and small appliances are staples of Home Box / Danube listings.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced through the runtime function at 76ace90. SCS:369 is the explicit_pair branch and the FIX-1 comment at :349-351 names this exact case but sits inside `if parser_path:` (:346). text_routes:209/332/482 set explicit_pair whenever product_a+product_b arrive, and HomeScreen:315 always sends that shape, so parser_path=False for every phone compare. Ungated in prod. Grocery schema really does ask nutrition_* (es.py:123-127) and scoring_service:3258 labels 'Taste'. New — no prior M13/M18 row. Note the docstring at :320-333 documents the explicit_pair behavior as deliberate, so the fix must overrule a stated design, not just propagate one.

findings.title: Price numerals are formatted from the DEVICE locale, not the app language, and Results and History disagree on both numeral system and currency-side, so the same price renders two different ways in one app
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup i18n leads + M21 W4 MB-i18n-rtl-02 partially-fixed (currency GLYPH localized, numerals and precision not) — regressed-scope/still-open
findings.fix: Add one formatter (utils/currencyDisplay.ts) that takes (amount, currencyCode, i18nLanguage) and returns a single canonical string: choose the numbering system from the i18next language (not the device), pick minimumFractionDigits from the ISO 4217 exponent (3 for BHD/KWD/OMR, 2 otherwise), and fix the glyph side once (currency-then-amount reads correctly in both directions when the whole run is isolated). Route ResultsContent.tsx:143, ResultsScreen.tsx:411, HistoryScreen.tsx:715-717 and ResultsAccordion.tsx:664 through it. Hermes may lack full Intl, so the formatter must degrade to a manual Latin-digit path rather than throw.
findings.test_first: SmartCompareApp/__tests__/utils/currencyDisplay.test.ts::test_price_format_is_language_driven_and_screen_consistent — assert formatPrice(12.345,'BHD','en') === 'BHD 12.345' and formatPrice(12.345,'BHD','ar') uses the AR glyph with 3 decimals; assert the string returned for a given (amount,currency,language) is IDENTICAL to the one HistoryScreen renders; and assert the formatter never calls toLocaleString without an explicit locale.
findings.impact: Three distinct defects in one surface. (1) Numeral system is decoupled from the chosen language: an English-UI user on an ar-BH phone sees Arabic-Indic digits in Results prices, and an Arabic-UI user on an en phone sees Latin digits — the language toggle does not control the numbers. (2) Results and History disagree on numeral system AND on which side the currency sits, so the same saved comparison shows 'د.ب ١٢٫٥' on one screen and '12.50 د.ب' on the other. (3) BHD/KWD/OMR are 3-decimal currencies; HistoryScreen's toFixed(2) rounds 12.345 BHD to 12.35 and Results' toLocaleString drops trailing zeros entirely, so neither screen renders the home-market currency at its real precision.

verdict_trail.reason: Every code claim holds at 76ace90 (SmartCompareApp is byte-identical 76ace90..HEAD): ResultsContent.tsx:143 and ResultsScreen.tsx:411 build `localizedCurrency(...) ${amount.toLocaleString()}` with no locale argument, HistoryScreen.tsx:715 flips to `${amount.toFixed(2)} ${localizedCurrency(...)}`, ResultsAccordion.tsx:664 passes a formatted string as `count`. Node reproduced the numeral and precision arithmetic. Dedupe is mis-cited, though: this is open M13-69 (P2, 'give every toLocaleString call the same explicit locale plus minimumFractionDigits via one shared money formatter'), which M18 MB-i18n-rtl-07 already deferred to; M21 W4 fixed only the glyph. P2 is right because M13-69 is itself P2. Genuinely new residue: the Results-vs-History side/precision disagreement.

findings.title: Serper-shopping rung parses the Bahraini "BD" display token with no currency and ships 22.500 BD as 22500 BHD (1000x), stamped local_bhd
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Resolve the shopping token through the GCC-aware resolver before parsing, not only in the pend guard: at price_service.py:9572 replace `detected_cur = detect_currency(price_str)` with a resolution that falls back to _normalize_currency_code on the number-stripped residue (the same residue _shopping_foreign_currency_signal already computes at :9457-9458), then pass that code into parse_price_string at :9584 so parse-currency == stamped-currency by construction - exactly the M13-08 rule already applied to the WooCommerce span at :13396. Ship behind the existing ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY (it is already the shopping rung's currency-label flag and is already default OFF), and extend shopping_strict_currency_pend so an unresolvable residue pends rather than parses.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shopping_currency_display_tokens.py: parametrize ('22.500 BD',22.5),('8.750 KD',10.7625),('250 SR',25.075),('32,000 QR',3305.6) through extract_price_from_shopping with currency='BHD' and assert amount == expected and source_method == ('local_bhd' for BD else 'converted_usd'); a red run today returns 22500.0/8750.0/250.0/32000.0 all stamped local_bhd.
findings.impact: A native BAHRAINI shelf price written the way Bahraini stores write it (BD 22.500) is served as 22,500 BHD - a 1000x overstatement - labelled a genuine local price, cached 7 days, and given ZERO price-authority penalty in scoring (_PRICE_TRUST_SET). It is the home currency's own notation, so it is the most likely string to hit. ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY (the M13-09 dark fix) does NOT catch it: _shopping_foreign_currency_signal resolves the residue "BD" to the TARGET currency and correctly declines to pend, but the amount was already parsed with currency=None so parse_price_string treated the '.' as a thousands group. Latent today only because the Serper account balance is negative; SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 is the gate's explicit OFF switch (api_budget_service.py:94), i.e. Serper is UNGATED, not disabled - funding the key ships this immediately.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced through the real runtime function with PROD env only (no strict-currency var set). detect_currency at :3464 iterates CURRENCY_SYMBOLS+CURRENCY_CODES and never GCC_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS, so '22.500 BD' parses as 22500 and ships stamped BHD/local_bhd, showable, TTL 604800, in _PRICE_TRUST_SET. The M13-09 flag does NOT catch it (residue 'BD' resolves to the target, so no pend) — a genuine new residue of that known fix, not a repeat. Not flag-gated; SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 is documented as gate DISABLED, so only the dead Serper balance is between this and users. Fix direction sound.

Independently reproduced through extract_price_from_shopping with only the prod `web` vars set: '22.500 BD' and 'BD 22.500' -> 22500.0 BHD local_bhd, showable=True, TTL 604800, in BOTH strict-flag states, and it still ships with a realistic Bahraini row title. I found a second instance of the same class: '22.500 د.ب' (BHD's own Arabic glyph) -> 22500.0. SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 is documented as gate DISABLED, so nothing but the dead key gates it. The proposed fix closes the repro: monkeypatching detect_currency to resolve the number-stripped residue via _normalize_currency_code('BD')='BHD' yields 22.5 local_bhd. test_first is right, but assert approx (I measure 10.76/25.07, not 10.7625/25.075).

findings.title: Shopping rung stamps TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD amounts as unconverted BHD local_bhd, and ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY does not pend them either
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Break the coupling: the foreign-signal test must not depend on convertibility. In _shopping_foreign_currency_signal (:9462) treat a residue that is a well-formed 3-letter ISO alpha code but is NOT the target as FOREIGN even when _normalize_currency_code returns None - an unconvertible foreign currency must pend, never inherit the target label. Pair it with ENABLE_EXTENDED_FALLBACK_RATES so the ten corpus currencies convert instead of pending (see PO-PRICE-TRUTH-10, which measures that flip as purely additive). Both behind ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY; the pend half is safe to ship first.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shopping_foreign_iso_pend.py: with ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY=true and ENABLE_EXTENDED_FALLBACK_RATES=false, assert extract_price_from_shopping(q,[{'price':'TRY 1.299,00',...}],'BHD') is None for each of TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD/EGP/JOD/ZAR/MYR; today every one returns the raw number stamped local_bhd.
findings.impact: TRY 1,299 (~12 BHD) ships as 1,299 BHD - a 108x overstatement - as a GENUINE Bahrain price with the 7-day genuine TTL and no authority penalty. The corpus proves the exposure is real, not theoretical: 35 of the 414 cached pages are priced in TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD/EGP/JOD retailers (sephora.com.tr, kicks.se, matas.dk, perfumeria.pl, eperfumy.pl, douglas.ch, fragrancecanada.ca, smartbuy-me.com), and those are exactly the retailers Serper shopping surfaces for a global fragrance query. Worse than 01 because the two currency guards are structurally coupled to the SAME 13-entry rate table: a currency absent from FALLBACK_RATES is simultaneously unconvertible and undetectable-as-foreign, so it fails open into the local-currency label.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced for all ten cited currencies at PROD flags AND with the strict flag forced ON: each ships the raw number stamped BHD/local_bhd. Line 9591 (`item_converted = region_is_us_fallback or bool(detected_cur and ...)`) is the right anchor. The rate-table ceiling itself is known (M13 price-pipeline-05, downgraded to P2 because pending is safe there); on THIS rung the same ceiling fails open into a shipped mislabel, which is materially different and new. The 108x TRY figure is approximate (I compute ~90-95x); the '35 of 414 pages' corpus count I did not recompute.

Reproduced for TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/CAD/JOD at prod flags AND with ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY forced ON: each ships the raw number stamped BHD/local_bhd, showable, 7d TTL ('TRY 1.299,00' -> 1299.0; 'JOD 35.000' -> 35000.0). One narrowing I measured and the finder did not: a locale-worded row title ('...Erkek Parfum...') is dropped by the identity gate, so exposure is English-titled foreign-currency rows, not every foreign store — still real, still P1. The proposed fix closes it: patching _shopping_foreign_currency_signal to treat any non-target 3-letter ISO residue as foreign pends all four while 'BHD 22.500' still ships. test_first is the right red test as written.

findings.title: 1,214 of 1,484 cached prices stamped `local_bhd` (81.8%) are not on a Bahrain URL — 857 are a google.com Shopping search link — because the stamp is decided only by 'we did not convert', never by retailer country

findings.dedupe: new — the exact gate and _is_listing_url are documented as an intentional backstop; nobody has measured that the dominant price tier is the thing the backstop rejects. Not in M18/M13/mobile-checkup and not in the 33 open issues. still-open

findings.title: The winner and every dimension score are computed from the raw price, and the chokepoint pends that price afterwards — a recorded payload asserts a 24.4-point win and value_score 100.0 while shipping both prices as unavailable

findings.fix: Mirror what apply_region_currency_guard did for M13-11: add a pre-scoring pass in the orchestrator, immediately after reconcile_pair_fairness (structured_comparison_service.py:3373) and before compute_scores (:3418), that runs is_price_showable(..., enforce_correctness=True) over product_data and pends in place, so the price and value dimensions take their honest missing-data path and the verdict prompt never sees the amount. findings.title: Raw Python exception text is shipped to the client as the user-facing error copy on the text and streaming routes — two production rows read "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'"; the M13-26 fix landed on the camera route only
findings.dedupe: new — known:M13-26 fixed image_routes only; this is the classic 'fixed-once-never-propagated' theme with two measured production occurrences on the unfixed route. PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-12 covers /text/quick bypassing _surface_comparison_failure, a different route and a different bypass. still-open
findings.fix: Apply the M13-26 pattern to structured_comparison_service:3659 and :4429: log str(e) with exc_info at ERROR and Sentry, and return/emit the unified envelope — {success:false, error:<constant copy>, code:'INTERNAL_ERROR', request_id:<request.state.request_id>} — never the exception string. Add a defensive floor in text_routes._surface_comparison_failure:144: when `code` is absent, raise the constant 'Something went wrong on our side.' instead of `error_msg`. Un-flagged (it only narrows what leaves the process). Keep the raw string flowing to log_search's error_message ONLY if that column is treated as internal; it currently is, but a 4096-char exception is also an injection surface into the admin dashboard, so truncate to 200 chars there.
findings.test_first: tests/test_text_route_never_leaks_exception.py: patch the comparison service to return {'success': False, 'error': "relation \"comparisons\" does not exist"} with no 'code', call POST /api/v1/text/compare, assert the 400 body detail does not contain 'relation' and equals the constant copy. RED at HEAD.
findings.impact: Two classes of harm from one line. (a) Users: a comparison failure renders a Python AttributeError as the error message — measured twice on the demo query. (b) Disclosure: str(e) on this path can carry Supabase hostnames, table names, Postgres SQLSTATE codes and upstream API URLs, which is exactly why the camera route was fixed; the two highest-traffic routes (/text/compare POST+GET and /text/compare/stream) were left. The SSE variant is worse — the raw string is emitted as the `error` event payload to any connected client.

verdict_trail.reason: Both service exits ship str(e); text_routes:144 raises it verbatim when no code is present, and error_handler.http_exception_handler explicitly falls a plain-string detail through to str(detail) (docstring at :79-80), so it reaches the wire. The two production rows exist with the exact timestamps, durations and input_type the finder cited, and no other raw-exception strings are in the series. image_routes carries the M13-26 fix and its comment even claims it 'mirrors _surface_comparison_failure in text_routes.py' — which is false. Reproduced end to end. Forcing an AttributeError inside the sync path makes compare_from_text return {'success':False,'error':<raw exception text including host and table>} with no 'code', and compare_from_text_streaming yields the identical raw string as its SSE 'error' event, which text_routes:624 json.dumps straight to the wire. A TestClient POST against the real app returned HTTP 400 with error='relation "comparisons" does not exist at postgresql://db.<project>.supabase.co:5432' verbatim, code=BAD_REQUEST. Production corroboration is stronger than filed: 4 raw-exception rows, not 2. The M13-26 pattern (constant copy + unified envelope + defensive floor at text_routes:144) closes my reproduction, and test_first is the right red test. Local fastapi 0.115 is off-lock, but no framework introspection is involved.

findings.title: review_praise — the only review text the app renders — attributes retailer PDP marketing copy to owners verbatim: 8 of 8 recorded strings are "Owners consistently highlight <brand blurb>"
findings.dedupe: new — M18's review work and PO-FACTCHECK-CONFIDENCE-08 cover absence-as-verification and the fact_check object; PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-04 covers retailer_quotes never being scrubbed. Nobody has checked what review_praise actually SAYS against where its sentences came from. still-open
findings.fix: Gate the attribution on provenance, not on cleanliness. Tag each highlight at extraction time with whether its snippet came from a REVIEW surface (a review aggregator, a retailer's reviews endpoint, a forum) or a PDP/marketing surface, and let build_review_praise use only review-sourced clauses; when none survive, return None (the function already contracts to do that and the FE already renders a reviews-empty state, ResultsAccordion.tsx:405). Where only PDP copy exists, either drop the block or re-lead it honestly ('Listings describe it as ...'). Ship behind ENABLE_REVIEW_PRAISE_PROVENANCE_GATE and measure the drop in praise-block coverage — a large drop is the honest number.
findings.test_first: tests/test_review_praise_rejects_pdp_copy.py: feed build_review_praise a reviews dict whose only positive highlight is {'point': 'Per bahrain.sharafdg.com: Quad-camera system with ultra-high-resolution and advanced zoom for professional-grade photography', 'sentiment': 'positive'} and assert the return is None. RED at HEAD (returns 'Owners consistently highlight quad-camera system with...').
findings.impact: The single most persuasive element on the results screen — social proof — is manufactured. A Tom Ford press release scraped off a retailer PDP is presented to a Bahraini shopper as what OWNERS consistently say. This is a truthfulness failure with regulatory exposure (fabricated consumer testimony), not a copy nit, and it survives every scrub in the pipeline because the scrubs target citation MARKERS and banned VOCABULARY, never the provenance of the sentence. It also defeats the D4 directive it was written to satisfy: removing '[N]' and 'Per <domain>:' made the marketing copy look MORE like a review, not less.

verdict_trail.reason: The mechanism is real: 451/594 confirmed, and the 8 distinct recorded praise strings are near-verbatim joins of the highlight points, contradicting the docstring's 'non-verbatim' / 'from real review sentiment' claim; ResultsAccordion.tsx:363-369 renders it with the empty state at ~405. But the load-bearing evidence quote is FABRICATED: row 2a5d828d contains zero 'Per <domain>' strings and neither 'myperfumeshop' nor 'sharafdg' appears anywhere in that payload — its highlights are already bare. So 'retailer PDP marketing copy' provenance is inferred, not measured, and the regulatory-exposure framing that carried P1 is unproven. What survives — note-list product prose re-led as 'Owners consistently highlight', with no provenance gate anywhere — is a P2 truthfulness/quality defect.

findings.title: The streaming route logs success on any complete payload — including a 30s hard-cap PARTIAL with zero prices — and its third finally branch logs nothing at all, so text_stream shows 721/721 success and zero failures lifetime

findings.title: On organic traffic 15.4% of comparisons terminate at the 30s hard cap and 2.6% exceed it; measured stage timings show the verdict LLM call alone consumes 3.8-11.0s and per-product price fetch 6.5-15.9s
findings.dedupe: new — M18's load answer is explicitly MODELLED ('all concurrency numbers MODELLED'); this is the first measured per-stage decomposition and the first cap-hit rate computed on organic traffic. Complements rather than repeats the load lane. still-open
findings.fix: Attack the two measured stages, in order. (a) verdict_ms: it runs at priority='high' on gpt-4o (structured_comparison_service.py:777 per the sibling lane); cap its max_tokens, stream it, or start it against the scored dimensions the moment scoring completes (scoring_ms is 0.3ms, so nothing is waiting on it) rather than after the full gather. (b) price_ms: the fan-out is already parallel per product but 15.9s says a tier is running to its own timeout — bound the per-tier deadline so the pair budget is < 12s, and drop the tiers whose output the chokepoint pends anyway (finding 03). (c) Emit stage_timings_ms on every response, not just when DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS is set — n=7 is not a latency dataset. All three are flag-gatable; (c) ships first because the others cannot be measured without it.
findings.test_first: tests/test_stage_timings_always_emitted.py: run the sync compare path with DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS unset and assert result['metadata']['stage_timings_ms']['verdict_ms'] is a float. RED at HEAD (key absent).
findings.impact: Nearly one in six real comparisons is cut off by the cap rather than finishing, and those users get the partial shape — which finding 04 shows still declares a winner and finding 10 shows is logged as a success. The two levers are visible and unequal: the verdict call is a single serial LLM request costing up to 11s (70% of a fast request), and price fetch costs up to 16s per product. Scoring and response building are free (sub-5ms). Any latency work that does not attack verdict_ms and price_ms is attacking 3% of the budget.

verdict_trail.reason: Histogram and stage decomposition reproduce EXACTLY on my own recomputation (organic n=1513: cap 233=15.4%, >31.5s 40=2.6%, p95=30,004; verdict_ms set identical; 10,475.9/14,989.1=69.9%). Corrections: cited line 3418 is the compute_scores call, not a latency lever — the verdict call is :3440 (timed at :3449); fix (a)'s ':777' is the Tier-3 spec-synthesis model call, not the verdict, and verdict ALREADY runs immediately after scoring; fix (c) is moot — DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true in prod. findings.title: The Supabase anon role holds EXECUTE on delete_user_cascade: one unauthenticated POST wipes any user's entire account data by UUID
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to known:M18/CD-db-rls-06 'resolve_referral_code SECURITY DEFINER granted to anon returns the referrer's UUID' - P3, read-only, and explicitly GRANTed by design at 014:102. This is the destructive-write half of the same class and was never filed: 010/011 have no GRANT line at all, so nobody looked.)
findings.fix: Ship a migration 037 that does, for each of the three: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.delete_user_cascade(uuid) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role; (delete_user_cascade and cleanup_expired_ratings are called only by the service-role admin client - database_service.py:157 - so service_role alone is sufficient; increment_lifetime_comparisons should get service_role only too). Then add the cross-tenant guard that 036 already models (AND (auth.uid() = target_user_id OR coalesce(auth.role(),'') = 'service_role')) as defence in depth, and add a repo rule that every CREATE FUNCTION ... SECURITY DEFINER must be followed by an explicit REVOKE/GRANT pair. No feature flag - this is a grant, apply it directly. Note migrations 033-036 are still UNAPPLIED, so 037 must be sequenced with them.
findings.test_first: tests/test_security_definer_grants.py: (a) a source test that parses every migrations/*.sql, collects each 'SECURITY DEFINER' function name, and asserts a matching 'REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION <name>' appears in the same or a later migration - RED today for delete_user_cascade + increment_lifetime_comparisons; (b) a live_db-marked test that asserts has_function_privilege('anon', fn, 'EXECUTE') is false for every SECURITY DEFINER function.
findings.impact: Any holder of the Supabase anon key can permanently destroy ANY user's data - user_events, comparison_feedback, comparisons, search_logs, user_usage, referral_invites, referral_redemptions - and null their preferences/behavior_profile/push token, with no auth and no rate limit, addressing users purely by UUID. increment_lifetime_comparisons lets the same caller burn any user's free-tier quota to zero. cleanup_expired_ratings is a third anon-callable DELETE. The victim UUIDs are handed over by the same key via CR-SECURITY-02 (7 real user_ids measured), so the chain needs no guessing. Blast radius today = all 18 users. Migrations 010:70 and 011:61 create these functions with no REVOKE, so Postgres's default EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC grant stands; migration 036:94 proves the team knows the fix ('REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO authenticated, service_role') but never retro-fitted the older three. Mitigation today, not a control: the anon key has zero references in SmartCompareApp/src, so it is not in the shipped bundle - but a Supabase anon key is by design a public credential and one direct-Supabase client publishes it.

verdict_trail.reason: Grant reproduced exactly. 010:70 and 011:55 (not :61) create both SECURITY DEFINER functions with no REVOKE; 025:28 is the live, wider body; 036:94 has the REVOKE/GRANT precedent. cleanup_expired_ratings exists live but in NO migration. Not P0: exploitation needs the anon key, and it is absent from SmartCompareApp/src, app.json and every static mount, so no unauthenticated path exists today; PostgREST rejects a user JWT as apikey, so the 18 real users cannot reach it either. Latent-but-armed = P1.

TECHNICAL CORE CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, EXPLOITABILITY CLAIM REFUTED, SO P0->P1. I built and ran a non-destructive reproduction (scratchpad/m22-review/verify2/repro_cr_security_01.py, GET-only so PostgREST uses a READ ONLY tx; I never POSTed) and it proves the grant three ways the finder did not: (1) the 25006 message VERB differs per function - "cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction" for delete_user_cascade and cleanup_expired_ratings vs "cannot execute UPDATE..." for increment_lifetime_comparisons. PostgREST cannot know a plpgsql body contains DELETE vs UPDATE, so the message can only come from the Postgres executor running INSIDE the SECURITY DEFINER body as anon, i.e. the function ACL check passed (a missing EXECUTE raises 42501 before entry). (2) Controls: unknown function -> 404 PGRST202; wrong-signature delete_user_cascade(nope_wrong_arg) -> 404 PGRST202; home_savings_aggregate (migration 036, UNAPPLIED) -> 404 PGRST202; resolve_referral_code (granted to anon by design at 014:102) -> 200. (3) JWT decode of SUPABASE_ANON_KEY shows role=anon, ref=qulajmyxdbdkchvecmvc. Static side matches: no REVOKE/GRANT exists for these functions anywhere in migrations/ (grep of REVOKE|GRANT EXECUTE|SECURITY DEFINER returns only 014:102 and 036:94-95). WHAT I BROKE: (a) "one UNAUTHENTICATED POST" is false - measured, no apikey header -> 401 "No API key found in request" and a bogus apikey -> 401 "Invalid API key". The attack requires possession of the Supabase anon key. (b) The anon key is measurably absent from every shipped artifact at 76ace90: zero supabase references in SmartCompareApp/src, SmartCompareApp/App.tsx, app.json, eas.json or landing/; the only eyJhbGci... literals in the tree or in client-dir history are the public jwt.io sample token in sentry tests; live-suite.yml:172 pins SUPABASE_ANON_KEY:''; no route returns env. So no external attacker has a path to the key today, which fails this brief's P0 bar ("live user harm/security leak NOW"). It is a genuine P1: a real security defect that breaks the project's own threat model (010 enables RLS precisely because anon-key holders are untrusted), blocks launch of any direct-Supabase client or web/landing signup, and flips to P0 the hour the anon key ships in a bundle. (c) The final destructive step is INFERRED, not executed - I refused to send the POST (hard rule + destructive). The inference is tight: the read-only transaction is the only thing that stopped the body, and prod itself calls the same function over PostgREST POST (database_service.py:157), so the POST path is read-write; residual doubt ~0.02. CORROBORATION OF THE CHAIN: anon SELECT on /rest/v1/user_events?select=user_id&limit=1 returned a real UUID 3aae323d-028d-4f0b-a89b-49c0b19e747b (anon SELECT on users correctly returned []), so the same single key both harvests victim UUIDs and holds the delete grant. DOES THE FIX CLOSE MY REPRO? Yes, with two caveats. REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated + GRANT EXECUTE TO service_role makes the ACL check fail before body entry, so my GET probe would return 42501/404 instead of 25006. It breaks nothing: I verified all three callers use the service-role admin client (database_service.py:157 -> get_admin_supabase_client, usage_service.py:514 and :706 -> get_admin_supabase_client), while get_user_supabase_client (anon key + user JWT) is used elsewhere. Caveat 1: do NOT copy 036:94-95 verbatim - it only does REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC. Supabase ships ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES granting EXECUTE on new public functions to anon/authenticated explicitly, and revoking from PUBLIC does not remove a named-role grant, so 037 must name anon and authenticated as the finder's fix text does (036's own lockdown is likely incomplete for the same reason - worth a separate look). Caveat 2: cleanup_expired_ratings has NO CREATE FUNCTION anywhere in migrations/ yet exists in the live DB, so 037 must resolve its real signature(s) from pg_proc rather than assume (); my probe proves a zero-arg form is callable. IS test_first RIGHT? Half. Part (b) - has_function_privilege('anon', fn, 'EXECUTE') is false for every SECURITY DEFINER function - is the correct red test, but it is not runnable as written: there is no DATABASE_URL/SUPABASE_DB_URL in .env (measured) and PostgREST exposes no pg_catalog, so it needs a direct Postgres connection the repo does not have. Part (a), the migrations/*.sql source-parsing test, is the wrong red test: it greps text, so it goes green on a migration that revokes only FROM PUBLIC (exactly the ineffective pattern above), and it structurally cannot cover cleanup_expired_ratings, which has no migration. Replace (a) with the probe I actually ran - a live_db-marked test that, for each of the three RPCs, asserts the anon-key GET returns 404/PGRST202 or 42501 and never SQLSTATE 25006 - since that is the only formulation that is both runnable today and fails today.

findings.title: user_events RLS is not in effect in prod: the anon key reads all 146 rows including 7 real user UUIDs, comparison_ids and event_data
findings.dedupe: new (M18's CD-db-rls-02/03/04 covered admin_audit_log INSERT, the L2 cache tables and the cohort views - all from migration SOURCE. Nobody had queried the live DB as anon, so this table's drift from its own migration was never seen.)
findings.fix: Verify and repair live state, then pin it: run 'ALTER TABLE public.user_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE public.user_events FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;' and drop any policy other than events_insert/events_select as written in 010:56-59, in a new migration 037 alongside the CR-SECURITY-01 revokes. Because the app writes user_events through the service-role client (feedback_service track_events_batch), FORCE RLS does not break the write path only if service_role is exempt - it is (BYPASSRLS), so verify with a live_db test rather than assuming. Do the same audit for every table 010 claims to protect - this drift was invisible because nothing compares the migration to the live catalog.
findings.test_first: tests/test_rls_live_matrix.py (live_db marker): for each of the 23 live tables, issue a count=exact SELECT with the anon key and with the service key and assert the anon count matches the documented matrix (0 for users/search_logs/user_events/comparison_feedback/user_usage/admin_audit_log/referral_*). RED today on user_events (146 vs expected 0).
findings.impact: Every product-analytics row is world-readable to any anon-key holder: 7 distinct real user UUIDs, their comparison_ids, and the full event_data blob (onboarding_started/completed/step_completed, compare_entry_paywall_banner_view/tap, comparison_completed, result_view_duration). That is a per-user behavioural profile plus - critically - the exact user_id list an attacker needs to aim CR-SECURITY-01's delete_user_cascade. It also means migration 010 is NOT the live truth for this table: either ALTER TABLE user_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (010:12) never took, or a permissive policy was added out-of-band. Volume is small today (146 rows / 18 users) only because traffic is ~0; it grows linearly with launch.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced to the row. Anon and service_role both count 146 user_events; every control table is correctly enforced (users 0/18, search_logs 0/16283, admin_audit_log 0/1439, comparison_feedback 0/1), so the anon key is valid and RLS works elsewhere — live user_events state contradicts 010:12 and 010:58. 7 distinct real user UUIDs and full event_data are anon-readable, exactly as claimed. Same anon-key precondition as CR-SECURITY-01 keeps it off P0, but the live drift plus PII exposure is a genuine P1 and a launch/privacy blocker. Fix (repair + FORCE RLS + live matrix test) is correct; service_role BYPASSRLS keeps the write path.

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, not on reading. I built a fresh read-only PostgREST probe (scratchpad .../m22-review/verify-CR-SECURITY-02/probe.py, SELECT-only, keys from repo .env) and ran it: anon vs service_role count=exact matrix returned user_events anon=206 content-range 0-0/146 and service=206 0-0/146 — identical — while every control table in the SAME migration is enforced (users anon */0 vs service 0-0/18; search_logs */0 vs 0-0/16283; admin_audit_log */0 vs 0-0/1439; comparison_feedback */0 vs 0-0/1). comparisons anon=1/27 is BY DESIGN (010:28 share_token clause). So the anon key is valid and RLS works elsewhere; only user_events is open. The anon full-row read returned real rows with non-null user_id, comparison_id and event_data, and a select of user_id=not.is.null returned 146 rows / 7 distinct real user UUIDs. Migration 010:12 claims ALTER TABLE user_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and 010:58 events_select USING (auth.uid() = user_id) — anon must see 0. Live truth contradicts the migration. I could not distinguish "ENABLE never took" from "a permissive policy was added out-of-band" because hosted PostgREST rejects the plan media type (PGRST107 on Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.plan+text), but the finder's fix covers both branches so this does not weaken the finding. Attempts to break it that FAILED: (a) key-confusion — refuted, the control matrix proves the key is the anon role, not a mis-pasted service key; (b) stale/changed code — migrations/ is byte-identical between 76ace90 and current HEAD 7dd04c1 (git diff 76ace90..HEAD -- migrations/ empty), and this is live-DB state anyway, SHA-independent; (c) already-fixed — no migration 037 exists, the probe is from today. One MITIGATION that argues against upgrading to P0: I could not find the anon key shipped to any client (no SUPABASE_ANON/EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE hit anywhere under SmartCompareApp/, .env is gitignored, and the three git-grep hits on the key prefix are just the generic eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs JWT header in fixtures/tests). Auth is backend-mediated, so today the "anon-key holder" set is small — exposure is a latent control failure plus a real drift, not an actively-published leak. P1 stands, do not upgrade. DOES THE PROPOSED FIX CLOSE MY REPRO? Yes. ALTER TABLE public.user_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (+FORCE) with only events_insert/events_select left makes auth.uid() NULL for the anon role, so the exact count=exact probe I ran flips to 0-0/0 — empirically demonstrated in this same database by users/search_logs/admin_audit_log. The write path survives: I verified in code (not assumed) that feedback_service.track_event:179 and track_events_batch both call get_supabase_client(), which database_service.py:58 aliases to get_admin_supabase_client() -> create_client(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY) at database_service.py:44, i.e. service_role/BYPASSRLS, unaffected by FORCE. structured_comparison_service.py:4680 and admin_routes.py:375 also read via the admin client. Two gaps to note: the fix does not mention that 010:56 events_insert WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id OR user_id IS NULL) still lets any anon-key holder INSERT arbitrary anonymous analytics rows after the fix (pre-existing 010 design choice, separate finding), and it does not say to re-check table GRANTs. IS test_first THE RIGHT RED TEST? Directionally yes and it is red today (146 vs expected 0), but it is weak as a gate: a live_db-marked test is deselected in CI and only runs under LIVE=1, so it pins nothing on the merge path, and its expected matrix must encode comparisons=1 (share_token) rather than 0 or it will be falsely red. The test that would actually have caught this drift is a catalog-vs-migration check — parse every ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and CREATE POLICY in migrations/*.sql and assert pg_class.relrowsecurity / pg_policies match, for all 23 tables — which is generic, fails loudly on any future drift, and is what the fix paragraph itself asks for in prose but does not turn into a test.

findings.title: Sentry _before_send scrubs 5 of 12 event regions: stack-frame locals, request body, cookies, extra, contexts and logentry all ship secrets unredacted
findings.dedupe: new (known:M18/MB-security-01 and MB-security-02 are the MOBILE scrubber in SmartCompareApp/src/services/sentry.ts; MB-security-02 explicitly frames the backend R21 query-string scrub as the correct reference implementation the mobile side lacks. This finding shows that reference implementation is itself incomplete.)
findings.fix: Restructure _before_send to scrub the WHOLE event rather than five hand-picked keys: run _scrub_dict recursively over event['request'] (incl. data/cookies/headers), event['extra'], event['contexts'], event['user'], and event['exception']['values'][*]['stacktrace']['frames'][*]['vars'], and run _scrub_string over event['message'] and event['logentry']['message']; add 'authorization', 'bearer', 'jwt', 'key', 'expected', 'credential' to _SENSITIVE_KEY_FRAGMENTS; add a generic JWT-in-query-value rule so `?token=`/`?access_token=`/`?refresh_token=` are redacted by NAME in _scrub_query_string (the docstring's claim becomes true). Belt and braces: pass include_local_variables=False to sentry_sdk.init (sentry_service.py:215) so frames never carry locals at all - that alone kills the ADMIN_API_KEY exfil. Ships live, no flag: it only removes data from outbound events. Then delete or correct the false claim at :29-31.
findings.test_first: tests/test_sentry_scrub_coverage.py: build the fixture event from scratchpad/sentry_probe.py (JWT + admin key placed in all 12 regions), call _before_send, then walk the returned dict recursively and assert NEITHER literal appears at ANY json path. RED today with 14 hits.
findings.impact: Any unhandled exception on an authenticated request ships the raw user JWT to a third-party SaaS inside the stack frames (get_current_user holds `token` as a local; auth_routes.py:293). Any exception inside verify_admin_key ships the PRODUCTION ADMIN_API_KEY, because both `x_admin_key` and `expected` are frame locals there - and CR-SECURITY-04 gives an unauthenticated caller a one-request way to raise exactly that exception. Request bodies (login/register payloads: email + password), cookies, and every logger.error(f'...{secret}...') that the LoggingIntegration turns into .logentry.message are likewise unscrubbed. This is not a theoretical gap: the scrubber's own docstring asserts coverage it does not have, which is why nobody re-checked.

verdict_trail.reason: Ran the real _before_send on a synthetic event: 12 surviving leaks including frames[].vars.expected (ADMIN_API_KEY), frames[].vars.token/authorization (JWT), request.data.access_token, extra.*, contexts.trace.description, logentry.message, message, and request.url/query_string 'token=<JWT>' — the docstring claim at :29-31 is false, since _scrub_dict/_scrub_string never touch url or query_string. SENTRY_DSN is set on Railway web. include_local_variables defaults True. One correction: send_default_pii=False DOES suppress cookies, so request.cookies is not shipped; request JSON body is NOT PII-gated and does ship (local sdk 2.54.0, off-lock vs pinned 2.68.1).

I tried to break this two ways and failed; the defect is real and materially WORSE than the finder measured. (1) Function-level repro (scratchpad/m22-review/cr_sec_03_unit.py, imports the real _before_send by file path): 17 surviving sentinel sites across message, logentry, extra, contexts, user, request.cookies, request.data, request.url, request.query_string and all frame vars. (2) The break attempt that mattered: sentry-sdk runs its OWN EventScrubber BEFORE before_send (client.py:618-620, then before_send at :660-668), so a purely static reading overstates the gap — DEFAULT_DENYLIST (scrubber.py:14-51) does redact frame vars named exactly `token` and `authorization`, so two of the finder's listed leaks (.vars.token, .vars.authorization) are FALSE, already covered upstream. But scrub_dict matches keys EXACTLY (scrubber.py:115), is non-recursive by default, and scrub_event never touches contexts/logentry/message — so `x_admin_key`, `expected`, `access_token` and every nested value sail through. (3) Full-pipeline repro through the REAL runtime path (cr_sec_03_probe.py: real init_sentry() + capturing transport + FastAPI TestClient + the real app.api.admin_routes.verify_admin_key): one unauthenticated request with a raw 0xE9 byte in X-Admin-Key returns HTTP 500 and emits an event carrying 99 sentinel sites, including the production ADMIN_API_KEY verbatim at .exception.values[0].stacktrace.frames[19].vars.expected, the caller JWT at .request.data.access_token, and JWT+session cookie repeated in raw ASGI header tuples across 20 frames. It also proves the docstring at :29-31 false: .request.query_string comes out `token=<full JWT>&q=[QUERY_REDACTED]` — q redacted, token not. SENTRY_DSN is confirmed set on the Railway `web` service (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt), so this path is live at the deployed SHA. DOES THE PROPOSED FIX CLOSE IT — yes, but only both halves together, and I measured that too. Applying the finder's fix as a monkeypatch (recursive _scrub_dict over request/extra/contexts/user + frame vars, _scrub_string over message/logentry, the extra key fragments incl. `expected`, the ?token=/?access_token= query rule) TOGETHER WITH include_local_variables=False drives the same repro 99 -> 0 (cr_sec_03_fixcheck.txt). The scrub half ALONE, with locals still on, leaves 48 residual sites (cr_sec_03_fixcheck_localsON.txt): it does close the ADMIN_API_KEY, the access_token and the ?token= leaks, but _scrub_dict's list branch (sentry_service.py:122) only descends into dicts and strings, never into nested LISTS, so the ASGI `headers` list-of-[name, value] pairs keep the Bearer JWT and the session cookie. So: include_local_variables=False is not "belt and braces", it is load-bearing and should ship first; and if they want the scrubber to stand on its own, _scrub_dict:122 also needs list-of-list recursion. One caveat on the fix as written: adding the bare fragment `key` to _SENSITIVE_KEY_FRAGMENTS will redact benign keys (cache_key, key_features, keywords) across breadcrumbs and extra — prefer `admin_key`/`api-key`/`_key` over `key`. IS test_first THE RIGHT RED TEST — it is red today (my unit probe is exactly that shape: 17 hits) but it is the WEAKER of the two and would green-light an incomplete fix: a hand-built 12-region fixture cannot contain the ASGI list-of-lists header tuples the real SDK produces, so it passes at 48 live leaks remaining. Pin it with the full-pipeline test instead (or as well): real sentry_sdk.init with the app's own option set, a capturing transport, TestClient hitting the real verify_admin_key with a latin-1 non-ASCII X-Admin-Key, then assert no sentinel appears at any JSON path of the outbound envelope. Caveats: local sentry-sdk is 2.54.0 vs requirements.txt:142 pin 2.68.1 — local, off-lock; the mechanism (scrubber-before-before_send order, exact-key denylist, include_local_variables default True, max_request_body_size default "medium") is stable across 2.x but the exact frame count could differ in CI/prod. Kept at P1 rather than upgraded to P0: the exfil destination is the team's own Sentry project, not an attacker-readable channel, matching M13's own calibration where security-03 was downgraded for lacking cross-principal disclosure. Operationally it still warrants rotating ADMIN_API_KEY, since I could not check whether such a 500 has already fired in prod.

findings.title: verify_admin_key raises TypeError on any non-ASCII X-Admin-Key: an unauthenticated request 500s all 17 admin routes and pushes the real ADMIN_API_KEY into Sentry
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Make the comparison byte-safe and total: encode both sides first and compare bytes - 'if not expected or not hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key.encode("utf-8", "ignore"), expected.encode("utf-8"))' - and change the signature to 'x_admin_key: str = Header(default="")' so a MISSING header also produces the 403 path rather than a 422 (see CR-SECURITY-11). Apply the identical byte-encode to the two hmac.compare_digest sites in main.py's _AdminAuthenticatedStaticFiles (:234 header path, :244 Basic path) and to history_routes.py:148/:184. Ship together with the include_local_variables=False change from CR-SECURITY-03 so the exposure closes from both ends. No flag.
findings.test_first: tests/test_admin_key_non_ascii.py: parametrise verify_admin_key over ['é', 'ك', b'\xff'.decode('latin-1'), '', 'wrong'] and assert every one raises HTTPException(403) - never TypeError; plus a TestClient case asserting GET /api/v1/admin/costs with X-Admin-Key set to a latin-1 high byte returns 403, not 500. RED today (TypeError -> 500).
findings.impact: One unauthenticated GET with a single high byte in X-Admin-Key turns every one of the 19 admin-key-gated routes into a 500 (availability: trivial, unmetered on the mount side) and, on the very first such request, writes the plaintext production admin key into a third-party error tracker where it persists in the event payload. The admin key is the credential for the cost dashboards, the audit log, the cohort/referral analytics and the DELETE /api/v1/text/cache flush. Two separately-benign choices (compare_digest's ASCII restriction; unscrubbed Sentry frames) compose into a credential-disclosure primitive.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced against the real function: verify_admin_key('é'), ('ك') and (latin-1 0xFF) all raise TypeError; '' and 'wrong' correctly raise HTTPException 403. compare_digest's ASCII restriction confirmed independently. ErrorHandlerMiddleware is registered (main.py:154), catches it, and calls sentry_sdk.capture_exception at error_handler.py:154 (not :151); the deepest Python frame is verify_admin_key, whose locals are {x_admin_key, expected} — and CR-SECURITY-03 proves frame vars are unscrubbed. Route count corrected: 19 in admin_routes.py plus 3 in text_routes.py = 22, not 17.

Reproduced end-to-end through the real modules, not a lookalike; I could not break it. (1) Direct call of the real `app.api.admin_routes.verify_admin_key` (imported, sourcefile confirmed admin_routes.py:34): '\xff', 'eadmin' with acute-e, Arabic kaf, and the latin-1 view of UTF-8 'e-acute' ALL raise `TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported`, while '' and 'wrong' raise the intended HTTPException 403 and the correct key returns True - so the fault is specifically the non-ASCII byte, exactly as claimed. (2) Escalation confirmed through the WHOLE app: `TestClient(app.main.app, raise_server_exceptions=False).get('/api/v1/admin/stats/daily', headers={'X-Admin-Key': b'\xff'})` returns HTTP 500 SERVER_ERROR (ErrorHandlerMiddleware, error_handler.py:135-160), versus 403 for a wrong ASCII key and 200 for the correct one - unauthenticated, no rate-limit reached, no auth required. The CR-SECURITY-11 sub-claim also reproduced: omitting the header entirely gives 422, not 403. (3) The credential half is MEASURED, not modelled: I re-ran the raise under a real `sentry_sdk.init(...)` wired with the repo's own `app.services.sentry_service._before_send`, send_default_pii=False, and a local stub transport (no network, nothing sent to the real project) - the serialized event contains the plaintext ADMIN_API_KEY, in frame vars `{"x_admin_key": "'\xff'", "expected": "'SUPER_SECRET_PROD_ADMIN_KEY_123'"}` at admin_routes.py:37. My best break-attempt was that `_before_send` would scrub it: it does not - it scrubs exception values, breadcrumbs, request headers (incl. x-admin-key) and query strings, but never `stacktrace.frames[].vars`, and `sentry_sdk.init` at sentry_service.py:215 never passes `include_local_variables` (SDK default True, verified). SENTRY_DSN IS present in the prod Railway `web` var list, so the channel is live. Two corrections: the route count is 22 (`Depends(verify_admin_key)` = 19 in admin_routes.py + 3 in text_routes.py), not the 17/19 the finder gave; and the header-decode step is off-lock locally (starlette 0.38.6 vs lock 1.6.0) - latin-1 header decoding is ASGI-spec behaviour and `hmac.compare_digest`'s ASCII restriction is CPython stdlib, so I judge both version-independent, but the TestClient 500 itself is "local, off-lock". Kept at P1 rather than upgraded: the DoS reaches only internal admin routes (no user-facing flow), and the leaked key lands in the owner's own Sentry project, which the attacker cannot read - disclosure to a third-party store, not to the attacker. DOES THE PROPOSED FIX CLOSE MY REPRO: yes, measured. Re-running all seven cases through `hmac.compare_digest(x.encode('utf-8','ignore'), expected.encode('utf-8'))` yields 403 for every non-ASCII case, for '' and for 'wrong', and True only for the correct key - zero TypeErrors. Two notes: `.encode('latin-1','ignore')` would round-trip the actual wire bytes more faithfully than utf-8 (utf-8 re-encodes the latin-1-decoded string, so a non-ASCII ADMIN_API_KEY could never be matched byte-exactly), but since it fails closed to 403 either way and the key is ASCII in practice this is a refinement, not a defect; and the `Header(default="")` half of the fix is genuinely required - I measured the 422, so without it a missing header still bypasses the 403 path. The fix must ship with CR-SECURITY-03's `include_local_variables=False` as the finder says, since the byte-safe compare alone leaves every OTHER raising frame's locals exposed. IS test_first THE RIGHT RED TEST: yes, and it is RED today - the parametrised `verify_admin_key` cases raise TypeError instead of HTTPException(403), and the TestClient case returns 500 instead of 403. Two refinements I would make: '' in the parametrise list only exercises the direct-call path (a genuinely missing header 422s before the dependency body runs), so add an explicit missing-header case asserting 403-not-422; and add a third assertion using the stub-transport pattern I ran - capture the Sentry event and assert `ADMIN_API_KEY not in json.dumps(event)` - otherwise the test pins only the availability half and a future regression that re-enables local variables would slip through silently.

findings.title: The SSRF validator blocks the event loop on a synchronous DNS lookup - 11.07s measured for one hostile hostname, ~22s per unauthenticated /url/compare
findings.dedupe: new (M13's event-loop wave and M18's LS-event-loop-02/04 enumerate DB/Redis/adapter blocking sites; DNS inside the SSRF guard was never in either offload set or either finding list.)
findings.fix: Make validate_external_url async and resolve off-loop with a hard cap: 'infos = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(hostname, None), timeout=2.0)' (loop.getaddrinfo already dispatches to the executor), treat TimeoutError as blocked, and keep a thin sync wrapper for the non-async callers in price_service/shopify_pdp/sitemap_discovery that routes through asyncio.to_thread. Await it at all six url_routes sites. Give it its own flag ENABLE_ASYNC_URL_VALIDATION (default ON is safe here - the semantics are unchanged and the only behaviour delta is that a slow resolver now fails closed at 2s instead of blocking 11s) so it can be reverted independently of the offload waves. Ordering note: unlike the limiter-key change, this needs no offload precondition.
findings.test_first: tests/test_url_validator_nonblocking.py: monkeypatch socket.getaddrinfo to sleep 3s, then run two concurrent asyncio tasks - one calling the validator, one incrementing a counter every 10ms - and assert the counter advanced during the validation (RED today: it does not). Second node: assert a resolver that never returns is abandoned within 2.5s.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated caller freezes the entire deployment - every other user's compare, every /health probe, every SSE stream - for up to the resolver timeout per request, using nothing but a hostname. This is the cheapest DoS in the surface: no payload, no auth, no paid work. It compounds M18's LS-capacity-math-01 (the 10/minute limits are keyed on the shared Railway edge IP, i.e. deployment-wide), because the attacker only needs the handful of requests the limiter already lets through to hold the loop continuously. The site is in NEITHER offload set (ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD covers db_offload.run_db; ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD covers cache_service) so no existing flag mitigates it.

verdict_trail.reason: Loop blocking proved, not just asserted: with getaddrinfo monkeypatched to 3s, an asyncio ticker advanced 0 ticks during a 4.89s validate_external_url call (expected ~300 if off-loop). All six call sites confirmed at url_routes.py:91,112,148,175,197,216, every one inside an async def on the 1-worker uvicorn; POST /compare (:126-128, @limiter.limit('10/minute'), no auth dependency) validates both URLs. Caveat on the number: 11.465s for the NXDOMAIN host is MY Windows box, not Railway — the per-request stall in prod is resolver-bound, so '~22s' is modelled, not measured. Defect and severity stand.

Reproduced through the runtime module, not by reading. Repro at scratchpad/m22-review/repro_cr_security_05.py (output repro_out.txt); url_validator.py and app/api/url_routes.py are byte-identical between 76ace90 and the working tree HEAD (git diff empty), so the evidence holds at the review SHA. (1) The defect is real and deterministic: with socket.getaddrinfo monkeypatched to a 3.0s resolver, calling validate_external_url from a coroutine let a 10ms ticker task advance 0 times in 3.000s (~300 expected) — the loop is fully stalled, and the stall length is the resolver's, not a constant. (2) It is service-wide, not per-request: mounting the REAL app.api.url_routes.router on FastAPI and driving it over httpx ASGITransport, a control GET /ping issued 200ms after GET /api/v1/url/detect returned only at t=3.204s. (3) It is unauthenticated: the router (url_routes.py:22) declares no dependencies and is mounted at main.py:177; a credential-free prod GET /api/v1/url/detect returned 200. THREE CORRECTIONS to the finding, none of which move severity. (a) The "validates url1 AND url2, doubling it" claim is WRONG for the stated blackhole attack: `not validate(url1) or not validate(url2)` short-circuits on the first False, and my repro counted exactly 1 getaddrinfo call for a compare whose resolver fails. Doubling needs url1 to resolve slowly-but-successfully. (b) Understated the other way: with a succeeding resolver the same compare made 6 getaddrinfo calls, because url_extraction_service.py:101 and :111 re-validate the initial URL and every redirect hop inside the async fetch — so the per-request blocking budget exceeds the 6 route-level sites the finder enumerated (same pattern at price_service.py:14126/14147 and shopify_pdp_service.py:284). (c) The file is app/api/url_routes.py, not app/routes/url_routes.py. MAGNITUDE IS THE WEAK PART OF THE EVIDENCE, so I did not upgrade: the 11.07s figure reproduces in kind on this box (13.15s for a nonexistent .example host) but the finder's "control resolve took 0.024s" did not — example.com took 7.02s here, i.e. this Windows resolver is slow across the board, and prod latency was unusable as evidence (this box saw 7.0s / 25.7s on plain /health). The seconds-per-request number on Railway's glibc resolver is MODELLED; the blocking itself is measured. Kept at P1, not P0: it needs an attacker, prod traffic is effectively zero and no user is harmed today; not below P1 because it is unauthenticated, single-worker, deterministic, and no shipped flag mitigates it. DOES THE PROPOSED FIX CLOSE IT? Yes — I transplanted it verbatim (asyncio.wait_for(loop.getaddrinfo(host, None), timeout=2.0), TimeoutError treated as blocked): against the same 3.0s resolver the ticker advanced 127 times and the call returned False at 1.998s. Two caveats to carry into the fix. wait_for abandons the future but cannot cancel the in-flight C call, so the resolver thread still parks for the full resolver timeout — and loop.getaddrinfo runs on the loop's DEFAULT executor, which since M13-34 is the shared sized `qaren-worker` pool (ADAPTER_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS, default 40) also serving every M13-05/M13-06 to_thread offload, so a hostile flood converts loop starvation into pool contention with the DB/Redis offloads; give the resolve its own executor or a semaphore and state that interaction as the flag's precondition. Second, "keep a thin sync wrapper … that routes through asyncio.to_thread" is not implementable as written (to_thread is a coroutine, and the price_service/shopify_pdp/sitemap_discovery callers are themselves running inside executor threads) — those callers should keep the plain sync socket.getaddrinfo path. IS test_first THE RIGHT RED TEST? Yes in shape, and it is genuinely RED at HEAD — my node 1 is that test and it measures 0 ticks. Two hardening notes: add the node-2 assertion (drive the real router over ASGITransport and assert a concurrent control route is served during the validation) so a future refactor that awaits the validator but re-blocks in a helper still fails; and make the never-returns node use a stop-event-driven fake resolver, otherwise the abandoned non-daemon executor thread hangs the suite at teardown.
