Items (5)/(6) unreproducible without the finder's harness.

findings.title: comparison_feedback.winner_correct has no writer anywhere in the codebase, and it is the ONLY quality filter the few-shot rotation cron applies — the exemplar miner can never find a row
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Two-part. (a) Land the writer: add optional `winner_correct`/`price_correct`/`specs_correct` (3-state 'correct'|'wrong'|'unsure', matching the 027 CHECK) to FeedbackRequest in app/api/feedback_routes.py and pass them into save_feedback's `record` in app/services/feedback_service.py:139-152, guarded by a new default-OFF flag ENABLE_PER_AXIS_FEEDBACK so the mobile app can ship the UI on its own clock. (b) Until (a) has data, make the miner degrade honestly: in _fetch_top_decile_feedback, drop the `.eq("winner_correct","correct")` filter to a preference (fetch on `useful=true`, then rank rows that carry winner_correct='correct' first) and emit a WARNING when zero rows carry a non-null per-axis signal, so the cron says 'no per-axis feedback exists' instead of silently producing an empty rotation. Do not flip ENABLE_FEWSHOT_ROTATION before (a) has landed and at least _MIN_EXEMPLARS_PER_CATEGORY rows exist.
findings.test_first: tests/test_feedback_axis_persistence.py::test_winner_correct_round_trips — POST /api/v1/feedback with winner_correct='correct' through the real route, then assert the value comes back on the inserted comparison_feedback record; RED today because FeedbackRequest rejects/drops the field. Pair it with tests/test_few_shot_rotation.py::test_fetch_top_decile_returns_rows_when_only_useful_is_set — stub a client whose comparison_feedback table has useful=true and winner_correct=None and assert _fetch_top_decile_feedback returns it (or at minimum logs a warning); RED today because the .eq filter drops it.
findings.impact: Migration 027 added winner_correct/price_correct/specs_correct plus a partial index in June; the per-axis UI it was written for ('until B.3 wires the per-axis UI', 027 line ~66) never landed, so all three columns are 100% NULL in prod (measured: 0 of 1 rows non-null). _fetch_top_decile_feedback filters `.eq("useful",True).eq("winner_correct","correct")` — an AND over a column that is always NULL — so the moment ENABLE_FEWSHOT_ROTATION is flipped the rotation will run, mine zero exemplars, and log nothing that says why. The prompt-exemplar refresh loop is therefore permanently inert and will look like 'no good feedback yet' rather than 'the column is never written'. DARK FLAG: ENABLE_FEWSHOT_ROTATION is absent from the Railway `web` and `price-warmer` variable sets (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt), so this is unreachable today — severity capped at P2 per the brief.

verdict_trail.reason: Mechanism confirmed: no writer exists, column 100% NULL, miner returns 0. But two impact claims are wrong. main() lines 389-394 DOES log 'no useful+correct feedback yet - keeping the synthetic seed (no file write)' and returns None, so there is no 'empty rotation' and it does not 'log nothing that says why'. Title overstates: `.eq("useful",True)` is a second filter. Flag absent from both Railway services; only 1 comparison_feedback row exists at all, so even unfiltered the miner is below _MIN_EXEMPLARS. Latent, zero harm => P3.

findings.title: The daily re-engagement cron selects a phantom users.governorate column, so its eligible-user query 42703s and returns 0 users — the whole cron is a silent no-op even with the flag on
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: In _fetch_eligible_users, replace `governorate` in the select list with `demographics_profile`, and flatten it before handing rows to the service: `u["governorate"] = (u.get("demographics_profile") or {}).get("governorate")`. That keeps reengagement_service.py:178/188/332 untouched (it already expects a top-level key) and keeps the read on the one column that actually exists. Ship unflagged — it rides the existing dark ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES gate. While in there, change the `except` at cron_reengagement.py:54 from `logger.warning(...); return []` to also re-raise (or exit non-zero) when the exception is a PostgREST 42703, so a schema drift fails the cron loudly instead of producing a clean empty run.
findings.test_first: tests/test_cron_reengagement.py::test_eligible_user_fetch_selects_only_real_columns — build the select through the real _fetch_eligible_users against a fake client that records the column list, and assert every requested name is in the live users column set (or simply assert 'governorate' not in the list and 'demographics_profile' is). RED today. A stronger variant: a schema-contract test that reads the 22 live table column sets once and asserts every literal column string in every .select() across app/ + scripts/ exists — that single test would have caught all five phantom sites in this lane.
findings.impact: Every downstream detector is starved: main() iterates the empty list, so zero re_engagement_events rows are written and zero pushes are dispatched (measured: re_engagement_events has 0 rows). Worse, the failure is a caught-and-warned exception, so the cron exits 0 and looks healthy — this is exactly the #80 'cron failure visibility' class, but here the cron is not merely unobservable, it is structurally incapable of doing work. governorate is not a column at all; it lives inside users.demographics_profile JSONB (the value structured_comparison_service._cohort_summary reads at line ~4508), and reengagement_service consumes it as a TOP-LEVEL key (`user.get("governorate")` at reengagement_service.py:178) which the cron was supposed to supply. DARK FLAG: ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES=false on both Railway services, so no user is affected today — capped at P2 per the brief.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced exactly. Line 46 selects a column that does not exist; the except at 53-55 warns and returns []. Real fn returns 0 while 18 users have notifications_enabled=true. Dark flag ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES=false on both services caps at P2. Not a duplicate of M18 CD-uncovered-08 (that is the missing cursor, P3, same function). One fix gap: `users.last_comparison_at` has no writer either (0/18 non-null) and demographics_profile is null for 12/18, so repointing at demographics_profile alone still yields 0 eligible users.

findings.title: reengagement _compute_current_sentiment queries three columns that do not exist on product_reviews (sentiment_score, product_id, created_at) — the sentiment-drop detector can never fire
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Rewrite the lookup against the real shape: `client.table("product_reviews").select("reviews, fetched_at").eq("product_key", product_key).single().execute()`, then derive the score from the JSONB blob (e.g. a `sentiment` / `rating` key inside `reviews`) rather than a scalar column, and return None when the blob carries no such key — preserving the documented 'no false positives from missing data' contract. Also rename the parameter from product_id to product_key at the call sites so the identifier matches the column. If a real scalar column is genuinely wanted, that needs a NEW migration (037) adding product_reviews.sentiment_score plus a writer in review_service — do not add the column without the writer, or this becomes CR-DATA-MIGRATIONS-01 all over again.
findings.test_first: tests/test_reengagement_detectors.py::test_compute_current_sentiment_reads_real_columns — call the real _compute_current_sentiment with a fake client that asserts the requested table/columns/filters are ('product_reviews', {'reviews','fetched_at'}, 'product_key') and returns a row; assert a float comes back. RED today (the code asks for sentiment_score/product_id/created_at).
findings.impact: Three independent drifts in one 6-line query, so there is no partial degradation: the call always raises, the `except` at line 249 logs a warning and returns None, and the sentiment-drop re-engagement detector treats every product as 'no snapshot available' and skips it forever. Migration 012 never defined sentiment_score; nothing in app/ or scripts/ writes it; and product_reviews stores a JSONB `reviews` blob keyed by `product_key` with a `fetched_at` (not `created_at`) timestamp. This is the same phantom-column class as #65 and the fixed response_data referral bug, in a third module — evidence the class is systematic rather than a one-off. DARK FLAG: gated by the same ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES=false, so capped at P2.

verdict_trail.reason: All three phantom columns reproduced with the exact PostgREST hint quoted. Lines 238/239/240 confirmed; except at 248-250 warns and returns None, so the detector at line 165 always skips. Live product_reviews columns are id/product_key/brand/name/variant/reviews (+source/fetched_at). Same dark gate as -02 => P2 cap correct. Genuinely new (no prior review or open issue names product_reviews.sentiment_score). Fix nit: the proposed `.single()` on product_key will raise when a key has multiple snapshot rows — use .order('fetched_at').limit(1).

findings.title: Every analytics_service dashboard query is unbounded and silently truncated at PostgREST max-rows=1000 — 'popular queries' is ranked from 6% of search_logs, in arbitrary physical order
findings.dedupe: new — adjacent to known:M13-98 (P3) which flagged the SAME truncation mechanism at app/api/admin_routes.py:110 only; the four analytics_service sites were never named and are still open
findings.fix: Two changes, both unflagged corrections. (1) For the three windowed functions, add `.order("created_at", desc=True)` and page explicitly with `.range(offset, offset+999)` in a loop until a short page comes back, or better, replace the Python-side Counter with a server-side aggregate (the same pattern migration 036 uses for /home/savings: a SECURITY DEFINER SQL function `search_log_daily_rollup(p_since timestamptz)` returning day/count/cost/success_count, GRANTed to service_role only, whose cost does not grow with the table). (2) For get_popular_queries, which has no window at all, add a `.gte("created_at", since)` bound plus the same rollup, since ranking all-time queries by scanning the table will only get worse. In every case, compare `len(records)` against the exact count (`count="exact"`) and surface a `truncated: true` field in the response so a partial answer is never presented as a total.
findings.test_first: tests/test_analytics_truncation.py::test_daily_stats_does_not_silently_truncate — stub the supabase client so search_logs returns exactly 1000 rows with a content-range of `0-999/5000`, call the real get_daily_stats, and assert the result either contains all 5000 (paged) or carries `truncated=True`. RED today: it returns total_comparisons=1000 with no flag. Add a sibling asserting get_popular_queries issues at least one range/limit call.
findings.impact: Four dashboards are wrong, not merely stale: get_popular_queries (line 65, NO filter at all), get_daily_stats (line 19), get_cost_trends (line 87) and get_error_stats (line 126) all issue filter-only selects with no .limit()/.range() and no ORDER BY. PostgREST answers 206 with the first 1000 rows in whatever order the planner returns, and supabase-py surfaces that as an ordinary success — no exception, no truncation flag, no log line. So /admin/analytics reports total_comparisons=1000 for any window with more than 1000 rows (June alone had 9,157), total_cost is the cost of an arbitrary 1000-row slice, and the 'top queries' ranking is computed over ~6% of the corpus with no guarantee the slice is recent. Every historical cost/error-rate number a human read off this dashboard since the row count crossed 1000 is understated by an unknown factor. Not user-facing (admin only), hence P2 rather than P1.

verdict_trail.reason: All four unbounded filter-only selects confirmed at lines 19/65/87/126 — no .limit(), .range() or .order(). Truncation measured: raw select returns 1000 of 16283. Real functions reproduce the finder's numbers exactly (popular top-1 count 369; daily_stats(120) total 1000 with 13 days; cost_trends(120) count 1000). Operator-reachable behind ADMIN_API_KEY (set in prod). Dedupe should be widened: also adjacent to M18 CD-uncovered-03 (admin_routes cohort scans, P2) besides M13-98 (admin_routes:110) — but the four analytics_service sites are named in neither.

findings.title: STATUS #65 STILL-OPEN: the behavior-profile write path 42703s on TWO phantom columns before it ever writes, and all 18 prod users still carry behavior_profile={}

Ship behind a default-OFF ENABLE_BEHAVIOR_PROFILE_REBUILD so the first run (which will start writing non-empty profiles for the first time and thereby change scoring for existing users) is a deliberate flip, not a side effect of a deploy; verify with the same 18-user query before and after.
findings.test_first: tests/test_behavior_profile_wiring.py::test_update_behavior_profile_writes_a_profile — patch get_supabase_client with a fake whose `comparisons`/`comparison_feedback`/`user_events` tables raise PostgREST 42703 for any column outside the live set, run the real _update_behavior_profile, and assert users.update was called with a non-empty behavior_profile. RED today: the fake raises on 'category_used' and no update is ever attempted.
findings.impact: _update_behavior_profile (scs.py:4531-4553) issues four serial round trips inside ONE try; the FIRST (line 4545) raises 42703, so the feedback read, the events read, build_behavior_profile and — critically — the `users.update({"behavior_profile": profile})` at line 4552 never execute. The except at 4553 logs a warning and swallows it. Meanwhile _fetch_behavior_profile (line 4524) reads users.behavior_profile, which exists but is `{}` for every user, so the three-layer personalization stack silently runs on an empty profile on every authed compare while scoring still reports a behavioral scoring_method. Two distinct drifts feed it: comparisons has no `category_used` and no `products` column (its live columns are created_at, full_response, id, input_type, product_names, query, schema_version, share_token, user_id — the category and product list live INSIDE full_response), and user_events stores its payload in `event_data`, not `metadata` — the exact same `metadata` misnaming that broke all mobile analytics pre-M21-W1. Live and reachable today (ENABLE_COHORT_PERSONALIZATION=true), so P1; reported as STATUS only per the brief.

verdict_trail.reason: Both drifts reproduced at 76ace90 line 4545/4547 (scs.py changed after 76ace90 but not in this region). GitHub #65 is OPEN and cites the same code at its old line 4040 — still-open with fresh line and live-data evidence (0/18 users have a non-empty behavior_profile). One reachability correction: it is NOT gated by ENABLE_COHORT_PERSONALIZATION — _update_behavior_profile is called unconditionally for any user_id on both the sync (:3646-3650) and stream (:4356-4360) compare paths, which makes it more reachable, not less. P1 stands.

Could not break it. Live read-only SELECTs reproduce both 42703s; a fake client mirroring the live column set drives the REAL _update_behavior_profile and shows it dies at the first select with users.update NEVER attempted (calls=[('table','comparisons')]), exception swallowed at :4553. findings.title: Six live tables have no DDL in migrations/ at all — including user_events and comparison_feedback, whose only user_id query pattern has no index defined anywhere in version control

findings.fix: Add a single `migrations/000_baseline_schema.sql` capturing the current live DDL for users, comparisons, comparison_feedback, user_events, bahrain_approved_drugs and rating_cache — pull it from the Supabase dashboard's schema export (or `pg_dump --schema-only -t`) rather than reconstructing it by hand, mark it 'baseline: already applied in prod, present so a fresh environment can be built', and make every statement IF NOT EXISTS so re-applying is a no-op. In the same file add the two missing access-path indexes: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_events_user_created ON user_events (user_id, created_at DESC);` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_comparison_feedback_user ON comparison_feedback (user_id);`. findings.test_first: tests/test_migrations_cover_live_schema.py::test_every_queried_table_has_ddl — parse every `.table("x")` literal out of app/ and scripts/ (the AST walk this lane already wrote), collect every CREATE TABLE name from migrations/*.sql, and assert the first set is a subset of the second. RED today on six tables. A second assertion for the index side: for every (table, column) pair used in an `.eq()` that is also paired with an `.order()`, assert an index naming both appears in migrations/. RED on user_events and comparison_feedback.
findings.impact: The schema of the six busiest user-data tables lives only in the Supabase dashboard. Concretely: (a) nobody can rebuild a staging or CI database from migrations/ — a fresh apply produces a schema on which 010/011 fail immediately; (b) the index situation is unknowable from the repo, and for the two tables that matter it is unknowable AND undefined — structured_comparison_service.py:4546 filters comparison_feedback by user_id and :4547 filters user_events by user_id with `order(created_at desc).limit(200)`, and admin_routes.py:375 runs user_events `.eq(user_id).limit(50)` once PER USER inside a loop; none of those access paths has an index in version control; (c) constraint drift is invisible — this project has already been burned once by exactly this (migration 017's header documents comparisons.share_token silently being varchar(12) in prod against 22-char tokens, breaking sharing from Session 22 to 42 with 0 of 6 comparisons carrying a token). user_events is at 146 rows and comparison_feedback at 1 today, so there is no live latency harm — this is a correctness-of-the-record and future-growth finding, P2.

verdict_trail.reason: Core claim reproduced exactly: the six named tables have no DDL, so 001 (ALTER comparisons) and 010:8 (ALTER users ENABLE RLS) both fail on a virgin DB — migrations/ cannot rebuild the schema. Counts in the evidence are off and I corrected them: 20 CREATE TABLE statements (16 distinct names, one of which — spec_spine — is not live) covering 15 of 21 live base tables, not '22 covering 16 of 22'; 50 CREATE INDEX statements, not 46. Zero live harm at 146/1 rows, but a non-rebuildable migration set is a real, reproducible quality defect, so P2 stands.

findings.title: Migrations 010/011/012 are non-idempotent (bare CREATE POLICY / CREATE INDEX) so a re-run aborts the Supabase SQL editor's single transaction, and rollback/ has parity only from 023 onward
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Backfill idempotence into 010/011/012 exactly as 014 does: prefix every `CREATE POLICY x ON t` with `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS x ON t;` and change every `CREATE INDEX y` to `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS y`. This is a pure edit to already-applied files, so it changes nothing in prod but makes a replay safe. Then add rollback/ files for 010-022 following the shape of rollback/023_referral_lifetime_cap_ROLLBACK.sql — at minimum for 012 (the product-data tables) and 014 (the referral system), the two with real data behind them. Finally, wrap 010/011/012 in explicit BEGIN;/COMMIT; the way 025-036 do, so the transaction boundary is in the file rather than implied by the editor.
findings.test_first: tests/test_migration_idempotence.py::test_every_migration_is_replay_safe — read each migrations/*.sql, strip comments, and assert every CREATE POLICY has a matching DROP POLICY IF EXISTS earlier in the file and every CREATE INDEX / CREATE TABLE carries IF NOT EXISTS. RED today on 010, 011, 012. Extend tests/test_migration_index_predicate_immutability.py (which already comment-strips) rather than adding a new harness. A second test asserts every migrations/NNN_*.sql numbered >= 010 has a migrations/rollback/NNN_*.sql sibling — RED on 010-022.
findings.impact: Two hygiene gaps with the same root. (1) Re-running 010, 011 or 012 in the Supabase SQL editor raises 42710 'policy already exists' / 42P07 'relation already exists' on the first duplicate; because the editor wraps a multi-statement script in ONE transaction (a fact migration 036's own header calls out: 'a later failure silently rolls back earlier statements'), the operator gets a rollback of everything that ran before it and an ambiguous partial state to reason about. That is precisely the trap 014+ were written to avoid, and 010-012 were never backfilled. (2) rollback/ covers 023-036 but nothing for 010-022, so there is no documented undo for the entire RLS baseline, the product-data L2 tables or the referral system. Neither is a live defect — capped P3 — but both raise the cost of the next schema recovery, and this project has already lost a feature to schema drift once (017's post-mortem).

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. 010/011/012 use bare CREATE POLICY / CREATE INDEX with no DROP IF EXISTS and no IF NOT EXISTS, and carry no BEGIN;/COMMIT;, while 014 onward uses DROP-then-CREATE + IF NOT EXISTS. rollback/ holds 15 files, lowest 023. One evidence error corrected: 010 has 14 bare CREATE POLICY statements in lines 17-64, not 10; 011 also has 3 more bare CREATE INDEX (48-50) beyond idx_usage_user_period. Latent replay hazard only, nothing live => P3 right. Fix (backfill DROP IF EXISTS / IF NOT EXISTS into already-applied files) changes nothing in prod and is flag-free.

findings.title: No retention or cleanup exists for any append-only table (search_logs 16,283 rows and growing, product_prices 3,945), and the one cleanup function that IS deployed is called by zero code
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add a `migrations/037_retention.sql` defining one SECURITY DEFINER sweeper per table with an explicit window — e.g. `search_logs_prune(p_days int default 180)` deleting created_at < now() - interval, `product_prices_prune(p_days int default 90)` keeping the newest row per (product_key, region) regardless of age so the L2 cache is never emptied, and `admin_audit_log_prune(p_days int default 365)` — each REVOKEd from PUBLIC and GRANTed to service_role only, mirroring 036's lockdown. Wire them into a new `scripts/cron_retention.py` behind a default-OFF ENABLE_RETENTION_SWEEP so the first run is a deliberate flip, and log the deleted row count. Separately, either call the already-deployed cleanup_expired_ratings from that cron or drop the function — a deployed-but-uncalled SECURITY DEFINER routine is unnecessary attack surface.
findings.test_first: tests/test_retention_sweeper.py::test_prune_keeps_the_newest_price_per_key — against a fake client (or a live_db-marked fixture), insert two product_prices rows for the same (product_key, region) both older than the window, run the sweeper, and assert exactly one survives. RED today: no sweeper exists. Pair with tests/test_no_orphan_db_functions.py::test_every_live_rpc_has_a_call_site — assert every function name in the live /rpc OpenAPI paths appears in a `.rpc("...")` literal in app/ or scripts/; RED today on cleanup_expired_ratings.
findings.impact: Four tables are pure append with no TTL and no sweeper: search_logs (one row per compare — 16,283 rows for ~27 saved comparisons, so it is the highest-volume table by an order of magnitude and it stores raw user query text plus error strings indefinitely), product_prices (one row per L2 price fetch, deliberately append-only 'keeps history', 3,945 rows), admin_audit_log (1,439), and user_events. Nothing deletes them and nothing alerts on their size. Two consequences beyond disk: the retention gap is a privacy exposure (search_logs.query holds free-text user input forever, and delete_user_cascade only removes rows where user_id matches — anonymous rows, which are the majority given 12,505 'text' inputs against 18 users, are never reachable by a deletion request); and the growth silently worsens CR-DATA-MIGRATIONS-04, since every crossing of a 1000-row boundary makes another dashboard number quietly wrong. Volumes are small today and traffic is ~zero (Railway: 16 requests sampled in 24h), so P3.

verdict_trail.reason: Every measured number reproduced against live PostgREST, and the orphan-function claim is exact: cleanup_expired_ratings is in the live /rpc path set with zero references anywhere in app/, scripts/ or migrations/. No retention/purge/prune sweeper exists; the only DELETE FROM statements are inside delete_user_cascade, which is keyed on user_id — so anonymous search_logs rows are genuinely unreachable by a deletion request. Volumes tiny and traffic ~zero => P3 correct. The proposed 037 sweeper behind a default-OFF ENABLE_RETENTION_SWEEP is flag-safe. I did not re-verify the sub-claim '12,505 text inputs against 18 users'.

findings.title: STATUS M13-29 RLS gap still open by design: /events still writes through the service-role client, so the only control on a forged comparison_id is a UUID format check — inventory of all RLS policies, SECURITY DEFINER functions and GRANTs

findings.impact: INVENTORY (cr-security owns the exposure verdict; this is the DDL-vs-call-site map). RLS enabled on 15 tables across 010/011/012/014/028/029/030/031/032/035. Own-row policies: users (select/update/insert on auth.uid()=id), comparisons (select `auth.uid()=user_id OR share_token IS NOT NULL` per 017 — note the OR makes ANY shared row readable by ANY authenticated caller; both history_routes call sites re-check ownership with hmac.compare_digest, so it is contained in code, not in the policy), search_logs/comparison_feedback/user_events (insert `auth.uid()=user_id OR user_id IS NULL`, select own-row only), user_usage, referral_invites/redemptions/deep_review_credits/re_engagement_events (select-own, TO authenticated), pain_workflow_events, user_preference_history. Fully permissive: product_specs/product_prices/product_reviews carry `USING (true)` / `WITH CHECK (true)` for select AND insert (012:19-21,41-42,58-60) — anon-key writes to the L2 price cache are policy-allowed. RLS-enabled-with-no-policy (deny-all except service_role): verdict_critiques (030), eval_runs (031); service-role-only policies: products (032), spec_spine (035). SECURITY DEFINER functions: delete_user_cascade (010:72, redefined 025), increment_lifetime_comparisons (011:61), resolve_referral_code (014:99, GRANTed to anon+authenticated), home_savings_aggregate (036:51, GRANTed to authenticated+service_role, carries an auth.uid()=p_user_id cross-tenant guard, NOT YET APPLIED). Three GRANT EXECUTE statements total. CALL-SITE side: 51 of 141 sites touch `users` and the overwhelming majority go through get_supabase_client() = admin; the RLS-scoped get_user_supabase_client is used in only four places (database_service get_user_comparisons/get_comparison_by_id/delete_comparison/create_share_token, profile_routes:305, feedback_service.save_feedback when a token is present). M13-29's stated fix was applied to /feedback but NOT to /events.

verdict_trail.reason: Load-bearing claim reproduced: track_event (def :166, client at :179) and track_events_batch (def :201, client at :211) both call get_supabase_client(), documented at database_service.py:57-61 as returning the admin/service-role client, while save_feedback :142-145 takes access_token and uses get_user_supabase_client. So M13-29's client swap landed on /feedback and not /events; the 010 events_insert policy still does not constrain comparison_id. Line 194 was wrong (it is inside track_event's body) — corrected to 179. One inventory error: get_user_supabase_client has ~15 call sites (auth_routes 875/942, home_routes 215/599/822, profile_routes 184/305/474, database_service 247/280/300/343/448, feedback_service 143, referral_service 203), not four. findings.title: The products table is live, RLS-hardened and read by /admin/products, but its only writer has no callers — the table holds 0 rows and the product-stats dashboard is permanently empty
findings.dedupe: new

If product dedup is wanted, call `upsert_products_from_comparison(full_response)` from database_service.save_comparison right after the comparisons insert (line 225), wrapped in fire_and_forget so it can never break a compare, behind a default-OFF ENABLE_PRODUCT_DEDUP flag; it is a small upsert per compare and products is already indexed on canonical_name. If it is not wanted, delete upsert_product/upsert_products_from_comparison, delete the /admin/products route and analytics_service.get_product_stats, and add a migrations/037 dropping the products table — leaving a live table with an RLS policy, two indexes and no writer is strictly worse than either choice. findings.test_first: tests/test_product_ingest_wiring.py::test_save_comparison_upserts_products — call the real save_comparison with a two-product renderable payload against a fake client and assert an upsert reached the `products` table. verdict_trail.reason: Fully reproduced, line-exact. products is live with RLS + a service-role-only policy (032:59-64) and holds zero rows; upsert_products_from_comparison at database_service.py:543 has no production caller (only two tests), and upsert_product is called only from inside it; analytics_service.get_product_stats:158-162 reads the table and admin_routes.py:94 serves it, so GET /admin/products returns total_products 0 forever. findings.title: P3 sweep — six smaller code-versus-schema defects confirmed at 76ace90 (dead session_id column, admin N+1 count storms, LIKE that cannot use its index, count=exact downloading 1000 rows, per-user savings scans truncating at 1000, and a migration header that describes a column it does not add)

(c) Either add `CREATE INDEX ... ON admin_audit_log (event_type text_pattern_ops, created_at DESC)` or replace the LIKE with `.in_("event_type", [...])` over the known referral_* event types, which the existing index serves. (d) Add `.limit(1)` alongside count="exact" so only the header comes back. (e) Add `.limit(1000)` plus a `truncated` flag to both scans as a stopgap, and apply migration 036 so ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE can replace the home one outright (036's SQL was reviewed here and faithfully mirrors the Python: same schema_version=2 gate, same winner_index in (0,1), same BHD-only rule, same GREATEST(loser-winner,0) — plus a cross-tenant guard the Python path lacks). findings.test_first: (a) tests/test_events_session_id.py::test_session_id_reaches_the_row — POST /events with session_id and assert it lands in the record; RED (pydantic drops it). (b) tests/test_admin_cohort_uplift_query_count.py::test_uplift_issues_a_bounded_number_of_round_trips — count executes on a fake client for 200 users and assert <= 4; RED (~400 today). (d) tests/test_history_count_is_header_only.py — assert the count query carries a limit; RED. (e) tests/test_home_savings_truncation.py — 1,500 stub rows, assert the payload flags truncation; RED. findings.impact: (a) user_events.session_id exists and both track_event and track_events_batch support it, but no route supplies it — every one of the 146 rows is NULL, so session-scoped funnel analysis (the reason the column exists) is impossible; the compare_entry_* funnel events land with no session to group them by. (b) /admin/referrals/cohort-uplift issues up to 1,000 sequential blocking Supabase round trips per request (500 users x comparisons-count + user_events-count), and /admin/cohort/retention issues one per user; both run on the single event loop, so an admin page view can stall every concurrent compare — the same shape M18's LOAD ANSWER flagged, on a surface nobody load-tested. (c) a default-collation btree cannot serve a prefix LIKE, so the flagged-invite audit read seq-scans admin_audit_log (1,439 rows today) while idx_audit_event_time sits unused. (d) get_user_comparison_count asks PostgREST for count=exact with no limit, so it transfers up to 1000 uuids to read one header number, on every history-screen load. (e) both savings scans SELECT full_response for every one of a user's rows and truncate at 1000 with no error, so a heavy user's lifetime savings would silently plateau — the flag-OFF path is the one running in prod (ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE unset). (f) the 034 header tells a future operator the migration adds `brand`; brand actually came from 012, so someone verifying '034 applied' by checking for a new brand column would draw the wrong conclusion — the exact failure mode of CR-DATA-MIGRATIONS-07.

verdict_trail.reason: All six code claims reproduce at 76ace90 (cited files byte-identical 76ace90..HEAD 7dd04c1) and my own Supabase reads match the finder's numbers exactly. Two corrections: (b) duplicates M18 CD-uncovered-03 (P2, CONFIRMED, still open) and misstates the mechanism — _stats_for issues ONE count query per user, called twice (referred[:500] + organic[:500]) = up to 1,000, not '2 per user'; endpoint is /referrals/cohort_uplift, not cohort-uplift. (e)-home duplicates M18 LS-event-loop-01 / #116. Items (a)(c)(d)(f) and the truncation angle are new; P3 is right (floor) and the fixes are correct and flag-safe.

findings.title: settings.local.json permanently allows machine shutdown and blanket `Bash(git *)` with no deny list, so an agent can power off the dev box or force-push without a prompt
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Propose-only, three edits Ahmed makes: (1) delete the four shutdown/Stop-Computer entries and the two Stop-Process entries — a machine power-off should always cost one prompt; (2) replace `Bash(git *)` with the read/act split the workflow actually needs (`Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`, `Bash(git add:*)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`) and let push/reset/checkout/worktree prompt — that also lets the 41 redundant git entries be deleted; (3) add a `deny` block, which the file has never had, covering at minimum `Read(./.env)`, `Read(./.env.*)`, `Bash(git push --force:*)`, `Bash(git reset --hard:*)` and `Bash(rm -rf:*)`. The user already has the `git-guardrails-claude-code` and `careful`/`guard` skills installed at ~/.claude/skills/ that generate exactly this hook set — none of them has been applied to this repo (0 hooks configured).
findings.test_first: `tests/test_claude_permissions.py::test_no_destructive_permissions` — load .claude/settings.local.json and assert no allow entry matches `shutdown|Stop-Computer|Stop-Process|^Bash\(git \*\)$`, and assert `permissions.deny` exists and contains an `.env` read rule. RED at HEAD on both halves.
findings.impact: Three of these are unbounded and irreversible from inside a session. `PowerShell(Stop-Computer -Force)` and the three `shutdown /s` variants power off the machine with no prompt — they were approved once for a deliberate end-of-Session-50 wrap and have been standing authority ever since; any agent that decides a reboot would help can take the box down mid-wave with uncommitted worktrees. `Bash(git *)` unprompted covers `git push --force` and `git reset --hard` on a repo whose master is currently 7 commits ahead of origin/main. `Bash(curl:*)` unprompted is a live-write path to prod and to metered third-party APIs, in a repo whose own brief classifies prod writes and paid API calls as prohibited. There is no `deny` list, so nothing protects `.env` (which CLAUDE.md:638 says is the only place full API keys live) from `Bash(python:*)` or `Bash(curl:*)`.

verdict_trail.reason: Parsed the file myself: `permissions` has exactly one key, `allow`, with 192 entries; no deny, no ask, and grep finds no hooks anywhere under .claude/. Every quoted destructive entry is present verbatim, including three shutdown variants, PowerShell(Stop-Computer -Force), two Stop-Process entries, Bash(git *) alongside 41 redundant git entries, Bash(python:*), Bash(curl:*) and Bash(node -e *). The user-layer skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt:true is confirmed at ~/.claude/settings.json:34. Standing, irreversible authority on the dev box with no counterweight — P1 is right; not P0 because it is a latent grant, not an active leak.

Could not break it. Parsed at HEAD: permissions has ONLY allow (192 entries); no deny, no ask, no hooks anywhere under .claude/ (project settings.json holds only enabledPlugins); ~/.claude/settings.json sets skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true. All quoted destructive entries present verbatim. One refinement that strengthens rather than breaks it: the space-wildcard form Bash(git *) has uncertain matcher semantics in current Claude Code, but the unprompted force-push claim survives independently because the explicit colon-syntax Bash(git push:*) is in the list, as are Bash(curl:*) and Bash(python:*) with nothing denying .env. The proposed three-part fix closes my repro. test_first is the right red test - I ran it: RED on both halves.
