Every response the backend emits is a hand-built dict validated by nothing, which is the structural reason the wrong-shape-mock class of defect (findings 02 and 07, and the already-fixed referral `response_data` breakage) is undetectable by construction: a test can assert any key it likes because no model says which keys exist. It also means the 86%/85.84% coverage headline is computed over a denominator that includes 190 statements which can never be covered, and that `ComparisonResult` - the thing M20's winner-index normalization exists to compensate for - is documented in two places as 'never applied'.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced independently: coverage.py's own parser gives exactly the claimed statement counts and line ranges for all three files, corroborating the CI table quote, and nothing under app/ imports either model. product_schema.py:140 is indeed 'class ComparisonResult(BaseModel)'. 104+86=190 uncoverable statements — arithmetic checks out. One caveat the finder missed: a tracked LEGACY tree imports the name (backend/app/api/routes.py:30 'from app.models.schemas import'), but that resolves to backend/app/models/schemas.py, a different file, and backend/ is not what Railway runs (uvicorn app.main:app). Fix (a) should say so.

findings.title: All 245 jest suites run against a 143-line hand-written react-native facsimile with Platform.OS hardcoded to 'ios', so every Android branch in the app is untested
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Two steps, neither large. (1) Parameterise the platform: export `Platform` from the mock as a mutable object and add a shared test helper `withPlatform('android', fn)`; then add an Android pass over the 13 Platform-touching files (a jest project matrix - two `projects` entries in jest.config.js differing only in a setup file that sets Platform.OS - runs the whole suite twice for ~2x CI minutes and is the cheapest honest fix). (2) Add a contract test that asserts every named export the app imports from 'react-native' exists on the mock, driven by grepping `from 'react-native'` across src - so a new RN import silently resolving to undefined fails in CI instead of at runtime. No app flag.
findings.test_first: __tests__/mocks/reactNativeMock.contract.test.ts - collect every identifier imported from 'react-native' anywhere in src/ and App.tsx and assert `Object.keys(require('../../__mocks__/react-native'))` covers them; plus a red `authService.appleSignInAvailable` test under Platform.OS='android' asserting the early return.
findings.impact: '2320 jest tests pass / 242 suites green' - which CI now BLOCKS on - is a statement about a stub, not about React Native. Concretely: 15 of the 17 Platform branches only ever take the iOS side, so the Android path of `authService.ts:630` (Apple-Sign-In availability) and 12 other files is executed by no test, on a product that ships to Google Play ('Teen' rating, adaptive-icon.png). `Dimensions` is pinned to one 390x844 device, so no small-screen or tablet layout path is exercised; `I18nManager.isRTL` defaults false and is only flipped by hand in a few primitives tests (DirectionalIcon, SlideTransition), which is the real limit behind the CLAUDE.md claim that the RTL sweep is 'jest-proven in both directions'. Any drift between the stub's shape and the real RN API is invisible until a device sees it - the same failure class as the backend wrong-shape mocks.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. The react-native wholesale substitution is at jest.config.js:18, not 31 (31-32 is the ssl-pinning shim) — line corrected. Mock is 143 lines with Platform.OS hardcoded 'ios' (:70), Dimensions pinned to 390x844 (:72-75), I18nManager.isRTL false (:87). Only two test files ever supply a non-ios Platform, both playInstallReferrerService, so ~15 of 17 Platform branches (incl. authService.ts:630 Apple-Sign-In availability) are iOS-only in the suite CI blocks on. Minor: 17 hits span 14 files, one of which is a doc comment. Fix (projects matrix + export-contract test) is sound and flag-free.

findings.title: The 5 required status checks are bypassable: branch protection on main has enforce_admins false, strict false and no required review
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Repo-admin settings change, not code: enable `enforce_admins` (so the owner's own pushes are gated), enable `strict` (require branches up to date before merging), and set required_pull_request_reviews to at least 1 approving review - or, if a solo maintainer cannot self-approve, keep reviews off but turn on enforce_admins + strict, which are the two that actually change the outcome. Then correct the stale prose at ci.yml:107-112, which still describes the pre-#49 state. Record the settings in a test so a silent rollback is visible: no flag involved.
findings.test_first: tests/test_ci_gates.py::test_branch_protection_is_enforced_for_admins - a live_unit-marked node that GETs branches/main/protection and asserts enforce_admins.enabled is true, strict is true, and the 5 contexts are present. Red today on the first two.
findings.impact: Two real holes. (a) enforce_admins=false means the repo admin - who is the only committer here - can push directly to main and none of the 5 required jobs gate that push; the last 5 CI runs on main are all `event: push`, so this is the normal path, and the checks run AFTER the code is already on the branch Railway deploys from. (b) strict=false means a PR can merge while its base is stale, so the green tick belongs to a commit that was never combined with what main now contains - the classic semantic-conflict merge. Combined with no required review, 'all 5 jobs are REQUIRED' (the standing claim in CLAUDE.md and the M22 brief) overstates what actually blocks a bad change from reaching production.

verdict_trail.reason: Branch protection reproduced byte-for-byte: the 5 contexts are required but strict=false, enforce_admins=false and required_pull_request_reviews is absent, so the sole admin's direct pushes to main — the normal path here — reach the Railway deploy branch before any check runs, and a PR can merge on a stale base. ci.yml:107-112 prose is confirmed stale. Severity P2 is right: it weakens a gate rather than causing live harm, and the fix is a settings change plus a pinning test, no flag. Minor overreach: of the last 5 ci.yml runs, 3 are pushes to main and 2 are pull_request runs on doc branches.

findings.title: Re-engagement reads two more columns Postgres does not have, and both are mocked into existence by the tests that cover them
findings.dedupe: new (same defect CLASS as #65/the referral response_data breakage, different call sites; the failure-visibility half overlaps known:#80 still-open)
findings.fix: Same schema-manifest gate as finding 02: validate every column named in a `.select()` string against the applied schema at test time so a phantom name fails at commit. For the product side, either add the two columns in a migration (with an owner deciding whether sentiment_score belongs on product_reviews at all) or rewrite the two queries against columns that exist - and make the failure loud: replace the bare `logger.warning` swallow with a Sentry capture, which is #80's ask, so a flipped flag reports the real reason rather than an empty result. Do this BEFORE any ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES canary; it is a hard precondition, exactly like #128 is for ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE.
findings.test_first: tests/test_reengagement_internals.py::test_sentiment_select_names_only_real_columns and tests/test_cron_reengagement.py::test_eligible_user_select_names_only_real_columns - assert every column in the two `.select()` strings appears in the schema manifest derived from migrations/*.sql. Both RED today (sentiment_score, governorate).
findings.impact: DARK FLAG - `ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES=false` on BOTH Railway services (web and price-warmer), so this cannot harm a user today and is capped at P2 for that reason. But it means the re-engagement feature is pre-broken behind the flag in a way its own test suite cannot see: `_get_eligible_users` returns [] for every run (one phantom column kills the whole SELECT), so the cron would send zero pushes, and `_compute_current_sentiment` returns None for every product, so the decision_insight detector never fires. Anyone flipping the flag as a canary would read 'no pushes sent' as 'no users qualified' rather than 'the query 42703s', because both look identical from outside - and #80 (cron failure visibility) is exactly the missing signal.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced exactly. Both phantom columns confirmed live (42703). Prod flag ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES=false on web, and the only caller is scripts/cron_reengagement.py gated on that flag, so P2 cap is right. Genuinely new: 0 hits for 'governorate'/'sentiment_score' in the M18 verified JSON and M13 review. Evidence is understated if anything - product_reviews also lacks product_id and created_at (hint: 'product_key'), so all three columns in that select are phantom. Covering-test lines 83 and 224 quoted verbatim. Fix (schema manifest + Sentry, before any canary) is correct and flag-safe.

findings.title: The frontend gate measures no coverage at all: jest.config.js has no coverageThreshold and CI never passes --coverage, while the backend carries an 83% floor
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add `--coverage` to the CI jest invocation and print the summary, then ratchet the same way .github/black-clean-paths.txt works: land it reporting-only for one run to MEASURE the number, then set `coverageThreshold.global` in jest.config.js a couple of points below the measurement and raise it as it grows. Do not guess a threshold before the first measurement - that is the exact mistake the backend floor's own comment block documents (placeholder 60 vs measured 78). No app flag.
findings.test_first: tests/test_ci_gates.py::test_frontend_tests_measure_and_floor_coverage - the mirror of the existing backend node: assert the frontend-tests job's jest step passes --coverage and that jest.config.js declares a non-zero coverageThreshold.global. Red today.
findings.impact: The frontend half of the product - 2320 tests, 242 suites, and the screens that carry the M21 mobile fixes - has no measured coverage number and no floor, so a PR can delete every test for a screen and the blocking `frontend-tests` job stays green as long as what remains passes. Nobody can say today what fraction of SmartCompareApp/src is exercised. The asymmetry also makes the repo's coverage story misleading: '85.84%' is a backend-only number that reads as if it described the codebase.

verdict_trail.reason: Read jest.config.js in full: no collectCoverage/coverageThreshold/coverageReporters key. package.json scripts are exactly `"test":"jest"` and `"test:ci":"jest --ci"`; ci.yml:264 is `cd SmartCompareApp && npx jest --ci` with no --coverage; no coverage flag anywhere in the frontend-tests job. Backend contrast at ci.yml:103 confirmed. test_ci_gates.py has 30 test functions including test_backend_tests_measure_and_floor_coverage and no frontend counterpart. Only correction: the file is 54 lines, not the 60 claimed. Fix (measure-then-ratchet, no app flag) is sound.

findings.title: The coverage floor was never re-ratcheted: 83 against a measured 85.84 leaves ~685 statements of app/ that can go untested and still merge green
findings.dedupe: known:M13/#49 (the floor is documented in ci.yml) - status still-open, with the fresh 85.84 measurement and the observation that its stated trigger cannot fire
findings.fix: Decouple the ratchet from #89, which is the wrong trigger: the 11 baseline nodes are DESELECTED, so fixing them cannot move the CI percentage that the floor is set against. Raise the floor to 85 now (0.84 points of margin below the measured 85.84, the same one-point convention the file already uses) in the same PR that prunes the two green baseline rows from finding 03, and add a note that the floor is re-read from the last green main run rather than from #89.
findings.test_first: Extend tests/test_ci_gates.py::test_backend_tests_measure_and_floor_coverage with an assertion that the floor is >= 85, so lowering it silently fails. Red today (83).
findings.impact: 24124 statements at 85.84% = 3416 missed. At an 83% floor, 4101 may be missed - 685 statements of app/ could lose all coverage in one PR and the blocking job would still pass. That is roughly the size of a whole service module (usage_service.py is 279 statements, fact_check_service.py 263). The slack is deliberate and documented, so this is a P3 status item rather than a defect - but the stated trigger ('when the #89 failures are fixed') has not arrived and will not while #89 sits at 9 real red nodes, so in practice the ratchet has no schedule.

verdict_trail.reason: Floor and history confirmed at ci.yml:103 and ci.yml:63-67. Pulled the real backend-tests job log for run 33651445359 (headSha 76ace90) and both numbers match. Arithmetic recomputed independently: 24124-3416=20708 -> 85.8398%; 24124*0.17=4101 allowed missed; 4101-3416=685 slack; usage_service.py 279 statements and fact_check_service.py 263 both verified in the same log. One flaw in the FIX rationale, not the finding: fixing the 11 deselected nodes would re-include them and could move coverage, so 'cannot move the CI percentage' is wrong - the recommendation to raise the floor to 85 still stands and is CI-only, flag-safe.

findings.title: The blocking black gate covers 7 substantive files of 734 (0.95%), the ratchet rule was skipped for 23 of 25 new files, and the workflow's own drift number is stale
findings.dedupe: new (the allowlist mechanism is known from M13/#49; the ratchet violation, the 7-substantive-files count and the stale echo are measured fresh)
findings.fix: Enforce the ratchet mechanically instead of by prose: add a test that every .py file added since a pinned reference commit either appears in .github/black-clean-paths.txt or is black-clean, so a new dirty file fails at PR time and the allowlist can only grow. Refresh the ci.yml:159 echo to '715 of 734 (2026-09-05)' - or better, delete the hard-coded numbers from the echo entirely and let the step's own output be the record, since a literal in a shell echo will always go stale.
findings.test_first: tests/test_ci_gates.py::test_new_python_files_are_black_clean_or_allowlisted - for every path in `git diff --name-status <ref> HEAD -- '*.py' | grep ^A`, assert it is in the allowlist or `black --check` clean. Red today on 23 files.
findings.impact: The BLOCKING half of backend-lint gates 0.95% of the tree and one app/ module, so 'black is enforced' means almost nothing for the code that actually ships - a formatting change to price_service.py or scoring_service.py cannot fail it. The ratchet is not ratcheting: 23 of 25 files added in the M21 window went in dirty, which is why the drift number grew rather than shrank (701/719 -> 715/734). And the number printed on every run is 14 files stale, so the one visible signal the reporting step exists to provide is wrong.

verdict_trail.reason: Every measurement reproduced except the headline count. Allowlist = 18 non-comment entries; os.path.getsize gives TEN 0-byte __init__.py, leaving EIGHT substantive files (1 app/ module + 7 under tests/), not 11/7 - so 1.09%, not 0.95%. Title corrected. The rest holds exactly: black==26.5.1 (matching the pin) over a git-archive of 76ace90 gives 715/19 of 734; 25 new .py since 593ec1e, 23 not in the allowlist and all 23 black-dirty; allowlist grew 16->18. ci.yml:159 echo '701 of 719' is 14 stale. Fix (mechanical ratchet test, drop the literal) is correct.

findings.title: The value_math blanket xfail still grants amnesty to 35 nodes, and its expiry gate cannot fire on a partial A.6.x landing (only 2 of 6 symbols exist)
findings.dedupe: known:M13/#49 still-open (the 35 stubs and the xfail containment are documented); the partial-landing hole in the expiry gate and the 2-of-6 measurement are new
findings.fix: Tighten the expiry from all-six to any-one: make test_value_math_xfail_expires_when_a6x_ships fail as soon as ANY A6X symbol exists whose nodes are not individually excluded from the mark - or, cheaper and better, split tests/test_value_math.py into the ~11 nodes that assert already-shipped VALUE_FORMULA_BY_PRIORITY/_compute_value_score behaviour (no mark, real coverage, fix or adjust the pre-v1.1 coefficient assertions) and the ~24 that assert genuinely absent symbols (keep the mark, or narrow it with raises=(ImportError, AttributeError) now that the AssertionError group has been separated out - the file's own 'WHY THERE IS NO raises= NARROWING' note says the only obstacle was those 11 mixed-in nodes).
findings.test_first: tests/test_ci_gates.py::test_value_math_xfail_expires_when_any_a6x_symbol_ships - assert `_missing_a6x_symbols()` has length 6 (nothing landed) rather than merely being non-empty. Red today (4 missing, 2 present).
findings.impact: 35 test nodes are structurally incapable of failing. Two of the six symbols the amnesty is scoped to ALREADY EXIST (VALUE_FORMULA_BY_PRIORITY with pre-v1.1 coefficients, _compute_value_score), so the nodes that assert their behaviour are already covering SHIPPED code under a strict=False marker - a buggy change to either sits behind the marker with no signal. The expiry gate is all-or-nothing: it only reddens when ALL SIX exist, so a partial A.6.x landing (say the two response_builder helpers, or the two classifiers) extends the blanket amnesty over freshly-shipped code indefinitely. The file's own scope note ('do NOT add a test to this file that is expected to PASS today') is prose, unenforced. This is the documented design, so it is a status report - but the partial-landing hole is a real gap in the bound.

verdict_trail.reason: All four legs reproduce. pytestmark spans lines 63-69 with strict=False at :68; pytest --collect-only on the file gives exactly 35 nodes; the CI log for 76ace90 reports '37 xfailed' with zero XPASS occurrences in the whole log; importing at HEAD gives VALUE_FORMULA_BY_PRIORITY True, _compute_value_score True and the other four False. The partial-landing hole is real: _missing_a6x_symbols() at test_ci_gates.py:140-148 only asserts `missing` is non-empty (line 176), so any 1-of-6 shortfall keeps the amnesty. The split-the-file fix is correct and touches no app flag.

findings.title: P3 sweep: four smaller test/CI-truth defects (real DNS in the blocking job, a stale flaky-exclude, a lock gate that ignores the dev lock, and #128's zero-coverage confirmation)
findings.dedupe: (a),(b),(c) new; (d) known:#128 still-open, with the fresh coverage measurement
findings.fix: (a) monkeypatch `app.utils.url_validator.socket.getaddrinfo` in the test (or move it under live_unit) so the blocking job makes no network call. (b) delete the four dead entries from NETWORK_FLAKY_EXCLUDE and add a comment that entries are added only after an OBSERVED flake with a run link. (c) change lock_drift to accept a sequence of lock files and pass both requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt. (d) wire refund_anon_comparison_credit into the anon failure paths of /text/quick and /image/identify per #128, with the red test below, BEFORE any ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE canary.
findings.test_first: (a) assert the /url/detect test makes zero getaddrinfo calls (patch and count). (b) tests/test_regression_gate_diff.py::test_flaky_exclude_entries_are_still_flaky - assert every id in NETWORK_FLAKY_EXCLUDE still exists and is not live_unit-marked; red on the fifth entry. (c) tests/test_regression_gate_diff.py::test_lock_drift_covers_the_dev_lock - install-mismatch a dev-only pin and assert exit 4. (d) tests/test_anon_usage_refund.py::test_failed_anon_compare_refunds_the_reserved_credit - red today (no caller).
findings.impact: (a) one live-DNS dependency in a job that gates every merge - a runner-side DNS hiccup reddens main for a reason unrelated to the change, which is the flake class the gate exists to avoid. (b) the local regression gate reports 'no regression' for 4 nodes it never looks at, so a dev's green gate is 4 nodes narrower than CI's. (c) a dev on a drifting pytest can get a green certification the exit-4 guard was built to refuse - the guard's own docstring names framework-shape drift as the reason it exists. (d) hard precondition for ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE with no red test behind it.

verdict_trail.reason: (a) Proved, not inferred: with uv.socket.getaddrinfo patched to raise gaierror, POST /api/v1/url/detect returns 400 with one recorded call for 'amazon.ae', so the unmarked test's assert 200 is a live-DNS dependency in the blocking job; it PASSED in the 76ace90 CI run. (c) lock_drift is called once, bare, at line 286 - only requirements.txt. (d) refund_anon_comparison_credit has exactly two mentions in app/ (docstring :52, def :129) and zero in tests/; body line 135 is in the CI Missing list. (b) is right in substance but miscounted: the set holds FOUR entries total, not four plus a fifth - 3 CI-gated nodes are blinded locally and the rate_limiting entry is dead. Hooks note verified (core.hooksPath=.githooks).

findings.title: slowapi keys decorated limits on the CONCRETE request path, so rotating a path parameter fully bypasses the limit on 7 routes
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Pin the bucket to the ROUTE, not the URL. Cheapest correct change: build the Limiter with `key_style="endpoint"` (rate_limiter.py:125-129) so _endpoint_key becomes `<module>.<func>` — this is exactly the identifier the repo's own tests already assert on (`'app.api.history_routes.get_comparison' in limiter._route_limits`, tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py:76), so the two representations stop drifting. Verify at the PINNED slowapi 0.1.10 before shipping (local is 0.1.9). If key_style must stay 'url', pass an explicit `scope=` to each of the 7 decorators instead (e.g. @limiter.limit('20/minute', ...) with a constant scope string). This is a pure-code change with no flag, but land it AFTER LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-02's metering, because tightening these buckets while the anchor is still the shared edge IP converts an unbounded route into a deployment-wide one.
findings.test_first: In tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py add `test_share_view_limit_is_per_route_not_per_token`: loop 35 GETs to /api/v1/share/<a DIFFERENT valid-pattern token each iteration> and assert a 429 appears. Today it is 35x200 and the sibling test (:90-96, same token every time) passes — that asymmetry is the whole defect.
findings.impact: 7 of the 61 decorated limits are per-(client-key, concrete-URL) rather than per-route, i.e. no limit at all against a caller that varies the parameter: GET/DELETE /api/v1/comparisons/{comparison_id} (history_routes.py:139/170, 20/min), POST /api/v1/share/{comparison_id} (share_routes.py:21, 10/min), GET /api/v1/share/{token} (share_routes.py:53, 30/min), GET /api/v1/referrals/invite/{share_token} (referral_routes.py:257, 20/min), POST /api/v1/referrals/invite/{share_token}/quiz (referral_routes.py:289, 10/min), GET /api/v1/text/prices/{product} (text_routes.py:760, 20/min). Three are ANONYMOUS (share view, invite resolve, invite quiz, prices) and each does 1-N blocking Supabase/Upstash round-trips on the single event loop, so an unauthenticated caller can drive unbounded request rate at the one loop today. This also falsifies part of the M18 model: those 7 routes are NOT 'one bucket deployment-wide', they are unbounded.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced independently, twice. Synthetic mount: same-id 25 hits = 20x200/5x429, 25 distinct ids = 25x200/0x429. Then against the REAL app.main: /api/v1/share/<same token> x35 = 30x200/5x429, 35 DISTINCT valid tokens = 35x200, 0x429. Exactly 7 parameterised routes exist and all 7 carry a limit (git grep at 76ace90). Genuinely new: M18 LS-ratelimit-01 asserts "slowapi keys each decorated bucket on (key_func result, route scope)" — wrong, it is the concrete URL. Off-lock caveat CLOSED: I unpacked the pinned slowapi 0.1.10 wheel; key_style default "url" and _endpoint_key=request path are identical. Fix is correct, but flag it un-merges KEY-04's shared GET/POST buckets (doubles those budgets).

Reproduced with my own harness at BOTH local slowapi 0.1.9 and the PINNED 0.1.10 wheel (downloaded, path-injected, run): real `from app.middleware.rate_limiter import limiter` + real decorator on /api/v1/share/{token} -> same token x35 = 30x200/5x429; 35 DISTINCT tokens = 35x200/0x429. All 7 parameterised routes carry a limit at HEAD. The proposed fix closes my reproduction: rebuilding the Limiter with key_style='endpoint' turns distinct-token x35 into 30x200/5x429. test_first is exactly the right red test (distinct-token loop asserting a 429) and is red today. Novelty caveat: rate_limiter.py:113 already documents per-URL-path keying for default_limits; the decorated parameterised-route bypass is still unaddressed.

findings.title: GET /text/prices/{product} is unauthenticated, unmetered, and its 20/min bucket is per product string — an unbounded paid 6-region price fan-out
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Three things, in this order, and none needs a flag: (1) put the route behind the same optional-user + usage metering the compare routes use (get_optional_user + check/record usage as at text_routes.py:154), or gate it behind verify_admin_key like its undecorated neighbours DELETE /text/cache (:863) and GET /text/parse (:898) if it has no product consumer — grep the app for a caller first; (2) apply LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01's key_style/scope fix so 20/min actually means 20/min for this route; (3) bound the fan-out (it gathers ALL GCC_REGIONS unconditionally with no per-request region cap, cf. #70/#73). If the route has no shipped consumer, deleting it is strictly better than fixing it.
findings.test_first: tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py: `test_prices_rate_limit_survives_product_rotation` — 25 GETs to /api/v1/text/prices/probe-{i} with _get_price patched to a stub, assert a 429 appears. Pair it with `test_prices_requires_auth_or_admin` asserting 401/403 for an anonymous caller. Note the ONLY existing enforcement test for this route (:31-48) is marked @pytest.mark.live_unit and is therefore deselected in CI, so this route currently has ZERO enforcement coverage on the green path.
findings.impact: One unauthenticated GET per rotated product string = 6 parallel _get_price fan-outs, each of which misses cache, misses the L2 DB, and enters the paid tier cascade (Bright Data ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK=true, Scrape.do ENABLE_SCRAPEDO=true, Firecrawl ENABLE_FIRECRAWL=true per baseline/railway-web-vars.txt) plus curl fetches on the 40-thread executor and Upstash/Supabase reads on the single loop. Rate is unbounded because the 20/min bucket is per concrete /prices/<string>. Today's Serper spend is gated by SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0, but the Bright Data / Scrape.do / Firecrawl legs are NOT gated, and the event-loop + thread-pool amplification is unconditional — this is the single largest hole in the 'mis-keyed limiter accidentally guards the loop' premise the M18 ordering rule rests on.

verdict_trail.reason: Route read at 76ace90: no Depends(get_current_user)/get_optional_user, no usage_service call. Proved LIVE and anonymous with one Gate-0-rejected prod GET (no network cost): HTTP 200 with 6 regional_prices keys, no auth header. 6 GCC regions confirmed; size-aware cache key from brand/name/variant/region/search_query/category means a rotated string always misses L1+L2. Gate 0 is trivially passable (len>=3, starts alpha). Not in M18 (0 hits) or M13. THREE evidence line numbers are WRONG and must be corrected: the fan-out is :8000-8006 not 8180-8182, _get_price is :5460 not 5587, cache key :5493 not 5620. Caveat: I did not prove the Bright Data/Scrape.do/Firecrawl legs fire with SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0; the non-Serper shopify_gcc/catalog page-scrape channels do issue outbound curl per region, so outbound amplification is proven, paid spend is plausible not measured.

Reproduced through the REAL router (app.api.text_routes mounted with the real limiter, get_regional_prices stubbed): 25 GETs to /prices/probe-NNN = 25x200 with the handler reached 25/25 and zero 429s; the same product x25 = 20x200/5x429. FastAPI reports the route's dependencies as NONE (no auth), the body contains no usage_service call, and get_regional_prices gathers all 6 GCC_REGIONS. Three evidence line numbers in the record are wrong: fan-out is scs:8005-8009 (`for region` at :8006), _get_price :5460, cache key :5493. Fix (auth/meter + KEY-01 keying + fan-out cap) closes my reproduction; test_first is right, and its auth companion is the more valuable half. Paid-leg spend stays modelled; loop/thread amplification is proven.

findings.title: The limiter anchor is NOT one IP: production audit rows show 10 distinct Railway edge peers in 100.64.0.0/10, so the 'one bucket, ~5 concurrent compares' guard is ~N-fold looser than modelled
findings.dedupe: known:M18 LS-ratelimit-01 + LS-railway-metrics-01 (both P1) — still-open, and REFINED by the first live measurement of the anchor; the 'ONE bucket' phrasing in both is wrong in the direction of over-constraint
findings.fix: Do not treat the current limiter as a capacity guard in any activation plan; state the ceiling as a range ((paths x limit) x [1..N_peers]) and get a real bound from the offload work (#71/#73) and a concurrency semaphore on the compare pipeline instead. Then use the measured 100.64.0.0/10 as the trusted-hop allow-list for the #114 fix. Before relying on the count, re-measure it after real traffic resumes: the 24 real rows are all from 2026-04/05 and are a lower bound (only 5 auth sites ever write an IP).
findings.test_first: No unit test pins a live topology fact. The pinning artifact is an assertion in the activation runbook plus a startup log line: log `client_host=<request.client.host> xff=<raw X-Forwarded-For>` once per N requests behind a DEBUG flag (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09), then assert in the runbook that the observed client_host set is a subset of 100.64.0.0/10 before flipping any anchor flag.
findings.impact: Two corrections to the standing load model, both load-bearing. (1) The anchor is CONFIRMED as the Railway edge peer, and the exact CIDR to trust is now MEASURED: 100.64.0.0/10 — the #114 fix no longer needs to guess Railway's topology for the allow-list. (2) The number of buckets equals the number of distinct edge peers a burst lands on, and that is empirically >= 10, not 1. So 'every limit is ONE bucket deployment-wide' overstates the constraint by up to an order of magnitude: the aggregate compare ceiling is (paths x limit) x (distinct concurrent edge peers), and the ORDERING RULE's premise that the mis-keyed limiter bounds concurrent cold compares to ~5 is not safe to lean on. Conversely the DoS lever is undiminished: a caller sharing an edge peer with victims still denies them, and the caller cannot choose its peer, so this is a weaker guard AND an unfair, unattributable one.

verdict_trail.reason: The MEASUREMENT reproduces bit-for-bit (my own paged SELECT: 1439 rows, NULL=719, testclient=696, 24 real values across 10 distinct peers, all in 100.64.0.0/10, all 2026-04/05), and confirming the anchor is request.client.host is real value for #114. But the load-model INFERENCE is over-claimed: 10 distinct peers accumulated over two months of near-zero traffic is not 10 concurrent buckets during a burst, so "the guard is ~N-fold looser" / "aggregate ceiling x [1..N_peers]" is not established by this data. And the content is a refinement of still-open M18 LS-ratelimit-01 / LS-railway-metrics-01 and #114 (held by design), not a new user-reachable defect — P2 per the brief's scale (measurable quality issue), not P1.

findings.title: per_method=False merges GET/POST/DELETE on the same path into one bucket — /url/compare is 10/min for POST+GET combined, /comparisons/{id} is 20/min for GET+DELETE combined
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Decide it explicitly rather than inheriting it. If GET and POST of the same route are meant to be one budget (they are the same work), add a comment saying so at rate_limiter.py:125 and keep per_method=False. If DELETE /comparisons/{id} should not be able to consume the read budget, pass per_method=True on that decorator pair. Either way the number belongs in CLAUDE.md's capacity table, which currently implies one bucket per decorator.
findings.test_first: tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py: `test_get_and_post_compare_share_one_bucket` — alternate POST and GET /api/v1/url/compare and assert the 429 arrives on the 11th combined call, not the 11th of each. That pins whichever semantics are chosen.
findings.impact: Changes the per-route capacity table that any activation plan is built from. Affected pairs at HEAD: POST/GET /api/v1/text/compare (text_routes.py:153/295) share ONE 10/min bucket, not two; POST/GET /api/v1/url/compare (url_routes.py:127/167) share one 10/min; POST/GET /api/v1/url/extract (:69/:106) share one 10/min; POST/GET /api/v1/url/detect (:190/:210) share one 20/min; GET/DELETE /api/v1/comparisons/{id} (history_routes.py:139/170) share one 20/min. The client's documented SSE-to-REST fallback therefore consumes from the SAME bucket as the primary call for the /text/compare path. Merging is conservative (it under-serves rather than over-serves) but it means the compare surface is 3 buckets, not 6, and a user's own retry costs them their next real attempt.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced both experiments independently with the real imported limiter: GET+DELETE interleaved on ONE concrete /comparisons/<id> gave 20x200/4x429 with the first 429 at index 20; POST+GET /url/compare interleaved 12x gave 10x200/2x429 — i.e. one shared bucket, exactly as claimed. per_method=False default verified in the PINNED slowapi 0.1.10 wheel, not just local 0.1.9, so the off-lock caveat is closed. All five method-pairs verified at their exact 76ace90 lines. Not covered by M18. Severity P2 correct: merging under-serves rather than over-serves, so it is a capacity-table/documentation defect, not a security hole.

findings.title: referral_routes docstring claims the 20/min limit stops anonymous hammering — the limit is per share_token, so it does not
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Fix the code (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01) and then rewrite the sentence to say what the limit is keyed on, e.g. 'rate-limited 20/min per (client-key, route) — note the client-key is the shared Railway edge peer until #114 lands, so this is a deployment-wide budget, not per-caller.' Apply the same audit to the other anon parameterised route docstrings (share_routes.py:58 'No auth required.').
findings.test_first: Not a unit test — a docstring assertion cannot be pinned. The correct pin is LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01's rotation test on this exact route: `test_invite_resolve_limit_survives_token_rotation` (25 GETs to /api/v1/referrals/invite/<distinct valid token>?ref=<valid> must produce a 429).
findings.impact: A security control's own documentation asserts a property the code does not have, on an ANONYMOUS route that calls ReferralService.resolve_invite (multiple Supabase reads on the single event loop). Anyone auditing this file — including the M13-28 closeout that wrote the line — reads 'protected' and moves on. This is the M13 theme 'docs-as-wrong-truth' recurring on the exact control it describes. The format validation half of the claim IS true (both params are pattern-constrained); only the rate-limit half is false.

verdict_trail.reason: Docstring read verbatim at 76ace90 and the claim it makes is false in exactly the half the finder says. The route is GET /invite/{share_token} with @limiter.limit('20/minute') and Depends(get_optional_user) — anonymous-reachable — and its bucket is the concrete URL, so rotating share_token (which is only pattern-constrained, not existence-checked before the limiter) removes the limit entirely; I proved that rotation bypass on the structurally identical share route against the real app (35 distinct tokens, 0x429). The format-validation half of the sentence IS true. P2 is right: it is docs-as-wrong-truth on a live anon security control, derivative of KEY-01's root cause rather than an independent defect.

findings.title: The rate-limit test suite is green because every enforcement test hammers a CONSTANT path parameter; the one test that would matter is live_unit-deselected in CI
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add one rotation test per parameterised route (7 tests) asserting a 429 appears when the parameter varies; convert the six membership assertions into behavioural ones by hitting the route N+1 times; and un-live_unit the /text/prices test by patching `StructuredComparisonService._get_price` to a stub instead of letting it resolve a real price (the docstring at :42 already prescribes exactly this: 'Restore coverage by mocking `_get_price`, not by removing the marker'). Once LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01 lands, the rotation tests go green and stay as the regression pin.
findings.test_first: `test_every_parameterised_limit_survives_rotation` — parametrise over the 7 (path-template, sample-params) pairs, hit each 2x its limit with a DIFFERENT parameter each call, assert 429. It fails on all 7 today.
findings.impact: 9 tests assert 'this endpoint is rate limited' and all 9 pass while 7 of the 61 limits are bypassable by varying one path segment. The registration-style tests (`'app.api.history_routes.get_comparison' in limiter._route_limits`) are especially misleading: they assert the endpoint-function key exists while the runtime buckets on the URL — the two representations have silently diverged and the test asserts the one that is not used. Green here has meant nothing about enforcement since the file was written; this is the M13 'green-that-means-nothing' theme on the security surface.

verdict_trail.reason: Every claim checks out. I ran the exact command and got the exact result. test_share_view_rate_limited hammers one constant token 35x; the only /text/prices enforcement test is live_unit-marked and was the single deselected node; the registration tests assert `app.api.history_routes.get_comparison in limiter._route_limits` while the runtime buckets on the URL — the two representations have provably diverged (my real-app rotation run: 35 distinct tokens = 35x200). One factual correction to the evidence text: FOUR membership-only tests exist in TestRateLimitCoverage (history_list/history_get/history_delete/share_create), not six; the class has 9 tests, the file 16. P2 correct.

findings.title: admin_audit_log — the only vantage that records the limiter anchor — is 98% junk: 719 NULL + 696 'testclient' rows, with the test suite writing into the PRODUCTION audit table
findings.dedupe: new (M13-02 identified the shared-proxy-IP attribution defect; the test-harness pollution and the 719 NULLs are new and they are what blocks #114's verification)
findings.fix: Two separable changes. (a) Stop the pollution: the credential-stripping conftest already exists for the free tier — extend it (or a CI guard) so any test that can reach `record_admin_audit`/Supabase with a service key fails loudly unless LIVE=1 AND the URL is not the prod project; then purge the 696 'testclient' rows in a one-off migration. (b) Make the anchor observable: have audit_client_ip also record the raw X-Forwarded-For alongside the peer (a new nullable `forwarded_for` column, or inside the existing `details` JSON) so the hop count becomes readable from data the app already writes, with no new endpoint and no live-egress requirement. Both are prerequisites for closing #114, not follow-ups.
findings.test_first: `test_audit_writes_are_blocked_without_live_flag` in tests/conftest-adjacent coverage: assert that calling the auth audit path under the free-tier fixture raises/no-ops rather than reaching a real client. Plus `test_audit_client_ip_records_raw_xff` asserting the recorded row carries both the peer and the unmodified X-Forwarded-For string.
findings.impact: Three consequences. (1) #114 cannot be verified from stored data: there is no genuine client-IP series to inspect, so the hop topology has to be re-measured with new instrumentation (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09). (2) M13-02's stated goal — 'every audit row records the same proxy IP so the abuse-investigation surface cannot attribute anything' — is worse than described: 50% of rows record a test harness and 50% record nothing. Any future abuse investigation over this table is unusable. (3) A test run holding the prod SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY is writing rows into a production security-audit table; that is a data-integrity problem independent of rate limiting (696 of 1439 rows, ~48%).

verdict_trail.reason: Numbers reproduce exactly, but two load-bearing claims fail. (a) The present-tense 'test suite writing into the PRODUCTION audit table' is fixed: tests/_env_safety.py neutralize_credentials landed in e543eae 2026-08-25T18:10+03:00 (=15:10Z); the newest 'testclient' row is 14:01:05Z and the newest NULL 14:07:26Z — every polluting row predates the guard and none exist after. (b) The 719 NULLs are not 'nothing recorded' junk: audit_service.log_content_blocked passes no ip/user/endpoint by privacy design, and 718 of 719 NULLs are content_blocked. Real-defect residue is historical data hygiene only.

findings.title: 429s carry no Retry-After and no X-RateLimit headers, and the client only branches on USAGE_LIMIT — a shared-bucket 429 reaches users as an unexplained generic failure
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Set headers_enabled=True on the Limiter (rate_limiter.py:125-129) so every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset and 429s carry Retry-After, and propagate Retry-After through rate_limit_handler (error_handler.py:123-128, which currently drops all headers). Then add a RATE_LIMITED branch to api.ts alongside the USAGE_LIMIT one (:146 and :250) that surfaces a 'busy, retry in Ns' state and suppresses the automatic retry. Ship the client half on the next `eas update --branch preview` — note phones today run the 97b5f15 bundle, so the backend header is inert on-device until that OTA.
findings.test_first: Backend: `test_rate_limited_response_carries_retry_after` — drive one decorated route past its limit and assert the 429 has a Retry-After header and code=='RATE_LIMITED'. Client: a jest test on the api.ts interceptor asserting a 429 with code 'RATE_LIMITED' produces a distinct typed error (not the generic one) and does not trigger the retry path.
findings.impact: This is the user-visible face of the shared-bucket defect. When another caller exhausts a global bucket, the victim gets an untyped failure with no retry hint: the client cannot back off (no Retry-After to read, and slowapi would supply one only with headers_enabled=True), cannot distinguish 'you hit your quota' (USAGE_LIMIT, which routes to the paywall) from 'the deployment is rate-limited' (RATE_LIMITED, which should say 'try again in N seconds'), and will happily retry immediately — amplifying the burst that caused the 429. It also blinds the operator: with no X-RateLimit-Remaining on the wire and no client IP in Railway HTTP logs, there is no signal that a bucket is saturating until users complain.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced end-to-end. Limiter at rate_limiter.py:125-129 passes no headers_enabled; the default is False at BOTH the installed 0.1.9 and the PINNED slowapi 0.1.10 (checked the downloaded wheel, so this claim is on-lock). error_handler.py:122-128 -> _build_error_response (:41-52) constructs JSONResponse with content only, no headers. A driven 429 carried only content-length/content-type. api.ts:146-152 and :250-258 branch on 429 solely for USAGE_LIMIT. One sub-claim is wrong and does not change the verdict: the axios interceptor does NOT auto-retry a 429 (api.ts:155-156 retries only 401), so 'will happily retry immediately' is unsupported. P2 stands: decorated limits are live without any flag, but prod traffic is ~16 req/24h so nobody is hitting a 429 today.

findings.title: #114 status: leftmost-XFF anchor is a TOTAL bypass (measured 40/40 pass while rotating the header) — correctly HELD, and here is the exact live verification that unblocks it
findings.dedupe: known:#114 (and M13-02 / M18 LS-ratelimit-01 / CLAUDE.md:347) — still-open, HELD BY DESIGN; new here are the measured 40/40 bypass, the measured trust CIDR, and a verification procedure that needs no live egress guessing
findings.fix: EXACT LIVE VERIFICATION PROCEDURE for #114, all read-only and all now cheap because the target CIDR is measured (100.64.0.0/10, LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-03). Step 1 — instrument: behind a new default-OFF flag LOG_PROXY_ANCHOR, log one line per request (or 1-in-N) from a place that sees the raw ASGI scope: `anchor peer=%s xff=%r fwd=%r host=%s` with peer=request.client.host, xff=request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for'), fwd=request.headers.get('forwarded'), host=request.headers.get('host'). Put it in RequestIDMiddleware (app/middleware/request_id.py:10-14), which is the OUTERMOST middleware and therefore sees the scope before anything rewrites it. Step 2 — vantage: hit prod from TWO known-distinct public IPs (a phone on cellular and the dev box), each sending NO XFF, then each sending a forged 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4'. A handful of requests, not a burst. Step 3 — read the deploy logs for those request_ids (Railway HTTP logs do NOT carry IPs or headers — measured, they are `METHOD PATH STATUS Nms` only — so the app must log it; note deploy logs are retained per-deployment and older deployments are purged, so read them the same day). Step 4 — decide from the data: (a) `peer` must be inside 100.64.0.0/10 for every request, confirming the trust anchor; (b) count the commas in the received `xff` for the no-forgery case — that count IS the hop count, and the real client is at index -(hops trusted); (c) in the forged case, confirm the edge APPENDED the real peer to the RIGHT of '1.2.3.4' — if it did, leftmost is proven attacker-controlled in prod and rightmost-after-trusted is the correct anchor; if the edge REPLACED the header, the leftmost reader is safe and #114 can close as written. Step 5 — implement the winner: prefer `--forwarded-allow-ips=100.64.0.0/10` on the uvicorn start command (railway.json:7) with NO app change, but see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-11 first — uvicorn's CIDR support is version-dependent and `--proxy-headers` is already on by default, so the flag that actually matters is forwarded-allow-ips. Until steps 1-4 produce data, #114 stays HELD BY DESIGN.
findings.test_first: `test_leftmost_xff_is_not_the_key_when_a_trusted_hop_appended` — construct a request with 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 203.0.113.9' and assert _rate_limit_key returns 203.0.113.9 (the hop the trusted edge appended), not 1.2.3.4. It fails today. Note tests/test_m13_02_proxy_aware_ratelimit.py:48 `test_flag_on_two_xff_two_keys` currently ASSERTS the broken behaviour, so that test must be inverted as part of the fix.
findings.impact: Confirms the hold is correct and quantifies it: flipping ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT as written does not merely weaken the limiter, it removes it — every decorated limit becomes unenforceable by any client willing to send a header, AND admin_audit_log.ip_address (auth_routes.py:437/465/488/506/644, same helper) becomes fully attacker-authored, which is worse than today's useless-but-honest edge IP. Meanwhile the flag is the only thing standing between the deployment and per-client keys, so it also blocks #72 and the whole capacity story.

verdict_trail.reason: The mechanism and the 40/40 measurement reproduce exactly, and #114 is confirmed still open and correctly held. Severity drops to P2 per the brief's dark-flag rule: ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT is absent from the Railway `web` variable set, so _leftmost_xff_ip is unreachable in prod — the harm only exists if the flag is flipped. Supporting details also check out: RequestIDMiddleware is added last in main.py (:160) hence outermost, so it is the right instrumentation point; tests/test_m13_02_proxy_aware_ratelimit.py:48 test_flag_on_two_xff_two_keys does assert the leftmost behaviour and would have to be inverted; and the 100.64.0.0/10 anchor is independently corroborated by the 24 real audit rows, all 100.64.0.x.

findings.title: memory:// storage status: still the only backend, still per-process and restart-wiped, and the redis client needed to fix it is already a pinned dependency
findings.dedupe: known:M18 LS-ratelimit-03 (P2) + LS-railway-metrics-04 (P2) + #72 — still-open, unchanged at HEAD; new here is the concrete wiring (RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI + rediss:// + in_memory_fallback) and that redis is already pinned
findings.fix: Add a dedicated storage URI env rather than reusing UPSTASH_REDIS_URL (which is the https REST endpoint): read `RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI` in _get_storage_uri and fall back to 'memory://' when unset, so the default stays byte-identical. Populate it with the Upstash TLS endpoint (rediss://default:<token>@<host>:6379) — Upstash serves both REST and native TLS Redis on the same database, so no new vendor is needed and redis==8.1.0 is already installed. Also set in_memory_fallback=[ANON_LIMIT] and in_memory_fallback_enabled=True in the Limiter constructor at the same time: today swallow_errors=False and the fallback is disabled, so once storage is remote a Redis blip turns every limited request into a 500 rather than degrading. Measure the Upstash RTT from Railway before flipping — the limiter adds one storage round-trip to EVERY request on 61 routes and that RTT has never been measured (M18 gap).
findings.test_first: `test_storage_uri_honours_env_and_defaults_to_memory` — assert _get_storage_uri() returns 'memory://' with the env unset and the exact env value when set. Plus `test_limiter_falls_back_when_storage_raises` — patch the storage to raise and assert the request is served (fallback) rather than 500ing.
findings.impact: Unchanged since M18 and it is the gating step for everything else in the safe order. Consequences: (a) every Railway deploy, crash or OOM restart resets all buckets to zero, so a redeploy is a free reset of the register/login/account-delete brute-force counters (railway.json sets restartPolicyMaxRetries 3); (b) adding a second uvicorn worker or a second replica — the obvious first response to the single-loop ceiling — silently MULTIPLIES every limit by the worker count, so the capacity fix and the security control fight each other; (c) per-user keys (#72) are pointless without shared storage, because a user's budget would be per-process. The blocking reason given in the comment is real but narrow: the code only knows the REST URL. cache_service.py:23-37 already branches on https:// vs redis://, so the codebase already understands both shapes.

verdict_trail.reason: Every element verified at HEAD and at runtime. _get_storage_uri (rate_limiter.py:103-110) has no Redis branch and no env override; the constructed limiter's storage is limits.storage.memory.MemoryStorage. The fix's premises also hold: swallow_errors=False and the in-memory fallback is empty/disabled, so a remote-storage blip would 500 rather than degrade; redis==8.1.0 and limits==5.8.0 are pinned at requirements.txt:136 and :91; cache_service.py already branches https:// vs redis://. This is what actually ships (no flag gates it), so P2 is right — it is a capacity/robustness ceiling, not live user harm at ~0 traffic. Minor: 63 @limiter.limit decorators in app/, not 61.

findings.title: The prescribed fix is partly a no-op: uvicorn already runs proxy_headers=True, and at uvicorn 0.30 --forwarded-allow-ips does exact-string matching with no CIDR support
findings.dedupe: new (corrects the fix prescribed by known:M13-02, M18 LS-ratelimit-01 and CLAUDE.md:347 — the mechanism they describe is right, the remedy they name is half no-op and half footgun)
findings.fix: Before touching railway.json:7, determine the pinned version's actual semantics: in the Railway shell or a container built from requirements.txt, run `python -c "import uvicorn,inspect;from uvicorn.middleware.proxy_headers import ProxyHeadersMiddleware;print(uvicorn.__version__);print(inspect.getsource(ProxyHeadersMiddleware))"` and read whether trusted_hosts parses networks. If 0.52.4 supports CIDR, set the start command to `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT --forwarded-allow-ips=100.64.0.0/10` (drop --proxy-headers, it is redundant) and NEVER '*'. If it does not, enumerate the observed peers as an explicit comma list, or skip the server layer entirely and do the anchor in _rate_limit_key as rightmost-after-trusted. Either way land it with LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09's logging so the change is observable rather than assumed.
findings.test_first: `test_uvicorn_trusted_hosts_parses_the_configured_cidr` — a version-pinning test that constructs ProxyHeadersMiddleware(app, trusted_hosts='100.64.0.0/10') and asserts a request whose peer is 100.64.0.7 is trusted. It is the cheapest guard against the silent-no-op deploy and it will fail loudly if a uvicorn bump changes the semantics.
findings.impact: Every prior write-up of this fix (M13-02's 'Run uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips', M18 LS-ratelimit-01's fix field, CLAUDE.md:347, the M18 W4 lane) prescribes `--proxy-headers` as if it were the missing switch. It is already on. The only switch that matters is --forwarded-allow-ips, and it has two traps that would make a 'fix' silently do nothing while looking shipped: (1) at 0.30-era semantics, passing the measured CIDR `100.64.0.0/10` puts the literal string in a set and matches no peer, so XFF stays discarded and the limiter stays mis-keyed — a green deploy with zero behaviour change; (2) passing `--forwarded-allow-ips='*'` takes the always_trust branch, which returns `x_forwarded_for_hosts[0]` — the LEFTMOST, client-controlled hop — reintroducing exactly the bypass #114 is held for, at the server layer instead of the app layer.

verdict_trail.reason: Half refuted, and the refuted half is the headline. I downloaded the PINNED uvicorn 0.52.4 wheel: ProxyHeadersMiddleware was rewritten around a _TrustedHosts class that explicitly parses networks via ipaddress.ip_network and tests membership with 'ip in net', so passing 100.64.0.0/10 is NOT a silent no-op at the version that ships — trap (1) is false in prod and only true of the local off-lock 0.30.0 build the finder read. Trap (2) survives at 0.52.4: always_trust returns _parse_host_port(x_forwarded_for_hosts[0]), i.e. the leftmost client-supplied hop. The 'proxy_headers already True' correction of M13-02/CLAUDE.md:347 also survives. Nothing is live (railway.json:7 passes neither flag), so P3.

findings.title: Safe order of change, restated with the measured evidence: three of the four prerequisites are now cheap, and step 0 is a metering fix that cannot wait for them
findings.dedupe: known:M18 ordering rule (offloads before limiter key) — still-open and RESTATED with measured evidence; the new content is step 0 and the demotion of the limiter from 'the guard' to 'a leaky guard'
findings.fix: SAFE ORDER at HEAD 76ace90. STEP 0 (do NOW, does not wait on anything): meter or gate GET /text/prices/{product} (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-02) and fix the URL-vs-route bucket key (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01) — these CLOSE holes in the current guard, they do not widen it, so the 'offloads first' constraint does not apply; and add the anchor logging from LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09 plus the audit-table hygiene fix from LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-07, which are read-only instrumentation. STEP 1: offload flags ACTIVE and canaried (#71/#73 — the four W3 flags measured absent, so every hot-path Supabase/Upstash round-trip is still inline on the single loop); nothing that raises effective request throughput may precede this. STEP 2: Redis-backed limiter storage (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-10 — RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI + rediss:// + in_memory_fallback), because both a second worker and per-user keys are meaningless while buckets are per-process and restart-wiped; measure Upstash RTT from Railway first, since this adds a round-trip to all 61 routes. STEP 3: verified per-client anchor — run LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09's procedure, then apply the winner via --forwarded-allow-ips=100.64.0.0/10 (checking LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-11's version trap) or rightmost-after-trusted in _rate_limit_key; this is the step that closes #114 and it is the first step that CHANGES who shares a bucket, so it must not precede STEP 1. STEP 4: per-user keys for authed routes (#72) — only meaningful after STEP 2 (shared storage) and STEP 3 (a real client anchor); key on user_id where present, falling back to the verified IP. STEP 5: ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS, and only now, because the blanket 10/min on /health and the app-open reads is survivable ONLY with a per-client key (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-13). STEP 6: raise the limits, using headers (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-08) to observe saturation rather than guessing. Do not reorder 3 before 1, and do not treat step 0 as blocked by step 1.
findings.test_first: A CI guard, not a unit test: `test_activation_preconditions_are_documented_and_ordered` reading the flag matrix from CLAUDE.md and asserting ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS cannot be enabled in a config where ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT is off — i.e. make _default_rate_limits_enabled() return False (with a loud log) unless the anchor flag is also on, so the documented precondition is enforced by code instead of by a comment.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /url/* routes do a blocking socket.getaddrinfo on the event loop per user-supplied URL - measured 11s freeze of the whole deployment per unresolvable host
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to mobile-checkup lead 'POST /url/compare unmetered+no history' and to #114's limiter key, but neither names the on-loop resolver; url_validator.py is in no prior review's file list)
findings.fix: Move the resolution off the loop and bound it: make `validate_external_url` an `async def` that does `await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(hostname, None), timeout=2.0)` (the loop's own getaddrinfo already runs in the executor), returning False on TimeoutError/gaierror - and update the 8 call sites in url_routes.py / url_extraction_service.py / price_service.py / shopify_pdp_service.py to await it. Keep a thin sync shim for the warmer/CLI paths. No flag needed: the change is strictly a tighten (a hostname that cannot resolve in 2 s was already going to fail the fetch), but if a flag is wanted, gate the 2 s ceiling behind ENABLE_SSRF_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT and leave the offload unconditional. Ship BEFORE any /url/* traffic and before the #114 limiter re-key, since re-keying raises the per-caller ceiling on this path.
findings.test_first: tests/test_url_validator_offloop.py: monkeypatch socket.getaddrinfo to `lambda *a, **k: time.sleep(3) or []`, then in an asyncio test start a background `asyncio.sleep(0)` heartbeat task that stamps time.monotonic() every 10 ms, call the /url/compare handler via httpx.ASGITransport with a bogus host, and assert the heartbeat gap never exceeds 200 ms. RED today (gap == 3 s x2).
findings.impact: Whole-deployment availability. One anonymous HTTP request with two hostnames whose nameservers black-hole freezes the single uvicorn event loop for the full resolver timeout (measured 11 s/host on the dev resolver; glibc default RES_TIMEOUT=5 x RES_DFLRETRY=2 = ~10 s/nameserver on Railway, MODELLED). During the freeze NOTHING else runs - not other users' compares, not /auth/*, not /health. railway.json's healthcheck (30 s) is served by the same loop, so ~3 such requests in flight fail the healthcheck and Railway restarts the only replica (ON_FAILURE, max 3 retries). The route's slowapi limit is 10/min but keyed on the shared Railway edge IP (#114), i.e. 10/min DEPLOYMENT-WIDE - 10 requests x 22 s = 220 s of loop block per 60 s window, a permanent wedge from a single caller. Non-adversarially, any DNS hiccup or a user pasting a dead retailer URL costs every concurrent user 11-22 s of added latency, which the 15 s price race and 30 s STREAM_HARD_CAP convert into TIMEOUTs for unrelated requests.

verdict_trail.reason: Code matches exactly at 76ace90; I reproduced 12418/11278 ms (no negative caching) through the real module and confirmed the function is not a coroutine, so every call site is a plain sync call inside `async def`. Live in prod unauthenticated (GET /api/v1/url/detect -> 200). Genuinely new: M13-86 only patches getaddrinfo in tests; mobile-checkup #6 is metering/history; no prior row names the on-loop resolver. Corrections: prefix is /api/v1/url/*, the extraction function is `fetch_page` not `fetch_page_html`, 11 call sites not 8, and the healthcheck-restart amplification is UNPROVEN (Railway healthcheckPath gates a new deploy; ON_FAILURE fires on process exit, not on post-deploy health polling). Understated, not overstated: the same blocking call is on the real price path.

I tried to break it and could not. I built the repro the brief asks for (scratchpad/m22-review/verify2/repro_v2.py: real `app.main:app` over httpx.ASGITransport, a 10 ms asyncio heartbeat measuring max loop gap, socket.getaddrinfo stubbed to sleep 3 s then raise gaierror) and it goes RED at 76ace90 — and at current repo HEAD 7dd04c1, since `git diff --stat 76ace90..HEAD -- app/utils/url_validator.py app/api/url_routes.py` is EMPTY. The decisive measurement is not the wall time (which a caller could dismiss as "his own request is slow") but case C: a victim `GET /health` issued while the attacker sits inside getaddrinfo returned 200 after **3004 ms** against a 3000 ms stub — i.e. an unrelated request on the single loop paid the entire resolver cost. `/health` is `async def` (main.py:307-308), so it has no threadpool escape. All 7 /api/v1/url/* routes introspect as `sub_dependencies=0, endpoint_is_async=True`, and unauth GET /api/v1/url/detect returns 200 both locally and in prod. So the structural claim, the unauthenticated reachability and the loop-blocking are all reproduced, not inferred. THREE CORRECTIONS, all narrowing the arithmetic but not the severity. (1) The finder's "calls it TWICE before any work = ~22 s" is WRONG: `if not validate_external_url(url1) or not validate_external_url(url2)` short-circuits, and I measured gai_calls=1 / hosts=['bh1.example'] when url1 is the bad host; 2 calls happen only when url1 resolves successfully first (measured: gai_calls=2, hosts=['ok.example','bh3.example']). Worst case per compare request is ~1x the resolver timeout, so the impact section's "10 x 22 s = 220 s of block per 60 s window" should read ~10 x 10-13 s = 100-130 s — still greater than the 60 s window, so the "permanent wedge from a single caller" conclusion survives unchanged. (2) The 11-12 s magnitude in the finding, and my own 13.50 s / 12.67 s through the real route with the REAL resolver, measure MY BOX, not Railway. I proved this box's resolver is pathological: `curl -w '%{time_namelookup}'` against the already-cached prod hostname gave namelookup 3.34 / 24.86 / 19.45 s (total 10.1 / 57.9 / 24.2 s, code=200 each time). Consequently every prod wall-clock probe I took (detect 32.5 s, 18.5 s, 13.3 s; health 12.9 s) is client-side noise and I discarded it — I can neither confirm nor refute prod-side magnitude from here. Railway-side ~10 s (glibc RES_TIMEOUT 5 x 2) stays MODELLED, and I agree with verifier 1 that the healthcheck-restart chain is UNPROVEN. P0 does not depend on either: the pathological host is fully attacker-supplied and unauthenticated, so the attacker picks the block duration by pointing url1 at a domain whose nameservers black-hole. (3) Line/route facts check out exactly: url_validator.py:30, url_routes.py:91/112/148/175/197/216, limiter keyed by get_remote_address at rate_limiter.py:52-58 with ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT off. DOES THE PROPOSED FIX CLOSE THE REPRO? Yes, measured. I ran the finder's exact proposal (`await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(host, None), timeout=2.0)` returning False on TimeoutError/gaierror) against the same 3 s stub: it returned False at 2.01 s with MAX_LOOP_GAP = **32 ms**, indistinguishable from the 31 ms idle baseline (assert gap <= 200 ms PASSES). So the loop-blocking defect is fully closed by the proposal. Verifier 1's caveat is still worth carrying but is MODELLED, not measured: `wait_for` cancels the await, not the libc call, so the worker thread stays occupied for the full ~10 s, and `loop.getaddrinfo` uses the default executor which main.py:168-171 bounds to 40 (app/utils/executor.py) shared with the ~33 to_thread adapter sites — 40 concurrent bogus URLs could starve that pool. My thread-count probe could NOT demonstrate this (active_count stayed 2 before and after the timeout) because httpx.ASGITransport does not run lifespan, so the bounded executor was never installed in my harness; treat "wait_for alone is sufficient" as unproven and size a dedicated resolver pool. IS test_first THE RIGHT RED TEST? Right shape — it is essentially what I built and it is genuinely red today (3000 ms gap vs a 200 ms assert) — but it has two defects as written. (a) `lambda *a, **k: time.sleep(3) or []` returns `[]`, so the IP loop finds nothing and validate_external_url returns **True**; the handler then falls through into `compare_from_urls` and does real network, making the test slow, network-dependent and flaky. Raise `socket.gaierror` after the sleep instead — the handler then short-circuits to a clean 400 with zero network (my run: status=400, body `{"success":false,"error":"URL blocked by security policy"...}`). (b) Because of the `or` short-circuit, do not assert "gap == 3 s x2"; assert a single max gap, or use url1-resolvable/url2-bogus to actually exercise two resolves. Also warm one request first and keep the threshold at 200 ms — idle heartbeat jitter on Windows measured 16-31 ms.

findings.title: supabase create_client() runs per request and sits OUTSIDE the run_db lambda, so both offload flags leave a 355ms certifi SSL-context build plus a cold connection pool on the event loop
findings.dedupe: new (M18 LS-capacity-math-02's verify_reason notes in passing that the user-scoped client is 'a new create_client per call vs cached admin', but it is not a finding, the auth_service factories are not named, the outside-the-lambda placement is not observed, and the SSL-context cost was never quantified)
findings.fix: Memoize both auth_service factories the way database_service.py:38-45 already memoizes admin: module-level `_auth_client`/`_admin_client` singletons behind a lock, and replace `get_user_supabase_client(token)` with the cached anon client plus a per-call `postgrest.auth(token)` on a request-scoped shallow wrapper (or drop to `get_admin_supabase_client()` + explicit .eq(user_id) filters where RLS is not actually load-bearing). Pass `ClientOptions(postgrest_client_timeout=...)` at the same time (see finding 04). If the risk of sharing a mutated postgrest auth header across concurrent requests is a concern, keep a small keyed pool of anon clients rather than one-per-request. Ship unflagged - the construction is pure setup with no behavioural fork - but land it BEFORE flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD so the flag's measured benefit is not swamped by this.
findings.test_first: tests/test_supabase_client_reuse.py: patch supabase.create_client with a counter, drive GET /auth/me and GET /usage/status through TestClient twice each, assert the counter increments at most once per distinct (url, key) pair for the whole test (currently 2 per request, 8 total).
findings.impact: This is the single largest per-request loop cost that neither offload flag can remove, and it is the one nobody has costed. Even at a conservative Linux/Railway estimate of 20-60 ms per SSL-context load (MODELLED; the 355 ms figure is dev-box Windows), an app-open burst of 4 authed reads costs 7 create_clients = 140-420 ms of pure CPU on the only loop, on top of every RTT M18 already counted; at the dev-box figure it is 2.5 s. Because no client is ever reused or closed, every Supabase call also pays a fresh TCP+TLS handshake instead of keep-alive (measured +390 to +540 ms end-to-end on this box) and leaks an unclosed httpx pool per request until GC. Flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD - the whole point of #115/#116 - therefore buys much less than the flag's docstring claims (db_offload.py:1-8 says it moves 'the REQUEST-PATH HOT SET' off the loop).

verdict_trail.reason: Every cited line is exact at 76ace90 (no diff 76ace90..HEAD in these files). Both factories build a fresh client per call; database_service memoizes only admin; construction sits outside the run_db lambda at auth_service:256-257 and home_routes:214. I reproduced the cost independently: 245-416 ms steady-state, 261 of 312 ms inside httpx create_ssl_context. Prod sets NEITHER offload flag, so the blocking is live today, not dark-flag-gated; every authed request pays it via get_current_user. Genuinely new: M18's only mention is an aside in LS-capacity-math-02's verify note. Modelled arithmetic checks out (7x20-60 = 140-420 ms). Caveat on the fix: sharing one anon client with per-call postgrest.auth() can leak a JWT across concurrent requests, and the admin+".eq" alternative drops RLS - take the keyed-pool branch.

I tried to break the confirmation and could not: the defect manifests in a running reproduction, not just on reading. I drove the REAL `app.main` app through TestClient with BOTH offload flags ON (ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD=true, ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD=true), patching only `auth_service.create_client` / `database_service.create_client` with a counter that probes `asyncio.get_running_loop()` at construction time (succeeds = on the loop thread; would raise inside `asyncio.to_thread`). Every single construction reported on_loop=True, and the per-request counts are HIGHER than the finder measured, not lower: /auth/me 2, /usage/status 2 (1 on the second request), /comparisons/history 3, /home/savings 2 — all ON-LOOP. So `run_db` provably cannot remove this: the call stacks show `get_current_user>verify_token>get_auth_client` and `get_me>get_user_profile>get_admin_client`, i.e. construction outside the lambda. Prod makes it worse, not dark-gated: baseline/railway-web-vars.txt (46 lines) contains zero OFFLOAD entries, so today the RTT is inline on the loop too. Cost: I re-measured independently and PARTLY qualified the finder's attribution — `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())` alone costs 415-950 ms on this box (certifi bundle 270,954 bytes), confirming the certifi CA parse as the real cross-platform driver, but cProfile of one create_client also shows 0.364 s of the 0.618 s in `winreg.QueryValueEx` via `httpx._utils.get_environment_proxies` — a Windows-only proxy-registry read that does NOT exist on Railway. So the dev-box 355 ms headline overstates Linux more than the finder's certifi-only framing implies; his own conservative MODELLED 20-60 ms/Linux figure and the 7x = 140-420 ms burst arithmetic are unaffected and are what the severity rests on. Not enough to downgrade: the defect is the unbounded per-request count and its placement on the only event loop, which is version- and platform-independent, and it is the one cost neither #115/#116 flag can buy back. Does the proposed fix close my reproduction? Yes, the memoization half does, measured: swapping both factories for a `(url, key)`-keyed cache dropped 4 requests from 7 constructions to 2 (both on the first request, 0 thereafter). But only the two `auth_service` factories are safe to memoize as written — my probe shows `get_user_supabase_client` is live on /comparisons/history (x2) and /home/savings, and that path mutates `client.postgrest.auth(token)`, so a single shared anon client would leak one user's JWT into another's concurrent query; take the keyed-pool branch there, as the first verifier also warned. Is test_first the right red test? Right shape, wrong number: driving /auth/me and /usage/status twice each yields 7 constructions and 2 distinct (url, key) pairs, not "8 total" — because `database_service._admin_client` is already memoized while `auth_service.get_admin_client` is not, so the second /usage/status costs 1. The assertion "at most once per distinct (url, key) pair" fails 7-vs-2 today and passes under the fix, so it is a valid red test once the count is corrected to 7.

findings.title: The Upstash client is built with library defaults: httpx.Client(timeout=None) plus a 3-second time.sleep retry - a stalled Upstash blocks the single event loop forever, and any transient error freezes it 3s per command
findings.dedupe: new (M18/M13 costed Upstash RTT at 163 ms and flagged the calls as on-loop, but no prior finding notes that the client has no timeout at all or that the retry path sleeps 3 s on the loop; no open issue covers it - #71 is about moving Redis off the loop, not bounding it)
findings.fix: Construct the client explicitly: `Redis(url=..., token=..., rest_retries=0, rest_retry_interval=0)` and then force a bounded transport - `redis_client._http._client = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(2.0, connect=1.0))` immediately after construction (the library exposes no timeout kwarg in 1.7.0), or wrap the module's `_redis_get`/`_redis_set`/`_redis_incr`/`_redis_expire` helpers so each command runs under a bounded budget. Every cache helper is already fail-open on exception (cache_service.py:62-64, 77-79), so a timeout degrades to a cache miss, which is the intended behaviour. This is a hard prerequisite for flipping ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD too: off-loop a hung command still parks a pool thread forever and drains the 40-thread executor.
findings.test_first: tests/test_cache_service_timeout.py: assert `cache_service.redis_client._http._client.timeout.read is not None and <= 2.0` and `redis_client._http._retries == 0`; plus a loop-starvation test that patches the transport to sleep 3 s, calls `_redis_get` from an async test with a 10 ms heartbeat task, and asserts the heartbeat gap stays under 200 ms.
findings.impact: Two distinct whole-deployment failure modes that no timeout anywhere in the app can bound. (a) NO TIMEOUT: if an Upstash POST stalls (TLS hang, black-holed route, provider incident), the sync httpx call never returns and the single uvicorn loop is blocked until the OS TCP stack gives up - minutes, not seconds. /health is served by that same loop, so the Railway 30 s healthcheck fails and the only replica restarts; on restart the first authed request hits the same stall. (b) RETRY SLEEP: on any raised exception the library does `time.sleep(3)` ON THE EVENT LOOP. M18 counts 40-60 Upstash commands per cold compare; a flapping Upstash therefore converts one compare into up to 3 minutes of frozen loop. This also silently breaks every wall-clock budget in the system (the 15 s price race, STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30) because those measure elapsed time while the loop is not running.

verdict_trail.reason: Code at HEAD matches the claim exactly and is unchanged 76ace90..a2efaa2. The app passes no rest_retries/rest_retry_interval/timeout anywhere (grep over app/ finds zero hits), and the library's sync transport is httpx.Client(timeout=None) with a time.sleep(3) retry — I reproduced both by runtime introspection and by reading the installed source. Reachable by any real authed user in the PROD flag state: ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD is absent from railway-web-vars.txt, so _is_token_revoked runs inline on the loop on every authed request. Genuinely new: no prior row or issue (#71 is off-loop, not bounded) mentions the missing timeout or the 3s sleep. The 40-60 commands/compare input is supported by M18 (60x3s=180s checks out). P1 correct — real defect reachable by users, but needs an external Upstash fault to fire, so not P0.

I tried to break this and could not — both failure modes MANIFESTED in a running reproduction through the real runtime module (imported app.services.cache_service, called cache_service._redis_get, the exact inline path taken when ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD is unset, which it is in prod). This upgrades the finding's own "measured_or_modelled: static" to MEASURED. (a) RETRY SLEEP: with a peer that accepts and immediately closes (TLS-EOF, i.e. an ordinary connection-reset blip), one _redis_get blocked the asyncio event loop for 3.638 s; a 5 ms-period heartbeat task got 0 ticks during the call (727 expected) and recorded a 3.638 s gap on its first tick after — total loop starvation from a single Redis GET, matching time.sleep(self._retry_interval)=3 on the loop. (b) NO TIMEOUT: with a peer that accepts and never replies (TLS handshake black-hole), the same call had NOT returned after 45 s with 0 heartbeat ticks; the process had to be killed by a watchdog (exit 7). Unbounded confirmed, not merely inferred. FIX: yes, it closes the reproduction, measured in the same run — Redis(url=..., token=..., rest_retries=0, rest_retry_interval=0) plus redis_client._http._client = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(2.0, connect=1.0)) turned case (a) into 0.016 s and case (b) into 1.015 s (bounded by connect=1.0, which does cover the TLS handshake in httpcore), and both still returned None with "Redis GET error" logged — fail-open preserved, so a bounded client degrades to a cache miss exactly as intended. TEST_FIRST: the loop-starvation half is the right red test and is precisely what I built (heartbeat gap 3.638 s vs a 200 ms assertion = red at HEAD, 0.016 s = green after). Two gaps worth fixing before writing it: (1) the free-tier test env has no UPSTASH_* creds, so module-level redis_client is None and the introspection assertion redis_client._http._client.timeout.read <= 2.0 would AttributeError rather than fail meaningfully — the test must set UPSTASH_REDIS_URL/TOKEN and (re)import, as my repro had to; (2) that introspection assertion is coupled to library privates (_http._client), so prefer the behavioural test as the pinning one and keep the attribute check only as a cheap canary. SEVERITY: P1 stands. It is a real defect reachable by any authed user (every request runs _is_token_revoked inline before the Supabase hop) but it needs an external Upstash fault to fire, so not P0; and it is not a mere quality issue (P2) since one command can freeze the single worker loop indefinitely, taking /health with it. Dedupe re-checked independently: grep for rest_retr|timeout=None|retry_interval|unbounded across the M18/M13 investigation docs returns only unrelated "unbounded" rows (SSE tail, /home/savings SELECT, admin scans); #71 is about moving Redis off the loop, not bounding it. Genuinely new. One honest caveat retained from verifier 1: introspection ran on the locally installed upstash-redis 1.6.0, which is OFF-LOCK vs requirements.txt:186 (1.7.0); I did not obtain a 1.7.0 wheel, so 1.7.0's identical defaults remain the finder's evidence — but the app-side defect (passing no kwargs and no timeout at all, cache_service.py:28) is version-independent. No fault was injected against live Upstash (brief HARD RULE 1); the servers in my repro were local sockets.
