(e) Add tests/test_startup_wiring.py::test_default_executor_is_actually_installed — boot the app through `TestClient` and assert `asyncio.get_running_loop()._default_executor._max_workers == default_executor_size()` and that the thread name prefix is `qaren-worker`; that one test converts a silent revert into a red build. Prefer migrating main.py:168 to the modern `lifespan=` context manager in the same change, since the shim is already deprecated in the locked FastAPI.
findings.test_first: tests/test_startup_wiring.py::test_default_executor_is_actually_installed (see (e) above) is the highest-value one and is red only under a future regression; tests/test_background_tasks.py::test_fire_and_forget_is_bounded — spawn 100 fire-and-forget coroutines that block on an event and assert no more than BACKGROUND_TASK_CONCURRENCY are running. Red today.
findings.impact: Individually minor, collectively they are the reason the concurrency model is hard to reason about: (a) makes the loop's real offered load larger than the request count suggests and is the amplifier behind findings 01/04; (b) turns every deploy into a small burst of abandoned upstream work and leaked sockets; (c) is a 40-thread resource nobody has counted; (e) is a latent trap that would silently un-do M13-34 — the single most load-bearing concurrency bound in the service — with no test and no log to catch it.

verdict_trail.reason: All five sub-claims reproduce at 76ace90, with corrections. (a) async_utils:54 create_task, no semaphore/counter/drain — but 42 call sites, not 41. (b)/(e) exactly one lifecycle handler (main.py:168), no shutdown, and FastAPI(...) at main.py:67 passes no lifespan. (c) sync deps confirmed; the 22 admin routes are 19 in admin_routes + 3 in text_routes, and executor.py's docstring indeed never mentions anyio. (d) _next_slot_at pruned only by a tests-only reset_domain_spacing(), and its path is behind a default-OFF flag. (a)'s loop-blocking half duplicates M18 LS-event-loop-08 (P3, still-open); only the boundedness is new. Lock-version claims about starlette 1.6.0/fastapi 0.141.1 NOT verified (local env off-lock, no wheel download), but the mechanism is confirmed in installed fastapi. P3 stands.

findings.title: MEASURED: Upstash REST RTT from the prod container is 178 ms and both offload flags are UNSET, so every cache HIT blocks the single event loop for a full round trip
findings.dedupe: known:#71 (Redis/Supabase off loop) and known:#116/M13-05 - both still-open; the RTT itself is new and is the number M18 recorded as never measured
findings.fix: Flip ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD and ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD ON in Railway for the web service - the code paths already exist and are documented byte-identical when OFF (app/utils/db_offload.py:30, app/services/cache_service.py:549), and the 40-thread executor is already installed (measured in the startup log). Per the M18 ordering rule the offloads must be ACTIVE and hop-count-verified BEFORE the #114 limiter key changes. Do it as two separate deploys with the /health probe and a stage-timing capture between them so the specs_ms/reviews_ms floor can be re-measured; if the floor drops off the 160-210 ms band the offload is genuinely live.
findings.test_first: A test that patches cache_service.redis_client.get to sleep 0.178 s, runs two compare_from_text coroutines concurrently through the real orchestrator with a fake OpenAI, and asserts the second one's wall clock is not inflated by more than 50 ms - red today because the sleep runs on the loop, green once the offload dispatches it to the executor.
findings.impact: M18 listed 'Upstash RTT from Railway NEVER measured' as the biggest unknown in the load model; it is 178 ms (median, min 176, max 197) and Supabase is ~285 ms (max 884 cold). Triangulation with the recorded stage timings (finding 02 of the lane's numbers file): 24 of 70 per-product lookup stage values - 10/14 specs_ms legs and 10/14 reviews_ms legs - sit in the 160-210 ms band, i.e. a cache HIT costs one full blocking round trip, not ~0. A 2-product warm compare therefore burns ~0.7-0.9 s of BLOCKED event loop on Redis alone before any real work, plus ~0.3 s for each inline Supabase write. This is what makes a second concurrent compare inflate the first one's wall clock (finding 05).

verdict_trail.reason: Code and flag state reproduce exactly. cache_service.py:541 carries the quoted docstring; the client at :27 is `upstash_redis.Redis` (sync REST), and both `_redis_offload_enabled` (:549) and `db_offload.run_db` (:30) default OFF. Neither ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD nor ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD appears in the 54-var prod list, so both are OFF. Caveat: the finder's probe used urllib per call (no keep-alive), so 178 ms includes DNS+TLS setup each time and is an upper bound on the pooled steady-state cost. Defect itself is open #71, not new.

Re-measured in the prod container with the REAL pooled client (/opt/venv/bin/python, upstash_redis + httpx 0.28.1, keep-alive across 12 GETs): 168-196 ms, one 368 ms outlier. That REFUTES the first verifier's caveat that 178 ms was an unpooled upper bound — it is the pooled steady state. Live `railway variables --service web` (54 vars) contains neither offload flag, and the in-container env dump agrees (<UNSET>). Reproduced the consequence: with get_cached sleeping the measured 178 ms, 4 reads block the loop 0.714 s and a co-scheduled 20 ms heartbeat gets 7/35 ticks; with ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD=true it gets 31/35, so the proposed flag flip closes my reproduction — but sequence it AFTER LS-CACHE-REDIS-01 or a hang relocates into the 40-thread executor. test_first is right in spirit; a heartbeat-tick assertion is sturdier than a 50 ms wall-clock one.

fable.note: measured Upstash RTT 178 ms (re-measured 168-196 ms with the pooled client); not a code defect, load-model input

findings.title: Admin analytics silently truncate at PostgREST's 1000-row cap: the dashboard reports 1,000 comparisons and $3.00 where the truth is 14,375 and $26.14 (8.7x cost understatement)
findings.dedupe: new (possibly adjacent to #66 'admin cost meters wrong'; the issue body was not readable this session because the GitHub MCP failed to connect, and the repo's own investigation files do not mention the row cap)
findings.fix: Give each of the four search_logs queries an explicit paging loop (.range(off, off+999) until a short page) or, better, replace them with a Postgres aggregate via RPC so the row set never crosses the wire - count/sum/avg belong in the database. Ship behind no flag (read-only correctness fix) but land a test first. While fixing, drop duration_ms==0 rows from avg_duration (finding 09) and add a 'rows_scanned' field to the response so a future truncation is visible rather than silent.
findings.test_first: A test that seeds 1,050 search_logs rows into a test schema, calls get_daily_stats(days=30) through the real analytics_service, and asserts total_comparisons == 1050 - red today (returns 1000).
findings.impact: Every operator-facing number is wrong by an unbounded factor that grows with traffic: GET /api/v1/admin/stats, /admin/costs, /admin/queries all read these functions (admin_routes.py:50/61/72/83). The same cap hits get_popular_queries (1,000 of 16,283 rows -> the 'top query' ranking is drawn from an arbitrary unordered 1/16th of the table) and get_cost_trends (identical $3.0038). At launch volumes the dashboard will freeze at 1,000 and report a flat cost line while real spend climbs. This is also why any prior 'cost per compare' read off the dashboard is untrustworthy.

verdict_trail.reason: Defect reproduces. I replayed the exact query shapes read-only against prod: get_popular_queries returned exactly 1000 rows against a true count of 16,283, and the 120-day window I recomputed independently gives 14,375 rows / cost 26.1448 — matching the finder byte for byte. No .range/.limit anywhere in analytics_service (I read all 180 lines; get_error_stats and get_product_stats have the same hole). Downgraded to P2: admin-key-gated, operator-facing only, no user harm and no spend gate, and it sits inside open issue #66 'admin cost meters wrong'. Note the finder used days=120, not the route default 30.

findings.title: _track_gpt_cost prices EVERY GPT call at gpt-4o-mini rates while the verdict call runs gpt-4o, so the recorded cost of the most expensive stage is understated ~16.7x
findings.dedupe: new (grep of docs/investigations/ for _track_gpt_cost, the rate constants and 'cost meter' returns nothing)
findings.fix: Replace the two magic numbers with a per-model rate table keyed by the model id the call actually used - _track_gpt_cost already receives the usage dict, so pass the model alongside it and look the rate up from a dict in model_config.py next to _ROLE_DEFAULTS (so a model swap moves both together). Ship unflagged; it only changes a recorded number. Also stamp the resolved model ids into metadata so a recorded comparison can be re-priced later, and note in the fix commit that all pre-fix cost rows are floors, not values.
findings.test_first: A test that calls _track_gpt_cost with usage={'prompt_tokens':1_000_000,'completion_tokens':1_000_000} for model 'gpt-4o' and asserts total_cost == 12.50 - red today (returns 0.75).
findings.impact: gpt-4o list price is $2.50/$10.00 per 1M vs the hardcoded $0.15/$0.60 - a 16.7x under-count on whichever share of tokens the verdict consumes, and the verdict is 20-70% of wall time in all 7 recorded stage-timing comparisons (median 5,768 ms of a 19,349 ms total). Everything downstream inherits the error: search_logs.cost (the $19.07 recorded across 1,501 real successes, mean $0.0127), the admin cost meters, and any unit-economics or pricing decision taken from them. Combined with finding 04 the true per-compare cost is materially above the $0.0127 the project believes.

verdict_trail.reason: Static claim fully reproduces. scs:7977 is the flat $0.15/$0.60 line; the verdict path scs:3440 `generate_comparison(...)` feeds scs:3450 `self._track_gpt_cost(usage)`; extraction_service.py:2331 `verdict_model = await model_router.get_model(priority="high")` and model_router_service.py:3 'Selects ``gpt-4o`` for high-priority calls (verdict generation)'; ENABLE_HYBRID_MODEL_ROUTING=true in prod. 16.7x arithmetic checks (2.50/0.15 = 10.00/0.60 = 16.67); test_first 12.50-vs-0.75 is right. Downgraded: nothing gates on this number — check_monthly_budget/track_api_cost (cache_service.py:715-732) have no live request-path caller, so it is a recording error, not a spend leak. 9 sites, not 8.

findings.title: Every failure-path log_search omits cost=, so failed comparisons record $0: 549 real failures burned 7,348 s of compute at a recorded zero
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Pass cost=result.get('metadata',{}).get('total_cost',0) on all four failure call sites, and make the orchestrator populate metadata.total_cost on the failure return shapes too (scs returns error dicts at :3115/:3227/:3275/:3354/:3639/:3781/:3829/:3964/:4407 - several build no metadata at all). Cheapest correct version: have the service always attach {'total_cost': self.total_cost} to whatever dict it returns, success or not, so no call site has to remember. No flag needed. Backfill is impossible; note in CONTEXT that pre-fix failure rows are $0 by construction.
findings.test_first: A route test that forces compare_from_text to return {'success': False, 'error': 'x', 'metadata': {'total_cost': 0.004}} and asserts the fire_and_forget log_search was called with cost=0.004 - red today (called without cost).
findings.impact: A failed compare is the EXPENSIVE case - it ran parse, fan-out, price races and often a verdict before timing out (the 549 failures average 13.4 s each) - and it is exactly the case recorded at $0. Imputing the measured success mean ($0.0127) onto the $0 rows gives ~$26.10 against $19.07 recorded, so the meter captures ~73% of spend before the gpt-4o mispricing in finding 03. Cost-per-successful-compare, the number that decides whether the product is viable, is therefore biased low twice over, and the bias grows precisely when the system is degraded (at overlap>=3, 60% of requests fail).

verdict_trail.reason: Fully reproduced, and stronger than stated. I read all seven log_search sites at HEAD: the three success calls pass `cost=result.get('metadata',{}).get('total_cost',0)` (text_routes :271/:420/:641, image_routes :258) while all four failure calls pass only query/user_id/success/error_message/duration_ms (text_routes :230/:386/:662, image_routes :285); database_service.py:474 defaults `cost: float = 0.0`. My own full-table pull: 3,315 failures, 0 with non-zero cost (finder's 549 was the d>=1000ms subset; I get 558). Imputation arithmetic checks. Downgraded to P2: measurement-only, no user harm, no spend gate.

findings.title: MEASURED concurrency cliff is at TWO in-flight compares, not the modelled 3-4: success falls 76%->54%->38%->0% and timeouts rise 5.9%->23.5%->59.7%->100%
findings.dedupe: known:M18 load answer - status regressed relative to the model (M18 modelled a 3-4 cliff and all-modelled concurrency; measured is 2, with n=68/72/18 in the overlapped buckets)
findings.fix: Do not raise concurrency; cut the median. The measured budget says where: verdict is 20-70% of total (median 5.8 s) and price_ms reaches the 15 s _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT on cold legs, while scoring and response-build are ~0.5 ms. Land the offloads (finding 01) to recover ~1 s, then either lower _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT or make the verdict streaming-first so a partial lands before the cap. Until median wall drops below ~12 s, treat 1 concurrent compare as the supported ceiling and say so in the launch runbook. Re-measure this exact table after each change - it is now a repeatable gate.
findings.test_first: A harness test (offline, fake OpenAI with a 20 s scripted delay) that runs 2 compares concurrently through the real route and asserts both complete inside STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS - red today.
findings.impact: This is the first measured concurrency number the project has - M18's '3-4' was modelled. It is worse than modelled AND it is a DEADLINE cliff, not a capacity cliff: single-request p50 is 19.9 s against a 30 s hard cap (only 10 s of headroom) and single-request p95 is already 30.0 s, i.e. AT the cap. A second concurrent compare adds 4-7 s to p50, which is enough to push the majority over. Loop-blocking (finding 01) does not saturate until roughly 60 compares/min, so the binding constraints in order are (a) the 30 s deadline vs a 20 s median, (b) the shared-IP 10/minute limiter, (c) OpenAI TPM. Any launch plan that assumes 3 concurrent users are safe is wrong by one user.

verdict_trail.reason: Partially reproduces. Re-deriving overlap on the identical subset I match overlap=1 exactly (n=1892, 76%, p50 19927, p95 30004) and get 57%/37% at overlap 2/3 (finder 54%/38%), but overlap>=4 gives n=45 succ 29%, not n=18 succ 0%/timeout 100%. Two structural problems: the overlapped population is essentially one engine and two days (overlap>=2: 2026-06 n=149, 2026-06-10 alone n=96; only 2 rows since 2026-08), i.e. not HEAD; and overlap is derived from duration_ms, so a slow/failing request mechanically lands in a high-overlap bucket — exposure and outcome share a variable.

findings.title: The 30 s stream hard cap does not bound the tail (ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE default OFF): 40 measured requests ran past 35 s, 12 past 60 s, max 103.7 s against a 120 s client timeout
findings.dedupe: new (M18 established the cap exists; the measured >35 s population and the unbounded-tail flag state are new)
findings.fix: Turn ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE ON (it is written, defaults OFF, and the docstring already prescribes 'Canary before flipping'), so the residual budget wraps the tail and expiry yields the best-available PARTIAL instead of an unbounded wait. Canary it on a single deploy with DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS still true and re-read the >35 s count from search_logs afterwards - the acceptance criterion is zero rows above STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS + 5 s. Keep STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 while doing it (do not change two variables at once).
findings.test_first: A test that patches the verdict call to take 90 s, runs the streaming generator with ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE=true, and asserts a PARTIAL is yielded within STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS+1 - and the mirror test with the flag OFF asserting today's unbounded behaviour, so the flag's effect is pinned in both directions.
findings.impact: The 'hard cap' is only hard up to the end of Phase 1; the verdict/critique/moderation tail rides free. Measured worst case is 103.7 s of a held connection on a single-worker single-loop server, which is 5x the median compare and long enough to be indistinguishable from a hang on the phone (the code comment names the client's 120 s axios timeout, so the user sees no error event at all - just a spinner). Twelve requests already exceeded 60 s. On a shared event loop each of these also occupies the process for its whole life, so one 103 s tail overlaps ~5 median compares.

verdict_trail.reason: Code claim confirmed: scs:1354-1364 says the wait_for wraps only Phase 1 and 'Flag OFF -> the tail is unbounded'; :1368-1376 defaults OFF; ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE is absent from the 54-var prod list, STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30. The measured half is misattributed: of 202 rows >35s only 50 are input_type='text_stream', and only ONE stream row is >=60s (84,057 ms). The headline max 103,697 ms is an input_type='text' row (POST, which has no cap at all). Every >35s row predates 2026-08 (2026-05: 144, 2026-06: 39, 2026-07: 1), so nothing measures HEAD. Latent, no current traffic.

findings.title: 78.3% of the request log is a synthetic harness (duration_ms=0, 0.15 s inter-arrival, 13 repeating queries), so every statistic computed over the raw search_logs table is contaminated
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Do not delete the rows (they are history); tag them. Add a nullable `source` column to search_logs, default 'api', and have log_search stamp it; then make the analytics functions filter `source='api'` and, as a belt-and-braces guard for the historical rows, exclude duration_ms=0. Separately, drop the `duration_ms: int = 0` default from database_service.py:474 and make it a required argument so no future caller can write a zero silently. Record in docs/CONTEXT that pre-2026-09 search_logs statistics need the d>=1000 filter to be meaningful.
findings.test_first: A test asserting log_search() raises TypeError when called without duration_ms - red today (defaults to 0).
findings.impact: Anyone reasoning from search_logs - the M18 load answer, the admin dashboard, any KPI or failure-rate claim - is reading a table that is three-quarters synthetic. Two concrete corrections fall out: the headline partial-answer rate is 0.73%, not ~10%, so 'Still gathering prices' is NOT a widespread product failure; and the true success rate on real traffic is 73.2%, not the 75-76% the raw series suggests. The rows also inflate every count-based metric by ~4.6x. Note I could not identify the writer: all 8 log_search call sites at HEAD pass duration_ms and so does the legacy backend/ tree, so it is a pre-June build or an out-of-tree harness.

verdict_trail.reason: Code anchor exact and every statistic reproduces, including against LIVE Supabase (not just the finder's cached sl.json). I re-derived each derived figure myself and all matched. All 8 log_search call sites at HEAD pass duration_ms explicitly, so the proposed 'make it required' change is flag-safe and cannot break a caller. Caveat: the proposed `source` column needs a migration, and 033-036 are still UNAPPLIED in this project, so the belt-and-braces d>=1000 filter is the part that actually ships. One number corrected: real success p50 is 20,973 ms, not 19,927 ms.

findings.title: The streaming surface records 0 failures in 721 rows against 26.0% on the identical non-streaming surface, because the (completed-but-client-gone) outcome logs nothing at all
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Restructure the finally block into three explicit outcomes rather than two: complete-and-delivered, complete-but-client-gone, and errored. The middle one should still log_search(success=True, cost=..., duration_ms=...) with a distinguishing marker (input_type 'text_stream_abandoned' or a metadata flag) and still save history and record the lifetime comparison - the work was done and paid for. Guard the new branch behind nothing; it only adds rows. While there, note that the same restructure makes the finally block's three costs symmetric, which is what test_first below pins.
findings.test_first: A generator test that sets complete_after_client_gone=True with a complete_response present and asserts exactly one log_search call is made - red today (zero calls).
findings.impact: A comparison that ran to completion and cost real money leaves no trace when the user backgrounds the app or the phone drops the connection - no analytics row, no history row, and no lifetime-usage increment (so the free-tier counter under-counts too). The measured 0-of-721 failure rate on the stream is not a quality result, it is missing data: the SSE outcome series cannot be used to compare streaming against non-streaming, which matters because streaming is the path the shipped client uses. This also means the true failure count in the series is higher than the 3,254 recorded.

verdict_trail.reason: The code defect is real: the else branch only refunds, it never logs, saves history, or records lifetime. But the measured framing is wrong three ways, so I rewrote the title. (1) The mechanism is backwards for the headline: the missing branch drops SUCCESSES, which would inflate a failure rate, not zero it; the genuinely swallowed failures are the mid-stream raise/cancel path. (2) The 721-row series is itself contaminated per finding 07 - only 10 rows have d>=1000, so 0% is meaningless. (3) Lines 685-689 refund deliberately (M13-37), so 'free-tier counter under-counts' is false; the real cost angle is a paid comparison given away free.

findings.title: avg_duration_ms averages the duration_ms==0 rows in, so the admin dashboard reports 8.3 s where the real per-compare mean is 19.5 s
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Compute latency percentiles, not a mean, and compute them only over rows with duration_ms > 0 (and, once finding 07's `source` column exists, only over source='api'). Return p50/p90/p95/p99 plus the count they were computed from, so a thin sample is visible. Fold this into the same aggregate-in-Postgres change as finding 02 so the analytics functions are touched once.
findings.test_first: A test seeding 100 rows of duration 20000 and 300 rows of duration 0, asserting the reported p50 is 20000 - red today (a mean of 5000 is reported).
findings.impact: The one latency number an operator sees says the product answers in ~8 s. It answers in ~20 s, with p95 at the 30 s cap. Every capacity and UX judgement taken from that figure - including 'is 30 s enough headroom' - is made against a number that is between 2.3x and 6.5x optimistic depending on which rows the 1000-row cap happened to grab. Compounded with finding 02, the dashboard's latency figure is computed over an arbitrary unordered 1/14th of the window.

verdict_trail.reason: Line 30 is verbatim as quoted and divides by every row in the window, zeros included. Operator-reachable today with no dark flag: admin_routes.py:44-50 exposes GET /admin/analytics/daily behind verify_admin_key. The arithmetic reproduces exactly. The specific 8,330 ms figure is cap-dependent (it comes from the finder's replica under the 1000-row PostgREST cap, which I did not re-run), but the defect is independent of the cap: 10,364 of 13,237 rows carry duration_ms=0. Distinct from #66 (cost meters, not latency). One correction: real-success p50 is 20,973 ms, not 19,927 ms.

findings.title: Prod runs in asia-southeast1 (Singapore) serving GCC users: measured 178 ms to Upstash and 131-884 ms to Supabase, while OpenAI and Serper are 3 ms away
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Two separable moves. (1) Cheap and immediate: co-locate Upstash and Supabase with the Railway region (or move the service to a region near both) so the 178/285 ms drop - this is a dashboard change, not a code change, and it is worth measuring before writing any code. (2) Reduce the number of hops: batch the per-product specs/reviews/price lookups into one Upstash pipeline call per product instead of one per stage, which turns 4-5 round trips per leg into 1. Re-run probe.py after each move; it is a 20-second read-only measurement.
findings.test_first: Not a unit test - a repeatable measurement: check probe.py into scripts/ as a read-only latency probe and assert in CI docs that Upstash p50 from the deploy region is under an agreed budget (say 40 ms) before launch.
findings.impact: The two dependencies on the request path that are NOT co-located are precisely the two that run inline on the event loop (finding 01). This reframes the fix: the 178/285 ms are not 'slow Redis' or 'slow Supabase', they are the price of a cross-region hop that is paid on every cache lookup and every log write. It also sets an upper bound on what offloading can buy - offloading removes the loop blockage but not the latency, so the specs/reviews cache-hit floor stays ~180 ms per lookup until the Upstash instance (and ideally the container) moves closer to the users and to each other. For GCC users this is compounded by the Singapore edge on the client side.

verdict_trail.reason: Region independently confirmed by my own recount of the raw HTTP capture: edgeRegion is asia-southeast1-eqsg3a on 4,742 of 4,742 requests, host web-production-58776.up.railway.app. I could NOT independently re-measure the in-container RTTs - `railway ssh -s web` returned no output in this non-TTY session - so I re-derived the medians arithmetically from the finder's raw sample arrays instead, and both match. The fix is sound and code-free for step 1 (a Railway/Upstash region move). Both dependencies being sync-on-loop is #71/#73 territory, still open; the measured RTT is genuinely new (M18 explicitly never measured Upstash RTT).

findings.title: Prod emits zero per-request application logs (13 deploy log lines for 3.27 days and 4,742 requests) and Railway drops every log older than the current deployment
findings.dedupe: known:#80/#68 adjacent (cron + fire-and-forget visibility) - both still-open; the measured 13-lines-per-3.27-days and the per-deployment retention boundary are new
findings.fix: Emit one structured log line per request from RequestIDMiddleware (method, path, status, duration_ms, request_id, user present y/n - no query text, which is user content and is already a log-flood vector per M13-25) at INFO. Separately, stop relying on Railway for history: the Sentry SDK is already initialised at startup, so ship the same line as a Sentry breadcrumb or forward logs to a sink that outlives a deploy. Note uvicorn's own INFO lines arrive at Railway with level=error because they go to stderr, which makes level filtering useless today.
findings.test_first: A middleware test asserting that a request through the app produces exactly one log record at INFO carrying request_id, path, status and duration_ms - red today (no record).
findings.impact: There is no server-side record of what happened for the entire June/July window that produced the 13,237-row series - I could not cross-check a single search_logs row against a request log, and neither can anyone debugging a production incident. Retention is effectively 'until the next deploy', and this project deployed 18 times in two days. Combined with fire-and-forget failures that do not reach Sentry (#68) and cron failures that are invisible (#80), the only observability that survives a deploy is the search_logs table - which finding 07 shows is 78% synthetic. Two useful startup facts DID survive and are worth recording: '[executor] default ThreadPoolExecutor installed: max_workers=40' and '[models] ... verdict=gpt-4o ...'.

verdict_trail.reason: I re-pulled the deploy logs myself rather than trusting the capture and got the identical 13 lines through 2026-09-05T17:34 (only later lines are another lane's 09-06 probing). RequestIDMiddleware is 15 lines and contains no logging call at all, so the zero-per-request-log claim is structural, not a sampling artifact. The retention claim also holds: the log window begins at container start 2026-09-02T15:54 despite `--since 168h`. uvicorn INFO arriving at level=error is confirmed verbatim. Dedupe is accurate - #80/#68 are adjacent and still open; the measured line count and retention boundary are new.

findings.title: 99.4% of all production HTTP traffic is the Sentry uptime bot hitting / (4,714 of 4,742 requests in 3.27 days) and it probes / rather than the configured healthcheckPath /health
findings.dedupe: known:#81 (/health probes) still-open; the traffic composition measurement is new
findings.fix: Point the Sentry uptime monitor at /health so the alert and Railway's own healthcheck watch the same route, and lower its frequency from 60 s to 5 min (that is 12x fewer edge requests for the same signal). Confirm neither / nor /health is inside a slowapi bucket that user traffic shares - main.py:132 already carries a comment about not 429-ing /health, so verify that comment still matches the code before the #114 key change lands. Also fix the stale runbook comment at main.py:302-304, which tells the reader to cron a hostname (smartcompare-backend-production.up.railway.app) that is not this deployment.
findings.test_first: Not a code test - a config assertion in the launch runbook plus a route test that GET /health and GET / are both exempt from the shared limiter bucket.
findings.impact: Three things fall out. (1) Real user traffic in the last 3.27 days is ZERO compares - the '16 requests sampled, all 2xx, p50 8 ms' in the review baseline is entirely this bot, so no prod signal about the compare path exists at all. (2) The bot generates 1,441 requests/day against the shared Railway edge IP; because every slowapi limit is one bucket on that IP (#114/#72), any limit that ever gets applied to / would be consumed by the monitor rather than by users - worth checking before the limiter key changes. (3) The monitor is watching a route that is not the healthcheck, so /health (the route Railway restarts on) is exercised 7 times in 3.27 days while / is exercised 4,715 times; a /health-only regression would be invisible to the alert.

verdict_trail.reason: Every measured number reproduces exactly from my own recount, but the severity does not survive. The cited anchor railway.json:8 is CORRECT code - the misconfiguration lives in an external Sentry monitor that is not in this repo, so there is nothing here to fix at that line. The only in-repo defect is the stale runbook hostname at main.py:302-304. Harm is nil: a 7 ms 200 on `/`, no spend, no user impact, and impact claim (2) is speculative and gated on #114 which is held by design. That is 'nit/latent' on the brief scale, not a measurable quality or cost issue. Re-anchored to the stale comment.

findings.title: MAX_MONTHLY_COST=100 is set on BOTH prod services but the monthly budget guard is dead code with zero call sites, so nothing caps spend
findings.dedupe: known:M13-49 / M13 quality-bloat 'cache_service 82-line orphan block' - still-open (the symbols are unchanged at 76ace90); the fresh evidence is that MAX_MONTHLY_COST is live on both prod services
findings.fix: Pick one and do it visibly: either delete the four symbols and the MAX_MONTHLY_COST/FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT constants and REMOVE the env vars from both Railway services (so nobody reads a cap that does not exist), or wire add_api_cost into the orchestrator's cost accounting and call check_monthly_budget at the front door of compare. Deleting is the honest cheap move; wiring is the right move before the OpenAI credits are topped up. Do not leave the variable set with dead code behind it.
findings.test_first: If wiring: a test that pushes cost:YYYY-MM past MAX_MONTHLY_COST and asserts POST /text/compare returns 503/429. If deleting: an import test asserting cache_service exposes no check_monthly_budget symbol.
findings.impact: This is a false-safety config landmine of exactly the kind the M18 campaign closed for SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT and the warmer. An operator reading the Railway variables sees a $100/month spend cap and reasonably concludes spend is bounded; it is not bounded by anything. The live orchestrator tracks cost in self.total_cost and never routes it to the Redis meter, so both the counter and the gate are inert. At launch, with OpenAI credits restored, the first runaway loop has no ceiling. M13 flagged the symbols as dead code (P2, delete-them advice); the load-relevant fact is that the env var is SET in prod, which converts dead code into a misleading control.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. The four symbols exist only as definitions in app/; every caller lives in the dead backend/ tree. add_api_cost is the sole writer of cost:YYYY-MM, so the meter reads 0.0. MAX_MONTHLY_COST is present in the variable-name list for BOTH web and price-warmer in baseline/railway-web-vars.txt (its =100 value I could not re-measure — Railway MCP returned Unauthorized — but the code default is 100 regardless). One title imprecision: per-provider CALL budgets do exist (api_budget_service PROVIDER_CONFIGS: firecrawl/scrapedo/serper/youtube); OpenAI, the dominant cost, has none. P2 stands as a still-open M13 row with new prod-config evidence.

findings.title: The container has an 8 vCPU / 8 GB quota but the start command runs one uvicorn worker with WEB_CONCURRENCY unset, so 7 of 8 cores are idle by construction
findings.dedupe: new (M18 established single-loop/1-worker; the 8 vCPU quota, the 166 MB RSS headroom and the missing WEB_CONCURRENCY as the CAUSE are new)
findings.fix: Before launch, evaluate --workers N (or WEB_CONCURRENCY) with N=2 as the first step, and gate it on two preconditions: (a) the slowapi limiter must use shared Upstash storage, not in-process (#72), otherwise N workers means N times the rate limit; (b) the executor is installed per process, so 40 threads becomes 40N - size it down accordingly. Add --proxy-headers at the same time (it is missing today and is needed for correct client IPs, which the limiter key work in #114 will depend on). Treat it as its own canary with the finding-05 overlap table as the acceptance measure.
findings.test_first: A startup test asserting that the limiter's storage_uri is a Redis URL and not in-process memory - red today - because that is the precondition that makes multi-worker safe.
findings.impact: Every M18 conclusion that starts 'single event loop' is correct, but the reason is a missing flag, not a resource limit: the plan is paying for 8 vCPU and using ~1. The measured RSS is 166 MB, so 4 workers would fit in 8 GB with room to spare. This is the cheapest available capacity lever and it was not on the M18 list - though it is NOT free: the app keeps per-process state (the module-level Upstash client, the 40-thread executor, any in-process caches) and slowapi's limiter storage would become per-process unless it is backed by shared Redis, which is exactly the trap #72 describes. So this is a lever to evaluate deliberately, not to pull.

verdict_trail.reason: Code half reproduced exactly; two claims in impact/fix are wrong. (1) Railway bills actual vCPU-seconds, not the 8-vCPU quota, so "paying for 8 vCPU and using ~1" is not a cost leak. (2) uvicorn defaults proxy_headers=True (verified on the installed Config signature; the pinned 0.52.4 keeps that default), and rate_limiter.py parses X-Forwarded-For itself, so "--proxy-headers is missing and needed" is incorrect — the real knob would be --forwarded-allow-ips. The cgroup 8 vCPU / 166 MB figures rest solely on the finder's own probe.out; Railway MCP/CLI is Unauthorized here so I could not re-run the ssh probe. Finder itself says do not pull the lever. No user harm, no defect → P3. The test_first premise is right.

findings.title: 44-50% of SUCCESSFUL comparisons per month record cost=0, so per-compare unit economics cannot be computed from the data the product collects
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Make 'not measured' distinguishable from 'zero': write cost as NULL when the orchestrator produced no cost metadata and 0.0 only when it genuinely spent nothing, and add a small breakdown (gpt_calls, serper_calls, scrape_calls) to the row so a $0 can be audited. Combined with findings 03 and 04 this makes cost-per-compare a number the business can quote. Ship with the same migration that adds the `source` column from finding 07 so search_logs is altered once.
findings.test_first: A test asserting that a comparison which made zero API calls writes cost=0.0 while one whose metadata lacks total_cost writes NULL - red today (both write 0.0).
findings.impact: Three separate mechanisms drive cost to zero - the failure paths (finding 04), the synthetic rows (finding 07), and genuine short-circuits (cache hits, category rejections) that legitimately spend ~nothing - and the schema cannot tell them apart, because 'this cost nothing' and 'we did not record what this cost' are the same value. The 3,920 rows at exactly $0.001 are the signature of a run that made one Serper call and stopped. Practical consequence: the mean of $0.0127 over real successes is the only defensible per-compare cost figure in the system, it rests on 1,501 rows all from June-July, and it is a floor for the two reasons in findings 03 and 04.

verdict_trail.reason: Every number independently re-derived from Supabase with my own paginated SELECT over all 16,283 search_logs rows, and every figure matches to the digit. The code claim is exact: text_routes.py:271 (and :420, :641) collapse a missing metadata.total_cost to 0, so "spent nothing" and "never recorded" are the same value. The finder's 13,237-row "series" is 2026-06 onward (9157+3363+714+3), which reconciles their 7,819 zero-cost rows against my full-table 10,457 exactly once 2026-03..05 (1523+142+973=2638) is removed. Genuinely new; adjacent to but distinct from #66 (admin cost meters).

findings.title: P3 sweep: five smaller measured mismatches between the recorded series, the code at HEAD and the prod configuration
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: (a) Set the code default to 30.0 so code and prod agree, or document the divergence next to the constant. (b) When the search_logs `source` column from finding 07 lands, also stamp a stable error CODE rather than prose, so the taxonomy survives copy changes. (c) Add created_at to product_prices (or stop describing fetched_at as growth) and decide whether a 43%-estimated, 84-day-median corpus can back a price claim at launch. (d) Nothing to fix in code; just stop quoting per-user numbers from this table. (e) Correct the hostname in the main.py comment.
findings.test_first: For (a): a test asserting the module default equals the documented launch value. For (b): a test asserting every user-visible error return carries a stable `code` field alongside its prose.
findings.impact: Individually minor, collectively they explain why the recorded series resists interpretation: the error taxonomy in the table is a mix of three code generations, the price corpus is a median 84 days stale and 43% estimated, and there is no user dimension at all. (a) means a reader of the code assumes a 25 s envelope while prod runs 30, which matters when reasoning about the finding-05 deadline cliff. (e) will send whoever sets up the uptime cron to the wrong host.

verdict_trail.reason: Four of five sub-claims reproduced exactly and the fifth is off by one distinct id. (a) scs:1365 default "25.0" vs prod STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 — confirmed. (b) the two prose strings have zero hits in app/ at HEAD and "blocked" is never assigned to an error_message (the only writer is text_routes result.get("error")); the incomplete/category/identify strings and TIMEOUT_FRIENDLY_MESSAGE (scs:1389) do survive. (c)(e) confirmed. (d) 18 non-null user_id rows is right but there are 2 distinct ids, not 3. Row counts drifted +1 overnight (3,946 / 10 fresh), consistent. P3 correct.

findings.title: Bright Data is the only live search provider today and its spend is unbounded, unmetered and invisible: ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE is not set in prod
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Set ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE=true on `web` and `price-warmer`. That single env flip activates the already-written path: `_bd_budget_precheck()` starts consulting `is_circuit_closed("brightdata") and has_budget("brightdata")` against the packaged 4,500/mo ceiling, and `_bd_record()` starts calling `record_usage`/`record_success`/`record_failure`, which is also what makes the provider appear truthfully on /admin/costs. Because the gate fails OPEN on a Redis fault (brightdata_service.py:80-81) the flip cannot manufacture an outage. Do it BEFORE any traffic, and prefer a ceiling declared in an env var rather than the packaged literal so the free-tier number cannot silently darken a paid zone the way SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT's 2200 was documented to.
findings.test_first: A test that constructs the exact prod env dict (ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK=true + key + zone, ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE unset), monkeypatches `api_budget_service.record_usage`, awaits `brightdata_service.bd_search_web('x')` with `_bd_post` stubbed, and asserts `record_usage` was called at least once. It fails today (0 calls) and passes once the gate is armed. Pair it with a config test asserting that whenever `_brightdata_enabled()` is True, `_brightdata_budget_gate_enabled()` is also True.
findings.impact: Bright Data SERP is the fallback that fires whenever Serper is unavailable — and Serper is at balance -50, so it 403s on every call. Every search leg of every compare therefore dispatches a BILLED Bright Data request with (a) no budget ceiling, (b) no circuit breaker, (c) no per-request meter, and (d) nothing written to the `budget:brightdata:<YYYY-MM>` key, so `/api/v1/admin/costs` reports `brightdata: {used: 0, limit: 4500, remaining: 4500}` forever. Modelled ~12-18 Bright Data requests per cold compare (4-way discovery x2 products + price-organic x2 + unified search x2 + specs/reviews legs; consistent with the ~10-per-cold-lookup measured 2026-08-31), i.e. the packaged 4,500/month free allowance is spent by roughly 250-375 compares and every request after that is billed with no ceiling and no way for the operator to notice.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced independently through the real modules with the exact prod knob set: gate flag absent -> _bd_budget_precheck() True, _bd_record() makes zero record_usage calls. baseline/railway-web-vars.txt has no ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE on web or price-warmer, while FALLBACK+key+zone are set and SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 forces every search leg down bd_search_web. Arithmetic checks (4500/18=250, 4500/12=375). Not P0: measured prod traffic is ~0 (16 reqs/24h), so no spend is leaking right now. Per-compare request count is modelled, not measured, despite the 'measured' label. Fix is correct and fail-open (:80-81).

Independently reproduced through the real modules with the exact prod knob set: bd_search_web dispatches and returns rows while record_usage/has_budget are called ZERO times and get_remaining('brightdata') stays 4500 forever. Mechanism correction the first verifier repeated from the finding: SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 does NOT route traffic to Bright Data — it makes the gate INERT (_serper_gate_engaged False, _serper_budget_ok True). Bright Data is reached via the 403/exception branch (measured: search_web with _serper_post raising 403 returned Bright Data rows). Not P0: prod traffic is ~0. The fix (env flip, fail-open at :80-81) closes the repro; test_first is exactly the right red test.

findings.title: The app's main compare shape (product_a/product_b) skips the OpenAI parse and spends a full provider fan-out on a comparison that cannot succeed while OpenAI is dead
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add an `openai` entry to `api_budget_service.PROVIDER_CONFIGS` and record success/failure around the 4 AsyncOpenAI clients, then gate the top of `_compare_from_text_impl` on `is_circuit_closed('openai')` behind a new default-OFF flag (e.g. ENABLE_LLM_PREFLIGHT_BREAKER) so flag-OFF is byte-identical. With the breaker open the route should return the existing CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE/503 body BEFORE `_fetch_product_data` and BEFORE any credit is consumed. Cheapest interim mitigation with zero code: while OpenAI has no quota, set ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK=false on `web` — Serper already 403s, so the search legs degrade to their benign empty shape and the compare fails in ~2s at zero cost instead of 31s at full cost.
findings.test_first: An async test that patches `extraction_service` so every OpenAI call raises a 429, patches `serper_service.search_web`/`search_product_prices` with counting stubs, and calls `service.compare_from_text(query='a vs b', explicit_pair=('a','b'))`. Assert the search stubs were called ZERO times. It fails today (they are called on every leg) and passes once the LLM preflight gate lands.
findings.impact: Every compare started from the app's two-field home screen spends real money — the Bright Data SERP requests of finding 01, plus any Firecrawl/Scrape.do render credits the escalation fires — and then fails at specs/verdict because OpenAI is dead. It also holds the single uvicorn worker for the full 30s hard cap, so at the M18 deployment-wide ceiling of ~10 compares/min the whole service is consumed producing nothing. The measured 2026-09-02 sample is 1 of 3 attempts (33%) doing this. Nothing anywhere short-circuits: `'openai' in PROVIDER_CONFIGS` is False (repro.py), so there is no breaker to consult and no signal that the LLM is unavailable before the money is spent.

verdict_trail.reason: Code path verified at 76ace90: scs:3250 'elif explicit_pair:' builds products deterministically, parse_product_query only in the else at :3269, and execution reaches the gather at :3327 with no LLM health check. HomeScreen.tsx:316 and text_routes:483 confirmed verbatim. Supabase SELECT reproduced both cited rows exactly. One correction: a LLM call CAN fire on this path - _resolve_pair_category escalates to classify_category_llm at scs:377 when names are blind - so 'never calls OpenAI' is too strong; the substantive claim (no breaker, fan-out spent before the doomed verdict) holds. Distinct from finding 03 by the measured 2.5s-vs-31s asymmetry.

I ran the real compare instead of reading it. With OpenAI unreachable (all async HTTP blocked, so no request left the box) an explicit_pair compare still dispatched 11 billed search legs and 51 adapter fetches, then failed INSUFFICIENT_DATA after 134.9 s — the STREAM_HARD_CAP did not bound the wall time. Two corrections: _resolve_pair_category can still make an LLM call on this path, and of the cited search_logs rows only the 31,008 ms one is this shape (the 22,995/2,554 ms rows say 'Could not identify two products' = the parser branch). Root overlaps COST-03. The preflight-breaker fix closes the repro; test_first (search stubs called ZERO) is exactly right and red today.

findings.title: OpenAI has no budget entry and no circuit breaker anywhere, so a dead key costs up to 6 upstream attempts per verdict and ~23s of the single worker on the cheapest failure path
findings.dedupe: known:M18/LS-capacity-math-03 still-open (that finding established the 429 storm triples request volume); the ROOT — that no `openai` entry exists in PROVIDER_CONFIGS so there is no breaker or budget to trip at all, and that prod ships the 6-attempt chain instead of the documented 3 — is new
findings.fix: Add `"openai": {"monthly_limit": <spend proxy>, "warn_at": ..., "is_lifetime": False}` to PROVIDER_CONFIGS and wrap the 4 client construction sites in a thin helper that calls `record_success`/`record_failure` on the response, then have that helper skip the dispatch when `is_circuit_closed('openai')` is False — all behind a new default-OFF flag so the deploy is byte-identical. Independently and immediately (env only, no deploy): set OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES=1 and OPENAI_FALLBACK_MAX_RETRIES=0 on `web` to move `verdict_chain_max_attempts()` from 6 to 3, which is exactly what #117 built the knobs for and what model_config.py:204 documents as the launch setting. Also give url_extraction_service.py:31 the same `max_retries=openai_max_retries()` the other three clients have.
findings.test_first: A test that patches the AsyncOpenAI client to always raise a 429 and drives `parse_product_query` N times, asserting that after CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD (3) consecutive failures the (N+1)th call short-circuits without an upstream dispatch. It cannot even be written today because no `openai` provider key exists — that is the finding. Plus a config test: `assert verdict_chain_max_attempts() <= 3` under the prod env dict.
findings.impact: Under a 429 storm — or the current permanent-dead-key state — every compare re-attempts the same doomed provider ~10-14 times (parse 1, specs 2, reviews 2, image Tier-3 2, price Tier-3 2, verdict 1 with a 6-attempt chain, plus L3 moderation), each with SDK-level retries and exponential backoff, and nothing ever trips. The measured 22,995 ms for a single failed parse is the concrete cost: the one-worker deployment can serve ~2.6 such requests/minute. At the M18 ceiling of 10 compares/min the loop is 100% consumed by retries against an endpoint that cannot answer, and because `insufficient_quota` never self-heals the state is permanent until a human notices.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced: PROVIDER_CONFIGS=['brightdata','firecrawl','scrapedo','serper','youtube'], openai absent; grep for is_circuit_closed('openai')/record_failure('openai') across app/ returns zero hits; retries resolve to 2/2 giving verdict_chain_max_attempts()=6 vs the 3 that model_config.py:204 documents as the launch setting; url_extraction_service.py:31-35 has no max_retries. Row b3910305 duration_ms=22995 confirmed (60/23=2.6 req/min, arithmetic correct). Minor: 5 AsyncOpenAI sites, not 4, and the '10-14 attempts' figure is modelled not measured. New root vs M18/LS-capacity-math-03, which only established the 429-storm multiplier.

Could not break it. Reproduced through the real modules: PROVIDER_CONFIGS = brightdata/firecrawl/scrapedo/serper/youtube, no openai; verdict_chain_max_attempts()=6 against the 3 the runbook calls the launch setting; no is_circuit_closed('openai')/record_* call site exists anywhere in app/. I also found the trap that makes the fix ORDER-dependent: today is_circuit_closed('openai') returns True (fail-open, never trips) while has_budget('openai') returns False (unknown provider ⇒ limit 0), so gating before adding the entry would dark every LLM call. The 22,995 ms parse row is real. The fix closes it; test_first is right and, as stated, unwritable today — pair it with the OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES config assertion.

findings.title: Scrape.do's dead token bills a phantom 5 credits per call and a 401/403 is not a breaker failure, so the dead integration retries forever and silently drains its 900/mo meter
findings.dedupe: new for Scrape.do; the Firecrawl half is known:#61 (Firecrawl cap/half-open/lossy breaker) — still-open, with the fresh detail that a 401/402 is missed by BOTH the meter and the breaker
findings.fix: Treat an AUTH/PAYMENT status as a breaker failure and as a no-charge: in `_scrapedo_scraper`, extend the failure set to `status in (401, 402, 403, 429, 503) or status == 0`, and in `_parse_request_cost` return 0 when the header is absent AND the status is >= 400 (a rejected request is not a billed render). Apply the identical widening to `_firecrawl_scraper` at scs:1630-1634. Ship both behind one default-OFF flag (e.g. ENABLE_AUTH_FAILURE_BREAKER) so flag-OFF is byte-identical. Independently, and immediately: set ENABLE_SCRAPEDO=false on `web` and `price-warmer` until a live token exists.
findings.test_first: `test_scrapedo_401_trips_breaker_and_bills_nothing`: stub `render_page_with_status` to return `(None, 401, 5)`, run `_scrapedo_scraper` three times with `record_usage`/`record_failure` spied, and assert `record_usage` was never called and `record_failure` was called 3 times. Today it asserts the exact inverse.
findings.impact: The Scrape.do token was documented dead (401) on 2026-06-26 and ENABLE_SCRAPEDO is still true in prod. Every render escalation therefore (a) fires a request that cannot succeed, (b) charges 5 phantom credits to `budget:scrapedo:<YYYY-MM>`, and (c) leaves the breaker CLOSED so the next candidate fires again. After ~180 such 401s the 900-credit meter reads exhausted and `_provider_gate_ok_async('scrapedo')` starts blocking — so the only thing that ever stops the dead integration is a counter of spend that never happened, and it will 'recover' on the 1st of next month and start again. Under burst this is ~2 wasted round trips per render domain per product on the hot 15s price path.

verdict_trail.reason: The code defect is exactly as claimed and reproduced: 401/403 sit in neither failure set, and _parse_request_cost returns 5 with no header. But the premise that the token is dead is not supported: the cited docs say the FREE PLAN 401s on the super/geoCode Business params (scrapedo_service._super_params, gated by SCRAPEDO_SUPER whose prod value is secret-filtered), not that the base token is dead. And a 403 relayed from a Cloudflare-walled target IS genuinely billed by Scrape.do, so metering it is defensible. Verifying a live 401 needs a Scrape.do call, forbidden by HARD RULE 1. Downgraded to a metering/breaker correctness issue; 900/5=180 arithmetic is correct.

findings.title: Every in-flight compare at deploy time burns a freemium credit: the refund is a fire-and-forget task created on a loop that is being torn down, and there is no shutdown handler or graceful-shutdown budget
findings.dedupe: new (M18 CD-wave-diffs-02 covers the cold-path-timeout credit burn and CD-interactions-01 the pre-verdict disconnect; neither covers the deploy/SIGTERM path or the missing shutdown handler)
findings.fix: Add a shutdown handler that holds a module-level `set()` of live background tasks and awaits them with a bounded `asyncio.wait(timeout=...)`, and pass `--timeout-graceful-shutdown 20` in railway.json's startCommand so uvicorn's drain is bounded and predictable instead of `None` (wait forever). Better still for the credit specifically: make the refund on the terminal branch a direct `await refund_comparison_credit(user_id)` rather than a fire-and-forget — the response is already finished, the extra ~200ms is charged to nobody, and it removes the whole class. Gate the awaited form behind a default-OFF flag (e.g. ENABLE_AWAITED_STREAM_REFUND) so flag-OFF is byte-identical.
findings.test_first: An asyncio test that drives the event_generator to the terminal `else` branch, then immediately closes the loop the way `asyncio.run` does (cancel all pending tasks) and asserts `refund_comparison_credit` never completed. Today it passes (the leak is real); after the fix the awaited refund makes it fail, which is the point — invert the assertion at that commit.
findings.impact: On SIGTERM uvicorn stops accepting and drains; when the connection finally ends, the generator's `finally` fires and CREATES a brand-new task for the refund (and for `log_search` and `save_comparison_and_track_cohort`). Those tasks have had no chance to run their first Supabase round trip before the loop is closed and pending tasks are cancelled. Result: every compare in flight at deploy time silently burns a free-tier credit (3 lifetime / 10 monthly), loses its history row and loses its analytics row — and because `fire_and_forget` only emits a `logger.warning` (#68), nothing reaches Sentry. Deploys are the routine event here, and each one hits every concurrent user.

verdict_trail.reason: Every static fact verified at 76ace90: the terminal else at text_routes:685-689 fire-and-forgets refund_comparison_credit; async_utils.py:54 is a bare asyncio.create_task; grep across app/ for on_event(/lifespan/SIGTERM returns exactly one hit, main.py:168 startup, and zero shutdown handlers; railway.json and Procfile both start uvicorn with no --timeout-graceful-shutdown; uvicorn==0.52.4 (requirements.txt:192). Tasks created inside the generator's finally are not in uvicorn's server_state.tasks, so Railway's post-grace SIGKILL kills them mid-flight. Distinct from M18 CD-wave-diffs-02 (cold-path timeout) and CD-interactions-01. Wholly unmeasured - Railway's kill timing was never observed - so confidence 0.82 is right.

Broke the impact claim. In the prod config (both offload flags unset) refund_comparison_credit calls _refund_credit_sync INLINE, so the coroutine has no yielding await: measured, it is lost only when the loop closes with ZERO further iterations, and completes in full after a single iteration. Uvicorn's post-finally path (response completion, connection close, lifespan shutdown) supplies many. log_search/save_comparison are the same shape via run_db-inline. So 'every in-flight compare at deploy burns a credit' does not reproduce; the residual is a SIGKILL landing before the finally, which the proposed awaited-refund fix does NOT close. Static facts hold. test_first would pass today for the wrong reason. Re-raise to P1 if the offload flags are flipped ON.

fable.note: vote + Fable agree: refund runs inline with the offload flags OFF and survives shutdown; becomes a real loss the moment ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD is ON -> W1-6 drain is a precondition for that canary

findings.title: All 42 fire-and-forget tasks are created without a strong reference, so CPython may garbage-collect a refund, a history save or an analytics write mid-flight
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Keep a module-level `_BACKGROUND: set[asyncio.Task] = set()` in async_utils; in `fire_and_forget` do `_BACKGROUND.add(task)` and `task.add_done_callback(_BACKGROUND.discard)` alongside the existing logging callback. Three lines, no flag needed (it can only make tasks MORE likely to complete), and the same set is then the natural thing for the finding-05 shutdown handler to drain. While there, upgrade the `_on_done` warning to a `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(exc)` — that closes #68 in the same edit.
findings.test_first: `test_fire_and_forget_survives_gc`: create a task from a coroutine that awaits an `asyncio.Event`, drop all local references, call `gc.collect()`, then set the event and assert the coroutine ran to completion. Assert `len(async_utils._BACKGROUND) == 1` while pending and 0 after.
findings.impact: A refund (`usage_refund.*`), a history save (`save_comparison.*`), a lifetime counter write or an audit row can vanish with no exception and no log line at all — the done-callback never runs because the task no longer exists. The probability rises with the number of simultaneously-pending tasks, i.e. exactly under the burst this lane is about: 42 sites and several tasks per compare means a 500-app-open burst creates hundreds of concurrently-pending unreferenced tasks. The observable symptom is 'a user's credit was consumed and their comparison is missing from History, and nothing anywhere says why' — indistinguishable from finding 05, which makes both harder to diagnose.

verdict_trail.reason: Facts verified: async_utils.py:54 is a bare create_task, the module has no strong-reference set (grep for _BACKGROUND returns nothing), add_done_callback stores the callback ON the task and creates no back-reference, and 42 call sites confirmed at 76ace90 with the exact per-file breakdown claimed (text_routes 17 + scs 11 + auth_routes 5 + image_routes 5 + feedback_routes 2 + auth_service 1 + review_service 1). runtime.txt pins python-3.12.9 and the CPython warning is real. But this is purely latent and, as the finder concedes, non-reproducible: a task suspended on an awaited future is in practice kept alive by that future's callback chain, so no occurrence has ever been observed or is measurable. P3 (nit/latent) per the brief scale; the 3-line fix is free and correct.

findings.title: DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true is set on BOTH prod services, adding two blocking Upstash round trips to the event loop per render candidate — against code comments that assert it is a prod no-op
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Set DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=false (or unset it) on `web`; keep it on `price-warmer` only if the off-clock warmer actually needs the attribution. Zero code change, no redeploy for the scs/response_builder readers — though note firecrawl/scrapedo cache the flag in a module global at first read (`_PRICE_PIPELINE_DIAG_FLAG`), so those two need a restart to pick it up. Then fix the two comments (scs:5841 and :7185) to say 'no-op WHEN THE FLAG IS OFF', since 'in prod' is currently false, and move `_log_invocation`'s two Redis reads behind the same offload dispatch the rest of the hot path uses.
findings.test_first: A config test over the captured Railway variable set asserting `DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS` is absent or false for the `web` service. Plus a unit test that patches `cache_service._redis_get` with a counter, sets DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true, calls `scrapedo_service._log_invocation('u')` and asserts the counter is 2 — pinning the cost so the next reader cannot miss it.
findings.impact: At the M18-measured 163 ms Upstash RTT from Railway, each render candidate pays 2 x 163 ms = ~326 ms of EVENT-LOOP BLOCKING before its request is even sent — and this path is not covered by ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD (neither offload flag is set in prod anyway). A cold compare that fires the render wave on 2 domains x 2 providers x 2 products = 8 invocations pays ~2.6 s of pure diagnostic loop-block, charged to every other concurrent request. It also emits `[PRICE_SUBSTAGE]`/`PRICE_PIPELINE_DIAG` INFO lines on the hot path, inflating log volume per compare. The comments make this invisible to anyone reading the code: they assert the opposite of what prod does.

verdict_trail.reason: Code behaves as claimed. scrapedo_service.py:85-97 and firecrawl_service.py:114-129 each call api_budget_service.get_remaining/get_breaker_state, both of which do cache_service._redis_get (blocking upstash_redis REST GET) — inside async render functions (scrapedo:119/175, firecrawl:153/207). DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true on web AND price-warmer; both offload flags absent. Two corrections: the cited scs comments are at 5680 and 7018, not 5841/7185; and the 163 ms figure is NOT a Railway->Upstash measurement — M18's own verifier records it as a local dev-worktree number with 'prod RTT is unmeasured', so 326 ms/candidate and 2.6 s/compare are unfounded in magnitude (the arithmetic itself is right). Fix is flag-safe; 'no redeploy' is slightly off since a Railway var change restarts the service anyway (which is what the module-global cache needs). New vs M18, which noted the flag but never the two Redis reads. P2 stands.

findings.title: The only two spend caps present in the Railway config — MAX_MONTHLY_COST and FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT — are read exclusively by functions with zero callers, so setting them does nothing
findings.dedupe: known:M13 data-06 / quality-bloat (dead check_rate_limit + FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT/MAX_MONTHLY_COST) — still-open, with the fresh and load-bearing addition that BOTH vars are actually SET in prod on both services, which turns dead code into active false assurance
findings.fix: Either delete the four dead functions and the two constants they alone read (M13's recommendation), or — better, given findings 01/03 — wire `MAX_MONTHLY_COST` into a real gate: have `api_budget_service` accumulate a per-provider dollar estimate alongside the existing request counters and short-circuit every paid dispatch when the month's estimate crosses it, behind a default-OFF ENABLE_MONTHLY_SPEND_CEILING. Whichever is chosen, do not leave a variable in the Railway UI that reads like a cap and is not one; if the functions are deleted, remove MAX_MONTHLY_COST and FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT from both services' variables in the same change.
findings.test_first: `test_no_orphaned_spend_caps`: assert that for every env var whose name matches `MAX_.*_COST|.*_DAILY_LIMIT`, at least one non-test module in `app/` reads it AND that reader has at least one caller. It fails on both names today.
findings.impact: An operator reading the Railway dashboard sees a $100 monthly cost ceiling and a 5/day free-tier limit and will reasonably conclude spend is capped. Neither is enforced anywhere. The real freemium limiter is `usage_service.TIER_LIMITS` (free daily = 3, not 5) and there is no monthly cost ceiling of any kind in the request path — combined with findings 01 and 03, the deployment has literally zero dollar-denominated spend control. That false assurance is the harm: it is the reason nobody has been looking.

verdict_trail.reason: Facts confirmed: `git grep` over app/ at 76ace90 returns ONLY the definitions in cache_service.py — check_rate_limit(:668), track_api_cost(:715), check_monthly_budget(:730), add_api_cost(:752) have no call sites; both names are in Railway's variable list for web and price-warmer; usage_service.TIER_LIMITS free daily = 3, not 5. But this is squarely M13-49 / data-06, and M13's own verification pass already DOWNGRADED data-06 P2->P3 for exactly this reason. The 'fresh' addition (the vars are set in prod) changes no runtime behaviour — nothing reads them on any path — so the harm is documentation-grade false assurance, i.e. latent. P2 overstates it; P3. Fix (delete the orphans and both vars together) is correct and flag-free; the alternative 'wire MAX_MONTHLY_COST into a real gate' is a new feature, not this fix.

findings.title: Cost accounting excludes every non-OpenAI provider AND every failed compare, so the admin dashboard's monthly total is structurally incapable of showing the spend that is actually happening
findings.dedupe: adjacent to known:#66 (admin cost meters wrong) — still-open; the two NEW parts are (a) `estimated_monthly_total` is arithmetically OpenAI-only by construction and (b) the failure-path `log_search` drops a `total_cost` the service already returned
findings.fix: Accumulate provider spend the same way OpenAI tokens are accumulated: have `_bd_record`, `_scrapedo_scraper` and `_firecrawl_scraper` add an estimated dollar amount to a per-provider Redis counter, expose those counters in `get_usage_summary`, and include them in `estimated_monthly_total` alongside the $30 fixed cost. Separately and cheaply: pass `cost=result.get('metadata', {}).get('total_cost', 0)` on the FAILURE-path `log_search` calls at text_routes:230 and :386 (the service returns `total_cost` on the INSUFFICIENT_DATA/TIMEOUT bodies — scs@76ace90:3118 and :3126 — so the value is already there and is simply being dropped).
findings.test_first: `test_failed_compare_logs_its_cost`: patch `compare_from_text` to return `{'success': False, 'code': 'INSUFFICIENT_DATA', 'total_cost': 0.004}`, POST /text/compare, and assert the `log_search` spy received `cost=0.004`. It receives 0.0 today. Plus `test_admin_costs_includes_every_paid_provider`: assert `set(summary) >= {'openai','serper','brightdata','firecrawl','scrapedo'}` with dollar values, not just credit counts.
findings.impact: There are three cost surfaces and all three are blind to the money currently being spent. `/admin/costs.estimated_monthly_total` will read $30 + a few cents of OpenAI while Bright Data burns its 4,500/month allowance. `get_usage_summary()` reports brightdata used=0 forever. `search_logs.cost` reads 0.0 for every failure — and while OpenAI is dead, EVERY compare is a failure, so the cost column is guaranteed zero no matter how much is spent. There is no artefact anywhere that would let an operator answer 'what did last month cost'.

verdict_trail.reason: Both halves reproduce. admin_routes.py:131 sums only fixed_costs_monthly (30.00) + openai_cost derived from comparisons.metadata.total_cost — no Serper/BrightData/Firecrawl/Scrape.do dollars. text_routes.py:230 and :386 (failure paths) omit `cost=`, while the success paths at :268 and :417 pass it, so every failed compare records 0.0; the baseline search_logs summary shows 2026-09 n=3, success=0, cost_sum=0.000. get_usage_summary does iterate brightdata (PROVIDER_CONFIGS:49) but _bd_record is a no-op unless ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE is on, and that flag is absent from Railway. One fix defect: the proposed snippet `result.get('metadata',{}).get('total_cost',0)` is WRONG on the failure path — the finder's own citations show total_cost is TOP-LEVEL on the INSUFFICIENT_DATA/TIMEOUT bodies (scs:3118/:3126), so that snippet still logs 0.0. Adjacent to #66; part (b) is genuinely new. P2 stands (operator visibility, not user harm).

findings.title: The Serper circuit breaker is written but was never switched on, so every compare fires ~14-18 live POSTs at a key that is guaranteed to 403, each on a fresh TLS connection
findings.dedupe: known:M13-32 (the breaker was built and shipped default-OFF) — status still-dark in prod at 76ace90, with fresh runtime evidence (repro2.py) of the per-leg waste and the ordering constraint against finding 01
findings.fix: Set ENABLE_SERPER_BREAKER=true on `web` and `price-warmer`. The path is already written and memoised so it adds no per-call Redis round trip (serper_service.py:311-327), and it fails OPEN on a Redis fault, so the flip cannot manufacture an outage. After 3 consecutive 403s the breaker trips for CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT (600s) and the Bright Data fallback is reached directly. Note the ordering constraint: this makes the Bright Data path hotter, so arm ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE (finding 01) FIRST.
findings.test_first: `test_serper_breaker_trips_on_403_storm`: with ENABLE_SERPER_BREAKER=true, drive `search_web` 5 times against a stubbed 403 and assert the underlying `client.post` was invoked at most CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD (3) times, not 5. With the flag in its prod state (off) the same test asserts 5 — pin BOTH so the config drift is visible.
findings.impact: Modelled per cold compare: ~7-9 Serper entry-point dispatches per product (1 shopping gl=us, 1 price-organic, 4 discovery, 1 unified, 1 images) x 2 products = ~14-18 live HTTPS POSTs to google.serper.dev that are known in advance to 403. Each is issued from a freshly-constructed `httpx.AsyncClient` (no pooling — #73/#70), so each pays a full DNS+TCP+TLS handshake on the single event loop before the 403 lands. That is pure latency and loop occupancy added to a compare that then also pays for Bright Data. Flipping the breaker would collapse all of them to one probe per 10-minute cooldown window.

verdict_trail.reason: Structure confirmed. ENABLE_SERPER_BREAKER is absent from railway-web-vars.txt for web and price-warmer, so _serper_breaker_enabled() is False, _serper_post short-circuits to _serper_post_impl unchanged, and _serper_record_failure returns before touching the breaker — the 403 branch at :449-450 is inert. SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 on web makes _serper_gate_engaged() False (declared>0 required), so the budget gate admits every call too. This is exactly M13-32, shipped default-OFF; still dark. Two corrections. (1) measured_or_modelled should be MODELLED: repro2.py only shows 1 Serper POST + 1 BD POST via search_web; the ~14-18 POSTs/compare is arithmetic. (2) The 'every compare, forever' magnitude is contingent — prod sets both SERPER_API_KEY and SERPER_API_KEYS (values withheld). With >=2 resolved keys, _mark_serper_key_exhausted fires on the 403 and _active_serper_key() then returns None, short-circuiting later entry points BEFORE any POST; only the single-key INERT path dispatches every time. Fix and the arm-BD-gate-first ordering are correct. P2 matches M13-32.

findings.title: A shared-bucket 429 reaches the user as a generic 'comparison failed' with no wait-and-retry cue and no Retry-After header, so the burst that caused it gets amplified by immediate retries
findings.dedupe: known:M18/LS-ratelimit-01 + LS-capacity-math-01 (the shared deployment-wide bucket) — still-open; NEW is the client-facing consequence: RATE_LIMITED has zero handlers on any compare screen, there is no Retry-After, and the resulting immediate-retry loop amplifies the burst
findings.fix: Two halves. Backend: have `rate_limit_handler` set a `Retry-After` header from slowapi's `exc.detail` window and include `retry_after_seconds` in the JSON body — a self-contained change in error_handler.py:122. Client: add a `RATE_LIMITED` branch to HomeScreen/ResultsScreen's `onError` (next to the existing `TIMEOUT` branch) that shows dedicated i18n copy in en.json and ar.json ('Lots of people are comparing right now — try again in a moment') and, ideally, disables the compare button for `retry_after_seconds`. Note the two-lever gap: the client half only reaches users on the next `eas update --branch preview`, so ship the backend half first — it at least stops the client from being blind.
findings.test_first: Backend: `test_rate_limit_response_carries_retry_after` — exceed a decorated limit against the TestClient and assert `response.headers['Retry-After']` exists and the body has `retry_after_seconds`. Client: a jest test on HomeScreen's onError with `{response: {status: 429, data: {code: 'RATE_LIMITED'}}}` asserting `Alert.alert` was called with the rate-limit i18n key, not `home.errors.comparison`.
findings.impact: M18 established that every decorated 10/minute limit is ONE deployment-wide bucket keyed on the shared Railway edge IP. So the 11th compare in any minute — from any user anywhere — 429s. That user is told 'we couldn't compare these' (main) or 'Request failed with status code 429' (shipped bundle). Neither says 'wait a minute'; neither is localized as a rate-limit in Arabic; and with no `Retry-After` the client has nothing to back off on. The predictable behaviour is an immediate re-tap, which lands in the same bucket, which extends the outage — a burst of 50 app-opens turns into a self-sustaining 429 storm from a 10/min bucket. This is the user-visible face of the capacity ceiling, and it is the part that makes the ceiling worse instead of degrading gracefully.

verdict_trail.reason: Every cited line reproduces at 76ace90. rate_limit_handler (:122-127) returns _build_error_response(429, 'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.', ...) and _build_error_response (:41-52) emits only {success,error,code,request_id} — no Retry-After header, no retry_after_seconds. STATUS_CODE_MAP:30 maps 429->RATE_LIMITED; main.py:151 registers the handler; text_routes carries four @limiter.limit("10/minute") compare routes, so the path is user-reachable. Client: api.ts:146-153 special-cases 429 ONLY when code=='USAGE_LIMIT', otherwise rejects; HomeScreen.tsx:394-399 renders t('home.errors.comparison') for any unrecognised structured code; the shipped 97b5f15 bundle is worse — HomeScreen.tsx:388 `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), error.message || ...)`, i.e. the raw axios 429 string. Only RATE_LIMITED handler in the app is ContactUsScreen.tsx:75. Correctly deduped against M18 LS-ratelimit-01/LS-capacity-math-01 (shared bucket) — the client gap and missing Retry-After are new. The retry-amplification impact is modelled (prod traffic is ~16 req/24h today), but the defect is real; P2 stands. Fix is correct and correctly notes the backend half ships first.

findings.title: Loop saturation is an unrecoverable failure mode: Railway does not health-check a live deployment and restartPolicy only fires on process exit, so a stalled worker is never restarted and the 'max 3 retries' budget is never even consumed
findings.dedupe: known:M18/LS-railway-metrics-03 (zero-HA, ON_FAILURE max 3) and LS-event-loop-09 (healthcheck shares the blocked loop) — still-open, and CORRECTED: the 'max 3 retries then permanent downtime' framing is optimistic, because a stalled loop never exits so ZERO restarts occur and Railway performs no continuous health check at all. Also known:#81 still-open.
findings.fix: (1) Stand up an external uptime probe against `/health` (Railway's own docs point at the Uptime Kuma template) — that is #81 and it is the ONLY thing that can detect this class. (2) Make `/health` slightly meaningful: have it report event-loop lag (e.g. `time.monotonic()` delta across an `await asyncio.sleep(0)`) so a saturated-but-alive loop is distinguishable from a healthy one, and let the probe alert on lag rather than on a hard timeout. (3) Raise restartPolicyMaxRetries from 3 toward Railway's default 10, since a crash-loop budget of 3 buys nothing but a permanent outage. (4) Add a second uvicorn worker (M18 LS-event-loop-07) so one stalled loop is not the whole service. None of this needs a code flag; (2) is the only code change and is additive.
findings.test_first: Not a unit test — a runbook probe: with the service live, issue N concurrent `/text/compare` requests and poll `/health`, asserting p95 `/health` latency stays under a threshold. That harness is what does not exist, which is the finding. As a code test: `test_health_reports_loop_lag` asserting the /health body contains a `loop_lag_ms` key.
findings.impact: Corrects the operational picture M18 recorded. A saturated event loop does NOT exit, so ON_FAILURE never triggers and the 3-restart budget is irrelevant — the deployment simply stops answering, indefinitely, until a human redeploys. Nothing detects it: /health would degrade (it shares the blocked loop, which is the useful part) but #81 is open and nobody polls it, so the degradation is unobserved. Combined with 1 replica x 1 worker this is a single stall away from a silent total outage with no alarm and no auto-recovery. The 30s `healthcheckTimeout` is also 10x tighter than Railway's 300s default; measured cold start is only ~1.3s today, so it is fine now, but it is a deploy-time cliff nobody has written down.

verdict_trail.reason: Every claim reproduced. Railway docs confirm both quotes verbatim; railway.json and main.py match; prod logs show one container start on 2026-09-02 and zero restarts; neither offload flag exists in the web var list. The mechanism (stall != exit, so zero restarts) genuinely CORRECTS M18 LS-railway-metrics-03's "3 restarts then downtime" framing, but the topology, restart budget and healthcheck-shares-loop facts are already M18 rows LS-railway-metrics-03 (P2) and LS-event-loop-09 (P3), both still-open. Not new; a valid known-status correction. Fixes are flag-safe (#81 probe, additive loop-lag). Line corrected: railway.json:8-11, not 5-10/6.

findings.title: P3 sweep: five latent cost/observability nits on the burst path

findings.fix: (a) Route `_get_4o_usage_today` through the same `_cache_get_async` dispatch the rest of the hot path uses, so it inherits ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD. Dedupe field is WRONG: (d) is verbatim M13-99 (P3, "code default (25.0) disagrees with the documented production value (30.0)"), still-open — cited there as scs:1144, now scs:1365.
