findings.title: Every authenticated request builds one or more brand-new Supabase clients, each parsing the CA bundle into a fresh SSLContext on the event loop; GET /history does it 3x
findings.dedupe: new — adjacent to open #73 (pooled httpx + bound GCC endpoint) and #71 (Redis/Supabase off loop), but both of those are about the CALL; this is about the CLIENT CONSTRUCTION, which run_db explicitly does not cover. Not in the M18 175-row set or M13.
findings.fix: Cache both auth clients the way get_admin_supabase_client already does: memoise get_auth_client() and get_admin_client() in auth_service as module singletons (they are stateless w.r.t. the request — only the anon/service key is baked in). For get_user_supabase_client, keep the per-request JWT binding but stop rebuilding the transport: construct ONE module-level httpx client / SSLContext and pass it into create_client via ClientOptions(httpx_client=...), or cache a single anon Client and call .postgrest.auth(token) per request only if the supabase-py version guarantees no cross-request token leakage — verify that before shipping, since a shared client with per-request auth() is a tenant-bleed risk under concurrency. Ship behind ENABLE_POOLED_SUPABASE_CLIENTS (default OFF) and land it BEFORE the #114 limiter re-key, per the M18 ordering rule that offloads must be active first. This is the concrete mechanism behind open issue #73 (pooled httpx).
findings.test_first: A test that monkeypatches ssl.SSLContext.__new__ (or supabase.create_client) with a counter, drives GET /api/v1/history through the real FastAPI TestClient with a valid token, and asserts the counter increments by 0 across two successive requests once the flag is ON (and by 3 today with it OFF) — pins both the current behaviour and the fix.
findings.impact: Structural, not incidental: on the single-worker uvicorn every authed request pays N synchronous SSLContext builds plus N cold TLS handshakes (each new httpx.Client has its own connection pool — verified `s1._transport is not s2._transport`). GET /history pays 3 (verify_token + get_user_comparisons + get_user_comparison_count); /home/savings, /home/smart-pick, /profile/* pay 2. Critically this is NOT covered by run_db: at auth_service.py:256 the construction runs inline and only the `client.auth.get_user(...)` call is wrapped, so flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD does NOT move it off the loop. This is a hard multiplier on the ~10 compares/min deployment-wide ceiling M18 modelled, and it is the one part of that ceiling nobody has costed. Magnitude on Railway/Linux will be well below 500 ms (CA parsing is much cheaper there) but the per-request count and the on-loop placement are the same.

verdict_trail.reason: Mechanism reproduced exactly: create_client builds one fresh SSLContext + its own httpx.Client/transport per call, and the construction sits OUTSIDE run_db at auth_service.py:256, so ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD cannot move it. GET /history = 3 constructions (verify_token, get_user_comparisons, get_user_comparison_count) confirmed. Genuinely new vs #73/#71 (those cover the call, not construction). Downgraded to P2: the only measured magnitude is a Windows dev box (I measured 670-930 ms/client, and a bare ssl.create_default_context costs 658 ms there — a local artifact, not Railway); Railway magnitude is unmeasured, prod traffic is ~0, and no user-visible defect exists. That is a cost/throughput issue by the brief scale. Minor: 15 real call sites of get_user_supabase_client, not 16.

findings.title: /home/savings caches its DEGRADED zero payload for 6 hours, so one Supabase hiccup hides a user's savings banner until the next day
findings.dedupe: new — #116 is closed and covered the cost of the scan and the bust-on-write contract; neither #116 nor the M18 set noticed that the degraded path writes the cache, nor that the 5min->6h change multiplied it.
findings.fix: Never cache a degraded result. In both branches, set a `degraded = True` marker in the except handler and skip the `_redis_set_async` call entirely when it is set (serve the zeros for this one request only), or cache with a short punitive TTL (30-60 s) so a transient error self-heals. Separately, make the flag-ON path fall back to the legacy scan rather than to zeros when the RPC raises PGRST202/PGRST404 specifically — a missing function is a deploy-ordering error, not a data answer. Gate the fallback under the existing ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE so flag-OFF stays byte-identical, and add a startup assertion (or a /health sub-check) that the RPC exists before the flag is allowed to be ON.
findings.test_first: Patch home_routes.run_db to raise, call home_savings via TestClient, and assert (i) the response is the zero payload AND (ii) home_routes._redis_set_async was never awaited — red today on both branches. Second test: patch the RPC to raise APIError(PGRST202) with the flag ON and assert the legacy scan ran and returned the real total.
findings.impact: Two live consequences. (a) TODAY on the legacy path: any transient Supabase error on the one uncached savings request pins savings_bhd=0, decisions_count=0, threshold_met=false into Redis for 6 hours — the SavingsBanner disappears entirely (the frontend hides it below threshold), and because bust-on-write only fires on save/delete, a user who runs no comparison sees nothing for the full 6h. #116 lengthened this TTL from 5 min to 6 h, so the blast radius of an already-existing bug was amplified 72x in the same change that was meant to make the endpoint cheaper. (b) WHEN the flag is flipped: because 036 is unapplied, EVERY user's first /home/savings call caches zeros for 6h, and applying 036 afterwards does not clear them — the product looks like it lost everyone's savings history for most of a day.

verdict_trail.reason: Code confirmed on BOTH branches: the except handler sets zeros then the cache write runs unconditionally with a 6h TTL. Prod flag state confirms the legacy branch is live (ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE absent from railway-web-vars.txt; code default OFF), so I re-anchored the finding to line 285, the prod-reachable write; 238 is the dark-flag one. Migration 036 unapplied confirmed live (PGRST202), so the flag-ON half is real but dark-flag-only => at most P2 per the brief. The live half needs a transient Supabase error to trigger, self-heals on the user's next save/delete (bust-on-write confirmed at history_routes.py:210 and feedback_service.py:59), and degrades to a hidden banner — a quality defect, not a P1. TTL arithmetic 6h/5min = 72x is correct.

findings.title: PostgREST silently truncates at 1000 rows: the LIVE /home/savings scan stops counting a user's savings at 1000 comparisons and reports a wrong total with no error
findings.dedupe: new — #116 (closed) named this query as unbounded in rows and payload and built the aggregate to fix the COST; the silent-truncation CORRECTNESS consequence of the 1000-row cap is not stated in #116, the M18 set, or M13.
findings.fix: Apply migration 036 and turn ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE ON — that is the real fix and it already exists; the aggregate is computed in Postgres and returns one row, so no cap applies. Until then, the legacy branch must not pretend to be complete: add `.limit(1000)` explicitly and, when exactly 1000 rows come back, either page with .range() until exhausted or stamp `"truncated": true` into the payload so the banner can say 'your last 1,000 decisions'. Do NOT leave the implicit cap in place. Also add a repo-wide lint/test that fails on any `.select(...)` reaching `.execute()` with no `.limit`/`.range`/`.single`/`.maybe_single` on the 21 sites listed in classify.txt.
findings.test_first: Seed 1,001 v2 comparison rows for one user in a test Supabase (or stub the client to return exactly 1000 rows for an unbounded select), call /home/savings, and assert decisions_count == 1001 — red today, and red in a way that no existing test catches because every fixture is far under the cap.
findings.impact: The failure mode is not the cost (which plateaus at ~19 MB per uncached call), it is CORRECTNESS: past 1,000 saved comparisons a user's savings_bhd and decisions_count silently freeze and then drift ever further below the truth, with a 200 response and no log line. It arrives exactly when the product succeeds. Today the ceiling is 10 rows for the heaviest of 6 users so nothing is wrong yet — this is latent, which is why it is P2 and not P1. The same silent cap applies to the other 20 unbounded table reads enumerated in classify.txt; the two that would be wrong FIRST are this one and /profile/monthly-stats (LS-DB-QUERIES-08).

verdict_trail.reason: The 1000-row PostgREST cap reproduces on this exact project, and the live flag-OFF scan has no .limit/.range — both confirmed. Arithmetic checks out (1000 x 19,026 B = 19.0 MB; ~90%/~99% under-report at 10k/100k). But this is purely latent: comparisons holds 27 rows total and the heaviest user is ~10, so there is no measurable quality or cost issue today, which is P3 ("nit/latent") on the brief scale — the finder's own text concedes "nothing is wrong yet". Also not fully new: M13-98 already established this exact silent-truncation class ("Admin /costs runs an unbounded month-wide select, so the number is silently truncated", admin_routes.py:110) and M13 rated it P3. New site, known class.

findings.title: Behaviour-profile recompute aborts on its FIRST query against three columns that do not exist, costing ~165 ms per compare and leaving personalization dead for 100% of users
findings.dedupe: known:#65 (behavior profile reads phantom columns, personalization DEAD) — STILL-OPEN. Fresh evidence this session: the exact three phantom columns named and confirmed live against prod schema, the abort-on-first-query semantics (so the cost is 1 round trip not 4), the measured 165 ms, and the decisive 0-of-18 behavior_profile population. Also touches #74 (bound behaviour-profile recompute), which is moot while the recompute never completes.
findings.fix: Map the three selects onto the real schema: `comparisons` has no category or products column, so category/product signal must come out of `full_response` (jsonb) — either select `full_response` and extract in behavior_service, or add a generated/derived column in a new migration; `user_events.metadata` is simply the wrong name for `event_data` and is a one-word fix. Do NOT ship the rename alone — with only the user_events fix the chain still dies on line 4545. Also split the single try into per-query try/except so one bad select degrades to an empty list instead of silently cancelling the profile write, and raise the log from warning to Sentry (open #68) since a 100%-failing write produced no alert for months. Fix under the existing #65 issue and re-verify by asserting behavior_profile is non-null for a test user after one compare.
findings.test_first: An integration test (live_db marker) that runs _update_behavior_profile for a seeded user against the real schema and asserts `users.behavior_profile` is non-null afterwards. A cheaper unit guard that would ALSO have caught this: a schema-contract test that reads the column list of each table from information_schema and asserts every column name appearing in a `.select(...)` string literal across app/ exists — that single test pins all three phantoms and the `response_data` class of bug for good.
findings.impact: Answers the lane's question precisely. COST PER COMPARE = exactly ONE wasted Supabase round trip (~165 ms measured dev-box, MODELLED lower from Railway), not four — the abort is early, so the phantom columns are cheaper than they look. The real damage is the silence: 0 of 18 users have ever had a behavior_profile written, so scs._fetch_behavior_profile (line 4524, which reads a column that DOES exist) always returns None, the /home/smart-pick dimension_sensitivity Tier-2 fallback (home_routes.py:628-640) never fires, and every 'personalized' code path downstream runs on defaults. Personalization is not degraded, it has never once worked in production. Two of the three phantom columns are the same class of bug as the `response_data` phantom that broke referral landings (fixed 2026-09-02) — the pattern is unfixed.

verdict_trail.reason: Confirmed at the cited line, with one evidence correction. All three phantom columns verified live (comparisons.category_used and .products -> 42703; user_events.metadata -> 42703, real column is event_data); comparison_feedback.useful is valid. The three run_db calls are sequential inside one try, so 4545 raises straight to the except at 4553 and the users.update at 4552 never runs — abort-on-first-query, i.e. one wasted round trip, is right. CORRECTION: the decisive number is wrong. behavior_profile is NOT null for anyone — all 18 users have it set to the empty dict {}. The conclusion survives because _fetch_behavior_profile tests truthiness ('if result.data and result.data.get("behavior_profile")'), so {} is falsy and personalization is still dead for 18/18. Correctly deduped to open #65; the user_events.metadata phantom and the abort semantics are fresh.

findings.title: GET /history selects * (pulling ~19 KB of full_response per row) to build a summary that never reads it, then spends a second client and an exact COUNT on the same page
findings.dedupe: new — M13/M18 covered the history route's rendering and pagination but not its projection or its double client construction.
findings.fix: Project only what the route uses. The two image URLs and winner_index come out of full_response.products, so either (a) select `id, query, product_names, input_type, created_at, full_response->'winner_index', full_response->'products'` using PostgREST's jsonb path projection to avoid hauling verdicts/specs/reviews, or (b) better, persist winner_index and the two image URLs as real columns at save time (a small migration) and drop full_response from the list query entirely. Reuse ONE client for both the page and the count by threading it through get_user_comparisons/get_user_comparison_count instead of each calling the factory. And return the count only when offset==0, or switch to `count='planned'`, so paging does not re-COUNT.
findings.test_first: A test that stubs the supabase client and asserts the select string passed for GET /history does NOT contain '*' and DOES contain exactly the projected columns; plus a call-counter assertion that get_user_supabase_client is invoked once, not twice, per /history request.
findings.impact: Three costs on the single-worker loop for one screen open: ~387-968 KB of wire transfer and jsonb deserialisation that is thrown away; a second create_client (see LS-DB-QUERIES-01, ~2 SSLContexts for this one route on top of verify_token's); and a `count="exact"` which makes Postgres do a real COUNT over the user's filtered set on every page rather than once. The index (user_id, schema_version, created_at DESC) from migration 020 covers the WHERE+ORDER correctly, so this is pure payload and round-trip waste, not a plan problem. It scales with history length in bytes-per-page and is the single largest avoidable transfer on any user-facing read.

verdict_trail.reason: All three legs verified at HEAD: select("*") at database_service.py:250, the route builds only id/query/product_names/input_type/winner_index/two image URLs/created_at and never returns full_response, and get_user_comparison_count at 442-455 constructs a SECOND client and runs count="exact" on every page (its .execute() is also not run_db-wrapped, unlike the page query). Payload arithmetic recomputed and correct: 20 x 19,359 B = 387 KB, 50 x = 968 KB, against ~8 KB emitted. Title corrected — full_response IS read (winner_index and products[*] images), it is just never returned, so the projection fix must keep the jsonb paths the route consumes. P2 is right: measurable transfer/round-trip cost on a user-facing read, no incorrect output.

findings.title: product_prices is append-only with no retention and the hot read sorts up to 416 rows to return 1, because the only index lacks fetched_at
findings.dedupe: new — #57 (L2 promote freshness) and #56 (category into _get_price) touch this module's semantics, not its index or its growth. Not in M18/M13.
findings.fix: Two changes, both small. (1) Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_prices_key_region_fetched ON product_prices (product_key, region, fetched_at DESC);` in a new migration — this makes the hot read a single index-only fetch of the first entry regardless of history depth, and makes idx_prices_key_region redundant (drop it in the same migration). (2) Add retention: either a scheduled job that keeps the newest N (say 10) rows per (product_key, region) and deletes the rest, or — since the read only ever wants the newest — change the write to an upsert on (product_key, region) and keep history in a separate append table only if the price-history feature is actually wanted. Prefer the index first (zero behaviour change, ship immediately); gate any deletion behind an explicit flag and a dry-run count.
findings.test_first: There is no cheap unit test for a missing index. The honest red test is a live_db benchmark: seed 500 rows for one (product_key, region), time get_cached_price, then assert it stays under a fixed budget — it fails before the index and passes after. Pair it with a static test asserting the migration set contains an index whose columns are exactly (product_key, region, fetched_at) so the index cannot be dropped silently.
findings.impact: For the hottest key Postgres must fetch all 416 index entries for that (product_key, region), heap-access them for fetched_at, sort, and discard 415 — twice per compare (once per product), on the L2 lookup that is supposed to be the CHEAP path that avoids a scrape. The table has no cleanup job of any kind (grepped all migrations and app/ for delete/retention/cleanup/purge/prune — only delete_user_cascade exists), so both the row count and the per-key sort depth grow without bound; the newest row is dated 2026-09-01, i.e. it is still growing. At 3,945 rows this is microseconds, but the growth is unbounded and the read is on the critical path of every comparison.

verdict_trail.reason: Every measured number reproduced exactly on my own full paging scan, and the code/index claims are literally true: the read orders by fetched_at DESC LIMIT 1 while the only matching index is (product_key, region), the write is a plain .insert (never an upsert), and there is no retention path anywhere in app/, scripts/ or migrations/. But the impact today is sub-millisecond by the finder's own admission ("At 3,945 rows this is microseconds"), the table accrued only 3,945 rows over the product's whole life, and the harm is entirely growth-projected — that is P3 ("nit/latent") on the brief scale, not a measurable cost issue. The proposed fix is correct and flag-safe (a pure additive index is a zero-behaviour-change migration; deletion correctly gated behind a flag + dry run).

findings.title: user_events has no index of any kind, yet is read with eq(user_id) + order(created_at DESC) on the compare path and written once per comparison
findings.dedupe: new — no prior review enumerated indexes per table. Adjacent to #74 (bound behaviour-profile recompute) only in that both touch this query.
findings.fix: Add a migration with `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_events_user_created ON user_events (user_id, created_at DESC);` — this covers scs.py:4547, admin_routes.py:375 and the cohort view join. Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_events_comparison ON user_events (comparison_id);` too, since 013's view and the cascade delete both key on it. No code change and no flag needed — an index addition is behaviour-preserving. Do it in the same migration that fixes the phantom `metadata` column in LS-DB-QUERIES-04, since neither is useful without the other.
findings.test_first: A static test over migrations/ asserting that every table read with a `.eq(<col>).order(<col2>)` pattern in app/ has a migration index whose leading columns match — generated from the enumeration in this review, it would flag user_events today and prevent the next table from shipping without one.
findings.impact: Every read is a sequential scan plus a sort. At 146 rows that is free, so nothing is broken now. But user_events is written once per comparison (comparison_completed) plus once per analytics batch, so it grows strictly faster than the comparisons table; migration 013's vw_cohort_feedback_lift view joins it, and admin_routes.py:362-380 loops over up to N users issuing one user_events query EACH inside a Python for-loop (an N+1 that becomes N sequential seq-scans). This is the cheapest fix in the lane and the one most likely to be forgotten until it is a production incident, because there is no failing signal until the table is large.

verdict_trail.reason: Code and migration claims hold exactly. But user_events is never CREATEd in migrations either, so the live index state is not knowable from the repo and I could not check it (PostgREST EXPLAIN disabled: PGRST107). Measured impact today is nil — 146 rows, and the finder's own timing was indistinguishable from any round trip. Per the brief scale that is latent, not a 'measurable quality/cost issue' → P3. Fix rationale has an error: migration 025 cascades on user_id, not comparison_id. Index is genuinely new vs M18/M13.

findings.title: /profile/monthly-stats runs an unbounded full_response month scan with zero run_db coverage — profile_routes is the only route module that never offloads a single query
findings.dedupe: new — M18's LS-event-loop findings and #71 established the blocking-on-loop theme and #115/M13-05 built run_db; no prior review enumerated WHICH call sites were left unwired, and profile_routes was not touched in 593ec1e..76ace90 so it was never re-checked.
findings.fix: Wire profile_routes into the existing offload: import run_db and _redis_get_async/_redis_set_async (or the module-local dispatch idiom home_routes already uses, so tests can patch a module-level symbol in both branches) and wrap all four .execute() calls plus the cache reads — flag OFF stays byte-identical by construction, so this is a safe no-flag change. Separately, replace the monthly-stats scan with a month-scoped variant of the migration-036 aggregate (add a p_month_start argument, or a second function) so the endpoint stops moving verdict blobs to compute a sum; keep it dark under the same ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE-style flag until 036 is actually applied.
findings.test_first: A test that patches app.utils.db_offload.sync_db_offload_enabled to True, monkeypatches asyncio.to_thread with a counter, hits GET /api/v1/profile/monthly-stats and asserts the counter is >0 — red today (zero offloads), green once wired. Plus the 1000-row truncation test from LS-DB-QUERIES-03 applied to the month window.
findings.impact: Two distinct problems in one module. (a) The month scan is the second unbounded user-facing full_response scan; it hauls whole verdict payloads to sum two floats per row, and it will silently under-report savings for any user exceeding 1000 comparisons in a month. (b) More consequential for the load story: ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is the deployment's lever for getting blocking DB work off the single event loop, and flipping it moves NOTHING in profile_routes — 4 blocking Supabase calls and a blocking Redis GET stay on the loop, plus the client construction from LS-DB-QUERIES-01. Anyone measuring the flag's effect will conclude it under-delivers without knowing which sites were never wired.

verdict_trail.reason: Verified at 76ace90: monthly-stats selects full_response for the whole month with no .limit(); referral_redemptions read is likewise unbounded; recent-decisions is limit(3); none of the four .execute() calls or the three cache reads use run_db/_redis_get_async. The 9-module run_db importer list is exactly right and excludes profile_routes. Reachable from the shipped app (api.ts:1163, HistoryScreen). ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is absent from Railway web vars, so half (b) is latent; the unbounded blob scan is live. Arithmetic checks out. One cite nit: the sync _redis_get is line 296, not 299.

findings.title: Admin 'top queries' ranks an arbitrary unordered 1000-row slice of 16,283 search_logs and reports it as popular queries
findings.dedupe: new — open #66 (admin cost meters wrong) covers the cost METERS' arithmetic; the silent 1000-row truncation feeding four analytics functions is a different mechanism and is not in #66, M18 or M13.
findings.fix: Stop pulling rows to count them. Each of these four is an aggregate: push them into Postgres as SECURITY DEFINER RPCs the way migration 036 does for savings (a GROUP BY query for popular queries; SUM/COUNT grouped by day for cost trends; COUNT grouped by error_message for error stats) and return a handful of rows. If an RPC is too much for now, the minimum honest fix is to add an explicit `.order('created_at', desc=True).limit(1000)` so the sample is at least the MOST RECENT 1000 and to stamp `"truncated": true, "sampled_rows": 1000` into every response so the dashboard cannot present a sample as a total. Same treatment for the unbounded `products` scan at :163.
findings.test_first: Stub the client to return exactly 1000 rows for an unbounded select and assert get_popular_queries either raises, pages, or sets truncated=true — red today, since it silently returns a top-20 computed from the partial set.
findings.impact: The admin analytics surface is quietly wrong, and wrong in a way that looks plausible. Because there is no ORDER BY, the 1000 rows PostgREST returns are whatever the plan yields — typically the physical/insert order, i.e. the OLDEST 1000 of 16,283 — so 'popular queries' reflects mid-June traffic and nothing since. get_cost_trends and get_error_stats (exposed at admin_routes.py:72 and :83) silently drop everything past 1000 rows in any window that large, under-reporting spend and error volume with no indicator. Anyone using this dashboard to decide whether the product is working is reading a stale 6% sample. Admin-only, so not user-facing — hence P2, not P1.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced the mechanism against prod. get_popular_queries has no .limit/.order/.gte; the three siblings only filter by date; products scan is unbounded. Measured: an unbounded search_logs select returns exactly 1000 of 16,283 rows and Content-Range 0-999, and the rows returned are the OLDEST (created_at 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-21) — so 'popular queries' today ranks March traffic, precisely as claimed. /stats/costs allows days up to 365, so that one truncates today too. Admin-key-gated, no user harm or spend → P2 correct. Not covered by M18 CD-uncovered-03 (admin_routes sites only) or M13-98 (/costs).

findings.title: Admin cost dashboard asks for 2000 comparisons and PostgREST hands back exactly 1000, so the monthly spend figure is silently halved at scale
findings.dedupe: new — related to open #66 (admin cost meters wrong) but a distinct mechanism (transport-level truncation of a deliberate bound, not meter arithmetic).
findings.fix: Same shape as LS-DB-QUERIES-09: this is an aggregate, so move it into Postgres — a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that returns (day, sum_cost, sample_count) grouped by day over the cutoff, which is one small round trip and no cap. As an interim, page with `.range()` until a short page is returned and add `.order('created_at', desc=True)` so a truncated result is at least the most recent window, and surface `truncated`/`rows_scanned` in the response body. Also project `full_response->'metadata'->>'total_cost'` instead of the whole blob so the transfer drops from ~19 MB to a few hundred KB, and route it through run_db.
findings.test_first: A test asserting that when the stubbed client returns exactly the requested limit the route either pages again or marks the result truncated — and, more valuable, a shared regression test that no `.limit(n)` with n > 1000 exists anywhere in app/, since the value is unachievable and therefore always misleading.
findings.impact: An explicit .limit() reads like a deliberate safety bound and is treated as one by every reader of this code, but half of it is fiction. Once the window contains more than 1000 comparisons the dashboard's openai_total and daily_burn are computed from an unordered ~1000-row subset and under-report spend without any indicator — on a cost dashboard, silently under-reporting is the worst possible direction to be wrong in. Secondary cost: at the measured median full_response of 19,026 B this route pulls ~19 MB (1000 rows) to sum one float per row, on the shared event loop, and it is not run_db-wrapped. Admin-only, days is capped at 90, and prod traffic is currently near zero, so this is P2.

verdict_trail.reason: Code and the transport measurement are both right: .limit(2000) at line 735 and I reproduced limit=2000 → 1000 rows, limit=999 → 999. But there is no live wrongness: comparisons holds 27 rows total, all created_at <= 2026-06-21, so any window <= 90 days returns far under the cap and the ~19 MB transfer figure is hypothetical. The identical defect on the sibling route (/costs, admin_routes.py:110, still unbounded at HEAD) is already filed as M13-98 at P3, so P2 here is inconsistent as well as unmeasurable. Latent → P3.

findings.title: P3 sweep — five smaller DB-layer defects: no retention on any growth table, smart-pick over-fetch, an exception per L2 specs miss, an admin N+1, and an unbounded fingerprint fan-in
findings.dedupe: new — (a) is adjacent to open #80 (cron failure visibility) but that issue presumes crons exist; none of (b)-(e) appear in M18, M13, the mobile checkup or the 33 open issues.
findings.fix: (a) Add a retention policy per table in one migration + a scheduled job: search_logs and user_events keep 90 days, admin_audit_log keeps 1 year (check any compliance requirement first), product_prices keep newest N per (product_key, region) as in LS-DB-QUERIES-06. Make the job report to the same place #80 wants cron failures to go. (b) Project the four fields _select_smart_pick actually reads instead of full_response, and wrap both queries in run_db to match the savings path in the same module. (c) Replace `.single()` with `.maybe_single()` (or `.limit(1)` and check the list) so a miss is a None, not a raise. (d) Replace the per-user loop with one `user_events` query using `.in_("user_id", uids)` and group in Python. (e) Add `.limit(50)` and treat hitting the limit as itself an abuse signal. Ship (c) and (e) immediately (both are one-liners with no behaviour change on the success path); (a) needs a product decision on retention windows before it can land.
findings.test_first: For (c), a unit test asserting get_cached_specs returns None for an unknown product_key WITHOUT any exception being raised or logged — red today. For (a), a static test asserting every table in the migration set is named in a retention config file, so a new growth table cannot ship without an explicit keep-forever decision. For (d), a call-counter test asserting the cohort-retention route issues O(1) user_events queries rather than O(users).
findings.impact: None of these is harmful at current scale — hence P3 as a group. Ranked by when they start to matter: (a) is the one with no natural ceiling and no owner, and it silently raises the cost of every unbounded scan already reported in this lane; (d) becomes a real admin timeout once the user table grows, and compounds with the missing user_events index; (b) is ~95 KB and two on-loop blocking calls per home screen open; (c) is a hot-path exception on the normal cache-miss branch, which is both slower than a None return and noisy in any profiler; (e) is a correctness risk only if a fingerprint is ever shared widely, in which case the abuse cap reads a truncated set.

verdict_trail.reason: All five sub-claims hold at HEAD; (c) reproduced live. But the dedupe line is wrong: (b) is M18 LS-event-loop-06 ('/home/smart-pick pulls 5 complete full_response payloads through a sync execute on the loop', P2, line moved 550→653) and (d) is M18 CD-uncovered-03 item (2) ('one user_events query PER USER inside the loop', P2) — both still open, neither new. (a), (c), (e) are new. (e) is in practice bounded by the same 1000-row PostgREST cap. 5 x 19,026 = 95 KB checks out.

findings.title: Every in-app result feedback is 422-rejected and lost: FeedbackCard's chips (accurate/detailed/fast) are not in the backend's VALID_MATTERED_MOST allowlist, and the UI shows "thanks" anyway
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Pick one direction and pin it with a test. Cheapest: map the three UI chips to allowlist members at the send site (accurate->'specs'? no — better) OR extend VALID_MATTERED_MOST in app/api/feedback_routes.py:37 with the three quality chips ('accurate','detailed','fast') the UI actually emits, exactly as VALID_LIFESTYLE was extended for the LifestylePicker vocabulary (auth_routes.py:150-157 documents that precedent and the same 'save didn't land' symptom). Then add the superset guard: tests/test_events_allowlist_superset.py already greps FE src/ for event_type literals — clone it for mattered_most so a future chip rename cannot silently re-break this. No flag needed; the change is additive and backwards compatible.
findings.test_first: A backend test that greps SmartCompareApp/src for `mattered_most: [` literals and asserts every literal chip key is in VALID_MATTERED_MOST (mirror of tests/test_events_allowlist_superset.py) — red today on accurate/detailed/fast. Plus a jest test that mocks api.post and asserts submitFeedback is called with a payload FeedbackRequest accepts.
findings.impact: 100% of the app's only in-result feedback control is silently discarded server-side. Zero comparison_feedback rows can ever be written from the shipped client, so the `useful` signal, migration-027 feedback correctness work, the cohort feedback-lift view (vw_cohort_feedback_lift) and the admin /cohort/feedback dashboard have no input at all. Users are shown a 'thanks' state for a write that never happened. Orthogonal to (and not fixed by) the 2026-09-02 comparison_id-as-query fix: this rejects on mattered_most, so it fails even on the History path where comparison_id IS a valid UUID.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced against the real model. UI chips accurate/detailed/fast are outside the backend allowlist, so every in-result feedback POST 422s while the card unconditionally shows the thanks state. Present in the shipped 97b5f15 bundle too, so it is live on phones, not just on main. Not in M18/M13/mobile-checkup rows or the 33 open issues; orthogonal to the comparison_id fix (rejection is on mattered_most). File/line/title accurate; fix (extend VALID_MATTERED_MOST + superset grep test) is additive and flag-free.

Wire-level repro: TestClient on the real feedback router returns HTTP 422 VALIDATION_ERROR for each of the three chips the shipped UI sends and HTTP 200 for 'price'. FE grep confirms MATTERED_OPTIONS keys are exactly accurate/detailed/fast, none in VALID_MATTERED_MOST, no mapping in api.ts:801-809; FeedbackCard.tsx:57-61 catches and sets the thanks state anyway. `git show 97b5f15:...FeedbackCard.tsx` proves the same chips are on the phone bundle, so it is live on devices too. ContactUsScreen sends [] and passes, so this is 100% of the result-feedback control. Fix (extend the allowlist) closes the repro; test_first (superset grep mirroring test_events_allowlist_superset) is the right red test.

findings.title: A transient Supabase outage force-logs-out every user: POST /auth/refresh returns 401 for its OWN upstream connection failure, and the client treats any 401 as "session definitively dead" and wipes the refresh token
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Backend: in app/api/auth_routes.py:539, branch on the categorised error — only credential/invalid-refresh-token failures raise 401; upstream connection/timeout failures raise HTTPException(503, detail={"code":"REFRESH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE","error":...}) so the unified envelope carries a distinguishable code. Give _categorize_auth_error a stable code field rather than matching on English substrings. Client: in authService.ts:283-297 treat sessionInvalid=true only for 401 AND (no code, or code in {AUTH_REQUIRED, INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN}); every 5xx and every network error must keep the session (it already does for non-401). Ship the backend half first — it is server-side and reaches phones without an OTA; the client half needs the next eas update.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test that patches app.services.auth_service.refresh_session to raise ConnectionError and asserts POST /api/v1/auth/refresh returns 503 with code REFRESH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, not 401. Client: a jest test that mocks api.post to reject with {response:{status:503,data:{code:'REFRESH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE'}}} and asserts clearSession was NOT called and sessionInvalid is falsy.
findings.impact: Any Railway->Supabase blip, DNS hiccup, or Supabase maintenance window during a boot refresh (App.tsx:189 initializeAuth, which runs on EVERY cold start) deletes both tokens from SecureStore (authService.ts:388-396) and returns the user to Login. Because initializeAuth is the first authed call of every session, one upstream blip logs out the entire active fleet simultaneously and the loss is unrecoverable without a password (or a Google/Apple re-consent). This also defeats the whole point of the M18 MB-flows-01 transient-vs-definitive split.

verdict_trail.reason: Read the whole path at HEAD. refresh_session catches EVERY exception and returns success:false (network branch or the else branch), and the route raises 401 unconditionally — so an upstream Supabase/DNS blip is indistinguishable from a dead token. Client clears the session on any 401, and initializeAuth runs refreshSession on every cold start, so one blip logs out the fleet. Static only (cannot induce a Supabase outage read-only), but every branch is determined by code. Fix (503 + stable code, client allowlist) is correct and backend half needs no OTA.

Both halves reproduced. Backend: get_auth_client patched to raise ConnectionError('getaddrinfo failed') -> POST /api/v1/auth/refresh returns HTTP 401 'Connection failed. Please try again.', indistinguishable from the invalid-token case (also 401). Broader than claimed: the `else` branch means ANY upstream exception yields 401. Client: a jest repro drove the real refreshSession with that 401 - sessionInvalid true and BOTH SecureStore tokens deleted; the contrast case (axios 'Network Error', no response) correctly keeps the session, proving the defect is the backend's mislabel. initializeAuth (authService.ts:442) runs this at every cold start. Fix closes both halves. test_first is nearly right but must patch get_auth_client (or the categorizer), not refresh_session - patching refresh_session to raise yields a 500, not the 401 path.

findings.title: Google/Apple signups never carry X-Device-Fingerprint and the social backend path never writes users.device_fingerprint_hash — the free-tier lifetime device lock and the referral device cap are both bypassed for every social account
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Client: in authService.ts, await getDeviceFingerprint() in both signInWithGoogle and signInWithApple and add it as an `X-Device-Fingerprint` header on the two raw fetches (same try/catch-tolerant pattern as register at :108-113 — never block sign-in on a fingerprint failure). Backend: extract the register block at auth_routes.py:365-391 into a shared `_apply_device_fingerprint(request, user_id)` helper and call it from social_login after a successful sign-in, reusing the existing _DEVICE_FINGERPRINT_RE validation so a garbage header still cannot poison a counter. Ship both halves; the backend half alone is inert (no header arrives), the client half alone is inert (nothing reads it on that route) — this is why the gap survived.
findings.test_first: Client jest: mock getDeviceFingerprint to return a known 64-hex string, call signInWithGoogle, assert global.fetch was called with headers containing 'X-Device-Fingerprint'. Backend: a route test posting /api/v1/auth/social-login with the header set and asserting the created user row has device_fingerprint_hash set and lifetime_comparisons_used inherited from a prior row on the same fingerprint.
findings.impact: Every user who signs up with Google or Apple gets users.device_fingerprint_hash = NULL. (a) Free-tier bypass: the migration-021 anti-farming gate that inherits lifetime_comparisons_used across re-signups on the same physical device does not apply — delete account, sign in with a second Google account, get a fresh lifetime-3 quota, repeatable indefinitely on one phone. (b) Referral abuse: LIFETIME_CAP in referral_service.py:685 fails open for social referrers, so the 3-lifetime-invites-per-device cap is unenforceable and each redeemed Loop-2 grant is 5 (free) or 10 (premium) bonus comparisons of real OpenAI+Serper spend. ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in prod today.

verdict_trail.reason: Grep and call-path reading confirm both halves: neither social fetch sends the header, and no backend social path writes device_fingerprint_hash (0 hits in auth_service.py; the inheritance write lives only in POST /register). Downstream fail-open verified in both consumers. Reachable in prod today: ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in the captured Railway web vars; no dark flag involved. New vs M18/M13/mobile rows and the 33 issues. Fix is correct and inert-until-both-halves-ship, as stated. Line 570 exact (Apple at 682-690).

Both halves reproduced independently. Client: jest drove the real signInWithGoogle with the native SDK mocked - fetch to /auth/social-login carried header keys exactly ['content-type'], no x-device-fingerprint, while the contrast test shows register() DOES send X-Device-Fingerprint. Backend: TestClient POST /auth/social-login WITH a valid 64-hex header, sign_in_with_social stubbed to succeed, admin Supabase client instrumented - ZERO table calls, so device_fingerprint_hash is never written (the inheritance block is register-only, auth_routes.py:365-391). Consequence chain verified in referral_service.py:786-798 (returns 0 without a hash) and abuse_detection_service.py:124-129. ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in the captured prod vars. Both fix halves are needed and close the repro; test_first is correct.

findings.title: The referral SAME_DEVICE abuse control can never fire: ShareBottomSheet's deviceFingerprintHash prop has no caller, so referral_invites.device_fingerprint_hash is always NULL
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: In ResultsScreen.tsx, resolve the fingerprint once (useEffect + getDeviceFingerprint(), swallow failures) and pass it to <ShareBottomSheet deviceFingerprintHash={fp} />; the wire format already matches the backend's `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` pattern since deviceFingerprint.ts:32-35 returns lowercase SHA-256 hex from expo-crypto. Alternatively call getDeviceFingerprint() inside ShareBottomSheet.handleTargetPress so no caller can forget it again — that is the safer shape given this prop has been optional-and-unset since it shipped. No flag needed; the field is already Optional server-side so nothing breaks during rollout.
findings.test_first: A jest test rendering ResultsScreen with a mocked getDeviceFingerprint, tapping a share target, and asserting the createShare payload contains a 64-char lowercase hex device_fingerprint_hash. Backend: a test asserting evaluate_invite returns flagged_reason=SAME_DEVICE when referrer and invitee share a hash — and a fixture check that the invite row written by POST /referrals/share is non-null.
findings.impact: Control 1 of the 3-control referral abuse system (documented priority order SAME_DEVICE > DISPOSABLE_EMAIL > BELOW_REAL_ACTION_THRESHOLD, abuse_detection_service.py:244-246) is dead code in production. The single most actionable fraud signal — one human running both sides of a referral on one phone — is never flagged, so /admin/referrals/abuse will report zero SAME_DEVICE flags no matter how much self-referral happens. Combined with MB-NETWORK-CONTRACT-03, both device-based referral defences are down while ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true.

verdict_trail.reason: Grep over SmartCompareApp/src returns exactly the three declaring lines and no caller; the sole mount passes visible/comparison/onClose/onShared/lifetimeRemaining only, so device_fingerprint_hash is always undefined on the wire and the invite row is NULL. Control 1 then short-circuits False. Stronger than the finder said: SAME_DEVICE does not merely flag — evaluate_invite's fail path returns before the grant, so the dead control also lets self-referral bonus credits (5 free / 10 premium) through. Live: ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true, and the prop is unset in the shipped 97b5f15 bundle too. Fix (resolve fp inside ShareBottomSheet) is right; wire format matches ^[a-f0-9]{64}$.

Reproduced by rendering ShareBottomSheet with the EXACT prop set its only mount site passes (ResultsScreen.tsx:797-810, verified unchanged at the shipped OTA 97b5f15) and pressing a share target: the createShare payload carried comparison_id 'cmp-1' and device_fingerprint_hash undefined, so referral_invites.device_fingerprint_hash is always NULL and abuse_detection_service._get_referrer_device_hash returns None -> is_same_device short-circuits False, making SAME_DEVICE unreachable in evaluate_invite (its only caller, referral_service.py:664). Harm is bounded - the 3-lifetime cap still works for email signups via users.device_fingerprint_hash - so P1 is at the low end but stands (dead abuse control + admin dashboard reports a false zero). Fix closes the repro; resolving the fp inside handleTargetPress is the safer shape, and then the component-level test I wrote is the right red test.

findings.title: RATE_LIMITED is unmapped everywhere on the client: a throttled text compare tells the user to "choose different products", and the URL/History/Profile paths render the backend's raw English "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to known:M18 MB-flows-11 which covered AUTH screens only)
findings.fix: Add `results.errors.rateLimited` / `home.errors.rateLimited` to en.json + ar.json ('We're busy right now — try again in a moment'), branch on `parsed.code === 'RATE_LIMITED'` in HomeScreen's two error handlers next to the existing TIMEOUT branch, add `if (status === 429) return 'timeout'` (or a new 'busy' kind) to classifyLoadFailure.ts, and replace every bare `parseApiError(err).message` render with a code-keyed lookup that falls back to neutral i18n copy (the pattern HomeScreen.tsx:394-399 already uses for text). Server-side, set a Retry-After header in rate_limit_handler so a future client can back off. No flag.
findings.test_first: jest: feed HomeScreen's onError a synthetic {response:{status:429,data:{code:'RATE_LIMITED',error:'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.'}}} and assert the alert body equals t('home.errors.rateLimited') and never contains 'Rate limit exceeded'. Repeat for the URL handler and HistoryScreen.loadHistory.
findings.impact: At the deployment-wide 10/min ceiling the app actively misleads: text users are told their products are the problem and are sent back to retype, which generates MORE requests against the same bucket; URL/History/Profile users see untranslated English that violates the no-scary-copy contract and is meaningless to Arabic users. There is no 'try again in a minute' copy anywhere in the app and no Retry-After is emitted or read. This is the failure mode a launch-day traffic spike produces first.

verdict_trail.reason: Every cited cell checked: backend emits code RATE_LIMITED on 429, the client has zero RATE_LIMITED references, api.ts intercepts 429 only for USAGE_LIMIT, the text path shows the wrong-products copy on any recognised code, and the URL/History/Profile/EditProfile/Results paths render parseApiError().message raw. classifyLoadFailure has no 429 branch so it falls to 'generic'. Trigger is real but needs the deployment-wide 10/min bucket to fill; prod traffic is ~zero today, so P2 (not P1) is right. Adjacent to but not a duplicate of M18 MB-flows-11 (auth screens) or #72 (limiter keying). Fix is correct, no flag.

findings.title: Profile privacy/notification toggles 422 for any user without a preferences row: buildNextPrefs sends priorities:[] against a min_length=1 model, then renders the raw Pydantic validation string
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: In ProfileScreen.tsx:131-143, when `previous?.priorities` is empty do not send a preferences PUT that cannot validate: either (a) route the two toggles through dedicated single-purpose endpoints the way the re-engagement sub-toggles already do (PUT /auth/reengagement-subs, api.ts:452-457) — add PUT /auth/ai-sharing and PUT /auth/notifications; or (b) relax UserPreferencesRequest.priorities to min_length=0 and let the downstream personalization treat empty as 'no stated priorities' (it already tolerates an absent prefs row at text_routes.py:340-344). (a) is the cleaner contract and matches the existing precedent. Either way, replace the `parseApiError(err).message ||` renders at :160/:183/:225/:298 with the i18n fallback first.
findings.test_first: jest: render ProfileScreen with getPreferences mocked to resolve null, tap the AI-sharing switch, assert either that no PUT /auth/preferences with priorities:[] is issued, or that the rendered error is t('profile.aiSharing.errorSave') and never contains 'Validation error'.
findings.impact: Any user who has not completed onboarding preferences cannot turn the AI-data-sharing opt-out (a PDPL/App-Store privacy control, ProfileScreen.tsx:127-129) or the notifications master toggle on or off. The switch flips, reverts, and shows an untranslated Pydantic string. That is a privacy control the user cannot exercise plus a copy-contract violation on the same tap.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced the 422 against the real model and read the full path: buildNextPrefs always sends priorities:[] when the cached prefs object is null, and getPreferences returns null both for a missing/{} row AND for ANY thrown error (bare catch), so a single failed prefs GET is enough to brick both toggles for any user. Rendered text is the raw Pydantic string. Same code in the shipped 97b5f15 bundle. One evidence nit: the rendered string is 'Validation error: body → priorities: …' (loc joined with ' → '), not 'Validation error: priorities: …'. P2 correct — needs prefs==null, not universal. Fix (a) matches the existing reengagement-subs precedent.

findings.title: No compare response ever echoes the saved comparison_id, so the referral share sheet is unreachable at the one high-intent moment and every feedback/event row from a fresh compare is unanchored
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-contract-03 (partial fix — History path only) — residual still-open
findings.fix: Make the save synchronous enough to return an id without adding user-visible latency: in text_routes.py (all three compare handlers) and in feedback_service.save_comparison_and_track_cohort, await only the `save_comparison` insert (a single PostgREST round trip, already on the hot path's tail) and keep the cohort-event + Loop-2 work fire-and-forget; stamp `result["comparison_id"] = saved["id"]` before returning. If the extra await is unacceptable on the single event loop, the alternative is to generate the row UUID client-side-of-the-DB (uuid4 in the route), pass it into save_comparison as an explicit id, and echo it immediately — zero added latency. Gate behind ENABLE_COMPARISON_ID_ECHO if you want a dark rollout; the client read at ResultsScreen.tsx:345 already tolerates the field being absent, so it is forward-compatible either way.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test asserting the JSON body of POST /api/v1/text/compare for an authenticated user contains a `comparison_id` that is a valid UUID and matches the row written to comparisons. Client jest: render ResultsScreen with a fresh-compare payload carrying comparison_id and assert ShareBottomSheet is mounted and trackEvents payloads carry that id.
findings.impact: Loop-1 — the growth mechanic the whole referral system exists for — can only be started from the History tab, never from the result the user is looking at seconds after their compare. Additionally every FeedbackCard submission and every ResultsScreen analytics event (share, share_sheet_opened, source_click, result_view_duration, demographics_*) fired from a fresh compare carries comparison_id: undefined, so user_events and comparison_feedback rows cannot be joined to the comparison they describe — which is exactly the join vw_cohort_feedback_lift and /admin/cohort/feedback depend on. M18 MB-contract-03 fixed the History half and explicitly left this half open.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced at 76ace90. All three compare handlers fire-and-forget the save and return the pre-save dict; no assignment of comparison_id onto any response exists in app/. The id is created only inside the background coroutine. Client correctly documents and tolerates the absence, so ShareBottomSheet is gated off and every fresh-compare event/feedback row is unanchored. P1 stands: user-reachable on the shipped bundle, and it blocks the referral Loop-1 mechanic. Fix is sound; the uuid4-in-route variant is the flag-safe one (no added await on the single loop).

Route-level repro, not reading: TestClient on the real text_routes router, authenticated via get_optional_user override, service/save stubbed. POST /api/v1/text/compare returned HTTP 200 whose body keys are exactly [metadata,overview,products,reviews,scoring,specs,success] - 'comparison_id' absent from the whole response text - while the fire-and-forget save side did produce a row id. Client side reproduces the consequence by construction (ResultsScreen.tsx:345/445/797 gates ShareBottomSheet on that id; the code comments admit it). Proposed fix (await only the insert, or pre-generate the uuid, then stamp result['comparison_id']) closes my repro exactly. test_first is right; note save_comparison does not currently accept an explicit id, so the zero-latency variant needs a signature change.

findings.title: An expired access token silently downgrades every compare to anonymous, and the 401-refresh interceptor can NEVER re-drive it because no compare route returns 401
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup section B lead 'expired access token silently downgrades a compare to anonymous' — still-open; this adds the answered question (the interceptor cannot re-drive it) and the no-AppState-refresh proof
findings.fix: Two independent halves. (1) Client: refresh proactively — decode the JWT `exp` (or store expires_at, which auth_service.py:202 already returns in the session) and have the request interceptor await getOrStartRefresh() when the token is within ~60s of expiry; and add an AppState 'active' listener that refreshes on resume. (2) Backend: make the silent downgrade visible — when an Authorization header is PRESENT but verify_token returns None, get_optional_user should signal it (either raise 401 so the existing interceptor self-heals, or stamp `metadata.auth_downgraded=true` on the response). Raising 401 is the cleaner fix and makes the interceptor do the job it was written for, but it changes the anonymous-caller contract, so gate it behind ENABLE_STRICT_OPTIONAL_AUTH (default OFF) and flip after the client-side proactive refresh has shipped in an OTA.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test asserting GET /api/v1/text/compare with an expired Bearer returns 401 under ENABLE_STRICT_OPTIONAL_AUTH=1 and 200-anonymous with the flag off. Client jest: fake a token whose exp is in the past, call streamComparison, assert refreshSession was invoked before the compare request went out.
findings.impact: A logged-in user gets an unpersonalised comparison that never appears in History, is never metered against their quota, and produces no comparison_id — while the app still shows them as signed in. The local counter drifts up while the server counter does not, so the client paywall and the server gate disagree in the user's disfavour. Silent: nothing surfaces, no Sentry event. Also means free-tier metering is trivially evadable by sitting on an expired token.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. get_optional_user swallows a bad/expired Bearer and returns None; verify_token's except returns None. All three text compare routes take it as an optional dep and POST /url/compare has no user dep at all. Client: getToken is a bare SecureStore read, no expires_at/exp anywhere, no AppState listener outside onboardingDraft, and the 401 interceptor short-circuits at api.ts:156 so it can never re-drive a 200-anonymous compare. Narrower than stated (any other authed 401 — history/profile/preferences — does drive a refresh), so the window is resume-then-immediately-Compare. P2 correct.

findings.title: ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE is a placebo: the only gated route the app reaches (/image/identify) is never sent X-Device-Fingerprint, and the three main compare routes have no anonymous gate at all
findings.dedupe: new (precondition for known:#128)
findings.fix: Before #128 is enabled: (1) send X-Device-Fingerprint on the camera identify fetch (api.ts:216-219 — await getDeviceFingerprint() next to getToken(), same swallow-on-failure pattern as authService.ts:108-113); (2) attach it to the axios instance globally in the request interceptor so every route can meter, not just the two that check; (3) extend the gate to GET/POST /text/compare and GET /text/compare/stream, which are the routes that actually cost money. Also record in the issue that fingerprint-based anon metering is advisory-only against a non-app client — the shared-edge-IP limiter (#114) remains the only involuntary control, which is exactly why #114's ordering rule must hold.
findings.test_first: Client jest: mock getDeviceFingerprint, call identifyFromImages, assert the fetch headers include X-Device-Fingerprint. Backend: a route test with ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE=1 asserting that an unauthenticated POST /api/v1/image/identify WITHOUT the header is refused (or at minimum logged as unmeterable) rather than silently running a paid Vision call.
findings.impact: Issue #128 queues ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE for activation; flipping it today changes nothing observable — device_fp stays None on every request, check_anon_usage_allowed never runs, record_anon_comparison never fires. Worse, the gate's stated purpose ('a caller could bypass the 3-lifetime/10-monthly tier by never signing in', text_routes.py:716-717) cannot be met by a scheme that depends on the caller volunteering an identifier, and the routes an unauthenticated abuser would actually hit are ungated. Capped at P2 because the flag is dark today (absent from the Railway web vars = OFF), but this is a hard precondition on #128 and on the refund wiring that issue tracks.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced exactly. The identify header object is Authorization-only; X-Device-Fingerprint has one send site in the whole app (register). The gate exists on exactly two routes, one of which the client never calls (no /text/quick reference in src). ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE is absent from the Railway web vars, so the gate is dark and P2 is the right cap — but the finding is correctly framed as a hard precondition on #128: flipping the flag today changes nothing observable, and the three routes that actually cost money are ungated. Fix is correct and flag-free on the client side.

findings.title: URL-compare failures collapse every structured code to BAD_REQUEST, so the client's CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE content-safety branch is dead on the URL path and the raw backend string is rendered instead
findings.dedupe: known:#69 (url/quick failures via D2 helper) — still-open; the dead client CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE branch is the new consequence
findings.fix: Replace both raise sites in url_routes.py (:157-161 and :180-184) with `surfaced = _surface_comparison_failure(result); if surfaced is not None: return surfaced` exactly as text_routes.py:250-256 does — import the helper rather than duplicating it. This is issue #69's body; doing it also closes the client-side dead branch for free. No flag: it strictly widens the codes the client already knows how to handle.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test patching compare_from_urls to return {'success':False,'code':'CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE','layer':'x'} and asserting POST /api/v1/url/compare returns 200 with code CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE (not 400/BAD_REQUEST), plus a TIMEOUT case asserting 503+code TIMEOUT.
findings.impact: On the URL entry mode the content-safety block screen (handleContentUnavailable -> the 'we can't compare this' alert with the tracked compare_entry_content_block event) is unreachable, so blocked-category URL compares are reported to the user as a generic failure with an untranslated backend sentence, and the analytics event that measures content blocking is never fired for URL mode. Timeouts on the URL path likewise arrive as 400 BAD_REQUEST instead of 503 TIMEOUT, so the soft retry copy never shows there either.

verdict_trail.reason: The route half reproduces (plain-string detail -> _is_structured_detail False -> code BAD_REQUEST), but the impact chain does not. compare_from_urls' only failure return is {success, error, details} with NO code key, and no CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE or TIMEOUT is produced anywhere on the URL path (grep: those codes live only in structured_comparison_service/image_routes). Applying _surface_comparison_failure would hit `if code:` falsy and raise the identical 400 plain string. The client branch is dead, but because the service never emits the code, not because the route flattens it. Latent tidy-up = P3.

findings.title: SSE terminal latch still ignores settle_complete — flag-ON streaming can pay for a second full compare after a successful settle
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #7 — still-open at HEAD (fresh line api.ts:713)
findings.fix: Treat settle_complete as terminal in api.ts: set `sawTerminal = true; clearWatchdog();` inside the case, and dedupe against `complete` while both events coexist (a `deliveredComplete` boolean so onSettleComplete after onComplete only updates, never re-latches). This must land BEFORE ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE is flipped — record it as a flip precondition next to the certificate-pinning one already documented at features.ts:44-51.
findings.test_first: jest: with _setExpoFetchSseForTests(true) and a mocked expo/fetch stream that emits settle_complete then throws, assert runRestCompare (api.get on /text/compare) was called ZERO times and onError never fired.
findings.impact: Latent. The instant ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE is flipped (the checkup's fix (b) for the dead progress UI), a stream whose only terminal event is settle_complete re-runs the entire comparison over REST: double OpenAI + double Serper spend per tap and double metering, which is precisely the #118 pathology the latch was added to remove. It also breaks outright when Bundle F drops the duplicate `complete` event. Capped at P2 per the dark-flag rule.

verdict_trail.reason: The line reproduces verbatim: case 'settle_complete' sets neither sawTerminal nor clearWatchdog. But the double-spend chain fails at HEAD three ways: (1) ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT=false, so the shipped path is REST; (2) every backend yield site emits ('settle_complete', x) immediately followed by ('complete', x), which latches; (3) onSettleComplete has NO consumer in the app, so on a settle-only terminal the user has received nothing and the REST fallback is correct, not a double charge for a delivered result. Real residual is the Bundle-F precondition. P3.

findings.title: Social-login raw fetches still have no timeout and no AbortController — a stalled sign-in hangs until the OS socket timeout (camera identify IS now bounded)
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #8 — camera half FIXED (api.ts:229-307), social-login half still-open
findings.fix: Wrap both fetches in the same AbortController + setTimeout pattern already proven at api.ts:229-307, with a ~30s budget (sign-in is a single Supabase round trip, not a compare), and map AbortError to the existing 'Sign-in cancelled'/network error return so the screens' current error rendering keeps working. No flag.
findings.test_first: jest: mock global.fetch to return a never-resolving promise, call signInWithGoogle with fake timers advanced past the budget, assert it resolves {success:false} rather than hanging.
findings.impact: A Google or Apple sign-in against a stalled connection leaves the button spinner up until the platform socket timeout (minutes on iOS), with no cancel and no error path, on the very first screen a new user sees. Duration needs a device to measure.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. Both social-login fetches are unbounded — grep for AbortController and 'signal:' in authService.ts returns zero hits, while api.ts does create a controller with IDENTIFY_TIMEOUT_MS for the camera path, so the camera half of mobile-checkup #8 is indeed fixed and the social half is not. Google's call at least has a catch that reports to Sentry; Apple's has neither timeout nor local catch. P2 is right: needs a stalled network to bite, no data loss, but it hangs the first screen a new user sees with no cancel. Fix (same AbortController pattern, ~30s) is correct and needs no flag.

findings.title: Force-update remains a dead wire: GET /api/v1/app/version is mounted and configurable but has zero client call sites, so APP_FORCE_UPDATE can never reach a phone
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #9 — still-open at HEAD
findings.fix: Add a fire-and-forget `GET /api/v1/app/version` in App.tsx's init (after fonts, before the auth check, with a short ~5s per-call timeout so it can never delay boot), compare against expo-application's nativeApplicationVersion with a real semver comparator, and render a blocking update screen only when `force_update && current < min_version`. Set the three APP_* vars on the Railway web service so the endpoint stops serving defaults. Ship the client half behind a remote-off default (force_update=false) so the first OTA that carries it is inert until you choose to use it, and unit-test the comparator (1.0.10 vs 1.0.9) before trusting it.
findings.test_first: jest: mock the version endpoint to return {min_version:'2.0.0', force_update:true} with a native version of '1.0.0' and assert the update gate renders; then min_version '1.0.0' and assert it does not. Plus a table test on the semver comparator covering 1.0.10>1.0.9 and 1.2.0>1.10.0 ordering.
findings.impact: There is no kill switch. If a shipped build has to be stopped (a bricking cert-pin rotation like 2026-07-06, a broken payment path, a legal takedown), the only lever is an EAS OTA to the preview channel — which cannot help a build whose network layer is the thing that broke. This is a launch-readiness gap, not a runtime bug, which is why it keeps surviving reviews.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced fully. Endpoint exists and is mounted; client has zero call sites (only node_modules noise); no APP_* var on the Railway web service, so it serves 1.0.0/false defaults. Correctly rated P2 — launch-readiness gap, no runtime harm today. Fix is sound and flag-safe (ships inert at force_update=false). Dedupe holds: mobile-checkup #9, still-open at HEAD.

findings.title: POST /image/identify is still completely unmetered for authenticated users, and POST /url/compare still has no auth dependency, no metering and no history save
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #1 and #6 — both still-open at HEAD, re-verified post-M21 (image_routes.py and url_routes.py untouched in 593ec1e..76ace90)
findings.fix: Mirror the text-route bracket in both. image_routes.py: consume_comparison_credit before the Vision call, refund_comparison_credit when fewer than 2 products are identified, record_lifetime_comparison on success. url_routes.py: add `user: Optional[Dict] = Depends(get_optional_user)`, the same consume/refund/record bracket, and a fire-and-forget save_comparison_and_track_cohort(input_type='url'); while there, add `selected_category: Optional[str]` to URLCompareRequest (the client has been sending it since the catfix and Pydantic's extra='ignore' has been dropping it, so the category chip is a no-op on the URL path) — or stop sending it at HomeScreen.tsx:433. No flag needed for metering; it is the documented intended behaviour.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test for POST /api/v1/image/identify as an authenticated user at the lifetime cap asserting 429 USAGE_LIMIT and that consume_comparison_credit was called; a second asserting refund on a 1-product identify. For POST /api/v1/url/compare, assert a comparisons row is written and the lifetime counter increments for an authenticated caller.
findings.impact: Two server-side freemium bypasses on routes the shipped app reaches from its own UI. A signed-in free user past every daily/monthly/lifetime cap can run unlimited full Vision+OpenAI+Serper comparisons through the camera tab and unlimited compares through the URL tab; no counter moves in either case. URL compares additionally never appear in History (so the user loses them) and produce no cohort/Loop-2 signal. Real OpenAI+Serper spend per call.

verdict_trail.reason: Both halves reproduced. image_routes.py's only gate is the dark anon flag (ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE absent from Railway vars, code default OFF) and it is `and not user` — so an AUTHENTICATED caller is unmetered regardless of the flag; no consume/refund/record anywhere. url_routes.compare_urls takes no user dependency and neither meters nor persists. Text routes do all three, proving intent. Not dark-flag-gated; reachable from the shipped camera and URL tabs. P1 correct (no P0 upgrade: OpenAI quota is exhausted and prod traffic is ~0, so no spend is leaking right now). Fix is right, including the URLCompareRequest gap.

Functional repro, not grep: every usage_service entry point (consume_comparison_credit, record_lifetime_comparison, record_comparison, check_usage_allowed, refund, get_usage_status) was stubbed to record the call and answer 'not allowed'; an authenticated POST /api/v1/image/identify with two identified products returned HTTP 200 action='comparison' having touched NONE of them - the caps are never consulted, so a capped user gets unlimited Vision+OpenAI+Serper compares. url_routes.compare_urls signature is (request, body) only, and the module contains no consume/record/save_comparison/get_optional_user at all; the shipped app posts it from HomeScreen.tsx:427 with selected_category, which URLCompareRequest (url1,url2,region) silently drops. Fix (mirror the text bracket) closes the repro; test_first is right - keep the refund on the 0/1-product returns once consume moves before the Vision call.

fable.note: = MB-RECONCILE-01 + MB-RECONCILE-07 (one metering unit)

findings.title: Neither compare handler has a re-entrancy guard: a double-tap fires two paid backend comparisons and leaks the first abort handle
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup section B flows lead ('compare handlers lack a re-entrancy guard') — still-open at HEAD
findings.fix: Add a module- or ref-scoped in-flight guard: `if (inFlightRef.current) return; inFlightRef.current = true;` at the top of both handlers, cleared in every terminal branch (onComplete, onError, the URL catch, and the abort path). Prefer a ref over the `loading` state so it is synchronous and immune to the render-flush race. Also abort any existing handle before assigning a new one at :321.
findings.test_first: jest: render HomeScreen, fire the compare press twice synchronously, assert streamComparison (or api.post for URL mode) was constructed exactly once.
findings.impact: Two full comparisons per double-tap: 2x OpenAI + 2x Serper spend, 2x quota consumption on the server (text path) while the client counter increments once, and an orphaned in-flight request whose setState lands on a screen that has already navigated. It also burns two of the deployment-wide 10/min compare bucket for one user intent.

verdict_trail.reason: The literal code claim is true — no `if (loading) return;`, no in-flight ref, and :321 clobbers the abort handle. But the evidence omits a material guard: HomeScreen.tsx:644 passes `disabled={loading}` into TwoInputShell, whose CTA is `disabled={!canSubmit}` with `canSubmit = bothValid && !disabled`. So every double-tap separated by a render flush IS blocked; only a same-frame/multi-touch race slips through. That makes the stated impact ('two full comparisons per double-tap', 2x spend, 2x quota) overstated and the defect latent, not a measurable cost issue. Fix (sync ref) is still correct and flag-free.

findings.title: P3 sweep — seven smaller client/backend contract gaps found while walking the 44 call sites
findings.dedupe: mixed — (a) known:M18 MB-perf-03 partial + mobile-checkup #3 still-open; (h) known:mobile-checkup #12 still-open; (b)(c)(d)(e)(f)(g) new
findings.fix: Give the axios instance a sane global default (~30s) and keep the 120s only as an explicit per-call override on the multipart upload; delete compareTextPair or add nocache to TextCompareRequest; add `if (status === 429) return 'timeout'` to classifyLoadFailure; add maxLength={100} to the History search input; delete the unreachable HomeScreen onComplete branch; drop `url` from the source_click event_data (keep source_name); either wire GET /auth/verify into a lightweight session check or delete the alias so 'verifyAuth' stops implying a validation it does not perform; and give HistoryScreen's useFocusEffect a [searchQuery] dependency.
findings.test_first: One jest test per item; the highest-value red test is (f): assert no trackEvent payload from ResultsScreen contains a key whose value matches /^https?:\/\//, which is the QA-6 contract stated in api.ts:836-838 and currently unenforced.
findings.impact: Individually minor: slow failure paths behind a 120s ceiling, dead exports, one untranslated validation string, one privacy-invariant breach in analytics, one misleading dead branch, and a search filter that silently resets. Collectively they are the residue of fixes applied to the compare path only and never propagated to the other 38 call sites — the 'fixed-once-never-propagated' theme M13 named.

verdict_trail.reason: All eight sub-items (a)-(h) read true at HEAD; I opened each cited line. findings.title: STILL OPEN: get_optional_user swallows expired-token failures and returns None, silently downgrading an authenticated compare to anonymous — no history, no metering, no personalization, and no 401 to trigger the client refresh

Catch only genuinely-unexpected exceptions (network to Supabase) and, in that case, log to Sentry rather than silently downgrading. This changes response codes on live routes, so ship it behind ENABLE_STRICT_OPTIONAL_AUTH default OFF and flip it after confirming on a device that the api.ts refresh-and-retry path actually re-drives a compare (M18 MB-flows-01's performRefresh rework is main-only, so verify against a build that has it).

findings.title: Metro runs with inlineRequires:false and there is no metro.config.js to override it, so all ~3,842 module factories execute at cold start before the first frame
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add a `metro.config.js` that starts from `getDefaultConfig(__dirname)` and sets `config.transformer.getTransformOptions` to return `inlineRequires: true`. Highest-leverage startup change available and behaviour-preserving for correctly-written modules, but it DOES reorder module-evaluation side effects - so land it behind a staged rollout (a preview-channel OTA first, watch Sentry for boot crashes) and audit the five module-scope side effects this lane enumerated (App.tsx:10 initSentry, App.tsx:74 configureGoogleSignIn, api.ts:22 setupCertificatePinning, api.ts:50/138 interceptors, i18n/index.ts:31 i18n.init), since inlining changes WHEN each first runs.
findings.test_first: A build-assertion test reading the exported source map and asserting the count of modules in the entry's synchronous require closure is below a ratchet; or, cheaper and RED today, assert the project's merged Metro config yields `inlineRequires === true`.
findings.impact: This is the multiplier that turns every bundle-size finding in this lane into a cold-start CPU finding. Nothing in the graph is deferred: the lucide barrel's 1,706 factories, Sentry's browser Replay/Feedback bundles, markdown-it, expo-camera and all 20 screens all run their top-level code before React mounts, on every launch, on the JS thread. Affects every user on every cold start; worst on low-end Android where the bytecode is also 57% larger (7.90 MB vs 5.05 MB).

verdict_trail.reason: Config facts all true and I reproduced the emitted evidence: `ls metro.config.*` ENOENT, ExpoMetroConfig.js:322 `inlineRequires: false`, babel.config.js adds only removeConsole + reanimated, and in my own export the App factory head is `var t=e(r(_d[0])),n=e(r(_d[1])),o=r(_d[2]),…` — hoisted requires exactly as claimed. Downgraded for three reasons: (a) the cited line does not exist — babel.config.js is 61 lines, so `line: 62` is out of range; (b) the headline "all ~3,842 module factories execute at cold start" is false as written — react-native's own index exposes many submodules through lazy property getters, and 3,842 is the map's source count, not the boot closure; (c) `measured_or_modelled: measured` is wrong — no cold-start ms was measured, so the impact is modelled. It is a missing framework-default optimization whose own fix needs a staged rollout, i.e. latent, not a live quality/cost defect: P3. Genuinely new (no `inlineRequires`/metro hit in M13/M18/mobile-checkup).
