findings.title: Five Cairo font weights that are never registered ship in every build: 469,608 B = 41.0% of the entire OTA asset payload
findings.dedupe: known:mobile ('5 unused Cairo font weights (~470 KB) ship in every build' - unverified startup lead) - still-open, now measured exactly at 469,608 B and root-caused to the package's 8 top-level requires. The Geist double-ship is new.
findings.fix: Import the three weights from their own subpaths (`@expo-google-fonts/cairo/400Regular/Cairo_400Regular.ttf` etc.) instead of the package root, so Metro only sees three requires; that alone drops 469,608 B. Then resolve the Geist duplication deliberately: either drop the three Geist entries from the app.json expo-font plugin (keeping the runtime useFonts path the code depends on) or keep the plugin and delete `geistFontMap`/`useExpoFonts` from fonts.ts. No flag - verify by asserting the exported TTF count.
findings.test_first: A build-assertion test asserting the exported asset manifest contains exactly the TTFs the app registers (6, or 3 if Geist moves fully native). RED today at 11.
findings.impact: Nearly half a megabyte of dead weight in every App Store binary and every `eas update` payload, on the metered mobile connections of the target Gulf market. With the Geist double-ship, ~0.85 MB of the 1.09 MB asset payload is avoidable or duplicated.

verdict_trail.reason: All arithmetic recomputed from the exported asset manifest and matches to the byte: 30 iOS assets / 1,145,042 B; 11 TTFs / 1,136,172 B; the eight Cairo weights sum to 753,428; the five unregistered ones (92,740+92,800+94,644+94,708+94,716) = 469,608 = 41.01% of 1,145,042; the three Geist TTFs = 382,744. Root cause confirmed: @expo-google-fonts/cairo@0.4.2 index.js is eight `export const X = require('./NNN/Cairo_NNN.ttf')` statements, untree-shakeable; fonts.ts:40-44 registers only 400/600/700. Geist double-ship confirmed: fonts.ts:32-35 `require`s the three TTFs AND app.json's expo-font plugin lists the same three paths. Fix works (the package has no `exports` field, and 400Regular/Cairo_400Regular.ttf exists) but is INCOMPLETE: fonts.ts:12-17 also imports `useFonts as useCairoFonts` from the package ROOT, so the barrel — and all eight requires — stays in the graph unless that import is switched to expo-font's useFonts too. Known:mobile lead, still-open.

findings.title: initSentry() runs AFTER the entire import graph, not before it - ES import hoisting silently defeats the invariant the comment above it asserts, so early-boot crashes are never captured
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Either make `src/services/sentry.ts` self-initialising at module scope and put `import './src/services/sentry';` as the first import (hoisting then works FOR you, since dependency order is preserved), or move the init into `index.ts` before `import App from './App'`. At minimum correct the comment so the next reader is not misled. No flag needed.
findings.test_first: A source-contract test (the granularity this repo's App.* tests already use) asserting the first import in App.tsx is the Sentry side-effect import and that no bare `initSentry()` call sits between import declarations. Better: a bundle-assertion test locating the App module in an export and asserting `initSentry` appears before the first screen require - RED today.
findings.impact: The exact failure class the comment was written to catch - a crash during font loading, i18n init or native-bridge setup at boot - happens with Sentry uninitialised and is therefore invisible in the dashboard. It is also what makes MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-03's splash-strand undiagnosable in production. Worse, the comment reads as a satisfied invariant, so a future reviewer will not re-check it.

verdict_trail.reason: Code and mechanism both reproduce. App.tsx:6-8 asserts Sentry must init 'before any other module'; the call sits at :10 between import declarations. I ran babel-preset-expo over a minimal App.tsx-shaped source: the side-effect import written AFTER initSentry() is emitted BEFORE it, so every imported module (i18n's init at i18n/index.ts:31, api.ts:22 setupCertificatePinning, all screens) evaluates first. Invariant is false; comment misleads. The finder's 'experimentalImportSupport:true' attribution is unverifiable (no metro.config.js exists) — hoisting is plain ESM/commonjs-transform semantics, which is stronger. P2 correct: blind spot in crash reporting, not user harm. Fix (side-effect-import-first, or init in index.ts) is correct and needs no flag.

findings.title: Every English user's splash is gated on loading three Arabic Cairo faces (283,820 B) that will never render, because useAppFonts ANDs the two font families unconditionally
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Split into `useAppFonts(lang)`: always load Geist, load Cairo only when the resolved language is 'ar' (or lazily on the first Arabic render via a small provider). Since the language resolves inside `init()` after the hook has mounted, the cleanest shape is a module-scope language cache written at boot, or gate the splash on Geist only and let Cairo resolve behind the first frame (Arabic text briefly falls back to the system face). No flag needed; land it together with MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-06 so the Cairo package is subpath-imported at the same time.

It runs in parallel with the (much larger) auth block so it is usually hidden - but it becomes the tail term the moment MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-02 is fixed, and it is pure waste for the majority-English tester population today.

verdict_trail.reason: Code claim fully confirmed and arithmetic is exact: fonts.ts:38-45 ANDs both families unconditionally; App.tsx:150/:274 gate the splash on it; app.json:81-88 embeds only the 3 Geist TTFs natively, so Cairo is the runtime load. 94480+94688+94652 = 283,820 B and 126048+127872+128824 = 382,744 B both check out. But severity is over-rated: no added splash time was measured, the load is local bundled-asset I/O running in parallel with a blocking network refresh, and the finder's own impact says it only 'becomes the tail term' once MB-02 is fixed — that is latent, i.e. P3. Fix (load Geist always, Cairo by resolved language / behind first frame) is correct and flag-free. Adjacent to, but distinct from, the mobile-checkup lead about 5 unused Cairo weights shipping.

findings.title: The boot path calls I18nManager.forceRTL() with no reloadAsync, so an Arabic device's very first launch renders the whole app left-to-right with Arabic strings until the user kills and reopens it
findings.dedupe: new (M18 has MB-i18n-rtl-02/03/04/05/09 but none covers the boot-time forceRTL-without-reload; the mobile checkup does not mention forceRTL at all)
findings.fix: Mirror the switcher: inside the `if` at App.tsx:174, after forceRTL, `try { await require('expo-updates').reloadAsync(); } catch {}` - guarded so dev/Expo Go still boots. Because a reload at boot is user-visible, gate it on first launch only (persist an 'rtl_applied' marker alongside the language key) so it can never loop. Ship dark behind a small const in `src/config/features.ts` if you want a canary; the loop risk is the only thing worth protecting against.
findings.test_first: A test driving `init()` with `getSavedLanguage` resolving 'ar' and a mocked `I18nManager.isRTL === false`, asserting `Updates.reloadAsync` was called exactly once. RED today - it is never called on the boot path.
findings.impact: First-run experience for the primary Gulf market: Arabic copy inside an LTR layout (mirrored chevrons wrong, tab bar and headers on the wrong side) for the whole first session, including onboarding. It self-heals on the second launch, which is exactly why it survives casual testing. Also affects any user whose stored language and native isRTL flag diverge, e.g. after a reinstall, since getSavedLanguage falls back to the device locale at i18n/index.ts:23.

verdict_trail.reason: Both call sites read exactly as claimed: App.tsx:173-177 sets allowRTL/forceRTL and nothing else, while useLanguage.ts:17-27 does the same and then reloads via expo-updates. expo-updates ~29.0.17 is a real dependency (package.json:43), so the fix is available on the boot path. Reachability is narrower than the title implies but real: app.json declares no `locales`/CFBundleLocalizations, so on iOS an Arabic-locale fresh install has I18nManager.isRTL false while getSavedLanguage() returns 'ar' (i18n/index.ts:23 device-locale fallback) - the branch fires and layout stays LTR until restart. On Android (supportsRtl default true) isRTL is already true and the branch usually will not fire. Device confirmation impossible here. P2 stands (self-heals on second launch, pre-launch app). Proposed fix is right; the first-launch marker to prevent a reload loop is the necessary guard.

findings.title: Push-token registration re-runs its full network dance on every authed cold start and can raise the OS notification-permission dialog over the splash; the documented already_registered short-circuit does not exist
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Actually use the flag: read REGISTERED_FLAG_KEY at the top of `doRegister()` and return `{registered:false, reason:'already_registered'}` when the stored token matches the current one, writing it on a successful PUT. Separately, never call `requestPermissionsAsync()` from the boot path - at boot proceed only when `getPermissionsAsync()` already reports 'granted', and move the request itself to the onboarding notifications step (or a first Results screen) where it has context. Both changes narrow behaviour; no flag needed.
findings.test_first: A test asserting `tryRegisterPushToken()` makes zero network calls when the registered-token flag already matches, and that it never calls `requestPermissionsAsync` when invoked from the boot path. RED on both today.
findings.impact: Two costs. (a) Every authed cold start makes two avoidable network calls (exp.host plus the PUT) that the file's own doc comment implies are skipped after the first success. (b) On the first authed launch the notification-permission dialog appears during boot, on top of the splash, with no priming screen and no context - the classic way to earn a permanent 'Don't Allow' from users who have not yet seen the product. The Step-17 onboarding notifications question exists precisely to prime this, and this call pre-empts it.

verdict_trail.reason: Verified line by line. REGISTERED_FLAG_KEY is declared at :22 and re-exported at :99 and appears nowhere else; the file's only import is `api` (:20) - no AsyncStorage - so nothing reads or writes it and the 'already_registered' member of the result union (:26) is unreachable. doRegister() therefore runs in full on every authed cold start from App.tsx:202. Re-ran the render myself (the first verifier did not) and both halves reproduce: pressing s17-not-now AND s17-allow both call onComplete with notifications_enabled absent, and buildPreferencesPayload/buildDemographicsPayload both drop the key when it is explicitly present. Backend UserPreferencesRequest DOES accept notifications_enabled (auth_routes.py:182) and reengagement_service.py:108 treats a missing key as ON, so both fix edits land and the push-consent impact claim holds. In pushTokenService.doRegister, replace the request at :64-68 with a read-only gate (`if (existing.status !== 'granted') return { registered:false, reason:'permission_denied' }`) and add a separate exported `requestPushPermission()` that Step17Notifications.handleAllow calls. Then have Step 17's onDone(granted===true) call tryRegisterPushToken() itself, and leave App.tsx:202/:246 as the idempotent token refresh for users who already granted. Ship it with the MB-FLOWS-STATE-06 fix so the answer is both asked at the right time and stored.

findings.impact: Every new signup. iOS shows the notification-authorization alert exactly once per install; after the user answers it, a second requestPermissionsAsync returns the stored status without any UI. So the user is asked cold at signup (worst-converting moment, no context), and then Step 17's 'Allow' button silently returns whatever they already said — a dead control dressed as a choice. On Android 13+ the POST_NOTIFICATIONS dialog can reappear once, so the user is prompted twice for the same thing. It also defeats the stated design rationale for having Step 17 at all.

App.tsx:246 in handleLoginSuccess (wired as RegisterScreen onRegisterSuccess at :88) fire-and-forgets tryRegisterPushToken, which has no persisted short-circuit (REGISTERED_FLAG_KEY is declared but never read as a gate) and calls requestPermissionsAsync at pushTokenService.ts:64. Step 17 is live, not dark: CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT = 100, so features.ENABLE_NEW_ONBOARDING is true for everyone and OnboardingFlow.tsx:604 renders Step17Notifications, whose handleAllow calls the same API. iOS shows the authorization alert once per install, so Step 17's Allow returns the stored answer with no UI. findings.test_first: An App.tsx routing test asserting 'Legal' appears in the root navigator's route names in BOTH auth branches (red today for the unauth branch), plus an RNTL RegisterScreen test that finds a pressable whose press calls navigate('Legal', {doc:'terms'}).

verdict_trail.reason: Both greps reproduce: zero terms/privacy/legal matches in RegisterScreen.tsx (701 lines) and LoginScreen.tsx (671 lines). The only Legal Stack.Screen is App.tsx:347-352, inside the authenticated `: (` branch opened at :338; ReferralLanding/InviteeQuiz are the only navigator-level routes (:437-440). Reinforcing detail the finder missed: Step16Account.tsx:213-226 renders 'Terms & Privacy' fine print styled as links with NO onPress, and that step is post-auth anyway (onboarding mounts only when isAuthenticated). Genuinely new (0 hits in M18 JSON / mobile-checkup). Not a dark flag. Kept P2 — compliance/store risk, not live harm, spend or security.

findings.title: The logout confirmation shows irreversible account-DELETION copy in every language except English — the EN-only .replace() never matches the Arabic string
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup flows lead ('Arabic logout confirmation shows account-DELETION copy … W4 was the RTL sweep — likely fixed, verify') — VERIFIED STILL-OPEN; W4 did not touch it
findings.fix: Stop deriving one string from another. Add a dedicated `profile.logoutConfirm` key to en.json ('Sign out of Qaren? You can sign back in any time.') and ar.json ('تسجيل الخروج من قارن؟ تقدر ترجع تسجّل الدخول في أي وقت.') and use it at ProfileScreen.tsx:305. Then add a copy-policy fence forbidding `.replace(` on any `t(...)` result in src/screens — the pattern is unfixable by translation.
findings.test_first: Extend __tests__/copy-policy.test.ts with a source scan asserting no `t('…')` call in src/ is followed by `.replace(`, and an i18n test asserting `profile.logoutConfirm` exists in both catalogues and that neither contains the deletion clause — red today.
findings.impact: Arabic is the primary launch locale (RTL forced at App.tsx:172-177, ar.json is a full parallel catalogue). Every Arabic user who taps Log Out is warned their action is permanent, which reads as account deletion — a scary-copy contract violation at the exact site and a plausible driver of abandoned logouts / support contacts.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced through the real catalogues. profile.deleteConfirm EN = 'Are you sure? This cannot be undone.' → replace() yields 'Are you sure? '; AR = 'هل أنت متأكد؟ لا يمكن التراجع عن هذا.' and the replace is provably a no-op (equality check true), so the Arabic user sees the irreversibility clause under the heading 'تسجيل الخروج'. No profile.logoutConfirm key exists in either catalogue. Same key is reused for real deletes at HistoryScreen.tsx:756 and EditProfileScreen.tsx:126. Arabic is reachable (i18n/index.ts getSavedLanguage → device languageCode 'ar'). One correction: the finder's repro command is wrong — the JSON files are FLAT dotted keys, so `JSON.parse(...).profile.deleteConfirm` throws TypeError; read `obj['profile.deleteConfirm']`.

findings.title: The Results screen has zero outbound purchase or source links — openRatingSource is defined and never called, and price.url is never rendered, so a comparison-shopping app dead-ends at the verdict
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup flows lead ('Results has no outbound purchase/source links at all; openRatingSource is dead code, price.url never used') — STILL-OPEN at HEAD despite ResultsScreen's +113-line M21 delta
findings.fix: Thread a handler through: add `onOpenSource?: (source: RatingSource) => void` and `onOpenPrice?: (url: string) => void` to ResultsContentProps, pass useCallback-stable versions of openRatingSource (and a price-url twin) from ResultsScreen.tsx:756+, and render them as a pressable retailer chip on each price row and a 'source' affordance on each rating pill. Validate the scheme (https only) before Linking.openURL, and use Linking.canOpenURL as ShareBottomSheet.tsx:180 already does. Ship behind ENABLE_RESULTS_OUTBOUND_LINKS defaulting OFF only if affiliate tagging must land first; otherwise no flag. Confirm 'source_click' is in feedback_routes.VALID_EVENT_TYPES before wiring the event, or /events will 422 the batch.
findings.test_first: An RNTL ResultsScreen test rendering a fixture with reviews.products[0].rating_source.url set, pressing the source affordance, and asserting Linking.openURL was called with that URL — red today (there is no affordance and no test file renders ResultsScreen at all).
findings.impact: The user reaches a verdict and has nowhere to go — no 'buy at X', no 'see the reviews we used', no way to verify a price. For a price-comparison product this is the terminal step of the core loop and the natural place for affiliate revenue (Awin/CJ are on the signup dossier). It also means the 'source_click' analytics event can never fire, so any funnel that expects it reads zero.

verdict_trail.reason: openRatingSource is defined at ResultsScreen.tsx:500 and referenced nowhere else in src/ (repo-wide grep: one hit). ResultsContentProps carries exactly the 18 props listed, none of which is a source/url handler. ResultsAccordion is the only component that even types rating_source (:35) and it explicitly suppresses those keys from render (:83 `if (key.endsWith('_source')) return false;`, :168). The recorded payload does carry 4 non-null rating_source.url (price.url null). One evidence correction: the Linking grep returns FOUR call sites, not three — ResultsScreen.tsx:503 is one of them, inside the dead function; the conclusion (no reachable outbound affordance) is unaffected. Kept P2: a missing affordance/revenue gap, not live harm.

findings.title: History search is silently reverted on every screen refocus by a stale useFocusEffect closure, submit blanks the whole screen including the search field, and a first-load network error renders the 'no comparisons yet' empty state
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #12 (flagged 'M21 risk HIGH — RE-VERIFY FIRST; likely partly addressed') — RE-VERIFIED STILL-OPEN at HEAD; the W3 rewrite fixed the perf items (#13/#14, HistoryRow is now memoised at :407) but not any of the three flow defects
findings.fix: (1) Wrap loadHistory in useCallback with [searchQuery] and pass it as the useFocusEffect dep — or read the query from a ref so the focus refetch honours the active filter. (2) Split the loading states: keep a `initialLoading` for the mount spinner and a `searching` that renders an inline indicator inside the search row, so :837 never unmounts the input. (3) In the catch, set a distinct `loadFailed` state and render a retry card instead of falling through to renderEmpty. Mirrors the classifyLoadFailure matrix already in src/services/failureClassification.ts. No flag.
findings.test_first: An RNTL HistoryScreen test: type a query, submit, assert the filtered rows AND that the search TextInput is still mounted; then fire the navigation focus event and assert getComparisonHistory was called with the query, not undefined. A third asserting a rejected first load renders a retry affordance, not history.empty.title. All three red today.
findings.impact: Search is effectively unusable on any flow that leaves and returns to the tab (tap a result → back; open Profile → back), which is the normal way people use it. The blank-to-spinner on submit is a jarring full-screen flash on every query. And an offline user is told their history is empty rather than that the fetch failed — the same class of wrong-state the M21 failureClassification work fixed on Results but not here.

verdict_trail.reason: Two of three sub-claims reproduce exactly, at the cited lines. (1) useFocusEffect(useCallback(loadHistory, [])) at :664-668 pins the first render's loadHistory (a plain const redeclared at :670) whose closure holds searchQuery='' (:655), so every refocus calls getComparisonHistory(50,0,undefined) and overwrites the filtered list. (2) onSubmitEditing at :878-881 sets loading=true, and the early return `if (loading)` at :837 unmounts header, hero and the search TextInput for a full-screen spinner. (3) is OVERSTATED: the non-401 catch does set no state, but it DOES `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), parseApiError(error).message)` — the user is told the fetch failed, with the empty state behind the modal, so 'told their history is empty rather than that the fetch failed' is wrong. Severity unchanged on the strength of (1) and (2).

findings.title: Camera shutter and gallery-pick failures are swallowed with an empty catch — a failed capture is an invisible dead tap on the primary scan surface
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup flows lead ('camera capture failures are silent') — STILL-OPEN; ScanCameraScreen.tsx untouched in 593ec1e..76ace90
findings.fix: In all three catches, capture the error to Sentry (Sentry.captureException with a `scan_capture` tag) and surface the existing non-scary copy: `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), t('home.errors.camera'))` — 'Snap that one more time — sharper focus this round.' already exists in both catalogues and is copy-policy clean. Also handle the `!photo?.uri` case the same way rather than returning silently. No flag.
findings.test_first: An RNTL ScanCameraScreen test that mocks takePictureAsync to reject, presses the shutter, and asserts Alert.alert was called (and that the slot indicator still reads '1 of 2') — red today.
findings.impact: The user taps the shutter and the slot indicator does not move. There is no feedback of any kind, so the rational reading is 'the app is broken'. Camera is one of the three compare entry modes and the one the Home screen defaults to (HomeScreen.tsx:105 `useState<InputMode>('scan')`). It is also the mode with the lowest measured usage — search_logs shows input_type camera = 11 of 13,237 rows — and a silently-failing shutter is a candidate explanation nobody can currently see, because nothing is reported to Sentry either.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced exactly at the cited line. Three silent exits confirmed (:185 guard, :189-190 catch, :206-207 picker catch), no Sentry import in the file, and the contrasting Alert at :237 confirms the inconsistency. Copy key `home.errors.camera` exists in BOTH catalogues, so the fix is copy-policy clean and needs no flag. m21_touched=false verified: zero commits touch this file in 593ec1e..76ace90, so the mobile-checkup lead is still-open. Impact numbers match the measured baseline. P2 correct — a dead tap, not a spend or security leak.

findings.title: The URL compare path never registers an abort handle, so HomeScreen's unmount/logout cancellation covers only the text path
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Create an AbortController in handleUrlCompare, pass `signal: controller.signal` to the axios call, set `abortRef.current = () => controller.abort()` before awaiting, and null it in both the success and catch paths exactly as the text path does at :332/:355. One small block; no flag.
findings.test_first: Extend __tests__/HomeScreen.abortOnUnmount.test.tsx (which already pins the text path) with a URL-mode case: start a url compare, unmount, assert the axios signal was aborted — red today.
findings.impact: Low today — URL compares are also unmetered and unsaved server-side (mobile-checkup #6), and search_logs shows no url-typed rows in the measured series. But the #118 protection is advertised as covering 'any in-flight compare' and silently does not, so a logout or tab teardown during a URL compare leaves a 35s request and its backend fan-out running.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. `grep -n 'abortRef|AbortController|signal'` returns ONLY 113/199/200/321/332/360 — every one on the text/SSE path; handleUrlCompare (406-473) has no controller and no signal option. The #118 cleanup at :199-200 therefore no-ops for URL compares as claimed. Line corrected: the api.post is at 426 (options at 437), not 419; handleUrlCompare starts at 406, not 395. P3 correct — no url-typed rows exist in the measured series, so exposure today is nil.

findings.title: P3 sweep — nine smaller flow/state defects found while walking the 60 navigation edges and 16 declared route names

findings.title: Nothing survives an app kill mid-onboarding: the 17-step flow holds all answers in component state and writes its first draft only after Step 17
findings.dedupe: new (M18 MB-flows-04 covered the POST-completion draft/retry only; this is the pre-completion gap it left)
findings.fix: Persist per step: in OnboardingFlow's handleNext, after fireEvent('onboarding_step_completed'), call `void saveOnboardingDraft({ ...data, __step: nextStep })` (the service already swallows storage errors by design, onboardingDraft.ts:104-107). On mount, NewOnboardingHost should read the draft and pass `initialStep`/`initialData` into OnboardingFlow — the props already exist and are honoured at :201-204 — resuming the user where they stopped, and clear the draft on completion as persistWithDraft already does. Ship behind ENABLE_ONBOARDING_RESUME defaulting ON only if you want a canary; the failure mode (a stale draft) is already handled by the existing clear-on-success path.
findings.test_first: A NewOnboardingHost test that renders the flow, advances to step 6, asserts AsyncStorage holds a draft naming step 6, then unmounts, re-renders the host, and asserts `onboarding-step-6` is the mounted step — red today (nothing is written before step 17, and the host always starts at 1).
findings.impact: Every user of the 17-step flow (CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100). A phone call, a background OS kill, a crash, or a Sentry-caught JS error at step 12 costs the user all twelve answers and restarts them at Step 1 — including the two theatrical waits (Step 14's 3.2s loading floor and Step 15's reveal). Since the server-side gate is `users.preferences_completed`, the app re-mounts the host and they must do the whole thing again. This is the most likely single cause of onboarding funnel drop between the `onboarding_step_completed` and `onboarding_completed` events, and it is invisible in analytics because an interrupted session simply looks like abandonment.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced. The 684-line orchestrator contains zero AsyncStorage/persist calls (the only 'persists' hit is a comment at :476). The sole production caller of saveOnboardingDraft is persistWithDraft (onboardingDraft.ts:219), invoked from NewOnboardingHost:126 inside handleComplete — i.e. after the flow ends. The mount effect calls flushPendingOnboardingDraft, which replays a COMPLETED run's draft only. Reachable in prod: CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100, and App.tsx passes onComplete only — no initialStep/initialData. Fix is sound and needs no flag; the resume props already exist and are honoured at :198/:206. Line corrected 203→206 (setField 279-285, host call :126). P2 correct: recoverable by redoing the flow, not a spend or security defect.

findings.title: Arabic-device first launch runs the entire session in LTR: boot calls forceRTL but never reloads, and I18nManager.isRTL is a module-load constant
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Make boot symmetric with the in-app switch: when `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL` at App.tsx:174, persist the language (saveLanguage) and then `await Updates.reloadAsync()` behind a one-shot AsyncStorage latch (e.g. `@qaren_rtl_bootstrapped`) so the relaunch can never loop, and render the splash until it happens; when reloadAsync is unavailable (dev client), fall back to a blocking 'restart Qaren to finish switching to Arabic' screen rather than silently continuing. Ship dark behind ENABLE_RTL_BOOT_RELOAD if a boot-time reload is considered risky, defaulting ON for lang==='ar' only.
findings.test_first: A jest test that imports App's init path with expo-localization mocked to `[{languageCode:'ar'}]` and `I18nManager.isRTL === false`, then asserts `Updates.reloadAsync` was called exactly once before the navigator mounts — red today. Plus a unit test pinning that `I18nManager.isRTL` is unchanged immediately after `I18nManager.forceRTL(true)` (documents the RN contract the code violates).
findings.impact: Every Arabic user's FIRST session — the 17-step onboarding, the first compare, the first Results screen — paints left-to-right with Arabic text: back chevrons point the wrong way (DirectionalIcon reads the stale I18nManager.isRTL via utils/rtl.ts:9), rows do not mirror, SlideTransition slides from the wrong edge, and the six textAlign ternaries take their LTR branch. This is the highest-stakes session in the funnel and the app never tells the user to relaunch. Bahrain/GCC is the entire target market.

verdict_trail.reason: Mechanism CONFIRMED: App.tsx:173-176 flips the native flag with no reload; the only reloadAsync in the app is useLanguage.ts:23; RN 0.81.5 caches isRTL as a module-load constant so forceRTL cannot change it in-session. But the finder's dedupe 'new' is FALSE — this is M13-62, already filed at P2 against the same file, still open at HEAD. Severity aligned to the prior rating: Arabic copy in an LTR shell for one session is cosmetic, not functional. Fix (latched reloadAsync) is sound and needs no flag.

findings.title: Two contradictory definitions of isRTL ship side by side — useLanguage().isRTL (i18n.language) vs I18nManager.isRTL (boot constant) — producing a half-mirrored UI
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Collapse to one source of truth. Export a single `useIsRTL()` (and a module-level `isRTL()` for StyleSheet.create-time use) that returns `I18nManager.isRTL` only, and make the language switch guarantee that constant is fresh by always reloading (MB-I18N-RTL-01's fix). Replace the four `useLanguage().isRTL` consumers with it, and delete `isRTL` from useLanguage's return so the wrong one cannot be picked up again. Keep `language` on useLanguage for copy decisions that are genuinely about language rather than direction (e.g. the Cairo/Geist choice in MB-I18N-RTL-04).
findings.test_first: A test that sets `i18n.language='ar'` while leaving `I18nManager.isRTL=false` and renders ResultsContent, then asserts the CohortBadge slide sign and the DirectionalIcon scaleX agree — red today (badge slides RTL, icon does not flip).
findings.impact: Not a clean 'RTL is off' state but a mixed one, which is worse to diagnose and worse to look at: some components mirror and some do not on the same screen. It also means QA cannot reproduce reliably — a tester who relaunches once sees a different app than a first-run user.

verdict_trail.reason: Two definitions CONFIRMED at HEAD and the consumer split is as claimed (I found one MORE the finder missed: OnboardingFlow.tsx:424 `flipForRTL(isRTL)` uses the language-derived value while DirectionalIcon uses the boot constant). But the divergence has NO independent trigger — it exists only inside MB-I18N-RTL-01's window or the swallowed-reload flash; steady state agrees. It also overlaps M18 MB-i18n-rtl-03 (P2, CONFIRMED, rtl.ts:8, 'two flip helpers exist'). P1 over-rates a consistency defect with no separate reachability.

findings.title: M21 W4's textAlign RTL 'fix' double-flips on BOTH platforms — RN swaps left/right itself, so 6 style sites now align to the WRONG edge in Arabic, and a contract test forbids the correct form
findings.dedupe: known:M21 W4 MB-i18n-rtl-05 + regressed
findings.fix: Revert all six entries to the bare physical value they had at 593ec1e (`textAlign:'right'` / `'left'`) and let RN do the single mirror it already does — or, better, express the intent directly and drop the branch entirely by using `textAlign:'end'`/`'start'`? (not supported by RN) — so: bare physical values plus a comment citing TextAttributeProps.java:294 and RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:195. Then INVERT the fence: __tests__/rtl/textAlignLogical.contract.test.ts:52-53 currently requires the ternary and forbids the literal, which locks the bug in; rewrite it to assert the literal and forbid `textAlign:\s*I18nManager\.isRTL`. No flag needed — this is a straight revert of a wrong fix.
findings.test_first: Replace textAlignLogical.contract.test.ts's two assertions with their negations, and add a rendering test that mounts ResultsAccordion with `I18nManager.isRTL=true` and asserts the flattened `specsCellValueLeft.textAlign === 'right'` (the value that, after RN's own swap, paints left). Red on the current code, green after the revert.
findings.impact: In Arabic, the Results spec table's two value columns swap sides relative to their centred label, the DimensionBars product-B legend name aligns away from its bar, the priorities percent column jumps to the leading edge of the mirrored bar row, and both character counters sit at the top-leading instead of bottom-trailing corner of their textareas. Results and Profile are the two screens the product is judged on. This is a REGRESSION: these six sites rendered correctly before M21 W4.

verdict_trail.reason: The central technical claim is CONFIRMED — I read all four RN 0.81.5 platform paths and every one mirrors physical left/right, so the comment at ResultsAccordion.tsx:883 and the test's premise are false; 593ec1e had the correct bare literals. Two corrections: only 5 sites regressed (InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:506 had no textAlign at 593ec1e — wrong, but new, not a regression), and it is NOT on any phone (97b5f15 still carries `textAlign: 'right'`), so no user is harmed today. Prior row MB-i18n-rtl-05 was P3; the inverted fence justifies P2, not P1.

findings.title: Cairo is loaded, blocks first paint, and is never applied to a single character — fontFamily.ar has zero consumers and the typography presets carry no fontFamily at all
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Make useTypography own the family, not just the leading: give each preset a `fontFamily` resolved from `fontFamily[language][weightBucket]` (map fontWeight 400/600/700 to regular/semiBold/bold) and have it key off `useLanguage().language` rather than isRTL, so the choice follows the LANGUAGE (correct) instead of the direction. Then migrate components off the raw `typography` import — the ~140 files that spread `...typography.body` are the work; a codemod plus an eslint no-restricted-import on `typography` from src/theme in screens/components fences it. If the migration is too large for one wave, the cheap 80% is to set the family once per screen root via a `<AppText>` wrapper or to add the family to the presets and accept that direct `typography` importers get the EN face. Also drop the unused Cairo weights (only 3 of 8 are imported, but the whole package ships).
findings.test_first: A test that renders any body-copy component under `i18n.language='ar'` and asserts the flattened style's `fontFamily === 'Cairo_400Regular'` — red today (undefined). Plus a fence test asserting `JSON.stringify(typography)` contains 'fontFamily' so the presets can never lose it again.
findings.impact: Every Arabic user reads the app in whatever Arabic face the OS picks (Geeza Pro / Noto Naskh), not Cairo — the entire 'Geist EN + Cairo AR' typography system in the design doc is dead. findings.title: BHD is never rendered with its 3 decimals — History truncates fils with toFixed(2), Home/Profile with toFixed(0), Results uses the device default, and the symbol swaps sides between screens
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Route every price through one `formatPrice(amount, currencyCode, t, language)` in src/utils that (a) looks the fraction-digit count up per ISO code (BHD/KWD/OMR = 3, SAR/AED/QAR/USD = 2) rather than assuming 2, (b) uses the same amount-then-symbol order everywhere — amount first matches both the Arabic convention and the existing hero copy — and (c) takes its digits from the MB-I18N-RTL-06 helper. findings.title: Choosing العربية hard-restarts the app with no warning — at onboarding step 2 it drops the user back to step 1, and from Profile it kills the session mid-task
findings.dedupe: new

Await switchLanguage instead of `void`-ing it so onChange cannot race the reload.

findings.title: switchLanguage guards on the stale I18nManager.isRTL, so after the boot-time forceRTL it can strand the app in 'English text inside an RTL layout' with no way back
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Fixing MB-I18N-RTL-01 removes the window, but harden this path regardless: (a) drop the `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL` guard and always call `allowRTL(true)` + `forceRTL(shouldBeRTL)` (both are idempotent) before deciding whether to reload; (b) decide the reload on the value the user actually asked for, tracked in AsyncStorage alongside the language, not on the stale constant; (c) replace the bare `catch {}` at :24 with a Sentry breadcrumb plus the 'please restart Qaren' screen from finding 01, so a failed reload is visible rather than silent; (d) remove the `lang === i18n.language` early return's ability to mask a direction mismatch by checking direction as well as language.
findings.test_first: A test that sets `I18nManager.isRTL=false` while the native flag is conceptually true, calls `switchLanguage('en')` from language 'ar', and asserts `I18nManager.forceRTL` was called with `false` — red today (never called).
findings.impact: A self-inflicted trap with no in-app escape: the user cannot fix the direction by toggling the language, because the toggle's own guard is reading a value that is already wrong. Reinstalling is the only recovery. Low frequency (needs the first-launch window of finding 01, or a swallowed reload) but the end state is unrecoverable, which is why it is worth pinning even though it is downstream of 01.

verdict_trail.reason: Every code claim reproduces, but the load-bearing impact — "unrecoverable, reinstalling is the only recovery" — is refuted. App.tsx:174-177 re-runs `forceRTL(shouldBeRTL)` on EVERY boot against a freshly-read constant, so the cold start after the trap corrects the persisted native flag and the one after it renders correctly: the mismatch lasts at most one session and self-heals. Combined with a rare precondition and being downstream of MB-I18N-RTL-01/M13-62, that is P3, not P2. The hardening fix (drop the guard, track intent, surface failed reloads) is still correct and flag-free.

findings.title: The 'vs' pill and the profile badge use a left:'50%' + translateX centring hack that RN half-mirrors, putting them ~2x the offset off-centre in Arabic
findings.dedupe: new

If the transform must stay, negate the translateX sign under `I18nManager.isRTL` the way SlideTransition already does.
findings.test_first: Render HomeEditorialSections with `I18nManager.isRTL=true` and assert the flattened smartVsPill style contains no non-zero `translateX` (or that its sign matches the direction) — red today.
findings.impact: Under Arabic the 'vs' pill on the Home smart-pick tile sits ~32px off the centre line between the two products, and the Profile badge ~24px off — the pill is the visual hinge of that tile, so it reads as a layout bug rather than a design choice. verdict_trail.reason: Styles reproduced verbatim at 76ace90. Mechanism holds, though the finder cited the WRONG architecture: app.json sets newArchEnabled=true, so LayoutShadowNode.java (old arch) is not the shipping path — but Fabric does the same swap (YogaLayoutableShadowNode.cpp:912-927 moves Edge::Left to Edge::Start when direction==RTL; iOS wires it at RCTFabricSurface.mm:181), and Yoga's computeRightEdge returns the Start inset under RTL. transform is never swapped (swapLeftAndRightInViewProps only touches borders). Arithmetic recomputed: RTL pill spans [c-w, c], centre c-w/2, plus translateX -16 = 32px left of centre when w=32 — as claimed. RTL is real (useLanguage.ts:16-19 forceRTL + reload). Not flag-gated but needs home/profile history to render; cosmetic. No prior row covers it (M18 mb-i18n-rtl-01..09 are icons/plurals/textAlign/digits/currency).

findings.title: P3 sweep — six latent i18n/RTL defects: dead bidi helper with no isolation anywhere, dead/empty catalog keys, an unmirrored shimmer, and a polyfill guard that never probes Arabic
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: (a) Either delete `writingDirection()` as dead code or wire it: apply `writingDirection()` plus an explicit `textAlign:'left'` to any Text that renders backend prose while the app language is 'ar', and wrap interpolated foreign-script values in U+2068/U+2069 (FSI/PDI) inside the catalog templates that mix scripts. (b) Delete the empty key from both catalogs or fill it. (c) Rename to `results.valueMatch.cheaperOfTwo` so no reserved suffix is exposed. (d) Negate the shimmer sweep sign under `I18nManager.isRTL`. (e) Extend the guard by testing `new Intl.PluralRules('ar').select(3) === 'few'` at app start and forcing the polyfill in when it is not — a five-line module in src/i18n imported before i18next, replacing the bare `import 'intl-pluralrules'`. (f) Normalise on one percent glyph across ar.json.

(a) is the one to watch: it is the rendering half of the known 'Arabic users get English verdict text' problem, and it means that even after the product lane fixes generation, any residual English (brand names, source hostnames, spec values) will still bidi-scramble inside Arabic sentences. verdict_trail.reason: All six sub-claims reproduced. (a) writingDirection() has zero consumers; a full python scan of src/ finds exactly 2 bidi control chars in the whole tree, both in ar.json (referrals.share.reward.now/later) — no isolates anywhere in code. (b)(c)(f) recomputed from both catalogs (896 leaf keys each): onboarding.language.subtitle is the only empty value in either; cheaper_of_two is a fixed phrase and its only caller DimensionBars.tsx:340 passes no count, so it resolves today; ar.json mixes U+066A (4 values) with ASCII % (2). (d) confirmed but the path is wrong — it is src/screens/LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:447, not src/components/; live via HomeScreen.tsx:882. (e) guard verified. All latent/cosmetic, none flag-gated. Fix (c) omits updating the caller at DimensionBars.tsx:373. Adjacent to but distinct from M18 MB-i18n-rtl-03 (icon flip helpers) and -02 (missing polyfill, now fixed by the import at i18n/index.ts:7).

findings.title: The whole Geist+Cairo type system is loaded at boot and never applied: `fontFamily` has zero importers and `typography` sets no fontFamily, so all but two text sites render in the OS system font
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Do NOT delete the TTFs — wire them. Add `fontFamily: fontFamily[lang][weight]` into the `typography` presets in theme/index.ts (or make `typography` a function of language, which is what useTypography already wants), so the loaded faces are the ones rendered. (a) The ring animation is a side-effect of React re-rendering: it appears to animate only while the counter's rAF loop is committing (~2.4s), then the rings sit frozen for the remaining ~25s of a real compare while `withRepeat(-1)` keeps burning UI-thread frames with zero visible output. (b) For any user with Reduce Motion enabled the three rings render at opacity 0 from the first frame — the loading hero degrades to a bare logo and a counter chip, which is a worse outcome than 'animation disabled'.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced at HEAD. LoadingRings.tsx:133-136 reads `const r = sv.value` during render; grep for useAnimatedProps/createAnimatedComponent in that file = 0 hits, so ring geometry only updates while the counter's rAF setState loop commits (motion.counterTick.duration, capped at t>=1). Reachable on every compare (HomeScreen.tsx:882 -> LoadingScreenVariants -> LoadingRings, plus ResultsScreen.tsx:638), `animated` defaults true (:64). The reduce-motion half checks out in reanimated 4.1.7: util.js:101 returns isReduceMotionOnUI.value for the default config and util.js:312-314 sets `animation.current = animation.toValue`, so rings land at RING_TARGET_R=150 -> progress 1 -> opacity 0 (one base frame first, not literally frame 0). The finder's self-refutation of the M18 orphan clause is correct. Matches M18 MB-perf-04 (P2) — same severity retained.

findings.title: useTypography — the entire Arabic 1.7x line-height fix — has ZERO production consumers; all 54 text files import the static English-tuned typography, and a passing test suite hides it
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Migrate the text-dense screens to `const ty = useTypography()` — Results (ResultsContent, ResultsAccordion, DimensionBars, FactualVerdict), History rows, Home editorial, Profile, and the onboarding steps — replacing `...typography.body` with `...ty.body`. Because StyleSheet.create blocks are module-level, the mechanical route is to move the affected text styles into a `useMemo(() => StyleSheet.create({...}), [ty])` inside each component, or to spread `ty.body` inline at the <Text> site over the static style. Ship it behind no flag (it is a pure line-height change), but land Results + History first and screenshot both locales.
findings.test_first: A repo-wide lint-style test: assert that no file under src/screens or src/components/results contains `...typography.body` / `...typography.title` / `...typography.caption` without also importing useTypography. RED at HEAD for ~54 files. Plus a render test that mounts ResultsContent under i18n language 'ar' and asserts the verdict Text's resolved lineHeight is fontSize * 1.7, not * 1.5.
findings.impact: Every Arabic screen renders body, title, caption and small text at the English 1.5x line-height. Arabic script carries dots below the baseline and hamza/madda above it; the design doc's own 1.7x figure exists because 1.5x crowds and clips them. This is the whole Arabic-readability deliverable, shipped as dead code with a green test suite behind it — the 'green-that-means-nothing' pattern M13 already named. It also compounds Dynamic Type: with the OS text size raised (allowFontScaling is on everywhere by default — 0 `allowFontScaling` / `maxFontSizeMultiplier` props in the app), tight Arabic leading clips sooner.

verdict_trail.reason: Every stated fact reproduces: `grep -rl useTypography src __tests__ App.tsx` returns only src/hooks/useTypography.ts and __tests__/hooks/useTypography.test.ts (zero production consumers); 54 .tsx under src reference `typography`; theme/index.ts:69-86 pins lineHeight at fontSize*1.5; the hook's AR_MULTIPLIER = 1.7/1.5 (:29). But this is not new: M18 already recorded the same defect class as MB-i18n-rtl-09 at P3 ('the arabicLineHeightMultiplier contract — which only 2 components app-wide actually consume'), which I confirmed at HEAD (only PaywallBanner.tsx and TwoInputShell.tsx). The hook predates the M18 base (present at 593ec1e, added by 01b460a), so it is a known-unmigrated design-spec deviation, not a M21 regression, and no clipping is demonstrated — RN does not clip text without a fixed height. Severity aligned to the M18 precedent.

findings.title: The brand emerald #10B981 measures 2.54:1 on white — it fails WCAG AA for normal text, for large text, and for UI components — and it is the app's link colour, its signature CTA fill and its selected-tab indicator
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Keep #10B981 for FILLS, BORDERS and large decorative marks (the winner outline, the vs pill, the ring hero) where it carries no text, and introduce a text-only emerald that clears 4.5:1 on white — #047857 (emerald-700) measures ~5.6:1 and #065F46 ~7.5:1; add it as `colors.accentText` and swap the 22 `color: colors.accent` sites plus the 32 `accentDark` text sites to it. For the `signature` Button variant either darken the fill to #047857 (white text then clears 4.5:1) or flip to black text on emerald (#0A0A0B on #10B981 = ~7.8:1). For the tab bar, keep the emerald tint but add a non-colour selected cue (the existing 4pt dot should become a 2-3px underline or a filled icon) so 1.4.1 Use of Color is satisfied independent of the ratio. Darken text.placeholder to #6B7280 (already in the palette at 4.83:1). No flag — it is a token swap, but it must be reviewed against the brand deck.
findings.test_first: A unit test over src/theme/index.ts that computes contrast for every (foreground token, background token) pair the app actually pairs and asserts >= 4.5 for text tokens and >= 3.0 for UI-state tokens. RED at HEAD for accent/accentDark/placeholder/warning/destructive on white. Pair it with a source-grep test that fails if `color: colors.accent` appears in any StyleSheet block (forcing the accentText token).
findings.impact: Low-vision users, and anyone in Gulf daylight, cannot read the app's link text, its signature emerald CTA label, or tell which tab is selected. This is the brand colour, so the failure is systemic rather than local — 22 text sites plus every emerald-filled button plus the tab bar. It is also the one accessibility class that gets cited in App Store accessibility complaints and in enterprise procurement checklists, and it is cheap to fix before launch and expensive after (it is a brand decision once marketing is live).

verdict_trail.reason: Recomputed every ratio independently with the WCAG 2.x sRGB-linearisation formula from the palette at theme/index.ts:3-31: #10B981/#FFFFFF 2.54, /#F8F8FA 2.39, /#ECFDF5 2.41, #059669/#FFFFFF 3.77, #9CA3AF/#FFFFFF 2.54, #F59E0B 2.15, #EF4444 3.76, accent-on-#0A0A0B 7.80 — all match the finding exactly. Site counts match exactly too: 22 `color: colors.accent` and 32 `color: colors.accentDark` in src. Button.tsx:93-94 signature fill = accent with text color cta.onPrimary #FFFFFF (:110-112); App.tsx:102-103 active tint = accent vs inactive placeholder; TabBarIcon.tsx:41 `const INACTIVE_COLOR = '#0A0A0B99';`. No prior M13/M18/mobile-checkup row covers contrast — genuinely new. Fix is a token swap, flag-free; its proposed replacements verify at #047857=5.48 (finder said ~5.6) and #065F46=7.68 (~7.5) — both still clear AA. P2 is right: quality/a11y, not a functional break.

findings.title: 42 of 128 interactive elements ship with no accessibilityRole — including three icon-only Results back buttons that announce nothing at all, and the EN/AR language switcher which never reports which language is selected
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityRole="button"` plus a translated `accessibilityLabel={t(...)}` to every icon-only control (the three ResultsScreen header buttons, ForgotPasswordScreen:127, RegisterScreen:438). Give ProfileScreen's language options `accessibilityRole="radio"` with `accessibilityState={{ selected: language === 'en' }}` (RN does not derive `selected`, unlike `disabled`). Give the History row and the Home/Profile editorial cards `accessibilityRole="button"` and a composed label ('iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24, compared 2 days ago'). Adopt a lint rule (eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y's has-accessibility-props / has-valid-accessibility-descriptors) so the count cannot regress. No flag — additive props only.
findings.test_first: A source-level test that runs the same JSX census as a11yscan.py over src/**/*.tsx and asserts every TouchableOpacity/Pressable carries accessibilityRole, and that any one whose children contain no <Text> also carries accessibilityLabel. RED at HEAD with 42 and ~8 violations respectively. Plus a render test on ResultsScreen's empty-state branch asserting getByRole('button', { name: /back/i }) resolves.
findings.impact: A VoiceOver/TalkBack user on Results in the loading, timeout or empty state has no way to know the top-left element is a back button (it announces as an unnamed element); on Profile they cannot tell whether the app is currently in English or Arabic; on Home the six category tiles and five trending rows do not announce as buttons; on the Paywall the restore-purchases control is unnamed. Because TouchableOpacity defaults `accessible={true}`, the elements ARE focusable — they are just unnamed or untyped, which is the worst combination: the user lands on them and learns nothing.

verdict_trail.reason: I wrote and ran an independent JSX opening-tag census over src/**/*.tsx and reproduced the finder's numbers exactly: TOTAL=128, noRole=42, noLabel=76, neither=35, accessibilityHint = 0 files. Opened the worst sites by hand and all match: ResultsScreen.tsx:629/:663/:710 are `<TouchableOpacity onPress={() => navigation.goBack()} style={styles.headerButton}>` wrapping only a DirectionalIcon+ArrowLeft (no role, no label, no text child); ProfileScreen.tsx:454/:460 language options carry only style-based selection; HistoryScreen.tsx:510 row has testID+style only. The 'cleared' sub-claim also checks out — RN 0.81.5 TouchableOpacity.js:279-285 merges a bare `disabled` into accessibilityState, so those 17 are correctly excluded — and OnboardingScreen is indeed dead at features.ts:30 CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT = 100. No prior review row covers a11y roles/labels. Fix is additive props, flag-free.

findings.title: 36 tap targets are smaller than 44pt and 25 of them have no hitSlop — including every Results header button (36x36) and the Profile language switcher (~27pt tall)
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: One-line each: add `hitSlop={{ top: 8, bottom: 8, left: 8, right: 8 }}` to every 36x36 and 40x40 control (36+16 = 52, 40+16 = 56) and `hitSlop` 12 to the 32x32 ones; give `langOption`, `govChip`, `consentButton`, `expandRow` and the chip styles `minHeight: 44` with `justifyContent: 'center'`. The safest single change is to add a shared `styles` constant (e.g. `export const HIT_SLOP_8`/`HIT_SLOP_12` in theme) and apply it, so the value is auditable. No flag — hitSlop expands the touch rect without moving any pixel.
findings.test_first: Extend the a11y census test to also resolve each touchable's style block and assert `(width ?? minHeight ?? paddingVertical*2 + lineHeight) + hitSlop*2 >= 44` on both axes. RED at HEAD for 36 sites (25 of them with hitSlop absent entirely).
findings.impact: Apple HIG requires 44x44pt and Android/WCAG 2.5.8 requires 48dp/24px minimum; 36x36 is 33% under on iOS. The affected controls are not incidental — they are the back and share buttons on Results (the screen every compare lands on), the settings gear on Profile, the header back on five secondary screens, and the language switcher. Users with tremor, large fingers, or a phone case mis-tap them; the Results back button mis-tap in particular lands on the TopMatchBadge centre area and does nothing.

verdict_trail.reason: I ran my own style-resolving scan (fixed w/h < 44, or no height/minHeight with paddingVertical <= 8) and got 35 under-44 sites with 28 lacking hitSlop, against the finder's 36/25 — same order, minor method drift, substance intact. Every named site reproduces: ResultsScreen.tsx:921 `headerButton: { width: 36, height: 36 }` used at :629/:663/:710 with no hitSlop; ResultsContent.tsx:205/:221 headerCircleBtn 36; ProfileScreen.tsx:343 36; ContactUsScreen:110 / EditPreferencesFlow:127 / LegalScreen:77 at 32; RegisterScreen:398 32; InviteeQuiz:293 and ReferralLanding:169 at 40; HomeScreen:695 h=28; FeedbackCard:70 h=36; HomeEditorialSections:205 h=40; ProfileScreen.tsx:796 `langOption` paddingVertical spacing.xs = 4. Counterexamples confirmed with hitSlop present: ImageSlotRow:47, HistoryScreen:628, PaywallScreen:253. New (no prior row). hitSlop/minHeight is flag-free and pixel-neutral.

findings.title: Nested touchables hide the inner control from VoiceOver: the History row's delete button and the camera slot's remove button sit inside accessible parents and are unreachable by screen reader on iOS
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Replace the nested button with an `accessibilityActions` entry on the row: `accessibilityActions={[{ name: 'delete', label: t('history.delete') }]}` plus `onAccessibilityAction={({nativeEvent}) => nativeEvent.actionName === 'delete' && onDelete(item)}` on the row TouchableOpacity — VoiceOver then exposes Delete in the rotor and TalkBack in its actions menu, while the visible × keeps working for sighted users. Do the same for ImageSlotRow (a 'remove' action on the slot). For the two modal backdrops, set the backdrop `accessible={false}` / `importantForAccessibility="no"` so it is not a focus stop at all and the inner close button becomes reachable.
findings.test_first: A render test on HistoryRow asserting `getByTestId('history-row-x').props.accessibilityActions` contains a 'delete' action and that firing `onAccessibilityAction` with actionName 'delete' calls the onDelete prop. RED at HEAD (the prop does not exist). A weaker but still-red variant: assert the row sets `accessible={false}` while the inner delete keeps its role.
findings.impact: A blind user can open a comparison from History but cannot delete one — the only delete affordance on the row is inside the row's own accessibility element. Same for removing a captured photo from a camera slot before comparing: the slot announces 'Slot 1' and the × is invisible to the screen reader, so the user cannot correct a bad capture. Both are single-purpose destructive controls with no alternative path (History has no swipe-to-delete, no long-press menu; the camera slot has no 'clear all').

verdict_trail.reason: Both headline cases reproduce exactly at HEAD. Outer TouchableOpacity defaults accessible=true (RN 0.81.5 TouchableOpacity.js:303 `accessible={this.props.accessible !== false}`), and it encloses the delete button. ImageSlotRow sets an EXPLICIT `accessible` grouping around the remove button. Live on phones: ImageSlotRow is unchanged between the shipped bundle 97b5f15 and 76ace90. One sub-claim is wrong: ConfidenceDetailsSheet is NOT a nesting case. Device behaviour (iOS grouping) is documented, not observed — finder says so. P2 stands.

findings.title: HomeEditorialSections is unmemoized and takes three inline arrow props, so every Home mode-tab tap re-renders the whole editorial subtree — four self-fetching sections and their remote images
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Wrap HomeEditorialSections in React.memo and hoist the three handlers into `useCallback` in HomeScreen (they close over `navigation`, `setSelectedCategory` and `handleModeChange`, all stable or stabilisable) — memo alone is a no-op while the props are arrow literals, so both halves are required. Optionally memoize the four sections too so a future prop change on one does not walk the other three. No flag; pure render-scheduling.
findings.test_first: Mirror the pattern already used in HistoryScreen.mobileJank.m21.test.tsx: spy on `deriveTone` (HomeEditorialSections.tsx:39 imports it and calls it twice per SmartPick tile at :87-88), render HomeScreen, fire a press on `home-mode-type`, and assert `deriveTone` was called 0 times after the tap. RED at HEAD.
findings.impact: Home is the app's landing screen and the mode segment is its most-tapped control. Each tap re-renders 767 lines of editorial JSX: the SmartPick card with two remote <Image> tiles, six category tiles each with an icon, a savings banner, and five trending rows — none of which changed. The sections' own fetched state survives (they are not remounted, so no extra network), but the reconciliation and the deriveTone() work per card repeat. This is exactly the class MB-perf-06 fixed on Results and left untouched on Home.

verdict_trail.reason: Code claims all reproduce; the impact does not support P2 and it is not new. M18 MB-perf-06 is titled 'Zero React.memo in the entire app' and was rated P3; M21 memoized Results and History and left Home — this is that row's residual, status still-open. Cost recomputed: no refetch (state survives), no image redecode, and deriveTone is a plain substring table lookup (deriveTone.ts BRAND_TONES), so a tap costs a small unmeasured reconciliation. '767 lines of editorial JSX' is the FILE length, not the rendered tree. Fix (memo + useCallback, both halves) is correct and flag-free.

findings.title: The app's only virtualized list ships with zero tuning — no initialNumToRender, windowSize, removeClippedSubviews, maxToRenderPerBatch or getItemLayout, and an inline keyExtractor
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-07 covered the row stagger and the per-keystroke row re-render (BOTH FIXED at HEAD — stagger capped at 6 steps via rowEntranceDelayMs at :117, row extracted into React.memo at :406, renderItem useCallback'd at :786, pinned by HistoryScreen.mobileJank.m21.test.tsx). The list's virtualization configuration was never in scope of that finding — this part is new.
findings.fix: Set `initialNumToRender={8}` (a phone shows ~4-5 of these rows), `maxToRenderPerBatch={8}`, `windowSize={7}`, `removeClippedSubviews={true}` (safe here — the rows have no nested horizontal virtualization), and hoist `keyExtractor` and `renderSectionHeader` to module-level constants / useCallback. `getItemLayout` is available too because rowV2 has a fixed composition, but measure the real row height first rather than guessing. No flag.
findings.test_first: A render test asserting the SectionList element's props include removeClippedSubviews true and a windowSize <= 10, plus that `keyExtractor` is referentially identical across two renders of HistoryScreen. RED at HEAD on all three.
findings.impact: windowSize 21 on a 50-row page with 2 remote images per row means the list can hold on the order of 100 decoded bitmaps mounted at once on a mid-range Android device, and removeClippedSubviews=false keeps the off-screen row views in the native hierarchy. Combined with -12 (iOS still decodes og:images at full resolution), this is the app's largest single memory surface. It is also the list that shows a spinner on every tab focus (-13), so the cost is paid repeatedly.

verdict_trail.reason: The prop list at 891-905 is complete and contains no virtualization prop; RN defaults re-derived from the installed source, not from memory. Page size 50 at :673 and 2 ProductImage per row confirmed, so the ~100-image window arithmetic holds (windowSize 21 x ~4-5 rows/screen > 50 rows available). Dedupe is accurate: MB-perf-07's two halves ARE fixed at HEAD (rowEntranceDelayMs caps at 6 steps, HistoryRow is React.memo'd, renderItem useCallback'd); virtualization config was never in its scope. Caution on the fix: removeClippedSubviews=true on iOS has a history of blanking cells — land it behind a device check.

findings.title: Nothing in the app queries AccessibilityInfo, and four components' docstrings claim a useReducedMotion behaviour that does not exist — the JS-driven motion on the loading screen ignores the OS switch
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add a `useReducedMotionPreference()` hook (Reanimated already exports `useReducedMotion`, or read `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` plus its `reduceMotionChanged` listener) and consume it in the three JS-driven places: LoadingRings jumps the counter straight to counterTarget; LoadingScreenVariants sets stageCursor to the real backend stage without the 900ms walk (or holds it); LoadingTipsCarousel shows one tip without rotation. Delete or correct the four false docstrings in the same change. Gate the StageChecklist haptic on the same preference. No feature flag — it is a strictly-reducing behaviour change.
findings.test_first: Mock AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled -> true, render LoadingRings with animated and counterTarget 2074, advance 0ms, and assert the counter chip already reads '2,074'. RED at HEAD (it reads '0' and animates). Second red test: assert LoadingScreenVariants does not schedule its STAGE_CYCLE_MS interval when reduce motion is on.
findings.impact: A user who has turned Reduce Motion on to avoid vestibular triggers still gets a rolling four-digit counter, a five-step checklist walking itself every 900ms, and rotating tip text for the full 25-31s of a compare, plus a haptic pulse per stage. The docstrings make this look handled, so a reviewer grepping for 'useReducedMotion' finds four reassuring hits and stops. Compounds with -02: for these users the Reanimated rings simultaneously resolve to opacity 0, so the ONLY thing moving on the loading screen is the motion that should have stopped.

verdict_trail.reason: Verified: four grep hits, all comments, zero AccessibilityInfo/useReducedMotion imports anywhere in src or App.tsx; the rAF counter and the two JS intervals are real and none consults the OS flag; Reanimated 4.1.7 does default to the system flag. Two impact corrections: the counter runs motion.counterTick = 2400ms (not the whole wait), and the 5-stage checklist walk finishes in 5 x 900ms = 4.5s then freezes at stageCount (the interval keeps firing but setState bails) — only LoadingTipsCarousel's 4s rotation runs the full 18-30s. Every file is unchanged since the shipped 97b5f15 bundle, so it is live. P2 stands.

findings.title: The 25-31s compare loading screen is silent to screen readers — no live region, no announcement — and StageChecklist labels each stage glyph with an untranslated English status word
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Put `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` on the caption Text (LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:271) and on the stage card (:283) so each stage advance and caption change is announced on Android, and call `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(t('loading.stage.x'))` on stage transitions for iOS parity. In StageChecklist, drop `accessibilityLabel={s.status}` from the glyph and instead put `accessibilityRole="text"` with a composed translated label on the ROW ('Checking prices, done'), marking the glyph `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` as ScannerReticle.tsx:39-40 already does correctly. This also directly serves the known SSE-honesty item (checkup #2): once the checklist is re-paced to the real ~30s envelope, the live region carries that honesty to screen-reader users for free. No flag.
findings.test_first: Render LoadingScreenVariants in comparison mode and assert `getByTestId('loading-caption').props.accessibilityLiveRegion === 'polite'`. RED at HEAD. Second: render StageChecklist with a 'done' stage under i18n language 'ar' and assert no rendered accessibilityLabel equals the literal 'done'.
findings.impact: A screen-reader user taps Compare and gets nothing for up to 30 seconds — no 'comparing', no progress, no stage change, no completion cue; the screen simply goes quiet and then Results appears. Because focus is not moved or announced on the transition either, the user's cursor may still be on the (now unmounted) Compare button. The stage glyphs that DO carry a label announce 'done' / 'pending' in English to an Arabic user, which is both untranslated and semantically wrong for a decorative glyph (accessibilityRole="image" with a status word as its name).

verdict_trail.reason: Both halves reproduce. LoadingScreenVariants.tsx (612 lines) has zero 'accessib' matches; the app has exactly one accessibilityLiveRegion (ResultsScreen.tsx:813) and zero announceForAccessibility/setAccessibilityFocus. The glyph label is the raw StageStatus union member while the row LABEL beside it IS translated (`label: t(row.key, ...)` at :199) — so the untranslated-English claim is specifically about the glyph and is correct. One calibration: baseline p50 is 0 (cache hits), so 25-31s is the p95/p99 tail, not the typical wait; p90 = 18.5s still leaves a long silent window. Fix is additive props plus an announce call, no flag. File unchanged since the shipped 97b5f15 bundle.

findings.title: The Paywall ships as a transparentModal with no accessibilityViewIsModal — VoiceOver can walk straight past it into the Home screen behind; 4 of 6 modal surfaces have the same gap
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityViewIsModal` to the four missing roots (PaywallScreen's container View, ConfidenceDetailsSheet's sheet View, CameraHelpOverlay's card, ProfileScreen's password modal content) — on iOS that hides everything outside the subtree from VoiceOver; pair it with `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` on the sibling content for Android. Then move focus on mount: `const ref = useRef(null); useEffect(() => { const tag = findNodeHandle(ref.current); if (tag) AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(tag); }, [])` on each sheet's title. Give the ConfidenceDetailsSheet backdrop `accessibilityRole="button"` + `accessibilityLabel={t('common.close')}` or make it `accessible={false}` so it is not an unnamed focus stop. No flag — additive props.
findings.test_first: Render PaywallScreen and assert its root View props include `accessibilityViewIsModal: true`; repeat for the other three. RED at HEAD for all four. The correct shape is already demonstrated in DemographicsBottomSheet.a11y.test.tsx, so the test can be cloned.
findings.impact: The paywall is the freemium gate — the one screen where the app must be unambiguous. A VoiceOver user swiping right past the paywall's last element lands on the Home screen's compare card behind it and can operate controls that are visually covered, including the Compare CTA that just sent them here. The same applies to the confidence-details sheet on Results and the password-change modal on Profile (where the covered content includes the sign-out row). Focus is also never moved into any of these sheets on open, so the user must hunt for them.

verdict_trail.reason: Census is exact: 6 modal surfaces, 2 carry accessibilityViewIsModal, 4 do not, and the Paywall really is the one route registered transparentModal (which keeps Home mounted in the same RN root — the strongest case). PaywallScreen's root View at :250 has no such prop and nothing in the app moves accessibility focus. Two calibrations: 7 routes use presentation:'modal', not 6; and for the three RN `<Modal>` cases iOS presents its own view controller, so the escape risk there is weaker than for the transparentModal — though the team already added the prop to two of those sheets, so the inconsistency is real either way. Device-unverified static claim; fix is additive props, no flag. Live: PaywallScreen/ConfidenceDetailsSheet/CameraHelpOverlay unchanged since the shipped 97b5f15 bundle.

findings.title: ProductImage's downsampling fix is Android-only — iOS still decodes full-resolution og:image bitmaps into 64-160pt tiles, and expo-image is still not a dependency
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-08 PARTIALLY-FIXED — resizeMethod="resize" landed in M21 (ProductImage.tsx was touched in 593ec1e..76ace90); the iOS half and the expo-image adoption named in the original fix are still open. Fresh evidence: expo-image confirmed absent from package.json at HEAD.
findings.fix: Add `expo-image` (SDK 54 aligned, no lockfile risk beyond the normal install) and swap the single <Image> inside this one primitive for expo-image's, passing `recyclingKey={imageUrl}`, `contentFit` mapped from the existing resizeMode prop, and explicit `width`/`height` where the tile size is known — every consumer inherits it because they all go through this primitive. If adding the dependency is not acceptable before launch, the cheaper interim is to pass concrete numeric `width`/`height` in the image style at each call site so iOS can at least size the decode, and to wrap ProductImage in React.memo so it stops re-diffing on unrelated parent renders.
findings.test_first: A source test asserting ProductImage imports Image from 'expo-image' and passes a recyclingKey — RED at HEAD. Interim variant: assert the rendered <Image> receives numeric width and height style values rather than '100%'.
findings.impact: On iOS the History screen still decodes up to ~100 full-resolution merchant og:images (routinely 1000-2400px) into 64-160pt tiles — the exact scenario MB-perf-08 described, now fixed on one platform only. Combined with -09 (windowSize 21, removeClippedSubviews false) this is the app's peak memory moment and the most likely OOM/jetsam on older iPhones. No device measurement was possible, so the magnitude is modelled.

verdict_trail.reason: Verified at HEAD: `Image` imported from 'react-native' (:29), `resizeMethod="resize"` at :111 with the Android-only comment, style width/height '100%' (tileImage :167-171), no React.memo, expo-image undefined in package.json. I strengthened it: app.json newArchEnabled:true and Fabric's RCTImageManager.mm:97 passes `clipped:NO`, so RCTResizeImageIfNeeded never runs on iOS — the full-res UIImage is retained. Known M18/MB-perf-08, Android half fixed, iOS half open. Fix caveat: the interim 'numeric style width/height' would NOT help (size comes from imageSource.size and clipped:NO skips resize); expo-image is the only working option.

findings.title: History's focus effect pins the first render's closure, so every tab return refetches unfiltered and blanks the screen — eslint flags it and the M21 rewrite left it in place

Search -> tap a row -> back returns the FULL unfiltered 50-row page while the TextInput still displays the query, so the list contradicts the visible filter. HistoryScreen is one of the three tab screens and was rewritten in M21 (+373/-272); its 45.04% branch coverage did not catch this and its tests are source-greps. eslint flagged it, but frontend-tests treats warnings as non-blocking by design (ci.yml:270 comment).

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced statically at HEAD, line-exact. useCallback with [] freezes render-0's callback, which closes over render-0's `loadHistory` const, which reads render-0's `searchQuery` ('') — react-navigation re-invokes that same frozen effect on every focus event. onSubmitEditing's inline arrow is re-created each render so search itself works; only refocus regresses. HistoryScreen stays mounted under the pushed Results screen (that is why useFocusEffect exists), and nothing resets searchQuery, so the list contradicts the visible filter. One correction: dedupe is NOT new — the 2026-09-02 mobile checkup item 12 filed exactly this at the pre-rewrite `:347-351` and flagged "RE-VERIFY FIRST"; this is the re-verification, still-open at :664-668. P1 stands.

Reproduced in a real render of HistoryScreen (scratch jest, deleted). Mount fetches (50,0,undefined); submitEditing fetches (50,0,'iphone'); exactly ONE focus callback is ever registered; re-invoking it fetches (50,0,undefined) while the TextInput value is still 'iphone'. I also read @react-navigation/core useFocusEffect: it stores the frozen effect and calls it on every 'focus' event, so this is deterministic, not incidental. The proposed dep fix closes THIS repro (measured: fixed shape refetches with 'iphone') but introduces a new defect - useCallback([searchQuery]) makes the focus effect re-subscribe per keystroke: typing 'iphone' fired 7 fetches in my measurement. Prefer a searchQueryRef read inside a []-stable callback. test_first is the right red test.

findings.title: __tests__/setup.ts silences console.warn and console.error for the whole suite, so React act()/key/unmounted-update warnings can never fail or even be seen — and the CI step calls this a 'console fence'

findings.fix: Replace the noops with jest.spyOn wrappers that record and, in an afterEach, FAIL the test on any console.error containing 'not wrapped in act' / 'unique \"key\"' / 'Warning:' unless the test opted out via an explicit allowlist helper. Land it warn-only for one pass to size the backlog, then flip to throwing. Rename the ci.yml:263 step to match reality until a fence actually exists. Test-infra only; no product flag.
findings.test_first: A meta-test: `it('fails when a component updates state outside act', () => { … })` plus, as the immediate red signal, temporarily removing the two noop lines and counting suites that go red — that count is the hidden backlog.
findings.impact: React logs 'An update to X inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)', 'Each child in a list should have a unique key', 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' and every error-boundary throw through console.error. All are permanently muted, so the suite cannot detect unwrapped async state updates — precisely the class of defect behind the M21 mobile-jank workstream — and a component that throws inside an error boundary can still show as PASS. It also makes the CI step name docs-as-wrong-truth: there is no console fence.

verdict_trail.reason: The defect reproduces: setup.ts:14-16 is a direct assignment (not a spy), so restoreAllMocks cannot undo it, and it loads for every suite. Two evidence errors to correct: the jest key is `setupFilesAfterEnv` at jest.config.js:53, not `setupFilesAfterEach` at :57; and a console fence DOES exist — just in the pytest job (tests/test_security_regression.py:502/513 test_no_bare_console_log_in_auth/_in_api), while the i18n half of the step name is real (4 files under __tests__/i18n). Only one jest file touches console, as claimed. Severity unchanged.

findings.title: ts-jest runs transpile-only (isolatedModules) under a deprecated `globals` block, so jest type-checks nothing — a mock returning a wrong shape is caught by neither gate at the moment it is used
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Move the ts-jest options out of `globals` into `transform: { '^.+\\.tsx?$': ['ts-jest', { tsconfig: { jsx: 'react' }, isolatedModules: true }] }` (mechanical, kills the 245 warnings and the ts-jest-30 cliff). Then add a type-conformance file that tsc DOES check, e.g. `__mocks__/__conformance__.ts` containing `const _rn: Partial<typeof import('react-native')> = RNMock;` for each mapped module — that single file converts every future mock-shape drift into a red tsc.
findings.test_first: Add `__mocks__/__conformance__.ts` with `const _rn: Partial<typeof import('react-native')> = RNMockDefault;` — RED today because the mock's Platform lacks `Version` and its FlatList/SectionList signatures do not match RN's generics.
findings.impact: Two consequences. (a) Jest gives no type feedback, so the only thing standing between a mock and a shape error is the separate tsc job — and tsc resolves `react-native` to the REAL package types, never to __mocks__/react-native.ts (moduleNameMapper is a jest-only concept), so nothing anywhere asserts that a mock is assignable to the module it replaces. That is the structural hole the Sentry-Python-shape precedent fell through and the one MB-TESTS-TRUTH-10 documents concretely. (b) The deprecated config form is scheduled for removal in ts-jest 30; a routine devDependency bump turns the config into a silent no-op (losing `jsx: 'react'`) and reddens all 245 suites at once.

verdict_trail.reason: Verified at HEAD and reproduced live. The globals block sits at jest.config.js:6-13 with isolatedModules:true at :11; ts-jest installed is 29.4.9 as claimed. My own run emitted the deprecation warning repeatedly plus an explicit second one naming the removal version, which independently confirms the v30 cliff the finder modelled. tsconfig.json declares no `paths`, so tsc genuinely resolves react-native to the real package and never to __mocks__ — the structural hole is real. Minor: the file-count arithmetic 146+250+20 sums to 416, not 410; it reconciles only via the 9 src/**/__tests__ files double-counted. Not load-bearing.
