findings.test_first: `it('shares the comparison deep link', async () => { render(<ShareBottomSheet .../>); fireEvent.press(getByText('share.whatsapp')); await waitFor(()=>expect(Share.share).toHaveBeenCalled()); })` — today this fails with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'share')`, which is the finding.
findings.impact: Any test that reaches Share.share or Linking.openURL throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` — which is why no test does, and is independent proof that the share sheet and the retailer/source clickout (the app's only outbound-link paths, both relevant to the affiliate launch step) are entirely unexercised. The reanimated divergences are quieter and worse: a non-stable useSharedValue means any dependency array containing a shared value churns in tests but not in prod (and vice versa), so a stale-closure or infinite-render bug can be present in exactly one of the two environments; a constant `interpolate` makes any assertion about an interpolated value meaningless; the singleton entering-builders mean HistoryScreen's per-row stagger assertion reads a call log polluted by every other component in the tree.

findings.title: CI pins node 20 while the dev box runs node 24.11.1, and the repo has no engines field, no .nvmrc and no preinstall check — so neither the version skew nor a stale node_modules is detectable
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add `"engines": { "node": ">=20 <21" }` (matching CI) plus a `.nvmrc` containing `20`, and set `engine-strict=true` in a checked-in .npmrc so npm refuses to install on the wrong major. Add a `preinstall`-independent staleness check as a `pretest` script — a 6-line node script that compares the mtime of package-lock.json against node_modules/.package-lock.json and exits 1 with 'run npm ci' — so a stale tree fails loudly at `npm test` instead of surfacing as one weird suite. Align @types/node to ^20. Tooling only; no product flag.
findings.test_first: `pretest` guard itself: touch package-lock.json, run `npm test`, expect exit 1 with the 'run npm ci' message. Today it runs the whole suite and reports a bogus module-not-found in plurals.test.ts.
findings.impact: Two failure modes with the same root. (a) Version skew: a suite that passes on node 24 can fail on node 20 (or the reverse) with nothing declaring which is canonical — and @types/node ^25 means tsc is type-checking against APIs node 20 does not have, an error class tsc cannot report because the types are the ones lying. (b) Staleness: CI always runs `npm ci` into a clean tree, so ONLY the developer's box can go stale, and the first symptom is a mysterious red suite that looks like a code defect — which is exactly what happened to plurals.test.ts and cost this campaign a false lead. There is no mechanism that tells a developer their install is behind.

verdict_trail.reason: Every fact checks out. package.json (read in full) has no engines, preinstall or postinstall — only 8 scripts; there is no .nvmrc or .npmrc in SmartCompareApp/ or the repo root; ci.yml pins node 20 at :175, :209 and :255; the dev box is node v24.11.1 per baseline/README.txt and my own node banner; @types/node is ^25.5.0 and tsconfig's `types: [jest, node]` puts it in scope for a test tree that really does import fs/path. Impact (b), staleness, is measured — README.txt records the plurals.test.ts false lead. Impact (a), skew, remains modelled: tsc exits 0 and 2320 tests pass on node 24 while CI is green on node 20. Line 74 is `"private": true`; the @types/node line is the better anchor.

findings.title: Every referral link prod mints points at qaren.app, which returns 522 and serves no AASA/assetlinks — Android App Links autoVerify fails and iOS universal links are dead
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Two independent halves. (1) Get the qaren.app origin actually attached (Railway `qaren-landing` service is referenced by RAILWAY_SERVICE_QAREN_LANDING_URL but the Cloudflare origin is timing out) and add the two well-known files: `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (Content-Type application/json, NO .json extension, `{"applinks":{"details":[{"appIDs":["<TEAMID>.com.qaren.app"],"components":[{"/":"/r/*"},{"/":"/c/*"},{"/":"/q/*"}]}]}}`) and `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (with the SHA-256 signing-cert fingerprint of the PRODUCTION keystore — EAS-managed credentials, `eas credentials`). Both must be served over https with no redirect. (2) Until (1) lands, stop minting dead links: make `APP_BASE_URL` read `os.getenv('APP_BASE_URL', 'https://qaren.app')` and point prod at the Railway host that already serves the referral landing, so shared links resolve. Neither half rides the OTA — (1) is DNS/edge + a static file, (2) is a backend deploy; the assetlinks fingerprint additionally cannot be finalised until the first production build exists.
findings.test_first: A backend test asserting `referral_service.build_invite_url(code)` returns a host that responds 200 to GET, plus a CI smoke step (or a monitored canary) asserting `GET https://<APP_BASE_URL>/.well-known/assetlinks.json` is 200 with content-type application/json and `GET /.well-known/apple-app-site-association` is 200 — red today on both.
findings.impact: The entire referral/invite loop is broken end-to-end for every real user, not just testers. (a) A shared link https://qaren.app/r/QR-XXXXXX opens a Cloudflare 522 error page — no landing, no install funnel, no invite-code hand-off. (b) On Android, `autoVerify: true` makes the OS fetch /.well-known/assetlinks.json at install; a 522 fails verification, so Android 12+ does NOT route qaren.app links to the app by default (the user must manually enable 'Open supported links'), disabling the ReferralLanding/InviteeQuiz deep-link paths in App.tsx:284 `prefixes: ['qaren://','https://qaren.app']`. (c) On iOS, the AASA fetch fails so applinks:qaren.app never activates. ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in prod, so the backend is actively minting these dead links today. This is a launch blocker for the referral growth mechanic and, if qaren.app is also the App Store listing's privacy-policy URL, an ASC submission blocker.

verdict_trail.reason: Core reproduces: referral_service.py:50 is a bare literal (zero getenv/environ in the file), no APP_BASE_URL in web vars, ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true, and I measured 522/522/523/404. But a load-bearing evidence claim is FALSE: landing/.well-known/apple-app-site-association and assetlinks.json DO exist at 76ace90, nginx-wired with the real Team ID — so fix-half (1) is wrong (they need the real cert fingerprint, not creation). That half is known M18 CD-uncovered-06 (P3, still-open, placeholder unchanged; no /r/ nginx location). No production build or App Store listing exists, ~0 prod traffic, 2 internal testers — P1 overstates it.

findings.title: App requests RECORD_AUDIO and ships a boilerplate NSMicrophoneUsageDescription although no audio/microphone API is used anywhere in the codebase
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: In app.json: delete `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO` from `android.permissions`, and pass the explicit opt-outs so no plugin can re-add it — change the expo-camera entry to `["expo-camera", { "cameraPermission": "...", "microphonePermission": false, "recordAudioAndroid": false }]` and the expo-image-picker entry to `["expo-image-picker", { "photosPermission": "...", "microphonePermission": false }]` (both plugins branch on `=== false`, and image-picker additionally calls withBlockedPermissions in that case, which is what actually strips it from the merged manifest). Then run `npx expo prebuild --clean` and assert NSMicrophoneUsageDescription is absent from ios/Qaren/Info.plist and RECORD_AUDIO is absent from android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. No flag needed — this is config, not runtime behaviour.
findings.test_first: A repo-level config test (jest, reads app.json) asserting `android.permissions` does not contain RECORD_AUDIO AND that the expo-camera/expo-image-picker plugin entries set `microphonePermission: false` — red today. Follow with a prebuild-output assertion in the release runbook.
findings.impact: Blocks App Store production submission on two fronts. iOS: the generated Info.plist declares microphone access with Expo's generic boilerplate purpose string for a capability the app never invokes — Apple 5.1.1 requires purpose strings that are specific and describe an actual use, and an undeclared-use permission is a standard rejection/Information-Needed trigger. Android: the Play listing will display 'Microphone' under app permissions and the Data safety form must be reconciled, for a permission with no feature behind it. This is a NEEDS-NATIVE-BUILD defect — no OTA can remove it, so it must land before the first production `eas build` or the build has to be redone.

verdict_trail.reason: Every mechanical claim reproduces, and the runtime side is stronger than claimed: a case-insensitive grep of src+App.tsx for audio|microphone returns ZERO hits (not one), the only camera use is CameraView still photos, ImagePicker is called only with MediaTypeOptions.Images, and package.json has no expo-av/expo-audio. Triple re-add path verified in node_modules. iOS boilerplate string resolution verified in the config-plugin source. Not in M18/M13/mobile-checkup. NEEDS-NATIVE-BUILD, no OTA can remove it, so it genuinely gates the first production eas build — P1 stands. Proposed fix (microphonePermission:false on both plugins) matches the code branches I read.

Reproduced by EXECUTING the real plugins, not reading them. Running expo-camera's withCamera against app.json's actual options and then invoking its ios infoPlist mod yields NSMicrophoneUsageDescription = 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your microphone' (Expo boilerplate) beside the app's real camera string, and android.permissions keeps RECORD_AUDIO. Runtime side is stronger than the finding says: case-insensitive grep for audio|microphone over src+App.tsx returns ZERO hits; only CameraView still photos and ImagePicker MediaTypeOptions.Images. The proposed fix CLOSES it, measured: with microphonePermission:false on both plugins, recordAudioAndroid:false, and RECORD_AUDIO removed from app.json, the mod output is NSMicrophoneUsageDescription undefined and android.permissions ['android.permission.CAMERA']. test_first (app.json config jest test) is right and red today. Caveat: 'Apple will reject' is modelled, not measured; the over-declaration and the needs-native-build gate are measured.

findings.title: initSentry() runs AFTER every imported module body (Babel hoists requires), so the new 'running unpinned' security alarm shipping in this OTA is dropped in exactly the failure mode it was written for
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Move the Sentry bootstrap into a module that is imported FIRST and does its work at module-evaluation time: create `src/services/sentryBootstrap.ts` whose module body calls `Sentry.init(...)` (not a function you call later), and make its `import './src/services/sentryBootstrap';` the first import in index.ts (the app entry, before App.tsx is required at all). Because Babel preserves require ORDER, a first-position side-effect import evaluates before every other module body. Independently, make the pinning alarm order-proof: in certificatePinning.ts wrap the failure path so it re-fires after init — e.g. record the failure in a module-scope flag and have the Sentry bootstrap (or App.tsx's first effect) flush it — so a synchronous throw is still reported. Both are JS-only and can ride the same OTA; no flag required.
findings.test_first: A jest test that requires the real entry graph with `@sentry/react-native` mocked and asserts `Sentry.init` was called BEFORE the api.ts module body ran (assert call ordering via a shared spy log), plus a unit test that makes `initializeSslPinning` throw synchronously and asserts `Sentry.captureMessage` is still observed after bootstrap — both red today.
findings.impact: Two effects, both on the bundle the pending OTA would install. (a) The brand-new unpinned-fleet alarm is a no-op in its PRIMARY documented case ('misbuilt binary, native-side error' / unlinked module), because that case throws synchronously before Sentry has a client — the whole point of MB-security-07 (console.* is babel-stripped in release, so Sentry is the only channel) is defeated and a fleet running with certificate pinning silently OFF stays invisible. If instead the native module is present and `initialize` REJECTS, the catch runs in a microtask after initSentry() and the alarm does work — so the control is 50% dead, in the half that matters. (b) More broadly, the stated invariant is false for every early-import crash (i18n init, font loading, api.ts module scope, screen module bodies) — none of those are captured, which is precisely the class of boot crash an OTA can introduce.

verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced the babel hoist with the app's own preset: requires emit before the initSentry() call, so App.tsx:6-10's stated invariant is false. api.ts:22 is a bare module-scope setupCertificatePinning(); the ssl lib's Proxy get throws synchronously inside initializeSslPinning's body (`return SslPublicKeyPinning.initialize(options)`), and since that throw happens while evaluating the await operand inside the try, the catch — and captureMessage — run during module evaluation, before any Sentry client exists. Correctly scoped: the sync-throw case is the misbuilt/unlinked binary only (in Expo Go __DEV__ takes the other branch), and a rejecting native initialize still reports. P2 right; fix (first-position side-effect import in index.ts + order-proof flush) is sound — index.ts requires App second.

findings.title: ISRG Root YE — the actual root of the live certificate chain — is not pinned; the fleet survives only because Root YE is currently cross-signed by ISRG Root X2, so a YE1 rotation re-bricks every build (the 2026-07-06 failure mode)
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add `const ISRG_ROOT_YE = 'sCkq5UWXjg+7mKu9lMhhYF5bGLsy7VI/UNW3tccdR7w=';` to certificatePinning.ts and insert it in `publicKeyHashes` immediately after ISRG_ROOT_X2, with a comment recording that it is the self-signed root of the CURRENT ECDSA issuance path and therefore survives any YE-family intermediate rotation. Verify the value with the openssl command already in the file's header before committing (I derived it from the live chain, not from a published LE page). This is pure JS and rides the pending OTA. Longer term, replace the hand-maintained list with a scheduled canary: a cron that pulls the live chain daily and fails loudly when no served SPKI is in the pinned set — that is the control that would have caught 2026-07-06 before users did.
findings.test_first: A jest test that reads the committed pin list and asserts it contains the SPKI hash of every certificate in a checked-in fixture of the live chain (chain.pem), red today for Root YE; plus a scheduled job asserting the same against the LIVE chain so the test decays into an alarm rather than a stale fixture.
findings.impact: Latent total-outage risk with a documented precedent: the file's own header records that on 2026-07-06 Railway rotated to intermediate YE1 and 'app bricked with Network Error'. Today the fleet is protected by TWO pins that both sit on the current ECDSA issuance path — YE1 (the intermediate, which rotates) and ISRG Root X2 (reachable only because Let's Encrypt currently cross-signs Root YE to X2). If LE rotates YE1 -> YE2 while serving the shorter, self-anchored chain (leaf -> YE2 -> Root YE), zero pins match and EVERY pinned build fails all backend calls — identical to July. The remedy is OTA-shippable, but only if an OTA can still be published, and a bricked app still downloads updates, so recovery is possible; the outage window is nonetheless hours-to-days. Not currently reachable, hence P2 not P1.

verdict_trail.reason: Independently re-measured the live chain and recomputed all four SPKI hashes: Root YE's pin is sCkq5UWXjg+7mKu9lMhhYF5bGLsy7VI/UNW3tccdR7w=, byte-identical to the finder's value, and it is absent from publicKeyHashes (lines 55-61 pin X2, X1, YE1, E7, E8, E5) — exactly 2 of 4 chain members pinned. Distinct from M18 MB-security-04 (the X1/RSA pin, which shipped and I verified present at line 44). Correctly rated P2: the brick needs BOTH a YE-family intermediate rotation AND a chain shortened past the X2 cross-sign, so it is not reachable today; the 2026-07-06 precedent is in the file's own header. Fix is additive JS, OTA-safe.

findings.title: No sourcemap upload exists on either lever — every JS crash from the pending OTA (and from the installed builds) arrives in Sentry unsymbolicated
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Two steps, both required. (1) Native builds: add an `env` block to eas.json's preview and production profiles carrying `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` as an EAS secret (`eas secret:create --name SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`), which lets the @sentry/react-native config plugin upload at build time. (2) OTA — this is the one that actually matters here: after every `eas update`, run the Expo sourcemap upload against the exported bundle (`npx sentry-expo-upload-sourcemaps dist` or `npx @sentry/react-native/scripts/expo-upload-sourcemaps dist` after `npx expo export`), so the update's debugId-tagged maps land in Sentry. Bake step (2) into docs/runbooks/qaren-canary-onboarding.md and the EAS deploy skill as a mandatory line after the publish command, next to the existing 'don't say OTA ships next — actually run the command' rule.
findings.test_first: Not unit-testable. The pinning check is a release-runbook assertion: after the next `eas update --branch preview`, confirm the update's bundle appears in Sentry -> Settings -> Debug Files / Artifacts for the matching debugId, then deliberately throw from a debug screen on a preview build and confirm the Sentry issue shows file:line, not `index.android.bundle:1:xxxxx`.
findings.impact: Every diagnostic control this OTA adds depends on Sentry being readable, and none of them are: the '[SECURITY] Certificate pinning init failed' message (-03), the '[GOOGLE-DIAG]/[B4-DIAG]' breadcrumbs and captureMessage that are the ONLY instrumentation for the open 'Google Sign-In fails on EAS preview' bug, the SSE-fallback breadcrumb, and any unhandled JS crash. In a release build babel strips all console.*, so an unsymbolicated Sentry stack (minified frames against a Metro bundle with no debugId mapping) is the entire diagnostic surface. Concretely: the Google Sign-In failure that currently blocks tester onboarding cannot be root-caused from the dashboard.

verdict_trail.reason: Every negative reproduces: eas.json has no env block on any of the three profiles, no sentry.properties / .sentryclirc / .env* exists under SmartCompareApp (find, excluding node_modules), and none of the eight package.json scripts uploads sourcemaps — while the @sentry/react-native plugin object form IS present at app.json:130-134, so the plugin is wired but tokenless. The eas-update point is right: an update republishes a new JS bundle to installed binaries, so a build-time map does not describe it. Not in M18's 175 rows; M13-114 only nits the SDK version and calls sourcemap upload a deferred follow-up. P2 correct (diagnostics quality, not live user harm); the two-step fix is accurate.

findings.title: CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100 has no guard anywhere — nothing in CI, tests or eas.json stops `eas update --branch production` from shipping the 17-step flow to 100% of App Store users
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-two-lever-06 still-open
findings.fix: Make the invariant mechanical rather than documentary. Add to __tests__/config/features.test.ts an assertion that fails outside build/test mode — e.g. `if (process.env.QAREN_RELEASE_CHANNEL === 'production') expect(CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT).toBeLessThanOrEqual(10)` — and, better, add a `scripts/preflight-release.js` that the runbook requires before any `eas update --branch production`: it reads features.ts, refuses when CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT > 10, and prints the diff of every exported const in src/config/ between the current HEAD and the last published production update. Wire it as an npm script (`npm run preflight:production`) and cite it in docs/runbooks/qaren-canary-onboarding.md §2 so it sits directly above the publish command.
findings.test_first: `__tests__/config/features.releaseGuard.test.ts`: with QAREN_RELEASE_CHANNEL=production set, expect CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT <= 10 — red today at 100, green once the operator resets it, and it stays red forever if someone reverts.
findings.impact: The documented soft-launch procedure is a comment and a runbook line with no mechanical backstop, and the mistake is one command away: the operator's muscle-memory command is `eas update --branch preview` (testers), and the production publish is the same command with one word changed. Shipping 100% removes the canary entirely — the whole point of Tasks 47/48 was a 10 -> 50 -> 100 ramp with metrics gates — so a regression in the new onboarding would hit every App Store user at once with no comparison cohort. verdict_trail.reason: Facts all reproduce — features.ts:30 = 100, the only assertion is a tautological 0..100 range check, hashBucket short-circuits at >=100, and `git diff 97b5f15..76ace90 -- SmartCompareApp/src/config/` is empty. But this is M18 MB-two-lever-06, which reviewed the same line, CONFIRMED it, rated it P3, and already prescribed exactly this remedy ('add to the App-Store-soft-launch checklist'). The finder's own dedupe admits it. Nothing has regressed and nothing new was found: no production-channel build or App Store listing exists, the 100 is deliberate policy for the two testers per CLAUDE.md, and the defect is a hypothetical future operator slip, not a live or reachable one. P3 per the brief's nit/latent band; the preflight-script fix is sound but is process hardening.

USER CONTENT -> Photos (camera/gallery -> /api/v1/image/identify, forwarded to OpenAI), Other User Content (typed product queries) — linked, App Functionality + Analytics. SEARCH HISTORY -> compare queries persisted in `comparisons`/`search_logs` — linked. DIAGNOSTICS -> Crash Data, Performance Data, Other Diagnostic Data (Sentry, tracesSampleRate 0.1) — linked unless Sentry is configured anonymously. verdict_trail.reason: Reproduced every cited line at 76ace90. §2.1/§2.2 really do omit demographics and any device identifier, while the code demonstrably sends both on a live, user-reachable path (onboarding flush + ResultsScreen call putDemographics; register always attaches X-Device-Fingerprint). §11 contradicts §2 as claimed and names Settings->Privacy while the toggle lives on Profile. findings.title: iOS privacy manifest declares required-reason APIs but no NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes at all, so the shipped manifest contradicts the nutrition label the app will need
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Add `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes` to app.json's `ios.privacyManifests`, one entry per type from the -07 enumeration, each with `NSPrivacyCollectedDataType` (e.g. NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeEmailAddress, ...Name, ...PhotosorVideos, ...SearchHistory, ...UserID, ...DeviceID, ...ProductInteraction, ...CrashData, ...PerformanceData, ...OtherDataTypes), `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked: true`, `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking: false`, and the matching purposes (NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality / ...Analytics). This is a native-build change — it must land before the production `eas build`, and no OTA can add it.
findings.test_first: A config test asserting `app.json -> ios.privacyManifests.NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes` is a non-empty array and that its set of NSPrivacyCollectedDataType values equals the set recorded in docs/privacy-data-inventory.md — red today (key absent).

The privacy manifest is the machine-readable half of Apple's privacy disclosure and is aggregated into the privacy report Apple generates for the app; a manifest asserting no data collection while the ASC label declares email, identifiers, photos, search history, usage and diagnostics is an inconsistency reviewers and the automated privacy-report tooling surface. findings.title: runtimeVersion is pinned to appVersion 1.0.0 with appVersionSource=remote and autoIncrement=true, so a future native change will NOT bump the runtime and an incompatible OTA will be delivered to old binaries
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: Either (a) switch to `"runtimeVersion": { "policy": "fingerprint" }`, which derives the runtime from the actual native fingerprint so any native change automatically forks the runtime and an incompatible OTA simply never reaches old builds; or (b) keep appVersion and add the discipline mechanically: a `scripts/preflight-release.js` check (same script as -06) that diffs SmartCompareApp/package.json dependencies and app.json between HEAD and the SHA of the last published update, and refuses to proceed when any dependency ships native code or app.json changed while `version` did not. (a) is strictly better and is a one-line app.json change, but it is itself a native-build change and must land with the next `eas build`.
findings.test_first: A preflight test fed two synthetic commits — one adding a pure-JS dep, one adding a native dep — asserting it passes on the first and fails on the second while app.json `version` is unchanged.
findings.impact: Latent, but it is the exact trap the team is one dependency away from: today's OTA is safe only because both new deps (axios, intl-pluralrules) happen to be pure JS. The next time a NATIVE module is added (a payments SDK, a new expo-* module, an SDK bump), runtimeVersion will not change, so `eas update` will happily publish a bundle that references a native module the installed binaries do not contain — expo-updates will consider it compatible and deliver it, and the app crashes on launch for everyone on the old build. The symmetric trap is already documented (M18 MB-two-lever-04: bumping expo.version BEFORE an OTA retargets it at a runtime no device has, reaching zero phones), so the policy is hazardous in both directions.

verdict_trail.reason: All cited config reproduced exactly, and the EAS semantics are right: plain autoIncrement:true with appVersionSource remote bumps buildNumber/versionCode only, leaving expo.version — hence runtimeVersion — pinned at '1.0.0' across future builds. The forward trap (native dep added, runtime unchanged, incompatible OTA delivered to old binaries) is new; M18 MB-two-lever-04 only recorded the reverse ordering rule. Fix (a) fingerprint policy is valid on SDK 54 and correctly flagged as itself a native-build change. P3 latent is right — no user harm today.

findings.title: OTA verdict for 97b5f15..76ace90: native-compatible and safe to publish to --branch preview, but M18's 'zero dependency changes' premise no longer holds — two new JS deps now ride the bundle

Do NOT publish to --branch production: no production build exists, so it reaches zero devices. Verify on device with a force-close/reopen TWICE, then check Arabic counts at 0/1/2/3/11 on Home and History (the only device-observable proof the intl-pluralrules install took) and confirm one analytics event returns 2xx.
findings.test_first: Not a defect; the pinning artifact is a release-runbook checklist item plus the preflight script from -06/-09 that diffs dependencies for native code before every publish.

Only Updates.* in src is useLanguage.ts:23. M18 MB-two-lever-04's 'zero dependency changes' premise is indeed regressed; the no-eas-build conclusion survives. On-device propagation claims are not device-verified but the code-side basis is.

findings.title: The OTA re-derives the paywall gate a second time and now hard-depends on backend `remaining.{daily,monthly}`; the silent fallback when those fields are absent is the M13-14 hard-3 dead-end with no alarm
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-two-lever-02 fixed-then-re-derived
findings.fix: Make the degradation visible rather than silent: when `status` is non-null but `hasBackendAxes` is false, fire a one-shot `Sentry.captureMessage('usage status missing remaining axes', { level: 'warning', extra: { keys: Object.keys(status) } })` before falling back, so a shape drift shows up in the dashboard the same hour instead of as a support ticket. Pair it with a backend contract test that pins the exact key set of `get_usage_status()`'s response (tier, used.{daily,monthly,lifetime}, limits.{daily,monthly,monthly_base,monthly_bonus,lifetime_free}, remaining.{daily,monthly,lifetime_free}) so a rename breaks CI rather than the paywall. No flag needed — both are additive.
findings.test_first: A jest test rendering useComparisonCounter with a status payload that has `limits` but no `remaining`, asserting the Sentry warning fires (red today) — plus a pytest asserting the exact top-level and nested key sets of get_usage_status().

The fragility is that the client's paywall now silently degrades to a hard lifetime-3 dead-end (dead-ending every premium and referral-bonus holder, exactly the M13-14 failure) whenever the backend stops emitting `remaining.daily`/`remaining.monthly` — a field rename, a serializer change, or an older backend behind a rollback — with no telemetry distinguishing 'legitimately out of quota' from 'client fell back'. And the only repair channel is another OTA, i.e. hours-to-days.

verdict_trail.reason: Both sides reproduced. HEAD really does gate on backend axes with a silent collapse to used<3, and the shipped 97b5f15 bundle uses the previous lifetime+bonus formula — the third formula in three months, as claimed. The safety argument also holds: /api/v1/usage/status has no response_model, so get_usage_status()'s dict (including remaining.daily/monthly) reaches the client verbatim, and every other return branch carries 'remaining' too. M18 MB-two-lever-02 is fixed (the 2026-09-02 OTA shipped the lifetime+bonus formula); the new latent risk is the untelemetered degradation. P3 correct — no harm at the deployed SHA. Fix is additive and flag-free as stated.

findings.title: No force-update or kill-switch wiring exists anywhere in the client, and expo-updates is never checked at boot — a bad OTA can only be undone by another OTA that takes two launches to land
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup 'force-update wire dead' still-open
findings.fix: Two independent pieces, both OTA-shippable. (1) Propagation: in App.tsx's init, after auth resolves, call `Updates.checkForUpdateAsync()` and on `isAvailable` do `fetchUpdateAsync()` then `reloadAsync()` behind a new `ENABLE_EAGER_OTA_RELOAD` const in features.ts defaulted FALSE — reloading mid-session is disruptive, so ship it dark and flip it only when a hotfix needs to land in one launch instead of two. (2) Kill switch: add a `min_supported_build` field to an existing unauthenticated endpoint the app already hits at boot, compare against `Application.nativeBuildVersion`, and render a blocking 'update required' screen; that is the only control that works when the JS bundle itself is the problem and must therefore be part of the FIRST production build, not a later OTA.
findings.test_first: A jest test asserting App.tsx calls checkForUpdateAsync exactly once per cold start when ENABLE_EAGER_OTA_RELOAD is true and never when false (red today — no call site exists), plus a test that a `min_supported_build` above the current build renders the blocking screen.
findings.impact: Status confirmation of a mobile-checkup lead, now measured at HEAD: the force-update wire is not merely dead, it does not exist. Consequences for the two-lever model: (a) there is no server-side way to stop a bad bundle — remediation is 'publish a fixed OTA and wait two cold starts per device'; (b) there is no way to require a minimum native version once the App Store build exists, so a breaking backend change would strand old binaries with no in-app message; (c) the only in-app accelerator for OTA propagation is an unrelated side effect — switching language calls Updates.reloadAsync(), which also applies whatever update was downloaded. Latent (P3) while the population is <10 testers; it becomes a real gap the day the production channel has users.

verdict_trail.reason: Client-side claim reproduced exactly: the force_update/min_version grep exits 1 (zero hits) and expo-updates appears only at useLanguage.ts:22-23 (a third grep hit, Step02Language.tsx:27, is a comment); app.json:147-149 carries only 'url'; init() does language/RTL, stable id and auth and nothing update-related. (1) The impact's 'there is no server-side way to stop a bad bundle' is wrong — app/api/version_routes.py:19 serves GET /app/version with min_version and force_update from APP_MIN_VERSION/APP_FORCE_UPDATE; the contract EXISTS and has no client consumer, so the fix is to consume it, not invent min_supported_build. findings.title: P3 sweep: five smaller release-hygiene items verified at HEAD
findings.dedupe: new
findings.fix: (b) Export the promise from setupCertificatePinning and await it in an interceptor guard so the first request cannot precede pinning init (JS-only, OTA-shippable). (c) Add the eas.json env block per -05. (e) Either gate tryRegisterPushToken behind a features.ts const that mirrors the backend's ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES, or move the prompt behind a pre-permission explainer at the moment the user opts into re-engagement — both JS-only. (a) and (d) need no action beyond keeping axios current.
findings.test_first: For (b): a jest test asserting the first api request awaits the pinning promise (red today). For (e): a test asserting requestPermissionsAsync is not called on launch when the push feature const is false.
findings.impact: (a) is a positive status answer to the lane's explicit question — the instrumentation survives, so fixing -03/-05 makes the Google Sign-In bug tractable without shipping new code. (b) is a narrow unpinned window at boot on every launch. (c) explains -05 mechanically. (d) means no device-shipping vulnerability remains, and the OTA is the delivery vehicle for the one that did. (e) is a small App-Review and conversion cost: prompting for notifications with no explainer and no active use.

verdict_trail.reason: All five sub-claims reproduced. (a) diagHead carries no token material; the console.log is __DEV__-guarded but the Sentry breadcrumb (:556) and captureMessage (:602) are not, and babel.config.js:23-33 removes only ExpressionStatements whose callee object Identifier is 'console', so both survive release — the instrumentation does ship. (b) real: setupCertificatePinning is async (certificatePinning.ts:48, awaits initializeSslPinning at :52) and api.ts:22 calls it unwaited at module scope; window is short (auth fires several ticks later) so latent, P3 right, and it is new vs M18 MB-security-04/07. (c) eas.json has no env on any of the 3 profiles; sentry.ts:230-232 falls back to FALLBACK_DSN. (d) arithmetic recomputed: 20 high/critical rows = 1 critical (tar) + 19 high, only 'expo' direct, all build-time; axios lock 1.16.1 -> 1.20.0 in 54ff871 (package.json range was ^1.13.4). (e) App.tsx:202 and :246 call tryRegisterPushToken, pushTokenService.ts:62-64 prompts, prod ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES=false.
